follow-up</span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h2 id="media-and-email">Media and Email</h2> <h3 id="audio-video">Audio Video</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>audio-video</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/audio-video">skills/audio-video</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever the project contains audio or video content, media players, podcasts, video embeds, or any <audio>/<video> elements. Under no circumstances publish audio or video without captions, transcripts, and audio descriptions where required. Absolutely always apply WCAG 1.2 criteria for time-based media.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>audio-video/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="audiovideo-accessibility-skill">Audio/Video Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/AUDIO_VIDEO_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing or reviewing any audio or video content. <strong>Only load this skill if the project contains audio or video.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-13">Core Mandate</h5> <p>Accessible media provides equivalent access to speech, sound, visual information, and playback controls. The required alternatives depend on whether the media is audio-only, video-only, synchronized, prerecorded, or live.</p> <p>Plan captions, description, transcripts, and sign-language access <strong>before production begins</strong>. Use qualified human review — unreviewed automatic output is not an accessible final deliverable. Keep alternatives easy to find next to the media, and preserve them when media is embedded, translated, archived, or moved to another platform.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-13">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Media content completely inaccessible to a disability group</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Access significantly impaired; workaround unreasonable to expect</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Access degraded but partially available</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Best-practice gap; marginal impact on access</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="what-the-media-requires-wcag-level-matrix">What the Media Requires (WCAG Level Matrix)</h5> <p>The time-based media criteria are cumulative — Level AA includes applicable Level A requirements.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Media type</th> <th>Level A</th> <th>Level AA</th> <th>Level AAA / additional practice</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Prerecorded audio-only</td> <td>Transcript (alternative for time-based media)</td> <td>—</td> <td>Enhanced presentation</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Prerecorded video-only</td> <td>Alternative or equivalent audio track</td> <td>—</td> <td>Media alternative (1.2.8)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Prerecorded synchronized audio+video</td> <td>Captions; audio description OR full media alternative</td> <td>Audio description</td> <td>Sign-language, extended audio description, media alternative</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Live synchronized audio+video</td> <td>No caption criterion</td> <td>Live captions</td> <td>Additional language/description services</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Live audio-only</td> <td>No criterion</td> <td>No criterion</td> <td>Equivalent live alternative (1.2.9)</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>No meaningful audio/visual information:</strong> video with no meaningful audio (silence, decorative music) doesn’t need captions. Audio with no speech can still need a transcript if meaningful sound communicates information. Decorative video conveys no information, but continuous motion can still require pause controls. If all important visual information is already spoken, no additional audio description is needed. Document these decisions per-file rather than assuming every video has identical requirements — and do not label primary media “an alternative for text” merely to avoid captions/ description/transcript.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-never-autoplay-audible-media">Critical: Never Autoplay Audible Media</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb404"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb404-1"><a href="#cb404-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Never do this --></span></span> <span id="cb404-2"><a href="#cb404-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><video</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"intro.mp4"</span> <span class="er">autoplay</span><span class="kw">></video></span></span> <span id="cb404-3"><a href="#cb404-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb404-4"><a href="#cb404-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Muted autoplay still needs reduced-motion handling and a pause control --></span></span> <span id="cb404-5"><a href="#cb404-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><video</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"background.mp4"</span> <span class="er">autoplay</span> <span class="er">muted</span> <span class="er">loop</span> <span class="er">playsinline</span></span> <span id="cb404-6"><a href="#cb404-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> controls</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Background animation — muted by default"</span><span class="kw">></video></span></span> <span id="cb404-7"><a href="#cb404-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {</span> <span id="cb404-8"><a href="#cb404-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> video[autoplay] { display: none; }</span> <span id="cb404-9"><a href="#cb404-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>WCAG 1.4.2 does not literally ban every autoplay instance — it requires a mechanism to pause/stop audio playing automatically for more than 3 seconds, or independent volume control. <strong>This project’s stricter rule: do not autoplay audible media at all</strong>, to avoid interfering with screen reader speech. If sound autoplays for any reason, the stop/pause/mute control must be the first keyboard stop on the page.</p> <p><strong>Muted autoplay does not resolve every issue:</strong> meaningful audio is unavailable while muted; moving content can distract or cause physical symptoms; motion for 5+ seconds alongside other content can need pause/stop/ hide (WCAG 2.2.2); users who request reduced motion should not get automatic decorative motion regardless of a caption track existing.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-captions-on-pre-recorded-video-with-audio">Critical: Captions on Pre-recorded Video with Audio</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb405"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb405-1"><a href="#cb405-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><video</span> <span class="er">controls</span> <span class="er">preload</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"metadata"</span> <span class="er">playsinline</span> <span class="er">poster</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"training-poster.jpg"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb405-2"><a href="#cb405-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><source</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"training.mp4"</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"video/mp4"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb405-3"><a href="#cb405-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><track</span> <span class="er">kind</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"captions"</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"training.en.vtt"</span> <span class="er">srclang</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"en"</span> <span class="er">label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"English captions"</span> <span class="er">default</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb405-4"><a href="#cb405-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><track</span> <span class="er">kind</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"subtitles"</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"training.fr.vtt"</span> <span class="er">srclang</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"fr"</span> <span class="er">label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Sous-titres français"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb405-5"><a href="#cb405-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p></span>Your browser cannot play this video. <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"training.mp4"</span><span class="kw">></span>Download the video<span class="kw"></a></span>.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb405-6"><a href="#cb405-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></video></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Use <code>kind="captions"</code> for tracks including dialogue AND meaningful non-speech audio; use <code>kind="subtitles"</code> for translated dialogue only — subtitles containing only dialogue are <strong>not</strong> a replacement for captions in the original language. Use only one <code>default</code> track per kind. Serve WebVTT as UTF-8 with the correct <code>text/vtt</code> media type.</p> <p><strong>Caption content must include:</strong> complete spoken dialogue/narration; speaker identification when not otherwise clear; meaningful sound effects/music cues (<code>[door slams]</code>); correct punctuation/capitalization preserving meaning; synchronized timing; readable cue duration/line breaks; placement avoiding important visual content. Do not remove words, simplify technical language, or censor in a way that changes meaning.</p> <p><strong>Never publish auto-generated captions without human review</strong> — a qualified person must review the complete file against the audio and correct substitutions/omissions/invented words, names/technical terms/numbers, missing negation, speaker changes, punctuation, and synchronization. Unreviewed auto-captions are at best <strong>Serious</strong>.</p> <p><strong>Open vs. closed captions:</strong> prefer closed captions (toggleable, customizable) when the platform supports them reliably. Open captions (permanently rendered) are a recognized WCAG technique and acceptable when closed captions aren’t available — don’t categorically reject them, but note users can’t turn them off or resize them independently.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-transcript-for-audio-only-content">Critical: Transcript for Audio-Only Content</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb406"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb406-1"><a href="#cb406-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><figure></span></span> <span id="cb406-2"><a href="#cb406-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><figcaption></span>Episode 12: Testing with screen magnification, 34 minutes<span class="kw"></figcaption></span></span> <span id="cb406-3"><a href="#cb406-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><audio</span> <span class="er">controls</span> <span class="er">preload</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"metadata"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Episode 12: Testing with screen magnification"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb406-4"><a href="#cb406-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><source</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"episode-12.mp3"</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"audio/mpeg"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb406-5"><a href="#cb406-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p></span>Your browser cannot play this audio. <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"episode-12.mp3"</span><span class="kw">></span>Download the episode<span class="kw"></a></span>.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb406-6"><a href="#cb406-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></audio></span></span> <span id="cb406-7"><a href="#cb406-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></figure></span></span> <span id="cb406-8"><a href="#cb406-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"episode-12-transcript.html"</span><span class="kw">></span>Read the Episode 12 transcript<span class="kw"></a></span>.<span class="kw"></p></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Transcript content</strong> (in the same sequence as the media): title/metadata; speaker names; all dialogue and narration; meaningful sound/music information; important on-screen text; for a <em>descriptive</em> transcript, visual actions/expressions/demonstrations/charts/scene changes; equivalent instructions/links for any interaction in the media.</p> <p>Publish as accessible HTML with a clearly named link immediately before/after the player — <strong>not only as a download or inaccessible PDF/image</strong>, and never only inside <code>aria-label</code>, a tooltip, or a visually-hidden element. A stable anchor URL (<code>#transcript-ep12</code>) makes it directly shareable and discoverable by search engines; collapsing in <code><details></code> for visual space is fine as long as the heading/anchor stay in the DOM. Keep transcript corrections synchronized with caption and media revisions.</p> <p><strong>Interactive transcripts</strong> (highlighting current passage, seek-by-timestamp) are enhancements, not substitutes for a complete linear transcript — use buttons for seek actions, give each an understandable time/topic, don’t move keyboard focus as playback advances, don’t force unpausable auto-scroll, respect reduced-motion, and preserve reading/copying when JS is unavailable.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-audio-descriptions-for-pre-recorded-video">Serious: Audio Descriptions for Pre-recorded Video</h5> <p>At Level A, WCAG 1.2.3 permits either audio description OR a complete media alternative. <strong>At Level AA, WCAG 1.2.5 requires audio description</strong> for prerecorded video content — a Level A transcript choice does not remove this AA requirement. If the main audio already communicates all important visual information, no additional description is necessary.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb407"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb407-1"><a href="#cb407-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><track</span> <span class="er">kind</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"descriptions"</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"training.descriptions.en.vtt"</span> <span class="er">srclang</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"en"</span> <span class="er">label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"English descriptions"</span><span class="kw">></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>This <code><track kind="descriptions"></code> technique is advisory in current WCAG techniques and depends on browser/player/AT support — <strong>do not rely on it without testing</strong>; provide a supported selectable track or described version when the player can’t present descriptions audibly.</p> <p><strong>Plan description during production</strong> — integrated description (speakers naturally stating names, reading on-screen text, explaining charts) is often clearest and can reduce separately-recorded description needed. Description should be objective, concise, timed around important dialogue, written by people with appropriate expertise, and reviewed with blind/low-vision users. Extended audio description (1.2.7, pausing video for more time) is <strong>Level AAA</strong> — needed only when pauses in the main audio are insufficient.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-accessible-media-player">Critical: Accessible Media Player</h5> <p><strong>Do not designate one player library as universally accessible</strong> — evaluate and test the specific version and configuration against the requirements below; pin dependency versions and review updates.</p> <p>Start with native <code><audio controls></code>/<code><video controls></code> when they provide what’s needed — native controls reduce custom code but vary by browser; test rather than assume sufficiency. <strong>A row of visually styled custom buttons is not an accessible player</strong> unless the complete behavior, state, timing, captions, description, seeking, and full-screen interaction are implemented and tested.</p> <p><strong>Controls and state:</strong> play/pause, stop, elapsed time/duration, seek, volume/mute, caption/language selection, audio-description selection, playback speed, chapters, full screen, picture-in-picture, transcript display as applicable. Every control needs an accessible name/role/state/ value — a play button can change its name to “Pause” while playing; a caption toggle can use <code>aria-pressed</code> when truly two-state; a timeline needs name/min/max/current-value and a useful text value (elapsed time). <strong>Do not announce every <code>timeupdate</code> event through a live region.</strong> Keep visible labels in accessible names for speech input; don’t communicate selected tracks or muted state through color alone.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb408"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode <p><strong>Keyboard:</strong> every control reachable in logical tab order; Enter/Space operate buttons natively; arrow keys operate ranges and documented composite widgets; focus never trapped in player or full-screen; focus stays visible and unobscured by auto-hiding controls; entering/leaving full screen preserves a logical focus location; controls don’t disappear while they or their descendants have focus. Single-character shortcuts must meet WCAG 2.1.4 (off/remap/scoped-to-focus) and must not intercept keys while typing in a field.</p> <p><strong>Visual/touch:</strong> text/icons meet contrast requirements; controls reflow at 400% zoom; touch targets meet WCAG 2.5.8; labels/icons remain understandable in forced-colors mode; pointer hover is never required to reveal the only path to controls; auto-hiding controls meet Content on Hover/Focus (1.4.13) and never hide the focused control.</p> <p><strong>Captions/description controls:</strong> easy to find without starting playback; current language and on/off state programmatically determinable; changing a track doesn’t unexpectedly reset playback; preferences persist when promised.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-embedded-and-third-party-players">Serious: Embedded and Third-Party Players</h5> <p>The content owner remains responsible for the experience delivered through an embed.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb409"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb409-1"><a href="#cb409-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><iframe</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"https://media.example.org/embed/accessibility-training"</span></span> <span id="cb409-2"><a href="#cb409-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> title=</span><span class="st">"Video: Accessibility testing training"</span> <span class="er">allowfullscreen</span><span class="kw">></iframe></span></span> <span id="cb409-3"><a href="#cb409-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"accessibility-training-transcript.html"</span><span class="kw">></span>Read the descriptive transcript<span class="kw"></a></span>.<span class="kw"></p></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Check: the iframe has a concise, content-identifying title; keyboard users can enter/operate/leave the player; controls have correct names/states/focus indicators; captions are published, accurate, and selectable; audio description is available; autoplay/ads/consent prompts/full-screen remain accessible; transcript and described-version links remain available <strong>outside</strong> the iframe; privacy/cookie overlays don’t block media controls. Do not trust a vendor’s accessibility claim without testing the actual configured player and current version.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-decorative-background-video">Moderate: Decorative Background Video</h5> <p>Avoid background video when a static image communicates the same design. If retained, it must:</p> <ul> <li>convey no information (keep <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> only if genuinely decorative)</li> <li>be muted with a static poster/fallback</li> <li>not autoplay when the user requests reduced motion</li> <li>have an always-available play/pause control</li> <li>meet flashing requirements</li> </ul> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb410"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb410-1"><a href="#cb410-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><video</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>CSS <code>animation-play-state</code> does not pause an HTML <code><video></code></strong> — control playback through the media element API. Do not automatically restart motion after a user changes preferences or manually pauses. If the video communicates information, remove <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> and provide all applicable alternatives — a decorative label does not make informative content decorative.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-live-captions-wcag-1.2.4-aa">Serious: Live Captions (WCAG 1.2.4 AA)</h5> <p><strong>Live synchronized media requires captions at Level AA — this is not qualified by a general “technically feasible” exception.</strong> WCAG 1.2.4 targets live synchronized broadcasts; it isn’t a blanket requirement to caption every private two-way call, but hosts/content providers must still provide the access their event and audience require.</p> <p>Plan before the event: contract and schedule captioning services (CART); give captioners names/terminology/scripts/slides/run-of-show materials; test caption display in the actual player/platform; verify language and speaker identification; provide a backup path for caption failure; ensure chat/polls/ controls are keyboard and screen-reader accessible; rehearse with interpreters. Monitor caption quality throughout — a caption badge or vendor setting is not proof attendees are receiving usable captions.</p> <p>When publishing an archive afterward: correct live captions; add/revise description; publish the transcript; remove inaccessible temporary chat/ polling artifacts; retest the recording as prerecorded media.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-wcag-1.4.2-audio-control-distinct-from-autoplay">Moderate: WCAG 1.4.2 Audio Control (Distinct from Autoplay)</h5> <p>Applies even when the user initiated playback: if audio continues playing automatically for more than 3 seconds, provide a way to pause/stop it or control its volume independently of system volume.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb412"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb412-1"><a href="#cb412-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"mute-toggle"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Mute background audio"</span> <span class="er">aria-pressed</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span><span class="kw">></span>…<span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <hr /> <h5 id="minor-sign-language-wcag-1.2.6-level-aaa">Minor: Sign Language (WCAG 1.2.6 — Level AAA)</h5> <p>Not required for AA conformance, but the highest-quality accommodation for Deaf sign-language-primary users — consider for high-priority content (safety information, onboarding, key announcements). Sign language is not universal — identify the specific language (ASL, BSL, LSQ, etc.). It’s a separate track/video, not a caption overlay — keep the signer’s face/hands/ body/signing space visible with adequate resolution/contrast/lighting/frame rate; synchronize with the program; keep captions from obscuring the signer; let users select/resize/reposition where the player supports it; review with Deaf sign-language users. Supplements rather than replaces captions.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="metadata-and-languages">Metadata and Languages</h5> <p>Before the player, provide visible info to help users decide whether/how to use the media: descriptive title, short purpose/summary, duration, spoken and sign languages, caption availability/languages, audio-description/ transcript availability, content warnings, and a date/version indicating staleness risk. Set page and language-of-parts markup correctly — caption/ description/media-alternative language normally matches the original; label translated subtitles/transcripts accurately. Do not use flags as the only language labels — name languages in text.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="production-workflow">Production Workflow</h5> <p><strong>Before recording:</strong> classify the planned media type and WCAG requirements; budget for captioning/description/transcripts/interpretation/QA; include important visual info in the script where natural; avoid unnecessary background audio/flashing visuals; choose a platform supporting required tracks; identify terminology/names/pronunciation for captioners.</p> <p><strong>During production:</strong> record clean speech with adequate volume; state important names/titles/URLs/chart conclusions aloud; leave pauses for standard audio description; keep essential text visible long enough to perceive; frame signers/demonstrations clearly; avoid placing visuals where captions/controls will cover them.</p> <p><strong>Before publication:</strong> review captions against the final audio; review transcript/description against the final edit; verify every language/track label; test the final encoded media, not just production files; test third-party embeds without an authenticated editor session; confirm alternatives remain available if the player fails; record reviewer/date/ version/follow-up issues.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-8">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Captions:</strong> watch the complete media with captions enabled and audio available for comparison; verify every spoken word, names/numbers/technical terms/negation, speaker/sound identification, synchronization, cue order/line breaks/duration; confirm captions don’t obscure visual content; test every language and full-screen presentation</li> <li><strong>Transcript/description:</strong> read the transcript without playing the media and confirm equivalent meaning; confirm visual info is included when a descriptive transcript is required; listen to the described version without watching the screen; verify description doesn’t cover important dialogue; include Deaf, hard-of-hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low-vision, and sign-language users in quality review</li> <li><strong>Keyboard/screen reader:</strong> reach every control by keyboard; operate buttons/ranges/menus/captions/description/speed/full-screen; confirm names/roles/states/values; confirm focus stays visible and logical as controls appear/hide; enter/exit embedded and full-screen players without a trap; confirm progress updates aren’t announced continuously</li> <li><strong>Visual/motion/touch:</strong> 200%/400% zoom; narrow viewports, both orientations; forced-colors/high-contrast; enable reduced motion before page load and confirm autoplay motion is suppressed; touch-operable pause controls; target sizes; flashing-content analysis if media might approach the threshold</li> <li><strong>Live-event:</strong> full rehearsal with caption/interpretation feeds; test attendee access without presenter privileges; simulate caption-service/ network failure; verify support-contact availability during the event</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated checks</strong> can detect missing accessible names on custom controls, invalid ARIA, keyboard focus-order problems, missing/malformed <code><track></code> attributes, WebVTT syntax errors, duplicate IDs, contrast issues, and audible-autoplay configuration — cannot establish caption accuracy, transcript equivalence, description quality, sign-language quality, or live delivery quality. Manual content and interaction review is required.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-5">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Failure</th> <th>Correction</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Treating live captions as optional when technically difficult</td> <td>Plan and provide captions for live synchronized media at AA — not qualified by feasibility</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Publishing unreviewed automatic captions</td> <td>Review and correct the complete caption file</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Captioning only dialogue</td> <td>Include meaningful non-speech audio and speaker identification</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Rejecting all open captions</td> <td>Evaluate as a valid technique when closed captions are unsupported</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Hiding an audio-only transcript behind only a download link</td> <td>Provide an easy-to-find accessible HTML transcript</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Treating a transcript as a replacement for AA audio description</td> <td>Provide audio description under 1.2.5 when visual info requires it</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Classifying extended audio description as AA</td> <td>It’s Level AAA (1.2.7)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Depending only on <code>track kind="descriptions"</code> without testing</td> <td>Test support; provide a supported described track or version</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Recommending one player as universally accessible</td> <td>Evaluate and test the selected version and configuration</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Publishing decorative custom controls without complete behavior</td> <td>Use native controls or implement and test the full player interface</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Announcing every playback-time update via live region</td> <td>Expose the timeline value without a continuous live region</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Claiming WCAG 1.4.2 literally bans all audible autoplay</td> <td>Apply the criterion accurately; adopt the stricter project rule separately</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Assuming muted autoplay is automatically acceptable</td> <td>Provide motion control and honor reduced-motion preferences</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Pausing video with CSS <code>animation-play-state</code></td> <td>Use the media element API</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Providing sign language without identifying the language</td> <td>Use the language required by the audience and label it</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Trusting a third-party accessibility statement without testing</td> <td>Test the configured current player; keep alternatives outside the embed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-13">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Media classified as audio-only/video-only/synchronized/live/prerecorded; applicable A/AA alternatives documented</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />No autoplaying audible media</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />If video autoplays (muted), <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> disables it; pause control always available</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />WCAG 1.4.2: audio continuing 3+ seconds has accessible stop/pause/mute</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Synchronised captions on all pre-recorded video with audio</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Auto-generated captions reviewed and corrected by a human before publishing</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Text transcript for all audio-only content; discoverable HTML, not PDF/download-only</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Transcript directly linkable via stable anchor URL</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Audio descriptions for all pre-recorded video with important unspoken visuals (AA)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Live synchronized media has a tested real-time caption service</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Media player evaluated/tested for this project — not assumed accessible from a library’s reputation</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All media player controls keyboard operable with type="checkbox" disabled="" />Embedded/third-party players have concise iframe titles; transcript/description links live outside the iframe</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Media metadata states duration, language(s), and available alternatives</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-13">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <ul> <li>1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only Prerecorded (A)</li> <li>1.2.2 Captions Prerecorded (A) — <strong>Critical if absent</strong></li> <li>1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative Prerecorded (A)</li> <li>1.2.4 Captions Live (AA) — <strong>Serious if absent, not excused by general feasibility</strong></li> <li>1.2.5 Audio Description Prerecorded (AA) — <strong>Serious if absent</strong></li> <li>1.2.6 Sign Language Prerecorded (AAA)</li> <li>1.2.7 Extended Audio Description Prerecorded (AAA)</li> <li>1.4.2 Audio Control (A) — <strong>Critical if autoplaying audio cannot be stopped</strong></li> <li>2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A)</li> <li>2.2.2 Pause, Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="email-accessibility">Email Accessibility</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> web</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> medium</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>email-accessibility</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> findings</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/email-accessibility">skills/email-accessibility</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> specialist</li> </ul> <p>HTML email accessibility under email client rendering constraints.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>email-accessibility/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="email-accessibility-specialist">Email Accessibility Specialist</h4> <p>You audit HTML email templates for accessibility. Email rendering differs from web — most CSS unsupported, no JavaScript, each client renders differently.</p> <h4 id="core-audit-areas-3">Core Audit Areas</h4> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Semantic Structure</strong> — Headings, <code>lang</code> attribute, <code><title></code>, logical reading order</li> <li><strong>Layout Tables</strong> — <code>role="presentation"</code> on all layout tables, no <code><th></code>/<code><thead></code></li> <li><strong>Images</strong> — Alt text, decorative <code>alt=""</code>, image blocking fallbacks, bulletproof buttons</li> <li><strong>Links</strong> — Descriptive text, underlined, adequate spacing</li> <li><strong>Color & Contrast</strong> — 4.5:1 minimum, inline styles, dark mode adaptation</li> <li><strong>Inline Styles</strong> — All styles inline, 14px min font, 1.5 line-height</li> <li><strong>Interactive Elements</strong> — Bulletproof button pattern, 44×44px touch targets</li> <li><strong>Screen Reader</strong> — Reading order on linearization, hidden preheader technique</li> </ol> <h4 id="client-constraints">Client Constraints</h4> <p>Gmail and Yahoo strip ARIA attributes and <code>role</code> — ensure accessibility through semantic HTML alone, ARIA as progressive enhancement only. Outlook uses Word rendering engine — ignores semantic elements.</p> <h4 id="output-contract-67">Output contract</h4> <p>Return only JSON matching <code>skills/a11y-core/schemas/findings.schema.json</code>. No prose, no summary, no restated instructions. One object, one array of findings.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. <li>Use <code>cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" border="0"</code> on layout tables</li> </ul> <h5 id="images">Images</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb414"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code images are blocked</li> <li>Many email clients block images by default — alt text is the only fallback</li> <li>Style images with <code>display: block</code> to prevent gaps in Outlook</li> <li>Use Covers captions, transcripts, audio descriptions, media player controls, and live captioning — the full WCAG 1.2.x domain.</p> <h4 id="wcag-1.2-coverage">WCAG 1.2 Coverage</h4> <p>Each SC, with its level and requirement.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>SC</th> <th>Level</th> <th>Requirement</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>1.2.1</td> <td>A</td> <td>Transcript for audio-only/video-only</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>1.2.2</td> <td>A</td> <td>Captions for prerecorded video</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>1.2.3</td> <td>A</td> <td>Audio description or text alternative</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>1.2.4</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Captions for live video</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>1.2.5</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Audio descriptions for prerecorded video</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="audit-checklist">Audit Checklist</h4> <ol type="1"> <li>Find all <code><video></code>, <code><audio></code>, <code><iframe></code> (embedded media) elements</li> <li>Check each <code><video></code> for <code><track kind="captions"></code> — missing = Critical</li> <li>Verify caption files exist and are valid (WebVTT/SRT syntax)</li> <li>Check for <code><track kind="descriptions"></code> for audio descriptions</li> <li>Audit media player controls: keyboard accessibility, ARIA labels, state management</li> <li>Check for autoplay: audio >3s must have pause/stop/volume control (WCAG 1.4.2)</li> <li>Verify transcripts exist for audio-only content</li> </ol> <h4 id="caption-quality">Caption Quality</h4> <ul> <li>99%+ accuracy, synchronized within 1 second</li> <li>Speaker identification for 2+ speakers</li> <li>Non-speech audio in brackets: <code>[applause]</code>, <code>[music]</code></li> <li>Maximum 200 words/minute, 32 chars/line, 2 lines/caption</li> </ul> <h4 id="media-player-aria">Media Player ARIA</h4> <ul> <li>Play/Pause: <code>role="button"</code>, <code>aria-label</code> reflects state</li> <li>Volume: <code>role="slider"</code> with min/max/now values</li> <li>Seek: <code>role="slider"</code>, <code>aria-valuetext</code> for time</li> <li>Captions toggle: <code>aria-pressed</code></li> <li>State announcements via <code>aria-live="polite"</code> region</li> </ul> <h4 id="output-contract-68">Output contract</h4> <p>Return only JSON matching HH:MM:SS.mmm</code></li> <li>Speaker identification: <code><v Speaker Name>Text</code></li> <li>Maximum 2 lines per caption, 32 characters per line</li> <li>Minimum display time: 1 second</li> milliseconds (not period)</li> <li>Blank line between entries</li> <li>No styling support (unlike WebVTT)</li> </ul> <h5 id="ttml-timed-text-markup-language">TTML (Timed Text Markup Language)</h5> <ul> <li>XML-based, used in broadcast and streaming</li> <li>Supports styling, positioning, and region layout</li> <li>IMSC (Internet Media Subtitles and Captions) is the web profile</li> </ul> <h4 <strong>NVDA addon development specialist</strong> – an expert in building, debugging, testing, packaging, and publishing addons for the <a href="https://www.nvaccess.org/">NVDA screen reader</a>. Your knowledge is grounded directly in the <a href="https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda">official NVDA source code</a> and the <a href="https://github.com/nvdaaddons">community addon development ecosystem</a>.</p> <hr /> <h4 id="core-principles-5">Core Principles</h4> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Source code is the authority.</strong> Every architectural claim is verified against <a href="https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda">github.com/nvaccess/nvda</a>.</li> <li><strong>Never block the main thread.</strong> NVDA runs a single-threaded main loop. Blocking calls freeze all speech, braille, and input handling.</li> <li><strong>Always call <code>nextHandler()</code>.</strong> Event handlers that skip this break all downstream processing.</li> <li><strong>Use the <code>@script</code> decorator.</strong> Modern NVDA addons use the decorator, not legacy <code>__gestures</code> dicts.</li> <li><strong>Test with the real screen reader.</strong> Verify addons with NVDA itself.</li> <li><strong>Package for the Add-on Store.</strong> Follow the official submission process.</li> </ol> <hr /> <h4 id="nvda-architecture">NVDA Architecture</h4> <h5 id="event-chain">Event Chain</h5> <pre class="text"><code>API Handler (IAccessible/UIA/JAB) -> eventHandler.executeEvent() -> Global Plugin 1 .event_*() -> Global Plugin 2 .event_*() -> App Module .event_*() -> Tree Interceptor .event_*() -> NVDAObject .event_*()</code></pre> <h5 id="script-resolution-order">Script Resolution Order</h5> <pre class="text"><code>1. gesture.scriptableObject 2. Global Plugins (all, in order) 3. App Module (focused app) 4. Braille Display Driver 5. Vision Enhancement Providers 6. Tree Interceptor 7. Focused NVDAObject 8. You parse HTML/JSX and produce a step-by-step narration of what a screen reader would announce, helping developers understand the accessible experience without needing a screen reader installed.</p> <p><strong>Important disclaimer:</strong> This is an educational simulation based on the ARIA specification and accessible name computation algorithm. Real screen reader behavior varies between NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, and Narrator. Always recommend real screen reader testing for production validation.</p> <hr /> <h4 id="simulation-modes">Simulation Modes</h4> <h5 id="mode-1-reading-order-default">Mode 1: Reading Order (Default)</h5> <p>Walk the DOM in reading order (top to bottom, following <code>aria-owns</code>, skipping <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> and <code>display: none</code>). For each element, announce:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Role</strong> — semantic role from element type or <code>role</code> attribute</li> <li><strong>Accessible name</strong> — computed via the Accessible Name Computation algorithm</li> <li><strong>State</strong> — <code>aria-expanded</code>, <code>aria-checked</code>, <code>aria-disabled</code>, <code>aria-pressed</code>, etc.</li> <li><strong>Description</strong> — <code>aria-describedby</code> content if present</li> </ol> <h5 id="mode-2-tab-navigation">Mode 2: Tab Navigation</h5> <p>Simulate pressing Tab repeatedly. Only visit focusable elements in DOM order (respecting <code>tabindex</code>).</p> <h5 id="mode-3-heading-navigation-h-key">Mode 3: Heading Navigation (H Key)</h5> <p>List all headings in document order with their levels. Flag: skipped levels, missing H1, multiple H1s.</p> <h5 id="mode-4-form-navigation-f-key">Mode 4: Form Navigation (F Key)</h5> <p>List all form controls with their labels. Flag: inputs without labels, missing required indicators.</p> <hr /> <h4 id="accessible-name-computation">Accessible Name Computation</h4> <p>Follow the algorithm from accname-1.2:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><code>aria-labelledby</code> — concatenate text of referenced elements</li> <li><code>aria-label</code> — use directly</li> <li>Native label association — <code><label for="id"></code>, wrapping <code><label></code></li> <li>Element content — text content for <code><button></code>, <code><a></code>, headings</li> <li><code>title</code> attribute — fallback</li> <li><code>placeholder</code> — last resort (not recommended)</li> </ol> <p>If no name is computed, annotate: <code>[No accessible name — screen reader will announce role only or skip entirely]</code></p> <hr /> <h4 id="process-2">Process</h4> <h5 id="phase-1-input">Phase 1 — Input</h5> <p>Ask the user what to simulate (file path, code snippet) and which mode.</p> <h5 id="phase-2-parse-and-simulate">Phase 2 — Parse and Simulate</h5> <p>Read the file, parse HTML/JSX, build the accessibility tree, walk in selected mode.</p> <h5 id="phase-3-findings">Phase 3 — Findings</h5> <p>Report elements with no accessible name, ARIA issues, tab order problems, heading hierarchy issues, form labeling gaps, and recommended fixes.</p> <h5 id="phase-4-follow-up">Phase 4 — Follow-Up</h5> <p>Offer to run a different mode, simulate a different component, or delegate to aria-specialist or testing-coach.</p> <h4 id="output-contract-70">Output contract</h4> <p>Answer the question. Keep the answer to what was asked, cite the criterion or API by name, and stop. Do not append a checklist that was not requested.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <h5 id="best-practices">Best Practices</h5> <h6 id="dos">Do’s</h6> <ul> <li><strong>Test with actual screen readers</strong> - Not just simulators</li> <li><strong>Use semantic HTML first</strong> - ARIA is supplemental</li> <li><strong>Test in browse and focus modes</strong> - Different experiences</li> <li><strong>Verify focus management</strong> - Especially for SPAs</li> <li><strong>Test keyboard only first</strong> - Foundation for SR testing</li> </ul> <h6 id="donts">Don’ts</h6> <ul> <li><strong>Don’t assume one SR is enough</strong> - Test multiple</li> <li><strong>Don’t ignore mobile</strong> - Growing user base</li> <li><strong>Don’t test only happy path</strong> - Test error states</li> <li><strong>Don’t skip dynamic content</strong> - Most common issues</li> <li><strong>Don’t rely on visual testing</strong> - Different experience</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="speech-recognition">Speech Recognition</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>speech-recognition</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/speech-recognition">skills/speech-recognition</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever the project must support speech input or voice control — dictation, “click by voice” grammars, Dragon NaturallySpeaking, Voice Control (iOS/macOS), Voice Access (Android), or any interface where users activate controls by speaking. Under no circumstances let an aria-label override a visible label without keeping the visible text intact and in order. Absolutely always ensure the accessible name contains the visible label, and load alongside keyboard/SKILL.md since speech tools commonly emulate keyboard and pointer input.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>speech-recognition/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="speech-recognition-accessibility-skill">Speech Recognition Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/SPEECH_RECOGNITION_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing or reviewing any interface that must support speech input or voice control. <strong>Load alongside <code>keyboard/SKILL.md</code> — speech tools often rely on keyboard and pointer emulation, so keyboard requirements are a foundation, not a substitute.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-14">Core Mandate</h5> <p>Speech recognition can dictate text, navigate interfaces, activate controls, emulate keyboard input, and operate a pointer. Speech recognition is not the same as speaker recognition — speech recognition interprets words and commands; speaker recognition tries to identify who is speaking.</p> <p><strong>Core principles:</strong> 1. Use visible, persistent labels — people must be able to determine what to say without guessing a hidden name 2. Match visible labels and accessible names — if a control has visible text, its accessible name must contain that text 3. Use native semantics — correct HTML names/roles/states/values/keyboard behavior give speech tools reliable information 4. Support more than direct label activation — keyboard emulation, name/number overlays, and pointer emulation vary by product 5. Do not require fine pointer control — provide alternatives to dragging, path gestures, and precise spatial interaction 6. Accept input from more than key events — dictation, paste, and autocomplete may change a field without firing expected keystrokes 7. Provide clear feedback — expose changed state, errors, confirmations, and results visually and programmatically 8. Test the supported environments — commands, overlays, and behavior vary by product, platform, and version</p> <p><strong>Who uses speech input:</strong> people with limited movement/strength/dexterity/ reach/endurance; repetitive strain injuries, pain, tremors, or fatigue; people using speech instead of or alongside a keyboard/pointer; people with cognitive/learning disabilities who find dictation easier than typing; temporary or situational limitations; people combining speech with a screen reader, magnifier, or switch. <strong>Speech users are not necessarily sighted</strong> — do not design or test on the assumption that everyone using speech can see a label, overlay, pointer, focus indicator, or visual result.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-14">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>A control cannot be activated by any speech-tool method (name, overlay, or keyboard/pointer emulation)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Accessible name doesn’t contain the visible label; validation depends only on <code>keydown</code> and silently rejects dictated/pasted input</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Repeated controls are hard to disambiguate; icon-only control has no accessible name</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Hidden context inserted before rather than after the visible label; inconsistent localization of names</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-visible-labels-must-be-contained-in-the-accessible-name-wcag-2.5.3">Critical: Visible Labels Must Be Contained in the Accessible Name (WCAG 2.5.3)</h5> <p>For a component with visible text or an image of text, the accessible name must <strong>contain</strong> that visible text — having it at the <em>start</em> of the name is documented best practice, not an additional normative requirement.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb446"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb446-1"><a href="#cb446-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Prefer: native text as the name --></span></span> <span id="cb446-2"><a href="#cb446-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"submit"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb446-3"><a href="#cb446-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb446-4"><a href="#cb446-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Wrong: accessible name is "Confirm changes", not "Save" --></span></span> <span id="cb446-5"><a href="#cb446-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"submit"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Confirm changes"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb446-6"><a href="#cb446-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb446-7"><a href="#cb446-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Acceptable when extra context is genuinely needed --></span></span> <span id="cb446-8"><a href="#cb446-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"submit"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Save document"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save<span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><code>aria-label</code>/<code>aria-labelledby</code> can override names derived from child content — inspect the <strong>computed</strong> accessible name rather than assuming every labeling source combines. Do not use placeholder text as the only label — it can disappear during dictation and isn’t a substitute for a programmatically associated <code><label></code>.</p> <p><strong>Keep visible words contiguous and in order:</strong></p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb447"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb447-1"><a href="#cb447-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Good: visible label starts the accessible name --></span></span> <span id="cb447-2"><a href="#cb447-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button></span>Delete <span class="kw"><span</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"visually-hidden"</span><span class="kw">></span>quarterly report<span class="kw"></span></button></span></span> <span id="cb447-3"><a href="#cb447-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb447-4"><a href="#cb447-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Avoid: hidden words interrupt the visible label --></span></span> <span id="cb447-5"><a href="#cb447-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Delete the quarterly report permanently"</span><span class="kw">></span>Delete report<span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>The second example contains “Delete” and “report” but inserts other words between them — some speech tools may not match the phrase a user sees. A hidden <em>prefix</em> (context appearing before the visible word) is not automatically a 2.5.3 failure if the visible text still appears intact, but it can still make direct label activation harder — prefer not to put hidden words before the text a person sees. Put format hints/constraints in an <code>aria-describedby</code> description, not the name.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-disambiguate-repeated-controls-without-renaming-them">Serious: Disambiguate Repeated Controls Without Renaming Them</h5> <p>Repeated labels (“Edit”, “Delete”, “Read more”) can cause a speech tool to present several matches — not automatically a conformance failure, but it increases effort. Prefer specific visible labels when concise:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb448"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb448-1"><a href="#cb448-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/services"</span><span class="kw">></span>Read about services<span class="kw"></a></span></span> <span id="cb448-2"><a href="#cb448-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/products"</span><span class="kw">></span>Read about products<span class="kw"></a></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>For compact repeated actions, add contextual text <strong>after</strong> the visible action:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb449"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb449-1"><a href="#cb449-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><li></span></span> <span id="cb449-2"><a href="#cb449-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Billing address</span> <span id="cb449-3"><a href="#cb449-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/account/billing/edit"</span><span class="kw">></span>Edit <span class="kw"><span</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"visually-hidden"</span><span class="kw">></span>billing address<span class="kw"></span></a></span></span> <span id="cb449-4"><a href="#cb449-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></li></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Do not make accessible names unique by replacing or reordering the visible label</strong> — “Modify billing address” is not a good hidden name for a visible “Edit” link.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-icon-only-controls">Moderate: Icon-Only Controls</h5> <p>Still need an accessible name under WCAG 4.1.2 (2.5.3 doesn’t apply when there’s no visible text label):</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb450"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb450-1"><a href="#cb450-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Close dialog"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb450-2"><a href="#cb450-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">focusable</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb450-3"><a href="#cb450-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><path</span> <span class="er">d</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"M6 6 18 18M18 6 6 18"</span><span class="kw">></path></span></span> <span id="cb450-4"><a href="#cb450-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></svg></span></span> <span id="cb450-5"><a href="#cb450-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Persistent visible text is usually more discoverable than an icon alone. A tooltip appearing only on hover/focus is <strong>not</strong> a persistent visible label — a person must first discover or target the control before it helps. If an icon-only design is retained: use a concise localized name; use a familiar icon consistently; provide adequate target size/spacing; ensure name/number overlays identify it; don’t use color or position as the only description; test with the supported speech tools.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-native-semantics-and-keyboard-operation">Critical: Native Semantics and Keyboard Operation</h5> <p>Speech tools often use accessibility APIs, keyboard emulation, or pointer emulation — native HTML supplies reliable role/name/state/value/focus/ activation behavior for free.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb451"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb451-1"><a href="#cb451-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Wrong: not a reliable button --></span></span> <span id="cb451-2"><a href="#cb451-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">onclick</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"saveDocument()"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save<span class="kw"></div></span></span> <span id="cb451-3"><a href="#cb451-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb451-4"><a href="#cb451-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Correct --></span></span> <span id="cb451-5"><a href="#cb451-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">onclick</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"saveDocument()"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save<span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Do not publish tables claiming a particular spoken phrase always works for every role — command grammar differs by speech product, platform, locale, and version. Correct semantics still improve compatibility and remain required for other AT. All functionality must be available through a keyboard interface (unless the function requires path-dependent input) — speech software can use that keyboard interface as one operating method. For custom widgets: use the correct role only when no native element suffices; implement the expected keyboard interaction; expose name/state/properties/ value; update programmatic state when visual state changes; follow an established APG pattern. See <code>skills/keyboard/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-dictation-and-text-entry-must-not-depend-only-on-keydown">Serious: Dictation and Text Entry Must Not Depend Only on <code>keydown</code></h5> <p>Speech dictation may insert, replace, or delete text without producing the same <code>keydown</code> sequence as a physical keyboard.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb452"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb452-1"><a href="#cb452-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Correct: responds to value changes regardless of input method</span></span> <span id="cb452-2"><a href="#cb452-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>search<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">addEventListener</span>(<span class="st">'input'</span><span class="op">,</span> () <span class="kw">=></span> <span class="fu">updateSuggestions</span>(search<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">value</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb452-3"><a href="#cb452-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb452-4"><a href="#cb452-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Wrong: dictation, paste, and autocomplete may bypass this logic</span></span> <span id="cb452-5"><a href="#cb452-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>search<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">addEventListener</span>(<span class="st">'keydown'</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="bu">event</span> <span class="kw">=></span> <span class="fu">updateSuggestions</span>(<span class="bu">event</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">key</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Text-entry controls should: use native inputs/textareas; have persistent visible labels; expose format instructions and errors programmatically; accept paste, dictation, autocomplete, and programmatic value changes; allow editing/correction before submission; avoid short time limits or speech-rate assumptions; not require a specific punctuation phrase when another valid value is acceptable; preserve entered content after validation errors. <strong>Do not infer that a lack of <code>keydown</code> means no input occurred</strong> — validate the current value at the appropriate event and again at submission.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-dragging-gestures-and-spatial-interaction-need-direct-alternatives">Serious: Dragging, Gestures, and Spatial Interaction Need Direct Alternatives</h5> <p>Dragging with a speech-controlled pointer can require several commands and precise timing.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb453"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb453-1"><a href="#cb453-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Reordering alternative --></span></span> <span id="cb453-2"><a href="#cb453-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><li></span></span> <span id="cb453-3"><a href="#cb453-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Budget report</span> <span id="cb453-4"><a href="#cb453-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Move up <span class="kw"><span</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"visually-hidden"</span><span class="kw">></span>Budget report<span class="kw"></span></button></span></span> <span id="cb453-5"><a href="#cb453-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Move down <span class="kw"><span</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"visually-hidden"</span><span class="kw">></span>Budget report<span class="kw"></span></button></span></span> <span id="cb453-6"><a href="#cb453-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></li></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>If drag-and-drop is also available, both methods should update the same model and provide confirmation. For sliders, pair the draggable control with a direct entry or step control:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb454"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb454-1"><a href="#cb454-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><label</span> <span class="er">for</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"volume"</span><span class="kw">></span>Volume<span class="kw"></label></span></span> <span id="cb454-2"><a href="#cb454-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><input</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"volume"</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"range"</span> <span class="er">min</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0"</span> <span class="er">max</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"100"</span> <span class="er">value</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"volume-value"</span><span class="kw">></span>Volume percentage<span class="kw"></label></span></span> <span id="cb454-4"><a href="#cb454-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><input</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"volume-value"</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"number"</span> <span class="er">min</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0"</span> <span class="er">max</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"100"</span> <span class="er">value</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"50"</span><span class="kw">></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>WCAG 2.5.7 requires author-created dragging to have a single-pointer alternative unless essential — <strong>a keyboard-only alternative does not necessarily satisfy this single-pointer requirement.</strong> Path-based or multipoint gestures need a single-pointer alternative under 2.5.1 too, unless the gesture is essential. See <code>skills/touch-pointer/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-focus-scrolling-and-overlays">Moderate: Focus, Scrolling, and Overlays</h5> <p>Some speech users emulate keyboard commands or combine speech with another input method — focus order, visibility, and unobscured controls remain important. Sticky headers/cookie notices/chat launchers must not hide a focused component (WCAG 2.4.11).</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb455"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb455-1"><a href="#cb455-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>html { scroll-padding-block-start: <span class="fu">var(</span><span class="va">--sticky-header-height</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">4</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="fu">)</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb455-2"><a href="#cb455-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="in">:focus-visible</span> { scroll-margin-block: <span class="dv">0.5</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Ensure: focus doesn’t move behind an open modal; closing a dialog returns focus to a logical control; direct activation scrolls the target into view when needed; overlays can be dismissed without dragging or precise pointer movement; no essential control is permanently covered at supported viewport sizes. Speech input can be combined with a screen reader, so interaction must not depend on seeing focus or an overlay.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-expose-state-results-and-error-feedback-programmatically">Serious: Expose State, Results, and Error Feedback Programmatically</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb456"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb456-1"><a href="#cb456-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-expanded</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span> <span class="er">aria-controls</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"filters-panel"</span><span class="kw">></span>Filters<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb456-2"><a href="#cb456-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"filters-panel"</span> <span class="er">hidden</span><span class="kw">></span><span class="co"><!-- Filter controls --></span><span class="kw"></div></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Update both <code>aria-expanded</code> and <code>hidden</code> together — similarly for <code>aria-pressed</code>, <code>aria-checked</code>, selected tabs, and slider values.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb457"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb457-1"><a href="#cb457-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"cart-status"</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"status"</span> <span class="er">aria-atomic</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span><span class="kw">></p></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Use visible text and an appropriate status-message pattern (see <code>skills/aria-live-regions/SKILL.md</code>) — don’t move focus for every confirmation. For errors needing immediate correction, associate the error with the field and use the form’s established error-summary strategy. Avoid feedback that is: shown only by color/animation/icon change; available only on hover; removed before it can be perceived; announced repeatedly for every dictated character; hidden from accessibility APIs; disconnected from the control that caused it.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-labels-symbols-and-localization">Moderate: Labels, Symbols, and Localization</h5> <p>Use the same human language for visible labels and accessible names — translate <code>aria-label</code>, hidden context, descriptions, and error messages with the rest of the interface. Do not normalize every symbol into an unrelated word — the correct name depends on function: a magnifying-glass icon used as a control is named “Search,” not “Magnifying glass”; a visible <code>X</code> used only as a close icon should have the function “Close.” Test speech matching in each supported interface and dictation language — a command working in English may not work after translation.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="product-and-platform-variation">Product and Platform Variation</h5> <p>Speech tools differ in how they activate a control by name, display name/ number/grid overlays, disambiguate repeated names, emulate keyboard/pointer input, handle embedded frames and shadow DOM, and switch between command/dictation modes. <strong>Do not put fixed command phrases, product versions, or compatibility claims into a project standard unless the project actively maintains and retests them.</strong></p> <p>Record the actual test environment:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Speech input product and version: Operating system and version: Browser and version: Input and interface language: Command, dictation, or mixed mode: Viewport, zoom, and text size:</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-9">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Static inspection:</strong> identify the visible label; inspect the computed accessible name/role; confirm visible words occur intact and in order in the name; check for hidden text before or inside the visible phrase; verify state/value/description relationships; confirm repeated controls can be distinguished; verify icon-only controls have concise names; verify names and hidden text are translated. Inspect the computed accessibility tree — don’t infer the final name by reading attributes independently.</li> <li><strong>Keyboard foundation</strong> (without a pointer): reach and operate all functionality; follow a logical focus order; open/use/close custom widgets; escape dialogs/menus/popovers; confirm focus stays visible and unobscured; complete drag alternatives.</li> <li><strong>Speech input test</strong> (per supported environment): activate visibly labeled controls by speaking the visible label using the tool’s documented grammar; inspect the tool’s name/number overlay for discoverability; distinguish repeated controls; operate icon-only controls and custom widgets; dictate/edit/replace/submit text; trigger and correct validation errors; navigate modals/menus/tabs/disclosures/ autocomplete; complete sorting/reordering/slider/map/canvas tasks through alternatives; confirm state changes and status feedback; repeat critical tasks after zoom/reflow/localization changes. Do not require every control to respond to one literal phrase like “Click [label]” — use the tested tool’s documented grammar.</li> <li><strong>Test with users</strong> who regularly use speech input — a technical pass cannot reveal the full effort of correcting recognition errors, disambiguating controls, or navigating a dense overlay.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated checks</strong> can detect controls without accessible names, some visible-label-in-name mismatches, invalid/missing roles/states, click handlers on non-interactive elements, and duplicate accessible names — cannot determine whether a speech product actually recognizes a label, whether repeated controls are practically distinguishable, or whether the total number of commands makes a task unreasonably difficult. Treat uncertain automated results as review items, not confirmed failures.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-6">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Failure</th> <th>Correction</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Visible “Save” button has hidden name “Confirm changes”</td> <td>Use “Save,” or a name beginning with “Save”</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Hidden words inserted inside the visible phrase</td> <td>Keep visible words contiguous and in order</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Every repeated link is visibly “Read more”</td> <td>Use specific visible text or append contextual hidden text after it</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Placeholder is the only field label</td> <td>Add a persistent, associated <code><label></code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Icon-only button has no accessible name</td> <td>Add a concise name; prefer persistent visible text</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Tooltip treated as a visible label</td> <td>Keep the label persistently visible when discoverability matters</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Styled <code><div></code> acts as a button</td> <td>Use <code><button></code> or implement the complete custom-widget contract</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Validation runs only on <code>keydown</code></td> <td>Respond to <code>input</code>, current values, and submission</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Reordering requires drag and drop only</td> <td>Add Move up/Move down or position controls</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Gesture is the only way to operate a feature</td> <td>Add simple controls for the same result</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Sticky content hides the focused control</td> <td>Adjust layout/scrolling; test at supported sizes</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>State changes only visually</td> <td>Update programmatic state and provide visible feedback</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Project documentation promises universal spoken commands</td> <td>Test and document the actual supported products and locales</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Testing assumes every speech user can see</td> <td>Include non-visual and combined AT use</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-14">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input used where it can provide the required control</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Custom controls follow supported keyboard and ARIA patterns</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Repeated controls can be distinguished efficiently without renaming them</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Icon-only controls have concise, localized accessible names</li> <li><input
