and correction update fields correctly</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Validation does not depend only on physical key events</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All (A)</li> <li>2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA)</li> <li>2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum (AA)</li> <li>2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A)</li> <li>2.5.3 Label in Name (A) — <strong>Serious if visible label not contained in accessible name</strong></li> <li>2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA)</li> <li>3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A)</li> <li>4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)</li> <li>4.1.3 Status Messages (AA)</li> </ul> <p>WCAG criteria describe outcomes, not product-specific spoken commands — a command failing in one environment may indicate a content defect, a product limitation, a localization issue, or an unsupported combination. Record the environment and investigate before assigning a standards failure.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="references-15">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/SPEECH_RECOGNITION_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md">Full best practices guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/perspective-videos/voice/">W3C WAI Speech Recognition Perspective</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html">WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.5.3 Label in Name</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html">WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.5.7 Dragging Movements</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/">ARIA Authoring Practices Guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/">Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions</a></li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> These rules target WCAG 2.2 AA. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h2 id="standards-law-and-reporting">Standards, Law and Reporting</h2> <h3 id="accessibility">Accessibility</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Author:</strong> web-quality-skills</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 3</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>accessibility</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Addy Osmani</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills">addyosmani/web-quality-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills/tree/afa8da942115f2961fdbfa80807ea0b232ff6c00/skills/accessibility">skills/accessibility</a></li> <li><strong>Version:</strong> 2.0</li> </ul> <p>Audit and improve web accessibility following WCAG 2.2 guidelines. Use when asked to “improve accessibility”, “a11y audit”, “WCAG compliance”, “screen reader support”, “keyboard navigation”, or “make accessible”.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>accessibility/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-a11y">Accessibility (a11y)</h4> <p>Comprehensive accessibility guidelines based on WCAG 2.2 and Lighthouse accessibility audits. Goal: make content usable by everyone, including people with disabilities.</p> <h5 id="evidence-led-audit-workflow">Evidence-led audit workflow</h5> <p>When a rendered page is available:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Run a live Lighthouse Accessibility audit when that capability is available; with Chrome DevTools MCP, use <code>lighthouse_audit</code>. Use mobile navigation mode for a general public page or snapshot mode when reloading would lose authenticated or user-created state.</li> <li>Use failed audit nodes to localize the relevant component or template instead of searching the whole repository for generic patterns.</li> <li>Inspect a rendered accessibility-tree snapshot for names, roles, states, landmarks, and heading structure; with Chrome DevTools MCP, use <code>take_snapshot</code>. Exercise the affected flow with the keyboard.</li> <li>Fix the source, then re-run the same audit and manual interaction.</li> </ol> <p>If the live tools are unavailable, use Lighthouse CLI or axe for automated coverage and complete the same manual checks. Automated tools detect only a subset of accessibility barriers: a score of 100 is not WCAG conformance, and a low score does not replace issue-level evidence.</p> <h5 id="wcag-principles-pour">WCAG Principles: POUR</h5> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Principle</th> <th>Description</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>P</strong>erceivable</td> <td>Content can be perceived through different senses</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>O</strong>perable</td> <td>Interface can be operated by all users</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>U</strong>nderstandable</td> <td>Content and interface are understandable</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>R</strong>obust</td> <td>Content works with assistive technologies</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="conformance-levels">Conformance levels</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 46%" /> <col style="width: 28%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Target</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>A</strong></td> <td>Minimum accessibility</td> <td>Must pass</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>AA</strong></td> <td>Standard compliance</td> <td>Should pass (legal requirement in many jurisdictions)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>AAA</strong></td> <td>Enhanced id="consistent-help-3.2.6-new-in-2.2">Consistent help (3.2.6) — new in 2.2</h6> <p>If a help mechanism (contact info, chat widget, FAQ link, self-help option) is repeated across multiple pages, it must appear in the <strong>same relative order</strong> each time. Users who rely on consistent placement shouldn’t have to hunt for help on every page.</p> <h6 id="form-labels-3.3.2">Form labels (3.3.2)</h6> <p>Every input needs a programmatically associated label. See the <a href="references/A11Y-PATTERNS.md#form-labels">form labels pattern</a> for explicit, implicit, and instructional examples.</p> <h6 id="error-handling-3.3.1-3.3.3">Error handling (3.3.1, 3.3.3)</h6> <p>Announce errors to screen readers with <code>role="alert"</code> or <code>aria-live</code>, set <code>aria-invalid="true"</code> on invalid fields, and focus the first error on submit. See the <a href="references/A11Y-PATTERNS.md#error-handling">error handling pattern</a> for full markup and JS.</p> <h6 id="redundant-entry-3.3.7-new-in-2.2">Redundant entry (3.3.7) — new in 2.2</h6> <p>Don’t force users to re-enter information they already provided in the same session. Auto-populate from earlier steps, or let users select from previously entered values. Exceptions: security re-confirmation and content that has expired.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb474"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb474-1"><a cognitive function tests (e.g., remembering a password, solving a puzzle) unless at least one of: - A copy-paste or autofill mechanism is available - An alternative method exists (e.g., passkey, SSO, See the <a href="references/A11Y-PATTERNS.md#live-regions-and-notifications">live regions pattern</a> for markup and a <code>showNotification()</code> helper.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-checklist-2">Testing checklist</h5> <h6 id="automated-testing-1">Automated testing</h6> <p>Prefer a live Lighthouse audit that returns failing rendered nodes directly to the agent. With Chrome DevTools MCP, this is <code>lighthouse_audit</code>. install @axe-core/cli <span class="at">-g</span></span> <span id="cb477-6"><a href="#cb477-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">axe</span> https://example.com</span></code></pre></div> <h6 id="manual-testing">Manual testing</h6> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>Keyboard navigation:</strong> Tab through entire page, use Enter/Space to activate</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>Screen reader:</strong> Test with VoiceOver (Mac), NVDA (Windows), or TalkBack (Android)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>Zoom:</strong> Content usable at 200% zoom</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>High contrast:</strong> Test with Windows High Contrast Mode</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>Reduced motion:</strong> Test with <code>prefers-reduced-motion: reduce</code></li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>Focus order:</strong> Logical and follows visual order</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><strong>Target size:</strong> Interactive elements meet 24×24px minimum</li> </ul> <p>See the <a href="references/A11Y-PATTERNS.md#screen-reader-commands">screen reader commands reference</a> for VoiceOver and NVDA shortcuts.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-issues-by-impact">Common issues by impact</h5> <h6 id="critical-fix-immediately">Critical (fix immediately)</h6> <ol type="1"> <li>Missing form labels</li> <li>Missing image alt text</li> <li>Insufficient color contrast</li> <li>Keyboard traps</li> <li>No focus indicators</li> </ol> <h6 id="serious-fix-before-launch">Serious (fix before launch)</h6> <ol type="1"> <li>Missing page language</li> <li>Missing heading structure</li> <li>Non-descriptive link text</li> <li>Auto-playing media</li> <li>Missing skip links</li> </ol> <h6 id="moderate-fix-soon">Moderate (fix soon)</h6> <ol type="1"> <li>Missing ARIA labels on icons</li> <li>Inconsistent navigation</li> <li>Missing error identification</li> <li>Timing without controls</li> <li>Missing landmark regions</li> </ol> <h5 id="references-16">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/">WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/">WAI-ARIA Authoring href="https://github.com/wshobson/agents/tree/156b7a5e7a8b93642628a339ee4039c925b34c7f/plugins/ui-design/skills/accessibility-compliance">plugins/ui-design/skills/accessibility-compliance</a></li> </ul> <p>Implement WCAG 2.2 compliant interfaces with mobile accessibility, inclusive design patterns, and assistive technology support. Use when auditing accessibility, implementing ARIA patterns, building for screen readers, or ensuring inclusive user experiences.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>accessibility-compliance/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-compliance-1">Accessibility Compliance</h4> <p>Master accessibility implementation to create inclusive experiences that work for everyone, including users with disabilities.</p> <h5 id="when-to-use-this-skill-1">When to Use This Skill</h5> <ul> <li>Implementing WCAG 2.2 Level AA or AAA compliance</li> <li>Building screen reader accessible interfaces</li> <li>Adding keyboard navigation to interactive components</li> <li>Implementing focus management and focus trapping</li> <li>Creating accessible forms with proper labeling</li> <li>Supporting reduced motion and high contrast preferences</li> <li>Building mobile accessibility features (iOS VoiceOver, Android TalkBack)</li> <li>Conducting accessibility audits and fixing violations</li> </ul> <h5 id="detailed-patterns-and-worked-examples">Detailed patterns and worked examples</h5> <p>Detailed pattern documentation lives in <code>references/details.md</code>. Read that file when the navigation tier above is insufficient.</p> <h5 id="best-practices-1">Best Practices</h5> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Use Semantic HTML</strong>: Prefer native elements over ARIA when possible</li> <li><strong>Test with Real Users</strong>: Include people with disabilities in user testing</li> <li><strong>Keyboard First</strong>: Design interactions to work without a mouse</li> <li><strong>Don’t Disable Focus Styles</strong>: Style them, don’t remove them</li> <li><strong>Provide Text Alternatives</strong>: All non-text content needs descriptions</li> <li><strong>Support Zoom</strong>: Content should work at 200% zoom</li> <li><strong>Announce Changes</strong>: Use live regions for dynamic content</li> <li><strong>Respect Preferences</strong>: Honor prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-contrast</li> </ol> <h5 id="common-issues-1">Common Issues</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Missing alt text</strong>: Images without descriptions</li> <li><strong>Poor color contrast</strong>: Text hard to read against background</li> <li><strong>Keyboard traps</strong>: Focus stuck in component</li> <li><strong>Missing labels</strong>: Form inputs without associated labels</li> <li><strong>Auto-playing media</strong>: Content that plays without user initiation</li> <li><strong>Inaccessible custom controls</strong>: Recreating native functionality poorly</li> <li><strong>Missing skip links</strong>: No way to bypass repetitive content</li> <li><strong>Focus order issues</strong>: Tab order doesn’t match visual order</li> </ul> <h5 id="testing-tools">Testing Tools</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Automated</strong>: axe DevTools, WAVE, Lighthouse</li> <li><strong>Manual</strong>: VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), NVDA/JAWS (Windows), TalkBack (Android)</li> <li><strong>Simulators</strong>: NoCoffee (vision), Silktide (various disabilities)</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 <code>accessibility-statement/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-statement-generator">Accessibility Statement Generator</h4> <p>You generate accessibility statements — user-facing web pages declaring conformance status, known limitations, and contact information. Distinct from VPAT/ACR (procurement documents).</p> <h4 id="statement-formats">Statement Formats</h4> <h5 id="w3c-model">W3C Model</h5> <ol type="1"> <li>Organization name and date</li> <li>Conformance status (Fully/Partially/Non-conformant)</li> <li>Standard targeted (WCAG version + level)</li> <li>Scope (pages/apps covered)</li> <li>Known limitations with workarounds</li> <li>Assessment approach</li> <li>Feedback mechanism with response commitment</li> <li>Compatibility (browsers, AT tested)</li> </ol> <h5 id="eu-model-public-sector-required">EU Model (Public Sector Required)</h5> <p>All of W3C, plus:</p> <ul> <li>Disproportionate burden declaration</li> <li>National enforcement body link</li> <li>Annual review commitment</li> </ul> <h4 id="workflow-9">Workflow</h4> <ol type="1"> <li>Check for existing audit reports</li> <li>Gather organization details (name, URL, contact, legal framework)</li> <li>Map findings to known limitations</li> <li>Classify conformance status</li> <li>Generate HTML or Markdown document</li> <li>Save to <code>ACCESSIBILITY-STATEMENT.md</code></li> </ol> <h4 id="conformance-classification">Conformance Classification</h4> <p>Each condition, with its status.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Condition</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>No critical or serious issues</td> <td>Fully conformant</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>No critical, 1-3 serious with workarounds</td> <td>Partially conformant</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Any critical OR many serious</td> <td>Non-conformant</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="output-contract-71">Output contract</h4> <p>Produce the file or script the task asks for. WCAG conformance is the technical standard; legal compliance adds jurisdiction-specific requirements, timelines, and documentation.</p> <h4 id="framework-coverage">Framework Coverage</h4> <ul> <li><strong>Section 508</strong> — US federal agencies/contractors, WCAG 2.0 AA + authoring/documentation requirements</li> <li><strong>ADA Title II/III</strong> — US state/local government + private sector, WCAG 2.1 AA per 2024 rule</li> <li><strong>EN 301 549</strong> — EU harmonized standard, Clauses 5-13 extend beyond WCAG</li> <li><strong>EAA</strong> — EU private sector from June 2025, e-commerce/banking/transport</li> <li><strong>AODA</strong> — Ontario/Canada, WCAG 2.0 AA, 3-year compliance reports</li> </ul> <h4 id="workflow-10">Workflow</h4> <ol type="1"> <li>Identify applicable frameworks by market, org type, product type</li> <li>Read existing audit results</li> <li>Map findings to framework-specific requirements</li> <li>Flag non-WCAG requirements (EN 301 549 Clauses 5-8, 10-13)</li> <li>Generate VPAT 2.5 or compliance status matrix</li> </ol> <h4 id="vpat-conformance-levels">VPAT Conformance Levels</h4> <ul> <li><strong>Supports</strong> — Fully meets criterion</li> <li><strong>Partially Supports</strong> — Some functionality meets criterion</li> <li><strong>Does Not Support</strong> — Majority does not meet criterion</li> <li><strong>Not Applicable</strong> — Not relevant to the product</li> </ul> <h4 id="output-contract-72">Output contract</h4> <p>Produce the file or script the task asks for. Used by <code>compliance-mapping</code> agent and any agent generating compliance reports.</p> <hr /> <h4 id="framework-comparison">Framework Comparison</h4> <p>Each framework, with its jurisdiction, WCAG version, scope and enforcement.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 18%" /> <col style="width: 22%" /> <col style="width: 24%" /> <col style="width: 12%" /> <col style="width: 22%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Framework</th> <th>Jurisdiction</th> <th>WCAG Version</th> <th>Scope</th> <th>Enforcement</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Section 508 (Revised)</td> <td>US (Federal)</td> <td>WCAG 2.0 AA</td> <td>Federal agencies and their ICT</td> <td>Administrative complaints, lawsuits</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>ADA Title II</td> <td>US (State/Local)</td> <td>WCAG 2.1 AA (DOJ 2024 rule)</td> <td>State and local government websites</td> <td>DOJ enforcement, lawsuits</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>ADA Title III</td> <td>US (Private)</td> <td>No explicit WCAG version; courts use 2.0/2.1 AA</td> <td>Public accommodations</td> <td>Private lawsuits, DOJ enforcement</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>EN 301 549 v3.2.1</td> <td>EU</td> <td>WCAG 2.1 AA (Chapter 9-11)</td> <td>Public sector + private sector ICT</td> <td>EU member state enforcement</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>European Accessibility Act (EAA)</td> <td>EU</td> <td>WCAG 2.1 AA (via EN 301 549)</td> <td>Private sector products and services (June 2025)</td> <td>Market surveillance, fines</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>AODA</td> <td>Ontario, Canada</td> <td>WCAG 2.0 AA</td> <td>Ontario organizations (50+ employees)</td> <td>Administrative penalties</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Accessible Canada Act</td> <td>Canada (Federal)</td> <td>WCAG 2.1 AA (guidance)</td> <td>Federally regulated entities</td> <td>CRTC/CTA enforcement, penalties</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Israeli Standard 5568</td> <td>Israel</td> <td>WCAG 2.0 AA</td> <td>Public websites and apps</td> <td>Civil lawsuits</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>JIS X 8341-3:2016</td> <td>Japan</td> <td>WCAG 2.0 AA</td> <td>Government websites (recommended)</td> <td>No enforcement (voluntary)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Chinese GB/T 37668-2019</td> <td>China</td> <td>Based on WCAG 2.0</td> <td>Government websites</td> <td>Administrative guidance</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="additional-non-wcag-requirements">Additional Non-WCAG Requirements</h4> <p>Some frameworks require more than WCAG conformance:</p> <h5 id="en-301-549-additional-requirements">EN 301 549 Additional Requirements</h5> <p>Each chapter, with its requirement and beyond WCAG.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 37%" /> <col style="width: 37%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Chapter</th> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Beyond WCAG</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Chapter 5</td> <td>Closed functionality (kiosks, ATMs)</td> <td>Yes — no WCAG equivalent</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Chapter 6</td> <td>Real-time text (RTT) communication</td> <td>Yes — no WCAG equivalent</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Chapter 7</td> <td>Video capabilities (captions, audio description)</td> <td>Extends WCAG 1.2</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Chapter 8</td> <td>Hardware accessibility</td> <td>Yes — physical product requirements</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Chapter 10</td> <td>Non-web documents</td> <td>Maps WCAG to document formats</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Chapter 11</td> <td>Non-web software</td> <td>Maps WCAG to native applications</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Chapter 12</td> <td>Documentation and support services</td> <td>Accessible help documentation</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Chapter 13</td> <td>ICT providing relay or emergency services</td> <td>Yes — no WCAG equivalent</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="european-accessibility-act-additions">European Accessibility Act Additions</h5> <ul> <li>Products: computers, smartphones, tablets, self-service terminals, e-readers</li> <li>Services: e-commerce, banking, transport, telephony, audiovisual media</li> <li>Microenterprises (<10 employees, <€2M turnover) exempt from service requirements</li> <li>Deadline: June 28, 2025 for new products/services</li> </ul> <h4 id="vpat-acr-mapping">VPAT / ACR Mapping</h4> <p>The Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) maps to three standards:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>VPAT Edition</th> <th>Standards Covered</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>VPAT 2.5 Section 508</td> <td>Revised Section 508 (WCAG 2.0 AA)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>VPAT 2.5 EU</td> <td>EN 301 549 (WCAG 2.1 AA + Chapters 5-13)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>VPAT 2.5 INT</td> <td>Section 508 + EN 301 549 + WCAG 2.x</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Conformance levels in VPAT:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supports — fully meets the criterion</li> <li>Partially Supports — some functionality meets, some does not</li> <li>Does Not Support — majority of functionality does not meet</li> <li>Not Applicable — criterion is not relevant to the product</li> </ul> <h4 id="accessibility-statement-requirements">Accessibility Statement Requirements</h4> <h5 id="w3c-model-voluntary">W3C Model (Voluntary)</h5> <ul> <li>Conformance status (Fully conformant / Partially conformant / Non-conformant)</li> <li>WCAG version and level targeted</li> <li>Known limitations with workarounds</li> <li>Assessment approach (self, external, automated tools)</li> <li>Feedback mechanism with response commitment</li> <li>Date of statement and last review</li> </ul> <h5 id="eu-model-required-for-public-sector">EU Model (Required for Public Sector)</h5> <p>All of the above, plus:</p> <ul> <li>Disproportionate burden declaration (if applicable, with justification)</li> <li>Link to national enforcement body</li> <li>Annual review requirement</li> <li>Date of last accessibility audit</li> </ul> <h4 id="compliance-timeline-quick-reference">Compliance Timeline Quick Reference</h4> <p>Each event, with its date and impact.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 28%" /> 2018</td> <td>Adopted WCAG 2.0 AA for federal ICT</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>EU Web Accessibility Directive</td> <td>September 2018 (new sites), September 2020 (existing)</td> <td>Public sector websites and mobile apps</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>ADA Title II WCAG 2.1 Rule</td> <td>April 2026 (large), April 2027 (small)</td> <td>State/local government web content</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>European Accessibility Act</td> <td>June 2025</td> <td>Private sector products and services</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>AODA Full Compliance</td> <td>January 2021</td> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> cross-cutting</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/kb-report-generation">skills/kb-report-generation</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> reference</li> </ul> <p>Reference data, not a reviewer. Format accessibility audit reports with severity scoring (0-100, A-F grades), scorecard computation, and compliance exports including VPAT/ACR and remediation priorities.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>kb-report-generation/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="report-generation-1">Report Generation</h4> <h4 id="report-file">Report File</h4> <p>Default output: <code>DOCUMENT-ACCESSIBILITY-AUDIT.md</code> in the project root.</p> <h4 id="required-sections">Required Sections</h4> <p>Every audit report MUST include these sections:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Audit Information</strong> - date, auditor, profile, scope, counts</li> <li><strong>Executive Summary</strong> - totals, pass rate, most common issue, effort estimate</li> <li><strong>Cross-Document Patterns</strong> - recurring issues, systemic failures</li> <li><strong>Findings by File</strong> - per-document issues with rule ID, severity, location, WCAG, impact, remediation</li> <li><strong>Findings by Rule (Cross-Reference)</strong> - rule-level aggregation across files</li> <li><strong>What Passed</strong> - acknowledge clean documents and categories</li> <li><strong>Remediation Priority</strong> - ordered by impact (Immediate / Soon / When Possible)</li> <li><strong>Accessibility Scorecard</strong> - per-document scores and grades</li> <li><strong>Metadata Dashboard</strong> - document properties health</li> <li><strong>Confidence Summary</strong> - breakdown by confidence level</li> </ol> <h5 id="optional-sections-include-when-applicable">Optional Sections (include when applicable)</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Template Analysis</strong> - when batch scanning detects shared templates</li> <li><strong>Comparison Report</strong> - when re-scanning against a baseline</li> <li><strong>CI/CD Recommendations</strong> - when no config files exist</li> </ul> <h4 id="severity-scoring-formula">Severity Scoring Formula</h4> <pre class="text"><code>Document Score = 100 - (sum of weighted findings) Weights: Error (high confidence): -10 points Error (medium confidence): -7 points Error (low confidence): -3 points Warning (high confidence): -3 points Warning (medium confidence):-2 points Warning (low confidence): -1 point Tips: 0 points Floor: 0 (minimum score)</code></pre> <h4 id="score-grades-3">Score Grades</h4> <p>Each score, with its grade and meaning.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Score</th> <th>Grade</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>90-100</td> <td>A</td> <td>Excellent - minor or no issues</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>75-89</td> <td>B</td> <td>Good - some warnings, few errors</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>50-74</td> <td>C</td> <td>Needs Work - multiple errors</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>25-49</td> <td>D</td> <td>Poor - significant accessibility barriers</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>0-24</td> <td>F</td> <td>Failing - critical barriers, likely unusable with AT</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="organization-modes">Organization Modes</h4> <p>Each mode, with description and best for.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 20%" /> <col style="width: 44%" /> <col style="width: 34%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Mode</th> <th>Description</th> <th>Best For</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>By file</td> <td>Group all issues under each document</td> <td>Small batches (< 10 files)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>By issue type</td> <td>Group all instances of each rule across documents</td> <td>Seeing patterns</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>By severity</td> <td>Critical first, then serious, moderate, minor</td> <td>Prioritizing fixes</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="vpatacr-compliance-export">VPAT/ACR Compliance Export</h4> <h5 id="conformance-levels-1">Conformance Levels</h5> <p>Each level, with its criteria.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Criteria</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Supports</td> <td>No findings for this WCAG criterion across any document</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Partially Supports</td> <td>Some documents pass, some fail</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Does Not Support</td> <td>All or most documents fail</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Not Applicable</td> <td>Criterion does not apply to scanned document types</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="supported-vpat-editions">Supported VPAT Editions</h5> <ul> <li><strong>VPAT 2.5 (WCAG)</strong> - maps to WCAG 2.2 criteria</li> <li><strong>VPAT 2.5 (508)</strong> - maps to Revised Section 508 standards</li> <li><strong>VPAT 2.5 (EN 301 549)</strong> - maps to EU accessibility directive</li> <li><strong>VPAT 2.5 (INT)</strong> - International edition (all three combined)</li> </ul> <h4 id="remediation-tracking-1">Remediation Tracking</h4> <p>When comparing against a baseline audit report:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Status</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Fixed</td> <td>Issue was in previous report but is now resolved</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>New</td> <td>Issue was not in previous report but appears now</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Persistent</td> <td>Issue remains from previous report</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Regressed</td> <td>Issue was previously fixed but has returned</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="progress-metrics">Progress Metrics</h5> <ul> <li>Issue reduction percentage: <code>(fixed / previous_total) * 100</code></li> <li>Score change: <code>current_score - previous_score</code></li> <li>Documents improved: count of documents with higher scores</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="severity-mapping-reference">Severity Mapping (Reference)</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> cross-cutting</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>kb-severity-mapping</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> none</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/kb-severity-mapping">skills/kb-severity-mapping</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> reference</li> </ul> <p>Reference data, not a reviewer. Canonical severity level definitions and cross-domain mapping for web, document, and markdown audits. Score impact ranges, WCAG conformance alignment, and cross-format normalization.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>kb-severity-mapping/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="severity-mapping">Severity Mapping</h4> <p>Canonical severity definitions shared across web, document, and markdown audit domains.</p> <h4 id="canonical-severity-levels">Canonical Severity Levels</h4> <p>Each level, with its definition, WCAG conformance and score impact.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Definition</th> <th>WCAG Conformance</th> <th>Score Impact</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Blocks access entirely for one or more user groups. No workaround exists.</td> <td>Fails Level A</td> <td>-15 to -22 points</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Severely impairs access; a workaround may exist but is unreasonable.</td> <td>Fails Level A or AA</td> <td>-5 to -10 points</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Causes friction or confusion; most users can still complete the task.</td> <td>Fails Level AA (advisory)</td> <td>-2 to -4 points</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Polish issue; no meaningful barrier for most users.</td> <td>Technique deviation</td> <td>-1 point</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="cross-domain-equivalents">Cross-Domain Equivalents</h4> <p>Each canonical level, with its web (axe-core or playwright), document (office or PDF) and markdown.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Canonical Level</th> <th>Web (axe-core / Playwright)</th> <th>Document (Office/PDF)</th> <th>Markdown</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Critical</td> <td><code>critical</code> (axe-core)</td> <td>Missing document title; untagged PDF; missing heading structure</td> <td>Broken anchor link leading to dead navigation</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Serious</td> <td><code>serious</code> (axe-core)</td> <td>Missing alt text on informational image; table has no headers</td> <td>Ambiguous link text (e.g., “click here”); missing alt text on image</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Moderate</td> <td><code>moderate</code> (axe-core)</td> <td>Merged table cells; color-only data encoding</td> <td>Skipped heading level; missing table caption</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Minor</td> <td><code>minor</code> (axe-core)</td> <td>Decorative image with non-empty alt; redundant bookmark</td> <td>Emoji in heading; em-dash used as list separator</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="score-impact-rules">Score Impact Rules</h4> <p>Score impacts listed above are <strong>additive per finding</strong>. When the same issue recurs across many elements:</p> <ul> <li><strong>First occurrence</strong> — full deduction</li> <li><strong>Same issue type, same page/file</strong> — no additional deduction (already counted once per issue rule)</li> <li><strong>Same issue type, different page/file</strong> — full deduction applies again to the new page/file score</li> </ul> <h4 id="conversion-rules-normalizing-cross-domain-reports">Conversion Rules (Normalizing Cross-Domain Reports)</h4> <p>When generating a unified report that combines web, document, and markdown findings:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Map each finding to the canonical severity level using the table above.</li> <li>Apply the score impact from the canonical level, not from the domain-specific tool’s internal scoring.</li> <li>For aggregated scores (portfolio or project level), compute each page/file score independently, then average.</li> <li>Do not double-count a finding that appears in both an axe-core scan and a Playwright behavioral scan – deduplicate by rule ID and element location.</li> </ol> <h4 id="confidence-modifier-web-domain">Confidence Modifier (Web Domain)</h4> <p>For web audits, confidence level modifies the base deduction:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Confidence</th> <th>Multiplier</th> <th>Source Signals</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Confirmed</td> <td>1.2x</td> <td>axe-core + agent code review + Playwright behavioral test</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>High (two sources)</td> <td>1.0x</td> <td>Any two of the three sources above</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>High (one source)</td> <td>1.0x (reduced base)</td> <td>Single automated tool, high rule reliability</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Medium</td> <td>0.7x</td> <td>Single source, medium rule reliability</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Low</td> <td>0.3x</td> <td>Single source, low rule reliability or heuristic</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Document and markdown audits do not use confidence multipliers – they use the base score impact only.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="wcag-3.0-preview">WCAG 3.0 Preview</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> cross-cutting</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> medium</li> 2.2.</p> <p><strong>Critical disclaimer you MUST state in every response:</strong></p> <blockquote> <p>WCAG 3.0 is currently an <strong>early Working Draft</strong> and is NOT yet a W3C standard. Do NOT abandon WCAG 2.2 compliance. All current legal and contractual obligations reference WCAG 2.x. This information is for forward-planning only.</p> </blockquote> <hr /> <h4 id="key-changes-from-wcag-2.2-to-3.0">Key Changes from WCAG 2.2 to 3.0</h4> <h5 id="conformance-model">Conformance (dark-on-light ≠ light-on-dark)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Range</td> <td>1:1 to 21:1</td> <td>Lc 0 to Lc 106</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="new-scope">New Scope</h5> <p>Each area, with You do not write or review code - that is the other specialists’ job. You teach the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines in plain language with practical examples. When a developer asks “what does WCAG 1.4.11 mean?” or “what changed in WCAG 2.2?”, you give them a clear, actionable answer - not a link to the W3C spec wall.</p> <h4 id="your-scope-17">Your Scope</h4> <ul> <li>WCAG 2.0, 2.1, and 2.2 success criteria explanations</li> <li>Conformance levels (A, AA, AAA) and what they mean</li> <li>What changed between WCAG versions</li> <li>When specific criteria apply and don’t apply</li> <li>Common misconceptions about WCAG</li> <li>The intent behind criteria (why the rules exist)</li> <li>Sufficient techniques vs advisory techniques</li> <li>Understanding statements of conformance</li> <li>How WCAG applies to different content types (web apps, SPAs, mobile web, documents)</li> </ul> <h4 id="you-do-not">You Do NOT</h4> <ul> <li>Write or review code (use the specialist agents for that)</li> <li>Run tests (use testing-coach for that)</li> <li>Make legal claims about compliance</li> <li>Cover WCAG AAA unless specifically asked (the team targets AA)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="wcag-structure">WCAG Structure</h4> <h5 id="the-four-principles-pour">The Four Principles (POUR)</h5> <p>Everything in WCAG falls under one of four principles:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 37%" /> <col style="width: 31%" /> <col style="width: 31%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Principle</th> <th>Meaning</th> <th>Example</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Perceivable</strong></td> <td>Users must be able to perceive the content</td> <td>Alt text for images, captions for video, sufficient contrast</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Operable</strong></td> <td>Users must be able to operate the interface</td> <td>Keyboard access, enough time, no seizure triggers</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Understandable</strong></td> <td>Users must be able to understand the content</td> <td>Readable text, predictable behavior, input assistance</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Robust</strong></td> <td>Content must work with current and future technologies</td> <td>Valid HTML, proper ARIA, compatible with assistive tech</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="conformance-levels-2">Conformance Levels</h5> <p>Each level, with its meaning and required.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 40%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> <th>Required?</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>A</strong></td> <td>Bare minimum. Without this, some users literally cannot access the content.</td> <td>Yes - always required</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>AA</strong></td> <td>The standard target. Covers the majority of accessibility barriers. Most laws reference AA.</td> <td>Yes - the A11y Agent Team targets AA</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>AAA</strong></td> <td>Enhanced. Ideal but not always achievable for all content types.</td> <td>Optional - nice to have</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Important:</strong> Conformance is inclusive. “Conforms to AA” means ALL Level A criteria AND all Level AA criteria are met. You cannot claim AA while failing any Level A criteria.</p> <h5 id="success-criteria-numbering">Success Criteria Numbering</h5> <p>Example: <strong>WCAG 2.1.1</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>2</strong> = Principle 2 (Operable)</li> <li><strong>1</strong> = Guideline 2.1 (Keyboard Accessible)</li> <li><strong>1</strong> = Success Criterion 2.1.1 (Keyboard)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="what-changed-in-wcag-2.2-vs-2.1">What Changed in WCAG 2.2 (vs 2.1)</h4> <p>WCAG 2.2 added 9 new success criteria. The ones that affect AA conformance:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 21%" /> <col style="width: 45%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Criterion</th> <th>Level</th> <th>What It Added</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Focused element must not be hidden behind sticky headers/banners</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>2.5.7 Dragging Movements</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Dragging functions must have non-drag alternatives</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Touch targets >= 24 x 24px (or sufficient spacing)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>3.2.6 Consistent Help</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Help mechanisms in same location across pages</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>3.3.7 Redundant Entry</td> <td>A</td> <td>Don’t make users re-enter info already provided</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>3.3.8 Accessible Authentication</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Don’t require cognitive tests for login</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>WCAG 2.2 also <strong>removed</strong> one criterion:</p> <ul> <li><strong>4.1.1 Parsing</strong> - removed because modern browsers handle parsing errors well. HTML validation is still good practice but is no longer a WCAG requirement.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="understanding-sufficient-techniques-vs-advisory-techniques">Understanding “Sufficient Techniques” vs “Advisory Techniques”</h4> <p>WCAG provides techniques to meet criteria. There are two types:</p> <p><strong>Sufficient techniques</strong> - If you use one of these, you pass the criterion. Example: For 1.1.1, providing <code>alt</code> text on <code><img></code> is a sufficient technique.</p> <p><strong>Advisory techniques</strong> - Recommendations that go beyond the requirement. Not required for conformance. Example: Providing long descriptions for complex images is advisory beyond basic alt text.</p> <p><strong>Failures</strong> - Common mistakes that violate a criterion. Example: Using <code>alt="image"</code> for all images is a documented failure of 1.1.1.</p> <p>You don’t have to use a specific technique. If you achieve the same outcome through a different method, you can still conform. The success criteria describe the outcome, not the method.</p> <hr /> <h4 id="how-to-answer-wcag-questions">How to Answer WCAG Questions</h4> <p>When a developer asks a WCAG question:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>State the criterion number and name</strong></li> <li><strong>Give the conformance level</strong> (A, AA, or AAA)</li> <li><strong>Explain in plain language</strong> what it requires and why</li> <li><strong>Give a concrete example</strong> of a pass and a fail</li> <li><strong>Note what it does NOT require</strong> (to prevent over-engineering)</li> <li><strong>Reference the relevant specialist agent</strong> if they need code help</li> </ol> <p>Example response:</p> <pre class="text"><code>WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA, new in WCAG 2.1) Requires: UI components and meaningful graphics must have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. Example pass: A text input with a #767676 border on a white background (contrast ratio 4.48:1). Example fail: A text input with a #CCCCCC border on white (contrast ratio 1.6:1 - the border is nearly invisible). Does NOT apply to: Disabled/inactive controls, purely decorative elements, photographs, logos. For code-level contrast checking, use @contrast-master.</code></pre> <h4 id="reference-files-41">Reference files</h4> <p>Read one only when the task reaches it. Do not read them all up front.</p> <ul> <li><code>references/complete-wcag-2-2-aa-success-criteria-reference.md</code> - Complete WCAG 2.2 AA Success Criteria Reference</li> <li><code>references/common-wcag-misconceptions.md</code> - Common WCAG Misconceptions</li> </ul> <h4 id="output-contract-75">Output contract</h4> <p>Answer the question. Keep the answer to what was asked, cite the criterion or API by name, and stop. Do not append a checklist that was not requested.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. Authoritative specifications for this skill: <code>skills/a11y-core/references/sources.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="web-accessibility">Web Accessibility</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 17</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>web-accessibility</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Magnus Hedemark</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/magnus919/agent-skills">magnus919/agent-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/magnus919/agent-skills/tree/54d81f7e02051df2f31130a136dc68f8add42130/web-accessibility">web-accessibility</a></li> </ul> <p>Design, build, and review accessible web interfaces with native semantics, keyboard and focus behavior, forms and recovery, responsive input, motion, assistive-technology testing, and WCAG 2.2-informed evidence. Use for a11y, WCAG, ARIA, screen-reader, keyboard, focus, dialog, form, widget, or accessibility review work across frameworks. Do not use this skill for unrelated requests; route to the nearest named specialist.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>web-accessibility/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="web-accessibility-1">Web Accessibility</h4> <p>Accessibility is successful task completion and recovery for disabled people, not a tool score. Define observable requirements before implementation, prefer native platform behavior where it fits, and gather bounded evidence in the supported browser and assistive-technology (AT) environment.</p> <h5 id="workflow-11">Workflow</h5> <ol type="1"> <li>Define the task, users, supported browsers/AT, input methods, and failure recovery. Start with <code>assets/acceptance-criteria-template.md</code>.</li> <li>Choose native HTML first. Load <code>references/semantics-and-names.md</code> for structure, native controls, accessible names, descriptions, and dynamic updates.</li> <li>Specify every interactive state: trigger, role/name/state/value, keyboard commands, focus entry/exit/return, pointer alternative, errors, and visible feedback. Load the focused pattern reference.</li> <li>Design for visual and input adaptation using <code>references/visual-input-and-motion.md</code>; distinguish WCAG requirements from product goals and exceptions.</li> <li>Implement only after the contract is defined. For custom composite widgets, first evaluate a proven native or maintained component in the chosen stack; APG examples are informative guidance, not production proof.</li> <li>Verify with <code>references/testing-and-evidence.md</code> and the design, implementation, and release templates. Record tool, version, scope, manual tasks, actual browser/AT combinations, failures, and blocked or not-applicable items.</li> <li>Do not issue a WCAG conformance or general accessibility verdict from an automated scan. A conformance claim needs a complete, scoped evaluation outside this skill’s automatic verdict.</li> </ol> <h5 id="load-on-demand">Load On Demand</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Need</th> <th>Load</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Standards status, source authority, or exact links</td> <td><code>references/source-index.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Native semantics, labels, accessible names, landmarks, live updates</td> <td><code>references/semantics-and-names.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Tab order, focus visibility, traps, restoration, route changes</td> <td><code>references/keyboard-focus-and-routing.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Labels, validation, recoverable errors, authentication</td> <td><code>references/forms-errors-authentication.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Modal dialogs, disclosure, responsive navigation</td> <td><code>references/dialogs-disclosures-navigation.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Tabs, comboboxes, listboxes, grids, menus, other composites</td> <td><code>references/composite-widgets.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Contrast, reflow, zoom, targets, drag, motion, media</td> <td><code>references/visual-input-and-motion.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Automated checks, manual protocols, AT matrix, evidence</td> <td><code>references/testing-and-evidence.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Framework or skill boundary</td> <td><code>references/routing.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Validate common outcomes without claiming conformance</td> <td><code>references/outcome-probes.md</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="decision-rules">Decision Rules</h5> <ul> <li>Treat WCAG 2.2 success criteria, HTML/ARIA specifications, and informative tutorials/patterns as separate layers. See <code>references/source-index.md</code>.</li> <li>Use WAI-ARIA 1.2 only when native host-language semantics do not provide the required behavior. ARIA changes semantics; it does not create keyboard behavior or visual presentation.</li> <li>Use the Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.2 algorithm for edge cases. Do not substitute a priority mnemonic; inspect the computed accessibility tree and name.</li> <li>For a modal, prefer <code><dialog>.showModal()</code> when it supports the target environment. Keep background content unavailable/inert, choose initial focus for the content and task, provide a visible close path, and return focus logically. Do not hide a backdrop with <code>aria-hidden</code> or hide an ancestor of the dialog.</li> <li>Treat ordinary responsive navigation as a disclosure over ordinary links, not an ARIA menu. Use menu semantics only with the application-menu keyboard contract.</li> <li>Target Size (Minimum) is 24 by 24 CSS pixels at WCAG 2.2 AA, subject to its spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent, and essential exceptions. A larger target may be a product goal.</li> </ul> <h5 id="completion">Completion</h5> <p>Stop when each acceptance criterion has direct evidence or a recorded failed, blocked, or not-applicable result. Report residual risk and the exact evidence boundary; do not turn absent testing into a pass.</p> <h5 id="when-not-to-use-2">When Not To Use</h5> <ul> <li>For Hugo template architecture, theme-wide layout, or CMS rendering concerns, use <a href="../hugo-theme/SKILL.md">hugo-theme</a> and its <a href="../hugo-theme/references/design-accessibility.md">design/accessibility reference</a>.</li> <li>For evidence gathering, scope decisions, or user-facing behavior outside accessibility, use <a href="../product-discovery/SKILL.md">product-discovery</a>, <a href="../product-methodology/SKILL.md">product-methodology</a>, or <a href="../product-design-and-ux/SKILL.md">product-design-and-ux</a>. Keep this skill responsible for accessibility interaction and conformance depth.</li> <li>For framework or library APIs, consult the current official documentation after defining this skill’s semantic and interaction contract. React implementation details route to <a href="../react/SKILL.md">react</a>; Vite configuration routes to <a href="../vite/SKILL.md">vite</a>.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="web-csv-reporter">Web CSV Reporter</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> web</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 3</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>web-csv-reporter</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> artifact</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/web-csv-reporter">skills/web-csv-reporter</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> helper</li> </ul> <p>Internal helper: export web findings to CSV with Deque University links.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>web-csv-reporter/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <p>You are a web accessibility CSV report generator. You receive aggregated web audit findings and produce structured CSV files optimized for reporting, tracking, and remediation workflows.</p> <p>Load the <code>help-url-reference</code> skill for the complete Accessibility Insights URL mappings and WCAG understanding document links.</p> <h4 id="output-path-2">Output Path</h4> <p>Write all output files to the current working directory. In a VS Code workspace this is the workspace root folder. From a CLI this is the shell’s current directory. If the user specifies an alternative path, use that instead. Never write output to temporary directories, session storage, or agent-internal state.</p> <h4 id="wcag-understanding-document-url-pattern">WCAG Understanding Document URL Pattern</h4> <pre class="text"><code>Base: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/ Map criterion number to slug: 1.1.1 -> non-text-content 1.3.1 -> info-and-relationships 1.3.5 -> identify-input-purpose 1.4.3 -> contrast-minimum 1.4.4 -> resize-text 2.4.1 -> bypass-blocks 2.4.2 -> page-titled 2.4.3 -> focus-order 2.4.7 -> focus-visible 3.1.1 -> language-of-page 3.3.2 -> labels-or-instructions 4.1.1 -> parsing 4.1.2 -> name-role-value</code></pre> <h4 id="csv-generation-rules-1">CSV Generation Rules</h4> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Encoding:</strong> UTF-8 with BOM for Excel compatibility</li> <li><strong>Quoting:</strong> Quote all text fields; escape internal quotes by doubling (<code>""</code>)</li> <li><strong>Dates:</strong> ISO 8601 format (<code>YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ</code>)</li> <li><strong>Empty fields:</strong> Use empty quotes (<code>""</code>) not NULL</li> <li><strong>Line endings:</strong> CRLF for cross-platform compatibility</li> <li><strong>Header row:</strong> Always include as the first row</li> <li><strong>File naming:</strong> Use the exact filenames specified above, or prefix with a user-provided project name (e.g., <code>myproject-WEB-ACCESSIBILITY-FINDINGS.csv</code>)</li> <li><strong>ROI score calculation:</strong> <code>instances x severity_weight</code> where Critical=10, Serious=7, Moderate=3, Minor=1</li> </ol> <h4 id="priority-assignment-rules-1">Priority Assignment Rules</h4> <p>Each severity, with its pattern type and priority.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Severity</th> <th>Pattern Type</th> <th>Priority</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Critical (any)</td> <td>Any</td> <td>Immediate</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Serious</td> <td>Systemic</td> <td>Immediate</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Serious</td> <td>Template</td> <td>Immediate</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Serious</td> <td>Page-specific</td> <td>Soon</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Moderate</td> <td>Systemic</td> <td>Soon</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Moderate</td> <td>Template/Page</td> <td>When Possible</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Minor</td> <td>Any</td> <td>When Possible</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="integration-notes-2">Integration Notes</h4> <ul> <li>CSV files can be imported into Excel, Google Sheets, Jira, Azure DevOps, or any tracking system</li> <li>The <code>finding_id</code> column enables cross-referencing between CSVs and the markdown audit report</li> <li>The <code>remediation_status</code> column supports delta tracking when comparing successive audit exports</li> <li>The <code>deque_help_url</code> column provides direct links to Accessibility Insights for developer self-service learning</li> <li>The <code>roi_score</code> in the remediation CSV helps teams prioritize fixes with the highest impact-to-effort ratio</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="multi-agent-reliability-8">Multi-Agent Reliability</h4> <h5 id="role-8">Role</h5> <p>You are a <strong>read-only reporter</strong>. You read audit reports and produce CSV files. You never modify source documents or audit reports.</p> <h5 id="output-contract-76">Output Contract</h5> <p>Return to <code>web-accessibility-wizard</code>:</p> <ul> <li><code>files_written</code>: list of CSV file paths created</li> <li><code>findings_exported</code>: total count of findings written to CSV</li> <li><code>scorecard_pages</code>: count of pages in the scorecard CSV</li> <li><code>remediation_items</code>: count of items in the remediation CSV</li> <li><code>status</code>: <code>success</code> | <code>partial</code> (with reason) | <code>failed</code> (with error)</li> </ul> <h5 id="handoff-transparency-8">Handoff Transparency</h5> <p>When invoked by <code>web-accessibility-wizard</code>:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Announce start:</strong> “Generating CSV export from web audit report: [N] findings across [N] pages”</li> <li><strong>Announce completion:</strong> “CSV export complete: [N] findings exported to [paths]. Scorecard: [N] pages. Remediation: [N] items.”</li> <li><strong>On failure:</strong> “CSV export failed: [reason]. No files written.”</li> </ul> <p>You return results to <code>web-accessibility-wizard</code>. Users see the export summary and file locations.</p> <h4 id="reference-files-42">Reference files</h4> <p>Read one only when the task reaches it. Do not read them all up front.</p> <ul> <li><code>references/csv-output-files.md</code> - CSV Output Files, Accessibility Insights Help URL Patterns</li> </ul> <h4 id="output-contract-77">Output contract</h4> <p>Produce the file or script the task asks for. Report what you wrote as a short list of paths and what each one changes. Do not restate the file contents.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. Authoritative specifications for this skill: <code>skills/a11y-core/references/sources.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="web-severity-scoring-reference">Web Severity Scoring (Reference)</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> cross-cutting</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>kb-web-severity-scoring</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> none</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/kb-web-severity-scoring">skills/kb-web-severity-scoring</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> reference</li> </ul> <p>Reference data, not a reviewer. Compute web accessibility scores (0-100, A-F grades) with severity scoring, confidence levels, and remediation tracking across audits.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>kb-web-severity-scoring/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="web-severity-scoring">Web Severity Scoring</h4> <h4 id="severity-scoring-formula-1">Severity Scoring Formula</h4> <pre class="text"><code>Page Score = 100 - (sum of weighted findings) Weights: Critical (confirmed, all three sources): -18 points Critical (high confidence, both sources): -15 points Critical (high confidence, single source): -10 points Critical (medium confidence): -7 points Critical (low confidence): -3 points Serious (high confidence): -7 points Serious (medium confidence): -5 points Serious (low confidence): -2 points Moderate (high confidence): -3 points Moderate (medium confidence): -2 points Moderate (low confidence): -1 point Minor: -1 point Floor: 0 (minimum score)</code></pre> <h5 id="scoring-profiles">Scoring Profiles</h5> <p>Use a profile to tune strictness by context while keeping comparable grade bands:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Profile</th> <th>Intended Use</th> <th>Multiplier</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>balanced (default)</td> <td>Standard product delivery</td> <td>1.0</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>strict</td> <td>Regulated/public-sector releases</td> <td>1.15</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>advisory</td> <td>Early design and prototyping</td> <td>0.8</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Apply the profile multiplier to each final deduction after confidence handling.</p> <h5 id="formula">Formula</h5> <pre class="pseudocode"><code>page_score = 100 for each finding: base = lookup(severity, confidence_level, source_count) // from table above multiplier = 1.2 if confidence_level == "confirmed" else 1.0 deduction = base × multiplier page_score = max(0, page_score - deduction)</code></pre> <p>The values in the lookup table above are <strong>base deductions</strong> (pre-multiplier). “Confirmed” findings (validated by all three sources: axe-core + agent review + Playwright) apply an additional 1.2× multiplier.</p> <p><strong>Example:</strong> One Critical finding at confirmed confidence = 18 (base) × 1.2 = <strong>21.6 points</strong> deducted → page score 78.</p> <h5 id="calibration-layer-v2">Calibration Layer (v2)</h5> <p>To reduce false-positive inflation and stabilize trends, apply a calibration coefficient by rule family:</p> <pre class="text"><code>calibrated_deduction = deduction × calibration_coefficient(rule_family)</code></pre> <p>Recommended initial coefficients:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 35%" /> <col style="width: 35%" /> <col style="width: 29%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Rule Family</th> <th>Coefficient</th> <th>Rationale</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Keyboard/focus</td> <td>1.1</td> <td>High functional impact at runtime</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Forms/labels/errors</td> <td>1.05</td> <td>High completion risk for core tasks</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Semantics/structure</td> <td>1.0</td> <td>Baseline scoring</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Link text/context</td> <td>0.9</td> <td>Higher context variance</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Content quality (alt/link clarity)</td> <td>0.85</td> <td>Needs human review more often</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Update coefficients quarterly from confirmed outcomes. Avoid changing coefficients more than +/-0.1 per cycle.</p> <h4 id="score-grades-4">Score Grades</h4> <p>Each score, with its grade and meaning.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Score</th> <th>Grade</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>90-100</td> <td>A</td> <td>Excellent - minor or no issues, meets WCAG AA</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>75-89</td> <td>B</td> <td>Good - some issues, mostly meets WCAG AA</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>50-74</td> <td>C</td> <td>Needs Work - multiple issues, partial WCAG AA compliance</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>25-49</td> <td>D</td> <td>Poor - significant accessibility barriers</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>0-24</td> <td>F</td> <td>Failing - critical barriers, likely unusable with AT</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="confidence-levels-4">Confidence Levels</h4> <p>Each level, with weight and when to use.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 28%" /> <col style="width: 46%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Weight</th> <th>When to Use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Confirmed</td> <td>120%</td> <td>Validated by all three sources: axe-core + agent review + Playwright behavioral testing</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>High</td> <td>100%</td> <td>Confirmed by axe-core + agent, or definitively structural (missing alt, no labels, no lang)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Medium</td> <td>70%</td> <td>Found by one source, likely issue (heading edge cases, questionable ARIA, possible keyboard traps)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Low</td> <td>30%</td> <td>Possible issue, needs human review (alt text quality, reading order, context-dependent link text)</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="source-correlation">Source Correlation</h5> <p>Issues found by both axe-core AND agent review are automatically upgraded to <strong>high confidence</strong> regardless of individual confidence ratings.</p> <p>Issues found by all three sources (axe-core + agent review + Playwright behavioral testing) are upgraded to <strong>confirmed confidence</strong> with a 1.2x weight multiplier. This applies when:</p> <ul> <li>axe-core reports a violation</li> <li>Agent code review identifies the same issue</li> <li>Playwright behavioral scan confirms the issue at runtime (e.g., keyboard trap confirmed by actual Tab traversal, contrast failure confirmed by rendered CSS computation)</li> </ul> <p>When Playwright is not available, the maximum achievable confidence remains <strong>High (100%)</strong>. The confirmed tier is additive — it never downgrades findings.</p> <h5 id="confidence-drift-guard">Confidence Drift Guard</h5> <p>Track predicted confidence versus post-triage outcome and compute drift:</p> <pre class="text"><code>drift = abs(predicted_confidence_score - observed_confirmation_rate)</code></pre> <p>Operational guideline:</p> <ul> <li>drift <= 0.10: stable</li> <li>drift 0.11-0.20: tune coefficients and source mapping</li> <li>drift > 0.20: freeze profile changes and run rule-level review</li> </ul> <h4 id="scorecard-format">Scorecard Format</h4> <h5 id="single-page">Single Page</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb487"><pre class="sourceCode markdown"><code class="sourceCode markdown"><span id="cb487-1"><a href="#cb487-1" aria-hidden="true" remediation ROI.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 31%" /> <col style="width: 26%" /> <col style="width: 41%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Pattern Type</th> <th>Definition</th> <th>Remediation ROI</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Systemic</td> <td>Same issue on every audited page</td> <td>Highest - usually layout/nav, fix once</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Template</td> <td>Same issue on pages sharing a component</td> <td>High - fix the shared component</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Page-specific</td> <td>Unique to one page</td> <td>Normal - fix individually</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="remediation-tracking-2">Remediation Tracking</h4> <h5 id="change-classification">Change Classification</h5> <p>Each status, with its definition.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Status</th> <th>Definition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Fixed</td> <td>Issue was in previous report but no longer present</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>New</td> <td>Issue not in previous report, appears now</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Persistent</td> <td>Issue remains from previous report</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Regressed</td> <td>Issue was previously fixed but has returned</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="progress-metrics-1">Progress Metrics</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Issue reduction:</strong> <code>(fixed / previous_total) * 100</code></li> <li><strong>Score change:</strong> <code>current_score - previous_score</code></li> <li><strong>Pages improved:</strong> count of pages with higher scores than previous audit</li> <li><strong>Trend:</strong> improving (score up 5+), stable (within 5), declining (score down 5+)</li> </ul> <h5 id="normalized-trend-metric-cross-audit">Normalized Trend Metric (Cross-Audit)</h5> <p>When audit scope changes between runs, use normalized change:</p> <pre class="text"><code>normalized_score = raw_score - (scope_variance_penalty) scope_variance_penalty = min(10, abs(previous_pages - current_pages) * 0.8)</code></pre> <p>Use normalized score for trend charts and use raw score for release gates.</p> <h4 id="output-metadata-recommended">Output Metadata (Recommended)</h4> <p>Include these fields in generated score artifacts for reproducibility:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb490"><pre id="critical">Critical</h5> <ul> <li>No keyboard access to essential functionality</li> <li>Missing form labels on required fields</li> <li>Images conveying critical information have no alt text</li> <li>Color is the sole means of conveying information</li> <li>Keyboard traps with no escape</li> </ul> <h5 id="serious">Serious</h5> <ul> <li>Missing skip navigation</li> <li>Poor heading hierarchy (skipped levels)</li> <li>Focus not visible on interactive elements</li> <li>Form errors not programmatically associated</li> <li>Missing ARIA on custom widgets</li> </ul> <h5 id="moderate">Moderate</h5> <ul> <li>Redundant ARIA on semantic elements</li> <li>Suboptimal heading structure (multiple H1s)</li> <li>Missing autocomplete on identity fields</li> <li>Links to new tabs without warning</li> <li>Missing table captions</li> </ul> <h5 id="minor">Minor</h5> <ul> <li>Redundant title attributes</li> <li>Suboptimal button text</li> <li>Missing landmark roles where semantic elements exist</li> <li>Decorative images with non-empty alt text</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h2 id="testing-scanning-and-review">Testing, Scanning and Review</h2> <li><strong>Trust tier:</strong> 3</li> </ul> <p>Use when running comprehensive WCAG accessibility audits with axe-core + pa11y + Lighthouse, generating context-aware remediation, or testing video accessibility. Supports 3-tier browser cascade with graceful degradation.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>a11y-ally/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="a11y-ally---comprehensive-accessibility-audit">/a11y-ally - Comprehensive Accessibility Audit</h4> <p><default_to_action> When this skill is invoked with a URL, Claude executes ALL steps automatically without waiting for user prompts between steps.</p> <h5 id="this-is-an-llm-powered-skill">THIS IS AN LLM-POWERED SKILL</h5> <p>The value of this skill is <strong>Claude’s intelligence</strong>, not just running automated tools:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 43%" /> <col style="width: 56%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Automated Tools Do</th> <th>Claude (This Skill) Does</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Flag “button has no name”</td> <td>Analyze context: icon class, parent element, nearby text → generate “Add to wishlist”</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Flag “image missing alt”</td> <td>Use Vision to see the image → describe actual content</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Flag “video has no captions”</td> <td>Download video, extract frames, analyze each frame with Vision → generate real captions</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Output generic templates</td> <td>Generate context-specific, copy-paste ready fixes</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>IF YOU SKIP THE LLM ANALYSIS, THIS SKILL HAS NO VALUE.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="execution-model">EXECUTION MODEL</h5> <p><strong>CLAUDE EXECUTES ALL STEPS WITHOUT STOPPING.</strong></p> <p>Do NOT wait for user prompts between steps. Execute the full pipeline:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Data Collection</strong>: Run multi-tool scan (axe-core, pa11y, Lighthouse) via Bash</li> <li><strong>LLM Analysis</strong>: Read results and analyze context for each violation</li> <li><strong>Vision Pipeline</strong>: If videos detected → download → extract frames → Read each frame → describe</li> <li><strong>Intelligent Remediation</strong>: Generate context-specific fixes using your reasoning</li> <li><strong>Generate Reports</strong>: Write all output files to <code>docs/accessibility-scans/{page-slug}/</code></li> </ol> <p><strong>WRONG:</strong></p> <pre><code>Claude: "I found 5 violations. Should I analyze them?" User: "Yes" Claude: "I see a video. Should I run the video pipeline?" User: "Yes"</code></pre> <p><strong>RIGHT:</strong></p> <pre><code>Claude: [Runs scan] → [Analyzes violations] → [Downloads video] → [Extracts frames] → [Reads each frame with Vision] → [Generates captions] → [Writes all files] "Audit complete. Generated 4 files in docs/accessibility-scans/example/"</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-1-browser-automation---content-fetching">STEP 1: BROWSER AUTOMATION - Content Fetching</h5> <p>Uses the <strong>qe-browser</strong> fleet skill as the browser engine. qe-browser wraps Vibium (WebDriver BiDi, 10MB Go binary) and provides the QE primitives we rely on. See <code>.claude/skills/qe-browser/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h6 id="primary-qe-browser-via-vibium-cli">1.1: PRIMARY — qe-browser via Vibium CLI</h6> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb493"><pre id="step-2-comprehensive-wcag-scan-multi-tool-parallel-resilient">STEP 2: COMPREHENSIVE WCAG SCAN (Multi-Tool, Parallel, Resilient)</h5> <p><strong>IMPORTANT:</strong> This step uses THREE accessibility testing tools for maximum coverage: - <strong>axe-core</strong>: Industry standard, excellent for ARIA and semantic issues - <strong>pa11y</strong>: Strong on contrast, links, and HTML validation - <strong>Lighthouse</strong>: Google’s accessibility scoring with performance correlation</p> <p>Combined detection rate is ~15% higher than any single tool.</p> <h6 id="resilience-architecture-v7.0-enhancement">2.0: RESILIENCE ARCHITECTURE (v7.0 Enhancement)</h6> <p><strong>Key improvements over v6.0:</strong></p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Feature</th> <th>v6.0 (Old)</th> <th>v7.0 (New)</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Tool execution</td> <td>Sequential</td> <td><strong>Parallel (Promise.allSettled)</strong></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Timeout handling</td> <td>Global 60s</td> <td><strong>Per-tool (60s/60s/90s)</strong></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Failure mode</td> <td>All-or-nothing</td> class="sourceCode" id="cb500"><pre class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb500-1"><a href="#cb500-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">cat</span> /tmp/a11y-work/scan-results.json</span></code></pre></div> <p>The results include: - <strong>pageInfo</strong>: Page structure, images, headings, media - <strong>violations</strong>: All violations from all tools (deduplicated) - <strong>byTool</strong>: Success/failure status per tool - <strong>toolsSucceeded</strong>: Number of tools that completed (1-3)</p> <h6 id="graceful-degradation-decision-tree">2.3: Graceful Degradation Decision Tree</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Tools Succeeded</th> <th>Action</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>3/3</strong></td> <td>✅ Full coverage - proceed with all results</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>2/3</strong></td> <td>⚠️ Good coverage - note which tool failed in report</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>1/3</strong></td> <td>⚠️ Basic coverage - proceed but flag limited confidence</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>0/3</strong></td> <td>❌ Retry with Vibium MCP, or document failure</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="mandatory---check-for-videos-and-trigger-pipeline">2.4: MANDATORY - Check for Videos and Trigger Pipeline</h6> <p>After reading href="#cb501-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Check scan-results.json for videos</span></span> <span id="cb501-2"><a href="#cb501-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> results <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">JSON</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">parse</span>(fs<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">readFileSync</span>(<span class="st">'/tmp/a11y-work/scan-results.json'</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb501-3"><a href="#cb501-3" aria-hidden="true" class="at">pageInfo</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">media</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">videoUrls</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">length</span> <span class="op">></span> <span class="dv">0</span>) {</span> <span id="cb501-4"><a href="#cb501-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">'=== VIDEOS DETECTED - TRIGGERING VIDEO PIPELINE ==='</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb501-5"><a href="#cb501-5" aria-hidden="true" id="step-3-context-aware-remediation-llm-powered">STEP 3: CONTEXT-AWARE REMEDIATION (LLM-POWERED)</h5> <p><strong>THIS IS WHERE CLAUDE’S INTELLIGENCE MATTERS.</strong></p> <p>Generic tools output: <code>aria-label="[DESCRIPTION]"</code> You output: <code>aria-label="Add to shopping cart"</code> because you understand context.</p> <h6 id="context-analysis-use-your-reasoning">3.1: Context Analysis (Use Your Reasoning)</h6> <p>For EACH violation, Claude must:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><p><strong>READ THE HTML CONTEXT</strong> - Don’t just see <code><button class="btn"></code>, see:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb502"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb502-1"><a href="#cb502-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span
