</tr> <tr class="even"> <td>No keyboard access</td> <td>Motor impaired, power users</td> <td>10-15%</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Missing captions</td> <td>Deaf, hard-of-hearing</td> <td>5-7%</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Flashing content</td> <td>Seizure sensitive</td> <td>0.5-1%</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Complex language</td> <td>Cognitive impairment</td> <td>10-15%</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="impact-severity-classification">4.2: Impact Severity Classification</h6> <pre><code>BLOCKS-USAGE: User cannot complete task at all - Missing form labels on required fields - Keyboard traps - Critical buttons without accessible names IMPAIRS-USAGE: User can complete task with difficulty - Low contrast (can read with effort) - Missing skip links (tedious navigation) - Incorrect heading structure (confusing) MINOR-INCONVENIENCE: Suboptimal but functional - Empty alt on decorative images - Redundant ARIA - Non-semantic HTML that works</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-5-roi-based-prioritization">STEP 5: ROI-BASED PRIORITIZATION</h5> <p>Calculate priority for each remediation:</p> <h6 id="priority-formula">5.1: Priority Formula</h6> <pre><code>PRIORITY_SCORE = (IMPACT_WEIGHT × USERS_AFFECTED) / EFFORT_HOURS Where: - IMPACT_WEIGHT: Critical=10, Serious=7, Moderate=4, Minor=1 - USERS_AFFECTED: Estimated % of users impacted - EFFORT_HOURS: Estimated fix time (0.25 to 8 hours)</code></pre> <h6 id="effort-estimation-guide">5.2: Effort Estimation Guide</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Fix Type</th> <th>Effort</th> <th>Complexity</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add aria-label</td> <td>0.25h</td> <td>Trivial</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Add alt text</td> <td>0.25h</td> <td>Trivial</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add form label</td> <td>0.5h</td> <td>Simple</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Fix color contrast</td> <td>0.5h</td> <td>Simple</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add skip links</td> <td>1h</td> <td>Simple</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Fix heading structure</td> <td>2h</td> <td>Medium</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add keyboard navigation</td> <td>4h</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Implement focus trap</td> <td>4h</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add video captions</td> <td>8h</td> <td>High</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="priority-output-format">5.3: Priority Output Format</h6> <pre><code>| Rank | Violation | Impact | Users | Effort | ROI Score | |------|-----------|--------|-------|--------|-----------| | 1 | Form labels missing | Critical | 15% | 0.5h | 300 | | 2 | Keyboard trap | Critical | 12% | 4h | 30 | | 3 | Low contrast | Serious | 10% | 0.5h | 140 | | 4 | Missing alt text | Serious | 8% | 0.25h | 224 |</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-6-production-readiness-assessment">STEP 6: PRODUCTION READINESS ASSESSMENT</h5> <h6 id="compliance-scoring">6.1: Compliance Scoring</h6> <pre><code>COMPLIANCE_SCORE = (PASSED_CRITERIA / TOTAL_CRITERIA) × 100 Production Ready if: ✓ Score ≥ 85% ✓ Zero critical violations ✓ Fewer than 3 serious violations ✓ All user journeys keyboard accessible</code></pre> <h6 id="pour-analysis-perceivable-operable-understandable-robust">6.2: POUR Analysis (Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust)</h6> <pre><code>| Principle | Guidelines | Pass | Fail | Score | |-----------|-----------|------|------|-------| | Perceivable | 1.1-1.4 | 12 | 3 | 80% | | Operable | 2.1-2.5 | 18 | 2 | 90% | | Understandable | 3.1-3.3 | 8 | 1 | 89% | | Robust | 4.1 | 4 | 1 | 80% | | **TOTAL** | | **42** | **7** | **86%** |</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-7-video-accessibility-pipeline">STEP 7: VIDEO ACCESSIBILITY PIPELINE</h5> <p><strong>Execute for EACH video detected on page.</strong></p> <h6 id="detect-and-extract-video-urls-mandatory">7.1: Detect and Extract Video URLs (MANDATORY)</h6> <p><strong>This step MUST be integrated into STEP 2 multi-tool <span class="at">-L</span> <span class="at">-A</span> <span class="st">"Mozilla/5.0"</span> <span class="at">--retry</span> 3 <span class="at">-o</span> /tmp/a11y-work/video.mp4 <span class="st">"FULL_VIDEO_URL"</span></span> <span id="cb521-6"><a href="#cb521-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb521-7"><a href="#cb521-7" aria-hidden="true" class="at">-i</span> /tmp/a11y-work/video.mp4 <span class="at">-vf</span> <span class="st">"fps=1/3"</span> <span class="at">-frames:v</span> 10 /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_%02d.jpg <span FAILS:</strong> 1. Document the failure reason in audit-summary.md 2. Still create video-captions violation in violations.json 3. Add remediation instructions WITHOUT generated captions 4. Mark video pipeline as “blocked” not “skipped”</p> <h6 id="analyze-each-frame-with-claude-vision-mandatory">7.3: Analyze Each Frame with Claude Vision (MANDATORY)</h6> <p><strong>USE THE READ TOOL ON EACH FRAME IMAGE.</strong></p> <p>Claude Code has native vision capabilities. When you Read an image file, you SEE it.</p> <pre><code>Read /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_01.jpg Read /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_02.jpg Read /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_03.jpg ... (continue for all frames)</code></pre> <p><strong>For EACH frame, describe:</strong> - <strong>SCENE</strong>: Setting, environment, lighting, location - <strong>PEOPLE</strong>: Who appears, what they’re doing, expressions, clothing - <strong>PRODUCTS</strong>: Items shown (for e-commerce: product names, colors, styles) - <strong>TEXT</strong>: Any visible text, logos, signs, prices - <strong>ACTION</strong>: Movement, transitions, what’s happening</p> <p><strong>Example output after reading frame_01.jpg:</strong></p> <pre><code>Frame 1 (0:00-0:03): A woman in white Adidas sneakers running on a forest trail. Morning light filters through trees. She wears black athletic leggings and a gray tank top. The Adidas three-stripe logo is visible on her shoes.</code></pre> <p><strong>THIS IS THE LLM VALUE.</strong> Generic tools output “[DESCRIBE CONTENT]”. You output actual descriptions because you can SEE the image.</p> <hr /> <p><strong>FALLBACK: If Read tool fails on images</strong></p> <p>Try Anthropic API directly:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb524"><pre class="sourceCode javascript"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb524-1"><a href="#cb524-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> Anthropic <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">'@anthropic-ai/sdk'</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb524-2"><a href="#cb524-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> fs <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">'fs'</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb524-3"><a class="kw">const</span> imageData <span class="op">=</span> fs<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">readFileSync</span>(<span class="st">'/tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_01.jpg'</span>)<span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb524-11"><a href="#cb524-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="dt">content</span><span class="op">:</span> [</span> <span id="cb524-12"><a class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb524-13"><a href="#cb524-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> { <span class="dt">type</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">'text'</span><span aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>LAST RESORT: Context-Based Inference (No Vision)</strong> If vision completely unavailable, infer from: - Video filename: “product-demo.mp4” → product demonstration - Page context: product page → product showcase - Surrounding text: nearby headings and descriptions</p> <p><strong>Document for each frame:</strong> - <strong>SCENE</strong>: Setting, environment, lighting - <strong>PEOPLE</strong>: Who, actions, expressions, clothing - <strong>OBJECTS</strong>: Products, props, equipment - <strong>TEXT</strong>: Visible text, logos, signs - <strong>ACTION</strong>: Movement, transitions - <strong>COLORS</strong>: Dominant colors, accessibility-relevant</p> <h6 id="generate-webvtt-captions">7.4: Generate WebVTT Captions</h6> <pre class="vtt"><code>WEBVTT Kind: captions Language: {detected-language} 00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.000 [Description from frame_01 analysis] 00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:06.000 [Description from frame_02 analysis]</code></pre> <h6 id="generate-audio-descriptions">7.5: Generate Audio Descriptions</h6> <pre class="vtt"><code>WEBVTT Kind: descriptions Language: en 00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.000 SCENE: [Detailed scene for blind users] VISUAL: [What's on screen] TEXT: [Any readable text] ACTION: [What's happening]</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-8-generate-comprehensive-reports">STEP 8: GENERATE COMPREHENSIVE REPORTS</h5> <h6 id="required-output-files">8.1: Required Output Files</h6> <p>Save ALL files to <code>docs/accessibility-scans/{page-slug}/</code>:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 37%" /> <col style="width: 62%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>File</th> <th>Contents</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>audit-summary.md</code></td> <td>Executive summary, scores, top issues, user impact</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>remediation.md</code></td> <td><strong>ALL copy-paste code fixes</strong> with context</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>violations.json</code></td> <td>Machine-readable violation data</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>implementation.md</code></td> <td>Video integration guide (if videos)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>*.vtt</code></td> <td>Caption and audio description files</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="audit-summary.md-template">8.2: audit-summary.md Template</h6> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb527"><pre class="sourceCode markdown"><code class="sourceCode markdown"><span id="cb527-1"><a href="#cb527-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu"># Accessibility Audit Report: {Site Name}</span></span> <span id="cb527-2"><a href="#cb527-2" aria-hidden="true" href="#cb527-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb527-9"><a href="#cb527-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>| Metric | Value |</span> <span id="cb527-10"><a id="nvda-windows---free">10.1: NVDA (Windows - Free)</h6> <pre><code>1. Download: https://www.nvaccess.org/download/ 2. Install and start NVDA (Ctrl+Alt+N) 3. Navigate to audited page Key Commands: - H: Jump through headings - F: Jump through form fields - B: Jump through buttons - T: Jump through tables - K: Jump through links - D: Jump through landmarks - Tab: Move through focusable elements Verify: - [ ] All headings announced with correct level - [ ] Form fields announce labels - [ ] Buttons announce purpose - [ ] Images announce alt text or "decorative" - [ ] Dynamic content changes announced (aria-live)</code></pre> <h6 id="voiceover-macos---built-in">10.2: VoiceOver (macOS - Built-in)</h6> <pre><code>1. Enable: System Preferences → Accessibility → VoiceOver 2. Toggle: Cmd+F5 3. Navigate to audited page Key Commands: - VO+U: Open rotor (headings, links, forms, landmarks) - VO+Space: Activate element - VO+Right/Left: Move through content - VO+Cmd+H: Jump to next heading Verify: - [ ] Rotor shows all headings hierarchically - [ ] Forms are navigable and labels announced - [ ] Focus order matches visual order - [ ] All content is reachable</code></pre> <h6 id="jaws-windows---commercial">10.3: JAWS (Windows - Commercial)</h6> <pre><code>1. Trial: https://www.freedomscientific.com/products/software/jaws/ 2. Start JAWS and navigate to page Key Commands: - H: Next heading - F: Next form field - B: Next button - T: Next table - Ins+F6: Heading list - Ins+F7: Link list Verify: - [ ] Virtual cursor mode works correctly - [ ] Forms mode activates in forms - [ ] All ARIA roles announced properly</code></pre> <h6 id="screen-reader-testing-checklist">10.4: Screen Reader Testing Checklist</h6> <table> <thead> Rules</h5> <h6 id="execution-rules-v7.0">Execution Rules (v7.0)</h6> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> run multi-tool scan with <strong>parallel execution</strong> (Promise.allSettled)</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> continue if at least <strong>1 of 3 tools</strong> succeeds (graceful degradation)</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> document which tools failed and why in audit-summary.md</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> use per-tool timeouts (60s/60s/90s) not global timeout</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> retry failed tools with exponential backoff before giving up</li> </ol> <h6 id="quality-rules">Quality Rules</h6> <ol start="6" type="1"> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> analyze context before generating fixes</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> include confidence scores with remediation</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> calculate user impact and ROI</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> generate copy-paste ready code</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> generate placeholder/template fixes</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> skip video pipeline if videos detected</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> complete without remediation.md</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> fail audit just because 1-2 tools failed (use graceful degradation)</li> </ol> <h5 id="gotchas">Gotchas</h5> <ul> <li>axe-core catches ~30% of WCAG issues — automated tools miss keyboard navigation, reading order, and cognitive issues</li> <li>Agent runs Lighthouse only and reports “accessible” — Lighthouse alone is insufficient, always run axe-core + pa11y too</li> <li>Screen reader testing requires actual screen reader interaction, not just ARIA attribute checks</li> <li>Video accessibility (captions, audio descriptions) is frequently skipped — check every <code><video></code> element</li> <li>Color contrast tools disagree on gradients and transparency — test with actual low-vision simulation</li> <li>Playwright+Stealth may be blocked by some sites — fall back gracefully, don’t skip the audit</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="accessibility-regression-detector">Accessibility Regression Detector</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> specialist</li> </ul> <p>Compare audits across commits to find new, fixed and regressed issues.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>accessibility-regression-detector/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-regression-detector-1">Accessibility Regression Detector</h4> <p>You detect accessibility regressions — issues previously fixed that have returned, or new issues from recent changes.</p> <h4 id="detection-modes">Detection Modes</h4> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Audit Report Comparison</strong> — Compare two audit reports, classify issues as New/Persistent/Fixed/Regressed</li> <li><strong>Git History Analysis</strong> — Scan changed files for accessibility anti-patterns</li> <li><strong>Baseline Management</strong> — Compare against <code>.a11y-baseline.json</code> known-good state</li> </ol> <h4 id="regression-classification">Regression Classification</h4> <p>Each category, with its definition and priority.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Category</th> <th>Definition</th> <th>Priority</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Regressed</td> <td>Was fixed, has returned</td> <td>Highest</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>New</td> <td>Not in previous audit</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Persistent</td> <td>Exists in both audits</td> <td>Medium</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Fixed</td> <td>Resolved since baseline</td> <td>Track</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="anti-patterns-in-diffs">Anti-Patterns in Diffs</h4> <p>Flag: <code>outline: none</code> without <code>:focus-visible</code>, div/span with click handlers, <code><img></code> without <code>alt</code>, positive <code>tabindex</code>, <code>aria-hidden</code> on focusable elements, heading level skips, missing label associations.</p> <h4 id="output-6">Output</h4> <p>Regression report with score delta, issue change counts (new/fixed/regressed/persistent), and prioritized regression list.</p> <h4 id="output-contract-78">Output contract</h4> <p>Return only JSON matching <code>skills/a11y-core/schemas/findings.schema.json</code>. No prose, no summary, no restated instructions. One object, one array of findings.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. Use when ensuring legal compliance (ADA, Section 508), testing for disabilities, or building accessible applications for 1 billion disabled users globally.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>accessibility-testing/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-testing-1">Accessibility Testing</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Consolidated</strong>: For comprehensive WCAG auditing with multi-tool testing (axe-core + pa11y + Lighthouse), video accessibility, and remediation, prefer <a href="../a11y-ally/"><code>/a11y-ally</code></a>. This skill provides a quick reference card for basic accessibility testing patterns.</p> </blockquote> <h5 id="browser-engine">Browser engine</h5> <p>Browser-driven a11y checks should go through the <strong>qe-browser</strong> fleet skill. <code>vibium a11y-tree --json</code> returns the full accessibility tree without visual rendering — feed it into axe-core via <code>vibium eval --stdin</code> for ruleset enforcement. See <code>.claude/skills/qe-browser/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <p><default_to_action> When testing accessibility or ensuring compliance: 1. APPLY POUR principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust 2. TEST with keyboard-only navigation (Tab, Enter, Escape) 3. VALIDATE with screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS) 4. CHECK color contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text) 5. AUTOMATE with axe-core, integrate in CI/CD pipeline</p> <p><strong>Quick A11y Checklist:</strong> - All images have alt text (or alt=“” for decorative) - All form fields have labels - Color is never the only indicator - Focus visible on all interactive elements - Keyboard navigation works throughout</p> <p><strong>Critical Success Factors:</strong> - Automated testing catches 30-50% of issues - Manual testing with real assistive tech required - Include users with disabilities in testing </default_to_action></p> <h5 id="quick-reference-card-1">Quick Reference Card</h5> <h6 id="when-to-use-2">When to Use</h6> <ul> <li>Legal compliance (ADA, Section 508, EU Directive)</li> <li>New feature development</li> <li>Before release validation</li> <li>Accessibility audits</li> </ul> <h6 id="wcag-2.2-levels">WCAG 2.2 Levels</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Target</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>A</strong></td> <td>Basic accessibility</td> <td>Minimum legal</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>AA</strong></td> <td>Standard (most orgs)</td> <td>Industry standard</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>AAA</strong></td> <td>Enhanced</td> <td>Specialized sites</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="pour-principles">POUR Principles</h6> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 35%" /> <col style="width: 29%" /> <col style="width: 35%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Principle</th> <th>Meaning</th> <th>Key Tests</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Perceivable</strong></td> <td>Can perceive content</td> <td>Alt text, contrast, captions</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Operable</strong></td> <td>Can operate UI</td> disabilities. Inaccessible software excludes 15% of humanity.</strong> Legal requirements: ADA, Section 508, EU Directive 2016/2102. $13T purchasing power. 250%+ increase in lawsuits.</p> <p><strong>Automated testing catches only 30-50% of issues.</strong> Combine with manual keyboard testing, screen reader testing, and real user testing with people with disabilities.</p> <p><strong>With Agents:</strong> Agents automate WCAG 2.2 compliance checking, screen reader simulation, and focus management validation. Use agents to enforce accessibility standards in CI/CD and catch violations before production.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="axe-rules">Axe Rules</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>axe-rules</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/axe-rules">skills/axe-rules</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill when configuring axe-core scans, reviewing automated accessibility test results, or writing tests that use <span class="citation" data-cites="axe-core/playwright">@axe-core/playwright</span>, <span class="citation" data-cites="axe-core/react">@axe-core/react</span>, or similar integrations. Provides a quick reference to axe 4.x rule IDs, their WCAG mapping, and default severity levels.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>axe-rules/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="axe-core-rules-reference-skill">Axe-Core Rules Reference Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/AXE_RULES_REFERENCE.md</code> and <code>examples/AXE_RULES_COVERAGE.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from those files. When in doubt, the example is authoritative. <strong>Note:</strong> the canonical files are organized around a specific test-fixture scanner project (numbered test pages). This skill re-presents the same rule set and severities as a general-purpose reference, independent of any particular fixture.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when writing, reviewing, or debugging axe-core scans.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-principle">Core Principle</h5> <p>Axe-core catches ~30–40% of WCAG issues automatically. It is the baseline, not the ceiling. Always pair automated scanning with manual keyboard and screen reader testing.</p> <p><strong>An axe-core result is evidence, not a conformance decision.</strong> Preserve the rule’s raw outcome (<code>violations</code>, <code>incomplete</code>, <code>passes</code>, <code>inapplicable</code>) exactly as axe reports it — do not overwrite or discard it when converting to a project finding. Cite this file, <code>AXE_RULES_REFERENCE.md</code>, or the rule’s own <code>dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/</code> page as the authority for a WCAG mapping; do not invent a mapping axe-core does not document for that rule. Record an unreviewed <code>violations</code> result as <code>evidence_status: automated-indicator</code> with <code>handling: review</code> — never as a confirmed standards failure — until a human confirms it. See <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html#policy-classification">Accessibility Finding Tracking: Policy Classification</a>.</p> <p><strong>Key tags to include in scans:</strong></p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb544"><pre class="sourceCode typescript"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb544-1"><a href="#cb544-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">withTags</span>([<span class="st">'wcag2a'</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">'wcag2aa'</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">'wcag21aa'</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">'wcag22aa'</span>])</span></code></pre></div> <p>Axe-core 4.11 includes 100+ automated checks across these categories: WCAG 2.0 A/AA (68 rules), WCAG 2.1 A/AA (26 rules), WCAG 2.2 A/AA (1 rule, disabled by default), Best Practices (30+ rules), WCAG AAA (3 rules, disabled by default), Experimental (9 rules, disabled by default), and Deprecated (7 rules, disabled by default).</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-axe-core">Severity Scale (axe-core)</h5> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>axe severity</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>critical</strong></td> <td>Blocks access for one or more disability groups</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>serious</strong></td> <td>Significantly impairs access</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>moderate</strong></td> <td>Creates friction; workaround exists</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <p>Disabled-by-default rules (deprecated <code>marquee</code>/<code>blink</code>/<code>audio-caption</code>) are not listed above — flag them if encountered, but they are not enabled in a default scan.</p> <p>The three WCAG AAA rules axe-core disables by default report against a level the project’s AA target does not require. <p>Automation covers ~30–40% of WCAG issues. Always pair with manual testing.</p> </blockquote> <hr /> <h5 id="references-17">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/AXE_RULES_REFERENCE.md">Full axe rules reference</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/AXE_RULES_COVERAGE.md">Axe rules coverage summary</a></li> <li><a href="https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/">axe-core rule descriptions</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core-npm/tree/develop/packages/playwright"><span class="citation" data-cites="axe-core/playwright">@axe-core/playwright</span></a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core">axe-core GitHub</a></li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> These rules target WCAG 2.2 AA. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="behavioral-a11y">Behavioral A11y</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>behavioral-a11y</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/behavioral-a11y">skills/behavioral-a11y</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill when writing, reviewing, or interpreting behavioral accessibility automation — tests that manipulate a rendered page (resizing the viewport, pressing real keys, capturing and comparing screenshots) rather than only inspecting static markup or a single computed accessibility tree. Covers Reflow risk (SC 1.4.10) and Focus Visible risk (SC 2.4.7) checks. Absolutely always report indicator results separately from confirmed failures. Under no circumstances treat a clean behavioral scan as WCAG conformance, or collapse <code>cantTell</code>/test-error/indicator outcomes into a single pass/fail signal.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>behavioral-a11y/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="behavioral-accessibility-automation-skill">Behavioral Accessibility Automation Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/BEHAVIORAL_ACCESSIBILITY_AUTOMATION.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when writing, running, or interpreting automated checks that manipulate a rendered page rather than only inspecting static markup or a single computed accessibility tree.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-15">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>A behavioral result is reported or gated as a confirmed failure without meeting the preconditions in this skill</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Indicator, <code>cantTell</code>, and confirmed-failure outcomes are collapsed into one pass/fail signal</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Fleet-scale findings are not clustered by root cause before reporting or triage</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Missing documentation of a check’s known false-positive/false-negative limitations</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-why-behavioral-checks-exist">Critical: Why Behavioral Checks Exist</h5> <p>Static analysis and single-snapshot browser rule scans (axe-core and similar) answer “is this attribute valid” or “does this element have an accessible name.” They cannot answer questions that only exist while a page is being <em>used</em>: does layout still work at a narrow viewport, does a keyboard user get a visible focus signal, does content clip when resized or spaced out, does a dynamic UI state (open menu, validation error, loading indicator) preserve the same guarantees as the initial page state.</p> <p>A behavioral check answers these by actually doing what a user would do — resizing, tabbing, hovering, waiting — and observing the result. That makes behavioral checks more expensive and more prone to environmental flakiness (animation, fonts, timing) than static checks, and it does <strong>not</strong> make them a conformance test.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-result-vocabulary">Critical: Result Vocabulary</h5> <p>Every behavioral check must use one of these result categories. Using them consistently is what keeps an automated result honest about what it actually established.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Category</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Indicator</strong></td> <td>Observed a signal correlated with a possible barrier, but did not rule out a legitimate explanation (an SC exception, intentional design, a false-positive-prone edge case). Route to human review.</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Confirmed failure</strong> (for that tested instance)</td> <td>Established every precondition needed to rule out common false-negative causes for <em>that instance</em>. Still not a full SC conformance claim.</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong><code>cantTell</code></strong></td> <td>Could not reach a reliable verdict — page did not stabilize, screenshot coverage could not be established, focus resolution hit an unsupported case. Distinct from both pass and failure.</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Test error</strong></td> <td>The check itself failed to run (navigation failure, unexpected exception) — distinct from <code>cantTell</code>, which means the page’s behavior was ambiguous, not that the check failed to execute.</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Manual review required</strong></td> <td>Categories automation does not attempt to resolve: whether an SC 1.4.10 exception legitimately applies, whether an indicator has sufficient contrast (SC 1.4.11) or size (SC 2.4.13), whether a focus order is logical.</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A clean result is not a conformance claim.</strong> A <code>no-overflow-detected</code> Reflow result means only that this check, at this viewport, on this page load, found no page-level horizontal overflow — nothing about content cut off, overlapped, or an SC 1.4.10 exception applied elsewhere. A <code>confirmed-no-visible-change</code> Focus Visible result means only that no pixel difference above the configured threshold was detected within the padded comparison region around that component, on that page load, after focus demonstrably moved to it — not an unconditional claim that no visible focus indicator exists.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-false-positives-at-site-and-fleet-scale">Critical: False Positives at Site and Fleet Scale</h5> <p>A false-positive probability that looks negligible for one target can produce frequent false alarms once the same check runs across many targets. Illustration: at a 0.5% false-positive probability per target with independent results, the chance of at least one false alarm across 200 targets is 1 − (1 − 0.005)²⁰⁰ ≈ 63%. This is an illustration of how per-target probabilities compound under an independence assumption — not a measured result, and rarely a valid assumption for real websites.</p> <p><strong>Correlation, not independence, is the normal case.</strong> Website findings are frequently correlated because pages share components, templates, stylesheets, and application shells. A single missing focus style in a shared button component can trigger the same finding on every page that uses it. <strong>Root-cause clustering is necessary</strong>: report a defect traced to one shared component as one systemic finding with N affected instances, not N unrelated defects.</p> <p><strong>False positives are not the same as flakiness.</strong> A false positive is an incorrect finding from a test that completed and produced a result. Flakiness means repeated runs against the same target produce inconsistent results — usually from timing, animation, or environment sensitivity. A false positive calls for narrowing what the check claims; flakiness calls for improving test stability (layout/visual-stability waits).</p> <p><strong>Precision must be measured, not assumed.</strong> Do not infer a precision figure from a nominal false-positive probability alone — that number is useful for reasoning about scale, not a claim about actual checks until measured against reviewed results.</p> <p><strong>Consequences:</strong> - Indicator-level results should produce reviewable evidence, not automatically block a build. - Blocking should normally be reserved for deterministic confirmed failures, reproducible regressions against a reviewed baseline, and recurrence of a previously confirmed defect. - <code>cantTell</code>, test errors, risk indicators, and reviewed exceptions remain distinct from a confirmed failure — collapsing any of them into “failure” for convenience defeats the purpose of the vocabulary above. - None of these results, individually or in aggregate, establishes WCAG conformance.</p> <p>See <code>skills/ci-cd/SKILL.md</code> for the resulting CI gating policy.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-reflow-risk-sc-1.4.10-in-detail">Serious: Reflow Risk (SC 1.4.10) in Detail</h5> <p><strong>What it does:</strong> sets a 320×720 CSS-pixel viewport, waits for layout to stabilize (<code>load</code>, <code>document.fonts.ready</code>, a quiet period with no change in <code>scrollWidth</code>/<code>scrollHeight</code>), attempts a horizontal scroll and reads the resulting scroll movement (comparing magnitude, not sign, so it works for right-to-left documents), measures <code>clientWidth</code>/<code>scrollWidth</code>, and best-effort identifies elements overflowing the viewport.</p> <p><strong>What it returns:</strong> a <code>verdict</code> of <code>no-overflow-detected</code>, <code>potential-reflow-barrier</code>, <code>cant-tell</code>, or <code>test-error</code>, plus dimensions, scroll data, and candidate overflowing elements.</p> <p><strong>What it cannot detect:</strong> - <strong>Clipped content with no scrollbar</strong> — <code>overflow: hidden</code> content that is silently truncated produces no scrollable overflow, so <code>scrollWidth</code>/<code>clientWidth</code> never diverge. This is a documented false-negative risk, not a solved case. - <strong>Whether an SC 1.4.10 exception applies</strong> — the check cannot know whether an overflowing element is a data table, map, diagram, or other component that requires two-dimensional layout for its meaning. - <strong>Delayed layout changes shorter than the configured quiet period.</strong></p> <p><strong>The SC 1.4.10 exception, precisely:</strong> it exempts <strong>parts of content that require two-dimensional layout for their usage or meaning</strong> — not the page as a whole. Normative examples: data tables, maps, diagrams, video players, games, presentations, interfaces requiring a persistently visible toolbar. Consequences a reviewer must check that automation cannot: - An excepted component does not exempt the rest of the page — headings, intro paragraphs, filters, search, and pagination around it must still reflow normally. - Within an excepted component, individual sections may still need to reflow — a table’s overall grid may need two dimensions, but a single cell’s text content does not automatically inherit that exception. - “Requires” is a meaning test, not a convenience test. A component that merely looks better in a wide fixed layout, without losing information or functionality if it reflowed, is not exempt.</p> <p>Automated overflow detection can flag a candidate. Only a human reviewer applying this test can confirm an exception.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-focus-visible-risk-sc-2.4.7-in-detail">Serious: Focus Visible Risk (SC 2.4.7) in Detail</h5> <p><strong>What it does, per Tab stop:</strong> records the active element before Tab; sends a real <code>Tab</code> key press (not a programmatic <code>.focus()</code> call, which would not exercise the same code paths); confirms focus moved and stayed in the document; resolves the deepest active element through open shadow roots; confirms the element is in the viewport; captures a screenshot of a padded region around the element’s bounding box; blurs and captures an unfocused reference of the same region; restores focus; compares the two region screenshots; repeats up to a configurable max stop count.</p> <p><strong>Why region-scoped, not whole-page, comparison:</strong> a whole-page pixel check cannot distinguish a focus indicator from an unrelated animation elsewhere on the page, and cannot distinguish “this element’s indicator disappeared” from “the previous element’s indicator disappeared while this one has none.” Region-scoped comparison, combined with tracking whole-page visual stability separately before testing begins, avoids both failure modes.</p> <p><strong>What it cannot detect:</strong> - <strong>Sufficient contrast, size, or usability of an indicator</strong> — a <code>visible-change-detected</code> verdict means pixels changed, not that they changed enough (needs contrast-tool or manual review). - <strong>Obscuration by other content</strong> — sticky headers, cookie banners, or other fixed-position content can sit on top of a real indicator; pixel comparison alone cannot detect overlap. Treat any current “pass” as silent on obscuration (SC 2.4.11) until a geometry-comparison module exists. - <strong>Cross-origin iframes</strong>, and same-origin iframes beyond a <code>cant-tell-no-coverage</code> acknowledgement. - <strong>Indicators rendered well outside the padded comparison region</strong> — a real but bounded tradeoff of region-scoped comparison; widen the padding for components known to use offset indicators. - <strong>Focus changes not driven by Tab</strong> (mouse- or script-triggered focus outside the sequential Tab order).</p> <p><strong>What a <code>confirmed-no-visible-change</code> result actually establishes:</strong> no pixel difference above the configured threshold was detected within the padded region around that component, on that page load, and all of the following held: focus demonstrably moved to it, it was applicable/rendered/ in-viewport, and the page was visually stable throughout. This is deliberately narrower than “no visible focus indicator exists” — a real indicator can still escape detection (outside the padded region, below the pixel-diff threshold, or obscured). It is also not a statement about contrast (SC 1.4.11), minimum size (SC 2.4.13), or obscuration (SC 2.4.11).</p> <p><strong>Focus order evidence:</strong> the same Tab traversal that drives this check can <em>record</em> the sequence of elements visited, but cannot judge whether that order is logical for the page’s content and task. Treat a recorded stop sequence as evidence for a human reviewer, not a verdict.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-documented-gaps-not-yet-automated">Moderate: Documented Gaps (Not Yet Automated)</h5> <p>These checks are documented as natural extensions of the Reflow/Focus Visible measurement approach but are not yet implemented as reusable modules. Do not claim automated coverage for them without saying so:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Focus obscuration</strong> (SC 2.4.11) — comparing the focused element’s bounding rectangle against sticky/fixed-position ancestors or overlapping elements.</li> <li><strong>Text resizing and clipping</strong> (SC 1.4.4 Resize Text) — same overflow/clipping signals as Reflow, but at 200% zoom rather than 320 CSS pixels. Resize Text and Reflow are distinct checks; do not conflate them (see <code>skills/manual-testing/SKILL.md</code>).</li> <li><strong>Text spacing</strong> (SC 1.4.12) — injecting the WCAG-specified user style override (line height 1.5×, paragraph spacing 2×, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em) and reusing overflow/clipping detection.</li> <li><strong>Content on hover or focus</strong> (SC 1.4.13) — verifying dismissible, hoverable, and persistent behavior of hover/focus-triggered content.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-running-these-checks-at-fleet-scale">Moderate: Running These Checks at Fleet Scale</h5> <p>Use these terms consistently when reporting or triaging results at scale:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Unique finding</strong> — one specific defect, described independently of how many pages or components it appears on.</li> <li><strong>Affected instance</strong> — one occurrence of a unique finding: one component, on one page, in one state, on one test run.</li> <li><strong>Affected page</strong> — a page containing at least one affected instance of at least one unique finding.</li> <li><strong>Probable root-cause cluster</strong> — a group of affected instances that share enough context (same component, template, stylesheet rule, generated markup pattern) that a single fix is likely to resolve all of them together. “Probable” until a reviewer confirms the shared cause.</li> </ul> <p>Raw page-level counts are not independent defects. “200 pages failed” is far less actionable than “1 unique finding (missing focus indicator on the shared header), 200 affected instances, 1 root-cause cluster.”</p> <p><strong>Suggested cadence:</strong></p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Scope</th> <th>When it runs</th> <th>Purpose</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Component fixtures</td> <td>Every pull request</td> <td>Fast, deterministic regression coverage for known patterns</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Changed pages and affected application states</td> <td>Every pull request</td> <td>Coverage matched to the actual diff</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Representative templates</td> <td>Every pull request</td> <td>Catch shared-component regressions before they reach every page using the template</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Full site or fleet inventory</td> <td>Scheduled (nightly/weekly), not every PR</td> <td>Coverage a PR-scoped run cannot afford; catches drift and pages outside the PR’s diff</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Manual review of representative findings per root-cause cluster</td> <td>After each scan producing new indicators</td> <td>Confirm or reject the cluster once, not once per affected instance</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Periodic sampling of clean (no-finding) results</td> <td>Scheduled, lower frequency</td> <td>Estimate false-negative risk</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>A check reporting no findings has not been shown to have zero false negatives — periodically sample clean results and review manually or with a different check.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-16">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />The check states its viewport, timing, and stabilization assumptions</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />The result distinguishes indicator, confirmed-for-this-instance failure, <code>cantTell</code>, and test error</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />The result includes machine-readable evidence (selector, rect, HTML excerpt) sufficient to locate the finding without re-running the check</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Documented limitations name specific false-positive and false-negative risks the check is known to have</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />The check’s own output states it does not establish WCAG conformance</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />CI integration reports indicators separately from confirmed failures and does not silently convert every indicator into a blocking failure</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />At fleet scale, findings are grouped into probable root-cause clusters and reported as unique findings with affected-instance counts, not one unrestricted item per affected page</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Blocking policy, if any, is limited to deterministic failures or reproducible regressions against a reviewed baseline — not first-seen indicators</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-15">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <ul> <li>1.4.4 Resize Text (AA) — not yet automated here; see Moderate gaps above</li> <li>1.4.10 Reflow (AA) — Reflow risk indicator</li> <li>1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA) — not yet automated here</li> <li>1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA) — not yet automated here</li> <li>2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) — Focus Visible risk indicator</li> <li>2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum (AA) — not yet automated here</li> <li>2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) — not covered by behavioral pixel comparison alone</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="references-18">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/BEHAVIORAL_ACCESSIBILITY_AUTOMATION.md">Full canonical guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/playwright/reflow-risk.mjs">Reflow risk implementation</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/playwright/focus-visible-risk.mjs">Focus Visible risk implementation</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/playwright/README.md">Playwright examples and tests</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/GOVTNZ/cwac">CWAC (GOVTNZ)</a> — this repo’s checks are independent reimplementations of CWAC’s documented method; CWAC is GPLv3, the canonical repo is MIT, no CWAC code was copied or translated</li> <li><code>skills/manual-testing/SKILL.md</code> — Reflow, zoom, and focus indicator manual testing</li> <li><code>skills/ci-cd/SKILL.md</code> — risk-indicator/build-gate CI policy</li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> These rules target WCAG 2.2 AA. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="bug-reporting">Bug Reporting</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>bug-reporting</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/bug-reporting">skills/bug-reporting</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever you are filing, reviewing, or generating accessibility bug reports — whether from automated tool output, manual testing, user reports, or testing with disabled people. The purpose of this skill is to make accessibility findings easier to report accurately, connect them to real people and tasks, and let developers reproduce, understand, and fix them without unnecessary back-and-forth. Absolutely always describe the barrier and its task impact before citing a WCAG criterion. Under no circumstances guess a disability diagnosis, treat automated tool output as a conformance conclusion, or expose secrets/personal data in a report.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>bug-reporting/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-bug-reporting-skill">Accessibility Bug Reporting Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/ACCESSIBILITY_BUG_REPORTING_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when filing, reviewing, or generating accessibility bug reports from any source — automated tool output, manual testing, user reports, or testing with disabled people.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-15">Core Mandate</h5> <p>A useful report lets another person understand the barrier, identify the people affected, reproduce it when possible, judge its impact, identify the responsible source, and verify the correction. Not every field applies to every finding — <strong>do not delay a valid report because a selector, tool rule, WCAG mapping, or code-level fix is unavailable.</strong></p> <p><strong>Principles:</strong> 1. <strong>Describe the barrier before the standard</strong> — state what task or interaction fails and under what conditions 2. <strong>Identify the people affected</strong> — describe access needs/interaction methods/AT when evidence supports it; never infer a diagnosis or imply one person represents an entire disability group 3. <strong>State the evidence basis</strong> — distinguish user reports, testing with disabled people, manual evaluation, automated results, and reasoned inference 4. <strong>Record observed facts</strong> separately from assumptions, suspected causes, and suggested fixes 5. <strong>Use complementary testing methods</strong> — automated, manual, and testing-with-disabled-people answer different questions; none substitutes for the others 6. <strong>Collect only relevant context</strong> — browser/AT/viewport/preferences matter only when they affect the result 7. <strong>Protect people and systems</strong> — remove personal data, credentials, tokens, and private content from every attachment 8. <strong>Treat tool output as evidence, not a conformance decision</strong> 9. <strong>Separate severity from priority</strong> — task impact and workaround quality inform severity; reach, frequency, deadlines, and business context inform priority 10. <strong>Fix the source when possible</strong> — a shared-component/template/token fix is usually safer than many page-specific patches 11. <strong>Close with verification evidence</strong> — a code change, automated pass, or visual check alone may not prove the user-facing barrier is gone</p> <hr /> <h5 id="terminology">Terminology</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Finding</strong></td> <td>An observed or suspected accessibility barrier or test result</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Issue</strong></td> <td>Tracked work that may contain one or more related findings</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Occurrence</strong></td> <td>One place or state in which a finding appears</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Root cause</strong></td> <td>The source producing one or more occurrences (e.g., a shared component)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Affected people</strong></td> <td>People whose task/experience is confirmed or reasonably expected to be affected — describe only as specifically as the evidence allows</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Manual accessibility evaluation</strong></td> <td>Human evaluation using relevant inputs/settings/AT — distinct from testing with disabled people</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Testing with disabled people</strong></td> <td>Disabled participants using representative tasks, providing evidence from lived experience</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Conformance conclusion</strong></td> <td>A conclusion about a defined scope, standard, level, and evaluation method</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A failed automated rule does not automatically prove a WCAG failure. A passed automated rule does not prove conformance.</strong> Confirm the result and its scope before making a conformance claim.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-16">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Severity</th> <th>Definition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Blocker</strong></td> <td>A core task cannot be completed, or there’s a serious safety/privacy/data-loss risk, with no reasonable workaround</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Major</strong></td> <td>A task fails, is unreliable, or requires a substantial workaround</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>The task remains possible but requires significant extra effort or assistance</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Localized friction without material task loss</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Needs review</strong></td> <td>The result or impact has not been confirmed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>This is an example scale, not a universal standard — calibrate locally with disabled people and product teams, and document local definitions.</p> <p><strong>Severity, priority, reach, frequency, and confidence answer different questions</strong> — do not conflate them:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Field</th> <th>Question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Severity</td> <td>How serious is the task-level consequence in <em>this</em> occurrence?</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Priority</td> <td>When should the team address it?</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Reach</td> <td>How many people/pages/components may be affected?</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Frequency</td> <td>How often does the occurrence appear?</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Confidence</td> <td>How certain is the finding/impact/cause understanding?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Frequency and reach can increase priority, but they do not change the severity of one occurrence</strong> — do not automatically escalate a low-severity issue to higher severity just because it appears on many pages; record that as a priority factor instead.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-minimum-information-for-a-useful-report">Critical: Minimum Information for a Useful Report</h5> <p>A report can be <strong>valid at intake without being ready for remediation</strong> — these are different bars. Do not reject a report from a user for lacking technical detail; a triager collects locators, standards mapping, and a verification plan afterward. See <a href="#actionable-findings-and-repeatability">Actionable Findings and Repeatability</a> below for the full stage model.</p> <p><strong>Valid intake</strong> needs only: title, location/state (as precisely as the reporter can safely give), task and impact, actual result, evidence basis.</p> <p><strong>Additional fields for evaluation and remediation</strong> — collected by triage, not required from the reporter:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Field</th> <th>What to record</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Title</td> <td>Component/location, failure, and task effect</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Location and state</td> <td>Safe URL/route, component name, build, and the state in which the problem appears</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>People affected</td> <td>Access needs/interaction methods/AT confirmed or likely affected; more than one group when relevant</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Evidence basis and confidence</td> <td>User report / testing with disabled people / manual evaluation / automated result / reasoned inference, plus uncertainty</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Task and impact</td> <td>What the person is trying to do, how the barrier affects it, workaround quality/cost</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Steps or conditions</td> <td>The shortest reliable path, including preconditions</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Expected result</td> <td>The user-facing behavior that should occur</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Actual result</td> <td>What was observed, including relevant AT output</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Environment</td> <td>Only the browser/OS/AT/input/viewport/zoom/preferences/locale that affect the result</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Evidence</td> <td>A small redacted excerpt or accessible attachment when it helps</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-write-a-specific-title">Critical: Write a Specific Title</h5> <p>Identify the component, failure, and consequence.</p> <p><strong>Good:</strong> <code>Checkout: card error text is not associated with the field</code> / <code>Account menu: keyboard focus moves behind the open dialog</code></p> <p><strong>Avoid:</strong> <code>Accessibility issue</code>, <code>Screen reader bug</code>, <code>WCAG failure</code> — these don’t identify the affected behavior. Including a WCAG criterion in the title is optional; the report should stay understandable to someone who doesn’t know the criterion number.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-record-location-and-state-safely">Critical: Record Location and State Safely</h5> <pre class="text"><code>Page or route: /checkout/payment Build or commit: 2026.07.18.2 Component: Payment form UI state: Form submitted with an invalid card number Account role: Test customer</code></pre> <p>Use an exact URL only when its query/fragment values are relevant AND safe to share. <strong>Remove or replace session identifiers, access tokens, email addresses, names, account numbers, and other secrets/personal data:</strong></p> <pre class="text"><code>Unsafe: https://example.com/orders/847291?token=secret-value Safe: https://example.com/orders/[test-order-id]</code></pre> <p>Never include production credentials — provide an approved test account through the organization’s secure process.</p> <p><strong>Element locators:</strong> start with a human-readable component name and location; add a stable technical locator if it helps (<code>[data-component="cookie-settings"] [data-action="close"]</code>, a tool-native selector, an accessibility-tree path, a test ID, or a short XPath). <strong>A full absolute DOM XPath should not be mandatory</strong> — absolute paths are brittle when wrappers, list positions, or generated markup change. If no reliable locator exists, describe the visible label, accessible name, role, nearby heading, and interaction state instead. Record iframe/shadow-root boundaries when relevant.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-preconditions-and-steps-to-reproduce">Critical: Preconditions and Steps to Reproduce</h5> <p>List only the steps needed to reach the failure, including input method and AT command when they matter:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Preconditions: - Signed in as a test customer - Cart contains one item - NVDA is running with Firefox Steps: 1. Open the checkout payment step. 2. Leave the card number empty. 3. Move to the Submit order button with Tab. 4. Activate the button with Enter. 5. Listen for feedback without moving focus.</code></pre> <p>For intermittent findings, record how many attempts reproduced it, timing/ network/loading conditions, and the earliest known build. <strong>“Cannot reproduce” is a triage state, not evidence the report is invalid</strong> — preserve the original conditions.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-separate-expected-and-actual-results">Critical: Separate Expected and Actual Results</h5> <p>Write expected behavior as an <strong>outcome</strong>, not a required implementation:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Expected: After submission, the card number error is associated with the field. When focus moves to the field, its label, invalid state, and error are available. Actual: The visible error appears, but the card number field has no programmatic error association. When focus moves to the field, NVDA announces only its label.</code></pre> <p>Avoid putting a specific ARIA attribute or JS method in the expected result unless the product contract requires that implementation — put possible code changes under “Suggested fix” instead.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-identify-people-affected-never-guess-a-diagnosis">Critical: Identify People Affected — Never Guess a Diagnosis</h5> <p>Connect the barrier to people and a task, not only to a technical defect or tool rule. Describe people in terms of access needs/interaction methods/AT <strong>when evidence supports it</strong> — do not guess a diagnosis, require disclosure of one, or imply every person in a disability group has the same experience.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Evidence status</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Reported or confirmed by affected people</strong></td> <td>A disabled person reported it, or it was observed while disabled participants performed the task</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Observed through manual evaluation</strong></td> <td>An evaluator reproduced it using the relevant method/setting/AT — evidence of behavior, not equivalent to testing with disabled people</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Likely</strong></td> <td>Affected population and impact reasonably inferred but not confirmed with affected people</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Unknown or needs review</strong></td> <td>From automation or technical inspection; user impact not yet established</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Useful:</strong> “People who use screen readers are likely to be affected, including some blind and low-vision people. Manual evaluation with NVDA and Firefox found that submission failure was not announced. The impact has not yet been confirmed through testing with disabled participants.”</p> <p><strong>Not useful:</strong> “This affects blind people and violates WCAG.”</p> <p>A report can identify more than one affected population — avoid assuming a one-to-one relationship between a WCAG criterion or automated rule and a disability group.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-record-only-the-relevant-environment">Serious: Record Only the Relevant Environment</h5> <p>An environment list is useful only when it describes conditions that produced the result — <strong>do not paste a generic browser/AT matrix into every issue</strong>:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Test date and time: 2026-07-18 14:30 EDT Browser: Firefox 140 Operating system: Windows 11 24H2 Assistive technology: NVDA 2026.1 Input: Keyboard Viewport: 1280 by 720 CSS pixels Zoom or text size: 200% text size Color scheme: Dark Forced colors: Active prefers-reduced-motion: reduce prefers-contrast: more Locale and language: en-CA</code></pre> <p>Use the value actually tested — <strong>do not infer a device type from a viewport-width breakpoint</strong>; viewport, input capability, browser, OS, and physical device are separate facts. Relevant CSS preference values: <code>prefers-color-scheme</code> (light/dark), <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> (reduce/no-preference), <code>prefers-contrast</code> (more/less/custom/no-preference), <code>forced-colors</code> (active/none).</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-add-technical-evidence-without-exposing-data">Serious: Add Technical Evidence Without Exposing Data</h5> <p>Technical evidence is optional when the observed behavior is already clear. Automated and technical findings normally need a focused HTML/DOM/ accessibility-tree/component excerpt before code-level remediation — <strong>triage collects this, not the reporter.</strong> A disabled person or other reporter may not know how to capture it, and requiring it before accepting a report excludes exactly the people best placed to notice a barrier. Don’t assume source HTML represents the live DOM or accessibility tree — client rendering and hydration can make them diverge; capture live-DOM/ accessibility-tree output when the finding depends on runtime state.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb552"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb552-1"><a href="#cb552-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><label</span> <span class="er">for</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"card-number"</span><span class="kw">></span>Card number<span class="kw"></label></span></span> <span id="cb552-2"><a href="#cb552-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><input</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"card-number"</span> <span class="er">name</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"card-number"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb552-3"><a href="#cb552-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"card-number-error"</span><span class="kw">></span>Enter a card number.<span class="kw"></p></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Explain what the excerpt demonstrates — here, the visible error isn’t programmatically associated with the field. Do not assume an excerpt shows the entire computed accessibility tree.</p> <p><strong>Before sharing HTML, DOM snapshots, logs, or screenshots, remove:</strong> tokens/ cookies/hidden credentials; names/addresses/account data; private form field values; unnecessary internal URLs or IDs. For screenshots/recordings: describe the relevant content in the issue text; use arrows/markers plus text, not color alone; provide captions/transcripts for video/audio; crop or redact faces/names/private content.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-standards-rules-and-test-results">Serious: Standards, Rules, and Test Results</h5> <p><strong>WCAG mapping</strong> — record the exact version, criterion, and level when known; use <code>suspected</code>/<code>needs review</code> when uncertain; don’t add criteria merely because a tool lists them as tags:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Standard: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships Level: A Relationship: Confirmed failure</code></pre> <p><strong>Tool/rule information</strong> for automated results:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Tool and version: axe-core 4.9.1 Rule ID and version: button-name Configuration: wcag2a, wcag2aa tags Test method: Automated Raw outcome: failed Human review: Confirmed / Rejected / Needs review</code></pre> <p>Keep a tool’s impact/confidence value separate from the project’s severity — tool metadata is a heuristic, not the task/context/workaround/root-cause assessment. <strong>If using ACT Rules Format 1.1, preserve one of its outcomes</strong> (<code>inapplicable</code>, <code>passed</code>, <code>failed</code>, <code>cantTell</code>, <code>untested</code>) — send <code>cantTell</code> results for human review; a <code>passed</code>/<code>inapplicable</code> result may still need other tests before a WCAG conclusion.</p> <p><strong>Obligation and handling are separate from the WCAG mapping.</strong> Assign them per standards mapping, not by inference from severity or lifecycle status:</p> <ul> <li><code>obligation</code>: <code>required</code> | <code>aspirational</code> | <code>advisory</code> | <code>unmapped</code> | <code>not-applicable</code>. <strong>A confirmed AAA finding under an AA baseline target is <code>aspirational</code>, not <code>advisory</code></strong> — record it as a visible stretch goal, not an arbitrary suggestion. A project may elevate a specific AAA criterion to <code>required</code>; cite the local policy or authority in <code>obligation_basis</code> when it does. Do not describe satisfying individual AAA criteria as WCAG AAA conformance.</li> <li><code>handling</code>: <code>report</code> | <code>review</code> | <code>suppress</code>. <strong>Send an unresolved automated indicator to <code>review</code>, never straight to <code>report</code> as a confirmed failure or to <code>suppress</code>.</strong> <code>suppress</code> requires a documented exception — narrow scope, reason, evidence, owner, and a review or expiry date — and never means the finding is resolved or deleted.</li> </ul> <p>See <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html#policy-classification">Accessibility Finding Tracking: Policy Classification</a> for the full definitions and worked examples.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-plan-complementary-testing-and-verification">Serious: Plan Complementary Testing and Verification</h5> <p>Automated testing, manual evaluation, and testing with disabled people answer different questions — state which methods are required, why, and their limits.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Automated:</strong> identifies machine-testable patterns and gives repeatable regression coverage; cannot determine full user impact, usability, or conformance. Preserve raw result/config; require human review before treating as a confirmed user-facing barrier; don’t treat an automated pass as sufficient closure evidence.</li> <li><strong>Manual accessibility evaluation:</strong> required when the result depends on human judgment or interaction — keyboard operation, focus, screen reader output, zoom/reflow, forced colors, labels/errors/status messages, and relevant states. Test a risk-based set of environments, not every combination for every issue.</li> <li><strong>Testing with disabled people:</strong> examines real tasks and lived interaction; can find barriers standards-based evaluation misses. Plan it when: the task is critical (authentication, payment, health, safety, public services); the barrier/fix has major or uncertain impact; the component is complex/novel; workaround quality is unclear; reports from disabled people conflict with technical results. Do not use disabled participants to rediscover obvious known failures that should be fixed first. One participant confirms that person’s experience — don’t treat them as representative of an entire disability group. This does not replace standards-based evaluation, and standards-based evaluation doesn’t replace learning directly from disabled people.</li> </ul> <p>Record a verification plan: automated checks required/planned/completed; manual checks required/planned/completed; relevant supported environments; testing with disabled people required/planned/completed with rationale.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-record-scope-frequency-and-root-cause">Moderate: Record Scope, Frequency, and Root Cause</h5> <pre class="text"><code>Observed occurrences: 7 Pages checked: 12 Pages affected: 5 States checked: Default, error, disabled Likely source: Shared address form component Unchecked scope: Mobile app and authenticated administrator flow</code></pre> <p>Don’t extrapolate from a sample without saying it’s an estimate — a sitewide template defect and seven unrelated content errors may share a count but need different work. <strong>Group findings conservatively</strong> — combine occurrences only when they share the same remediation unit or confirmed root cause; don’t merge findings merely because they share a rule ID or similar selector.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="suggested-fixes-and-acceptance-criteria">Suggested Fixes and Acceptance Criteria</h5> <p>A suggested fix is optional — label it as a proposal; the responsible team may know a safer source-level correction:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Suggested fix: Associate the error message with the field and expose the invalid state after validation.</code></pre> <p>Acceptance criteria should describe <strong>verifiable user-facing behavior</strong>, not just an attribute/selector/automated-rule result:</p> <pre class="text"><code>- Submitting the empty field identifies the card number error in text. - The field exposes the error association and invalid state programmatically. - Keyboard focus remains predictable. - The original interaction is manually retested. - Testing with disabled people is completed when required by the verification plan.</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="markdown-issue-template">Markdown Issue Template</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb558"><pre class="sourceCode analysis. This JSON format is optional — it must not require fields that don’t exist for manual or user-reported findings.</p> <p>The canonical, versioned, schema-validated format is <code>schema_version: "2.0"</code> or <code>"2.1"</code> (JSON Schema Draft 2020-12), defined in <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/schemas/README.html">examples/schemas/</a> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code>. <strong>Do not use <code>schema_version: "1.1"</code></strong> — that was an illustrative shape from an earlier draft of this skill and has been replaced. <code>"2.1"</code> adds an optional top-level <code>policy</code> object (<code>standards_obligations</code>, <code>handling</code>, <code>evidence_status</code>, <code>suppression</code>) for the obligation/handling classification above; a <code>"2.0"</code> record must not populate it. <code>policy</code> is never fingerprint identity and never alters <code>tracking.fingerprints</code>.
