correlated findings — see the <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/schemas/accessibility-finding-v2.example.json">complete example</a>, <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/schemas/accessibility-finding-v2-minimal.example.json">minimal example</a> for a finding with none of them, and the <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/schemas/accessibility-finding-v2.1-policy-examples.json">policy-classification examples</a> for eight worked <code>obligation</code>/<code>handling</code>/<code>evidence_status</code> scenarios. Do not compute a fingerprint by hand or duplicate the fingerprint algorithm here; see <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/fingerprints/README.html">Fingerprint Profiles</a> for the frozen, versioned <code>a11y/pattern/v1</code> / <code>a11y/occurrence/v1</code> contracts. A published fingerprint profile is immutable — an algorithm change requires a new profile version, never an in-place edit.</p> <p>Validate imports against the published schema; document null/omitted values per the schema’s own convention; plan migrations using the <code>equivalent</code> / <code>split</code> / <code>merged</code> / <code>unresolved</code> vocabulary in <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html">Accessibility Finding Tracking</a>. Preserve a tool’s raw output separately when exact round-trip fidelity matters (<code>source.raw_result_reference</code> / <code>evidence.references</code>).</p> <hr /> <h5 id="automation-and-ai-guardrails">Automation and AI Guardrails</h5> <p>Automation can collect and organize evidence — it should <strong>not invent certainty, affected populations, or lived experience.</strong></p> <p>An automated/AI-assisted workflow should: 1. Preserve the raw result, tool/rule version, config, time, and tested URL/route 2. Label the method: automated / semi-automated / manual / user-reported / testing with disabled people 3. Retain the tool’s original outcome; route <code>cantTell</code>/uncertain results to a review queue 4. Remove credentials and personal data before sending evidence to another system 5. <strong>Avoid generating a WCAG mapping, affected population, impact statement, severity, or root cause when the evidence doesn’t support it</strong> 6. Distinguish confirmed participant evidence from manual observation and reasoned inference 7. Require human validation per the project’s risk/triage rules before creating high-impact work or conformance claims 8. Group occurrences only when the remediation unit or root cause is sufficiently established 9. Update an existing issue with new occurrences instead of silently discarding duplicates 10. Preserve disagreements between a tool result, evaluator review, and participant feedback 11. Require manual user-facing retesting before closure when automation can’t verify the outcome 12. Record whether testing with disabled people is required/planned/completed with rationale 13. <strong>Never claim testing with disabled people occurred unless it actually did</strong> 14. Route each automated result to the active remediation queue, the investigation queue, or observation history — never place a raw, unreproduced automated result directly into active remediation 15. <strong>Never automatically reject a credible user-reported or potentially high-consequence barrier just because an internal rerun didn’t reproduce it</strong> — route it to bounded investigation instead 16. <strong>Record an unreviewed automated result as <code>evidence_status: automated-indicator</code> with <code>handling: review</code></strong> — never as <code>confirmed-standards-failure</code>, <code>confirmed-user-facing-barrier</code>, or <code>handling: suppress</code>, until a human confirms it. Do not disable an entire rule or engine because one target produces noise; suppress the specific, scoped finding instead.</p> <p>Do not close an issue only because the original automated rule passes — the implementation may have changed the selector, hidden the tested node, or introduced a different barrier.</p> <h5 id="actionable-findings-and-repeatability">Actionable Findings and Repeatability</h5> <p>A finding can be valid and worth preserving before the team has enough evidence to act on it. Use three destinations, not one undifferentiated queue:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Active remediation queue</strong> — reproducible, or otherwise sufficiently evidenced: precise safe location, technical evidence where applicable, owner, acceptance criteria, verification plan. WCAG mapping, severity, frequency, and fingerprint are useful but not prerequisites.</li> <li><strong>Investigation queue</strong> — credible but intermittent/insufficiently evidenced: must have an owner, current evidence, next action, evidence needed for promotion, and a review/expiry date. Don’t let an unowned <code>needs_review</code> finding sit indefinitely.</li> <li><strong>Observation history</strong> — compact, retention-bounded evidence for unreproduced automated results (fingerprints, location, tool/rule identity, scan run ID, first/last-seen, reason not promoted). Not the active human issue queue.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated-finding actionability gate</strong> — before an automated result enters active remediation, ask: <em>can the team locate the result, rerun or evaluate the check, inspect the affected output, and determine what would demonstrate correction?</em> If not, route it to investigation or observation history instead of creating an issue nobody can act on. This gate is about automated-finding volume; it does not add a reproduction or evidence requirement before accepting a human-reported finding as valid.</p> <p><strong>Comparable runs and <code>not_observed</code> vs. <code>not_tested</code>:</strong> a missing result is only meaningful when the rerun is genuinely comparable (same resource, successful load, required auth/state reached, same rule, scanner completed, no material exclusion change). Classify a timeout, auth failure, disabled rule, or incomplete crawl as <code>not_tested</code> — never as absence. Classify a genuine absence after a comparable run as <code>not_observed</code>, never silently as <code>resolved</code>.</p> <p><strong>Direct reproduction is preferred; equivalent evidence is accepted</strong> when exact reproduction isn’t possible — a focused HTML/DOM/accessibility-tree excerpt, tool output with config/version, a recording with explanation, repeated reports, or documented reproduction attempts. <code>Cannot reproduce</code> describes the team’s current evidence, not the reporter’s credibility.</p> <p>Don’t retain findings without a plan: an investigation item with no owner and no review date is functionally a discarded report.</p> <p>For the full stage model, the three destinations, the actionability gate, comparable-run rules, and aggressive-filtering consequences/exceptions, see <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html#actionability-valid-report-vs-ready-for-remediation">Accessibility Finding Tracking § Actionability</a> in the canonical repository. Do not restate the stage-promotion thresholds or fingerprint algorithm here; link to them.</p> <p><strong>Deduplication and tracking:</strong> a <strong>tracker ID</strong> (the issue tracker’s own ID) is the durable identity of tracked remediation work — it is assigned by a human filing or linking an issue, never computed from finding content. A <strong>scan request ID</strong> identifies why a scan ran; it is not automatically a tracker ID for every finding the scan produces. A fingerprint (an <strong>occurrence fingerprint</strong> for one location, or a <strong>pattern fingerprint</strong> for a correlation candidate across locations) can help correlate repeated results, but is a computed correlation key, not a permanent bug ID — a matching fingerprint supports grouping and investigation, it does not by itself prove a shared root cause. A short <strong>display ID</strong> derived from a fingerprint (e.g. <code>A11Y-PAT-EA3B846C4F12</code>) is a human-readable alias, never the authoritative value. If fingerprints are used: version the algorithm and profile. Record tool and rule versions as provenance; include them in fingerprint identity only when the applicable frozen fingerprint profile explicitly requires it. Normalize URLs/selectors carefully; expect fingerprints to change only within a new profile version, never silently; retain legacy identifiers when a fingerprint algorithm changes; do not infer mobile/desktop from a width threshold; don’t merge results solely because hashes match. Absence from a later scan does not by itself prove resolution — treat it as <code>not_observed</code> unless the scope was actually retested or otherwise verified.</p> <p>For the full model — including scan run IDs, legacy identifier migration, and the frozen <code>a11y/pattern/v1</code> / <code>a11y/occurrence/v1</code> fingerprint profiles with published test vectors — see <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html">Accessibility Finding Tracking</a> and <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/fingerprints/README.html">Fingerprint Profiles</a> in the canonical repository. Do not restate the fingerprint algorithm here; link to it.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="finding-lifecycle">Finding Lifecycle</h5> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Capture:</strong> record barrier, location, state, people affected, impact, evidence basis, safe evidence</li> <li><strong>Triage:</strong> confirm the result when possible, identify missing context, separate severity from priority</li> <li><strong>Isolate:</strong> find the source component/template/token/process producing the occurrences</li> <li><strong>Assign:</strong> an owner who can change the source, not just the individual page</li> <li><strong>Define:</strong> agree on user-facing acceptance criteria, supported environments, verification plan</li> <li><strong>Correct:</strong> fix the source; update docs/examples/content guidance</li> <li><strong>Prevent:</strong> add proportionate regression coverage</li> <li><strong>Retest:</strong> repeat the original interaction and relevant adjacent states/preferences/environments</li> <li><strong>Evaluate with disabled people:</strong> complete planned participant testing where required</li> <li><strong>Close:</strong> record what changed, verification evidence, remaining limitations, follow-up</li> </ol> <p>If a fix is partial, record the remaining occurrences/environments rather than closing the broader issue as complete.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="reporting-to-external-organizations">Reporting to External Organizations</h5> <p>Look first for an accessibility statement, <code>accessibility@</code> contact, or feedback form. Write for the person receiving the report, who may not be an accessibility specialist. Lead with the page/feature, the barrier observed, affected people/methods if known and safe to share, the task it prevents, concise steps and environment, and a request for acknowledgement. WCAG references and suggested fixes are optional. Do not include passwords, personal information, or sensitive documents — and don’t require a reporter to disclose a diagnosis. There is no universal response deadline; appropriate follow-up depends on the organization/contract/jurisdiction (this is not legal advice).</p> <pre class="text"><code>Subject: Accessibility barrier in [page or feature] Hello, I encountered an accessibility barrier in [page or feature]. Location: [safe URL, route, or feature name] Task: [what you were trying to do] Barrier: [what happened] People or interaction methods affected, if known: [description] Impact: [how this affected the task] Steps or conditions: 1. [Step] Expected: [user-facing outcome] Actual: [observed result] Relevant environment: [only details that affect the result] WCAG reference, if known: [version, criterion, and level] Please acknowledge this report and let me know how I can follow its status. Thank you.</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="common-reporting-failures">Common Reporting Failures</h5> <ul> <li>Requiring a full DOM XPath, HTML excerpt, tool rule, or WCAG criterion before accepting a report</li> <li>Copying an exact URL that contains a token or personal data</li> <li>Reporting only “fails WCAG” without describing the user-facing behavior</li> <li>Inferring a disability group or population-wide impact from a WCAG criterion or tool rule</li> <li>Treating a tool result as a confirmed defect or a conformance conclusion</li> <li>Treating an evaluator’s use of assistive technology as equivalent to testing with disabled people</li> <li><strong>Assigning severity from a tool’s impact field, or automatically increasing severity by occurrence count</strong> (that’s a priority signal, not severity)</li> <li>Claiming a viewport width proves the physical device type</li> <li>Listing every AT version instead of the environment actually tested</li> <li>Merging unrelated occurrences because the rule ID or selector looks similar</li> <li>Prescribing a code change without behavior-based acceptance criteria</li> <li>Skipping manual testing because an automated check passes</li> <li>Closing after a code merge or automated pass without repeating the original interaction</li> <li>Using disabled participants to rediscover known basic failures that should have been corrected first</li> <li>Generalizing one participant’s experience to an entire disability group</li> <li>Disclosing a reporter’s or participant’s diagnosis, identity, or private content without informed permission</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="pre-filing-quality-checklist">Pre-Filing Quality Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Location and state recorded with secrets/tokens/personal data removed from URLs</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Title identifies component, failure, and task effect (not “Accessibility issue”)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Steps to reproduce are numbered, minimal, and complete</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Expected and actual results stated as user-facing outcomes, not implementation prescriptions</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />People affected described only as specifically as the evidence allows — no guessed diagnosis</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Evidence basis and confidence level stated (user report / testing with disabled people / manual / automated / inference)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Only relevant environment fields recorded — not a generic browser/AT matrix</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Technical evidence (HTML/screenshots/logs) redacted of secrets and personal data</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />WCAG mapping marked confirmed/suspected/needs review as appropriate</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Severity assigned from task impact — not from tool output or occurrence count</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Frequency/reach recorded separately as a priority factor, not folded into severity</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Verification plan states which of automated/manual/disabled-people testing is required and why</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Findings grouped only when remediation unit or root cause is confirmed shared</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="commonly-violated-wcag-criteria">Commonly Violated WCAG Criteria</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> <col style="width: 25%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>SC</th> <th>Name</th> <th>Level</th> <th>Common Violations</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>1.1.1</td> <td>Non-text Content</td> <td>A</td> <td>Missing <code>alt</code> on images, unlabelled icon buttons</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>1.3.1</td> <td>Info and Relationships</td> <td>A</td> <td>Unsemantic heading structure, missing form labels</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>1.3.3</td> <td>Sensory Characteristics</td> <td>A</td> <td>Instructions relying on shape, colour, or position only</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>1.4.1</td> <td>Use of Color</td> <td>A</td> <td>Status conveyed by colour alone</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>1.4.3</td> <td>Contrast Minimum</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Text below 4.5:1 contrast ratio</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>1.4.4</td> <td>Resize Text</td> <td>AA</td> <td>Page breaks at 200% zoom</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>ci-accessibility</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> guidance</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/ci-accessibility">skills/ci-accessibility</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> specialist</li> </ul> <p>Set up and debug accessibility CI: baselines, SARIF and PR gating.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>ci-accessibility/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="ci-accessibility-agent">CI Accessibility Agent</h4> <p>You are a CI/CD accessibility specialist. You help teams set up, maintain, and troubleshoot automated accessibility scanning in their continuous integration pipelines.</p> <h4 id="your-scope-18">Your Scope</h4> <ul> <li><strong>Set up new pipelines</strong> — Generate CI config files for accessibility scanning</li> <li><strong>Manage baselines</strong> — Create and update <code>axe-baseline.json</code> files that track known violations so CI only fails on regressions</li> <li><strong>Configure thresholds</strong> — Set which severity levels block deploys vs. warn</li> <li><strong>SARIF integration</strong> — Configure output for GitHub code scanning (inline annotations in PR diffs)</li> <li><strong>PR annotations</strong> — Post accessibility summaries as PR comments with pass/fail verdicts</li> <li><strong>Troubleshoot failures</strong> — Diagnose why CI accessibility checks are failing and recommend fixes</li> <li><strong>Multi-platform</strong> — GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="phase-1-assess-current-state">Phase 1 — Assess Current State</h4> <ol type="1"> <li>Check for existing CI configuration files (<code>.github/workflows/</code>, <code>azure-pipelines.yml</code>, <code>.gitlab-ci.yml</code>, <code>Jenkinsfile</code>, <code>.circleci/config.yml</code>)</li> <li>Check for existing accessibility tooling (<code>package.json</code> for <code>@axe-core/cli</code>, <code>pa11y</code>, <code>lighthouse</code>)</li> <li>Check for existing baseline files (<code>axe-baseline.json</code>, <code>.a11y-cache.json</code>)</li> <li>Check for scan configuration (<code>.a11y-web-config.json</code>)</li> </ol> <h4 id="phase-2-configure-pipeline">Phase 2 — Configure Pipeline</h4> <p>Ask the user about:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>CI platform</strong> — GitHub Actions (recommended), Azure DevOps, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, generic shell</li> <li><strong>Scanning tool</strong> — axe-core CLI (fast, reliable), Playwright + axe-core (SPAs, auth pages), Lighthouse CI (includes perf/SEO)</li> <li><strong>Gating strategy:</strong> <ul> <li><strong>Strict</strong> — fail on any new violation</li> <li><strong>Standard</strong> — fail on critical/serious only (recommended)</li> <li><strong>Baseline</strong> — fail only when violation count increases (best for brownfield)</li> </ul></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> <ul> <li>SARIF upload to GitHub code scanning</li> <li>PR comment with summary</li> <li>Build artifact with full report</li> <li>Webhook notification (Slack, Teams)</li> </ul></li> </ol> <h4 id="phase-3-generate-configuration">Phase 3 — Generate Configuration</h4> <p>Generate the appropriate CI config with:</p> <ul> <li>axe-core scan targeting WCAG 2.2 AA tags (<code>wcag2a,wcag2aa,wcag21a,wcag21aa,wcag22aa</code>)</li> <li>HTML file discovery from PR changed files</li> <li>Baseline comparison when baseline file exists</li> <li>SARIF output for GitHub code scanning</li> <li>Clear pass/fail job summary</li> </ul> <h4 id="phase-4-baseline-management">Phase 4 — Baseline Management</h4> <p>The baseline pattern is critical for brownfield adoption:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Create baseline</strong> — Run axe-core, capture all current violations as <code>axe-baseline.json</code></li> <li><strong>CI comparison</strong> — On each PR, run axe-core and compare against baseline</li> <li><strong>Fail on regression</strong> — If new violations appear (not in baseline), fail the PR</li> <li><strong>Allow gradual fix</strong> — Violations in the baseline don’t block. Teams fix them over time.</li> <li><strong>Update baseline</strong> — After fixing issues, regenerate baseline to lock in improvements</li> </ol> <h4 id="phase-5-verify-and-document">Phase 5 — Verify and Document</h4> <ol type="1"> <li>Run the pipeline in a test PR to verify it works</li> <li>Generate a README section explaining the pipeline for the team</li> <li>Offer to set up scheduled full-site scans (weekly/monthly)</li> </ol> <h4 id="output-contract-79">Output contract</h4> <p>Answer the question. Keep the answer to what was asked, cite the criterion or API by name, and stop. Do not append a checklist that was not requested.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. Authoritative specifications for this skill: <code>skills/a11y-core/references/sources.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="ci-cd">CI CD</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>ci-cd</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/ci-cd">skills/ci-cd</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill when configuring or reviewing CI/CD pipelines, GitHub Actions workflows, or automated testing setups. Ensures accessibility regressions are caught before code reaches production by enforcing quality gates, structured reporting, and layered automated + manual testing across all pages and user preferences.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>ci-cd/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="cicd-accessibility-skill">CI/CD Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/CI_CD_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative. The canonical guide states synchronization with this skill is <strong>not automatic</strong> — re-check this file against canonical periodically.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when adding, reviewing, or maintaining CI/CD accessibility checks.</p> <p>For guidance on when to use AI skills versus automated scanners during audits, see <code>AI_AUDIT_GUIDE.md</code> in this repository.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-16">Core Mandate</h5> <p>CI can prevent known accessibility regressions, preserve tested semantics, and produce evidence for human review. <strong>It cannot establish WCAG conformance by itself.</strong> Automated rules, scores, snapshots, and AI output are inputs to an accessibility evaluation, not substitutes for one. This guide targets WCAG 2.2 AA for in-scope content — that target is not itself a conformance claim. A confirmed AAA-level finding under this AA target is <code>obligation: aspirational</code> by default (a visible, non-blocking stretch goal), not <code>advisory</code>, unless a project explicitly elevates that specific criterion to <code>required</code>.</p> <p>Principles: test complete user tasks and relevant states, not only page loads; run fast deterministic checks locally and repeat in CI; block known regressions using explicit reviewable rules; keep accessibility, performance, security, and functional signals distinct; test the final rendered/sanitized/ optimized output; keep humans responsible for severity, alternatives, exceptions, and release decisions; give workflows and agents the least authority needed for their task.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-17">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>A core or safety-critical task cannot be completed and no reasonable accessible alternative exists</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>A major task is blocked or requires an unsafe, unreliable, or highly burdensome workaround</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>A task remains possible but creates substantial difficulty, confusion, delay, or loss of information</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Impact is limited and the task remains understandable and operable</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Tool labels (axe <code>critical</code>/<code>serious</code>/<code>moderate</code>/<code>minor</code>, Lighthouse scores) are triage inputs, not project severity</strong> — map them into this taxonomy only after evaluating actual user impact on the affected task.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="a-layered-testing-model">A Layered Testing Model</h5> <p>No single tool covers accessibility requirements. Choose layers by the affected task and the likelihood/consequence of a regression:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Layer</th> <th>Useful for</th> <th>Does not establish</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Static analysis / lint</td> <td>Fast feedback on detectable source patterns</td> <td>Runtime behavior or final output</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Unit/component tests</td> <td>Stable component contracts (names, roles, states)</td> <td>Whole-page reading and focus order</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Browser rule scans (axe-core)</td> <td>Detectable rules in rendered states</td> <td>Complete WCAG coverage or usability</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Semantic assertions (role queries, ARIA snapshots)</td> <td>Accessibility-tree structure and changes</td> <td>Exact screen-reader speech</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Visual checks</td> <td>Theme/layout regressions, focus indicators</td> <td>Meaning, keyboard access, or text alternatives</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>End-to-end tests</td> <td>Operability, focus, state changes, errors</td> <td>AT interoperability by itself</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Manual and AT testing</td> <td>Quality, sequence, interaction, compatibility</td> <td>Universal behavior across all configurations</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Use <code>skills/manual-testing/SKILL.md</code> for checks automation cannot complete.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-define-the-ci-contract-before-choosing-tools">Critical: Define the CI Contract Before Choosing Tools</h5> <p>For each check, document: the user task/page/component/states covered; the command and config file; tool/browser/runtime/rule-set versions; whether the result warns, blocks, or only produces an artifact; the baseline/expected result; the owner and response process for failures; known false positives and untested requirements; and evidence retained for review.</p> <p>Do not describe a check as a merge gate unless branch protection actually requires it. Do not describe a warning as a failure.</p> <p><strong>Scores are not conformance percentages.</strong> A Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 does not mean 100% WCAG conformance, and 90 does not mean a page is 90% accessible — it measures the weighted audits Lighthouse ran in one configuration. Use individual audit results to investigate regressions. A score threshold can be an additional signal but should not be the only gate; also fail on specific rules/tasks the team has decided are blocking. Keep performance budgets separate — a performance score must not raise or lower accessibility severity.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb561"><pre class="sourceCode json"><code class="sourceCode clean scan means no violations were found in the tested scope — it does not mean no barriers exist. <strong>Missing axe-core checks on PRs is Critical</strong>; missing a color-scheme pass is also a coverage gap since theme-specific regressions often only appear in the untested scheme.</p> <p>Cover applicable combinations without an unnecessarily expensive matrix: desktop and narrow reflow viewports; system/light/dark theme; default and increased contrast; forced colors; reduced motion; default/hover/focus/active/ disabled/loading/success/error states; signed-in/signed-out/timeout/ permission states. Use pairwise or risk-based coverage for routine changes; test every combination for high-risk components (authentication, payment, safety, core navigation).</p> <hr /> <h5 An ARIA snapshot represents the accessibility tree, not a transcript of what every screen reader will announce — speech output also depends on the AT product, browser, OS, settings, mode, and user action.</p> <p><strong>Guidepup virtual screen reader</strong> (unit-level, exact spoken output):</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb564"><pre class="sourceCode typescript"><code class="sourceCode id="serious-visual-and-preference-regression-tests">Serious: Visual and Preference Regression Tests</h5> <p>Visual tests can find clipped text, missing focus indicators, theme-specific contrast changes, and reflow regressions. Keep separate reviewed baselines for materially different themes and forced-colors behavior. Do not use screenshot equality as the only contrast test — anti-aliasing, transparency, gradients, and rendering differences make pixel comparison unreliable; confirm computed colors and visually inspect where contrast is critical. Emulate reduced motion for deterministic tests, but never remove an animation from the product merely to make a screenshot pass.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-risk-indicators-and-build-gates">Critical: Risk Indicators and Build Gates</h5> <p>Behavioral checks such as Reflow risk and Focus Visible testing (see <code>skills/behavioral-a11y/SKILL.md</code>) produce indicators, not conformance verdicts. A small per-target false-positive probability compounds across many pages, components, states, or builds, and website findings are frequently correlated across shared templates and components. Converting every indicator into a blocking build failure produces noisy, low-trust CI and encourages bypassing the check rather than fixing the underlying pattern.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Result</th> <th>Default CI treatment</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Deterministic confirmed failure</td> <td>May block</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Confirmed regression against a reviewed baseline</td> <td>May block</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Risk indicator</td> <td>Report and route for review</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>cantTell</code></td> <td>Report as incomplete coverage</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Test error</td> <td>Report as scan-health failure</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Reviewed exception</td> <td>Do not block until its review expires</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Do not prescribe automatic blocking merely because a result is machine-readable. A first-seen risk indicator has not been reviewed and has not ruled out a normative exception (for example, the SC 1.4.10 two-dimensional-layout exception); blocking on it treats an unreviewed signal as a confirmed failure.</p> <p>Map “default CI treatment” onto <code>policy.handling</code>: a deterministic confirmed failure or reviewed regression is <code>report</code> (and may block); a risk indicator or <code>cantTell</code> is <code>review</code>, never <code>suppress</code>, until a human confirms or rejects it; a reviewed exception is <code>suppress</code> only with the full suppression detail below. <code>handling</code> is independent of <code>obligation</code> — do not use CI treatment as a stand-in for whether the underlying standard is <code>required</code>. Never disable an entire rule or engine because one target is noisy; suppress the specific, scoped finding instead. See <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html#policy-classification">Accessibility Finding Tracking: Policy Classification</a>.</p> <p>Fleet-wide and site-wide scans additionally require: separating unique root-cause clusters from affected instances and reporting both — not one issue per affected URL; comparing new findings against a reviewed baseline before deciding severity; recording the detector, browser, and baseline versions used for the scan; giving every reviewed exception an owner, a reason, and an expiry date; and periodically sampling apparently clean results to investigate false negatives, since a check with no findings has not been shown to have zero false negatives.</p> <p>See <code>skills/behavioral-a11y/SKILL.md</code> for the fixture/PR/scheduled-scan cadence and the definitions of unique finding, affected instance, affected page, and root-cause cluster used above.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-ci-workflow-security">Critical: CI Workflow Security</h5> <p>Apply these controls to accessibility workflows the same as build/deploy workflows:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Pin third-party actions to reviewed full commit SHAs, not tags</strong> — tags can move; commit SHAs cannot</li> <li><strong>Declare minimum <code>GITHUB_TOKEN</code> permissions explicitly</strong> at workflow or job level</li> <li><strong>Set <code>persist-credentials: false</code></strong> on checkout when later steps don’t need Git access</li> <li><strong>Avoid <code>pull_request_target</code></strong> for workflows that execute untrusted PR code</li> <li>Pass untrusted values through environment variables or files and quote shell expansions — never interpolate them into executable script text</li> <li>Do not expose secrets to forked or untrusted code</li> <li>Restrict network access and tools for AI/transformation steps where practical</li> <li>Add timeouts, concurrency controls, and bounded crawl limits</li> <li>Treat uploaded HTML, JSON, screenshots, traces, and logs as potentially sensitive</li> <li>Keep artifact retention no longer than the review process requires</li> <li>Use environments and required reviewers for any workflow that can deploy or modify external systems</li> <li>Do not claim a workflow “has no access to secrets” or “cannot merge” unless its token permissions, event context, tools, and platform controls actually demonstrate that</li> </ul> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb565"><pre class="sourceCode current official docs; resolve each action release to its full commit SHA; review transitive action code and release notes; validate fork behavior so untrusted PRs get no privileged secrets; verify the build path matches production; run the workflow in a test branch first.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-scheduled-scanning-and-the-github-accessibility-scanner">Serious: Scheduled Scanning and the GitHub Accessibility Scanner</h5> <p>Scheduled scans find drift, dependency changes, and pages missed by PR tests. <strong>Continue scanning even when known issues remain</strong> — pausing every scan because one issue is open can hide new regressions; prefer deduplication, stable fingerprints, and clear ownership over an alert-fatigue pause.</p> <p>For each scheduled scan, define: authorized target URLs and crawl boundaries; public vs. authenticated states; frequency/timeout/resource limits; issue deduplication and closure behavior; retention and redaction of reports; triage responsibility; and behavior when the scanner/target is unavailable. Never place authentication secrets, session data, or sensitive content in logs, issue bodies, artifacts, or AI prompts.</p> <p>The <strong>GitHub Accessibility Scanner</strong> (<code>github/accessibility-scanner</code>) is a public-preview action whose interfaces, permissions, and Copilot integration may change — review its current README, <code>action.yml</code>, and security guidance immediately before adoption. It requires a token and documents broader permissions than a read-only scan; treat that credential as privileged, use a dedicated fine-grained credential, and do not assume the default <code>GITHUB_TOKEN</code> is sufficient. If also using a separate remediation workflow, configure the scanner to skip Copilot assignment so two remediation systems don’t act on the same finding.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb566"><pre <h5 id="serious-ai-assisted-remediation-treat-all-scan-input-as-untrusted">Serious: AI-Assisted Remediation — Treat All Scan Input as Untrusted</h5> <p>An AI-generated patch is a <strong>proposal, not evidence a barrier is fixed</strong>. Issues, comments, labels, repository content, HTML, SVG, URLs, and scan output are all <strong>untrusted input</strong>.</p> <p>Required review sequence:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>A scanner or person records a reproducible finding</li> <li>A human triages the affected task, impact, confidence, and scope</li> <li>A maintainer <strong>manually</strong> triggers the remediation workflow with the issue number</li> <li>Copilot reads the issue as untrusted file data in an isolated copy — without the repository’s <code>.git</code> directory</li> <li>The workflow uploads a patch, changed-file list, and report (does not commit/push/PR/merge itself)</li> <li>A human reviews and applies an acceptable patch in a normal branch</li> <li>Relevant automated, manual, and AT checks are rerun on the final implementation</li> </ol> <p>A safe reference remediation workflow: is manual-only and requires explicit confirmation; gives the workflow token <strong>read-only</strong> content and issue permissions; keeps issue content out of shell commands, workflow expressions, and static prompts; limits the agent to read/write tools in an isolated working copy; <strong>denies shell, URL, and memory tools</strong>; blocks changes to protected policy/workflow paths; does not commit, push, open a PR, close an issue, or deploy; retains a review artifact for a limited period.</p> <p><strong>Do not</strong> trigger privileged AI remediation directly from an issue label, or paste an issue body into a shell command, <code>GITHUB_OUTPUT</code>, workflow expression, or static prompt — these are the classic script-injection paths for untrusted GitHub content.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-local-first-reproducible-setup">Moderate: Local-First, Reproducible Setup</h5> <p>Install dependencies in the repository and commit the lockfile — avoid requiring an unspecified latest global package.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb567"><pre class="sourceCode json"><code class="sourceCode json"><span id="cb567-1"><a href="#cb567-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">{</span></span> <span id="cb567-2"><a href="#cb567-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="dt">"scripts"</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="fu">{</span></span> <span id="cb567-3"><a href="#cb567-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="dt">"test:a11y"</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="st">"playwright test tests/accessibility"</span><span class="fu">,</span></span> <span id="cb567-4"><a href="#cb567-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="dt">"test:a11y:update"</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="st">"playwright test tests/accessibility --update-snapshots"</span><span class="fu">,</span></span> <span id="cb567-5"><a href="#cb567-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="dt">"test:a11y:ci"</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="st">"playwright test tests/accessibility --reporter=line,json"</span></span> <span id="cb567-6"><a href="#cb567-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">}</span></span> <span id="cb567-7"><a href="#cb567-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">}</span></span></code></pre></div> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb568"><pre class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb568-1"><a href="#cb568-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">npm</span> install <span class="at">--save-dev</span> @playwright/test @axe-core/playwright</span> <span id="cb568-2"><a href="#cb568-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">npx</span> playwright install <span class="at">--with-deps</span> chromium</span> <span id="cb568-3"><a href="#cb568-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">npm</span> run test:a11y</span></code></pre></div> <p>Use <code>npm ci</code> in CI so the resolved dependency graph matches the reviewed lockfile.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-shift-left-strategy">Moderate: Shift-Left Strategy</h5> <p>Catch problems in order from fastest to slowest feedback: (1) in-editor/local lint with framework-specific a11y rules, (2) pre-commit gate on changed files only (<code>husky</code>+<code>lint-staged</code> or <code>pre-commit</code>; keep total runtime ≤30–60s), (3) PR gate re-running in CI, failing on blocking regressions, publishing artifact links, (4) scheduled deeper scans with auto-labeled findings and trend metrics. No UI-impacting commit should be accepted unless local/pre-commit checks pass and PR CI checks are green.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="baselines-suppressions-and-exceptions">Baselines, Suppressions, and Exceptions</h5> <p>Prefer preventing new regressions while existing findings are assigned and remediated. A baseline is a temporary inventory, not proof existing barriers are acceptable. Every suppression/exception should include: the exact rule/ file/element/route/task affected; reason and supporting evidence; user impact and available workaround; an accountable owner and linked issue; an expiry or review date; and the narrowest practical scope. Do not suppress an entire rule when one reviewed instance is the exception. Do not update snapshots or baselines solely to make CI green.</p> <p>This is the same required detail as <code>policy.suppression</code> (scope, reason, evidence, owner, review or expiry date) — use that vocabulary in a machine-readable finding. Suppression is never resolution; a suppressed finding stays recorded and is excluded only from the specified reporting or enforcement surface.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="sustainable-automation">Sustainable Automation</h5> <p>Run fast targeted checks on every PR; reserve full crawls and large browser matrices for schedules, releases, or high-risk changes. Cache reviewed dependencies where it improves speed without hiding updates. Cancel obsolete runs when it can’t discard required evidence. Retain artifacts only as long as necessary. Avoid duplicate scanners providing the same evidence. Use deterministic tooling before AI when it can answer the question.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-17">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Affected user tasks, pages, components, and states are defined for each check</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Dependencies, browsers, actions, and configuration are versioned and reviewable</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Final rendered output is tested (not source templates alone)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Applicable themes, preferences, viewports, and interaction states are covered</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Automated results are interpreted within their documented limitations (score ≠ conformance; tool severity ≠ project severity)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Required manual and AT tests are completed or precisely handed off</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />New Critical and Serious barriers are not knowingly introduced</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Findings include reproducible evidence and an owner</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Suppressions and exceptions are narrow, justified, tracked, and dated</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Workflow permissions, untrusted input handling, secrets, and artifacts are reviewed</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Action references use reviewed full commit SHAs, not tags</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>persist-credentials: false</code> set where later steps don’t need Git access</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>pull_request_target</code> avoided for workflows executing untrusted PR code</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />AI remediation workflow is manual-trigger-only, read-only token scope, denies shell/URL/memory tools, and never commits/pushes/merges itself</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />The final workflow is validated in a test branch before production use</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Documentation and this skill are kept in sync (not automatic)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-automation-coverage-1">Key WCAG Criteria (automation coverage)</h5> <ul> <li>1.1.1 Non-text Content (A) — caught by axe-core / Lighthouse</li> <li>1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A) — caught by axe-core</li> <li>1.4.3 Contrast Minimum (AA) — caught by Lighthouse / axe-core (visual inspection still needed)</li> <li>4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A) — caught by axe-core + aria snapshots</li> <li>4.1.3 Status Messages (AA) — partially caught by axe-core</li> </ul> <blockquote> <p>Automation covers roughly 30–40% of WCAG issues at best. Pair with manual and assistive technology testing — see <code>skills/manual-testing/SKILL.md</code>.</p> </blockquote> <hr /> <h5 id="references-20">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/CI_CD_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md">Full best practices guide</a></li> <li><code>skills/behavioral-a11y/SKILL.md</code> — Reflow risk and Focus Visible risk indicators, result vocabulary, and false-positive-at-scale guidance</li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/SHIFT_LEFT_ACCESSIBILITY_AUTOMATION.md">Shift-left automation guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/GITHUB_ACCESSIBILITY_SCANNER_INTEGRATION.md">GitHub Accessibility Scanner integration</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions">GitHub Actions Secure Use Reference</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/script-injections">GitHub: Script Injections</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse-ci">Lighthouse CI documentation</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core-npm/tree/develop/packages/playwright">axe-core/playwright</a></li> <li><a href="https://playwright.dev/docs/aria-snapshots">Playwright aria snapshots</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.guidepup.dev">Guidepup virtual screen reader</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/github/accessibility-scanner">GitHub Accessibility Scanner</a></li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> These rules target WCAG 2.2 AA. href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/cli-audit">skills/cli-audit</a></li> </ul> <p>Audit live URLs using Playwright and Axe combined with WCAG skills</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>cli-audit/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="cli-audit-skill">CLI Audit Skill</h4> <p>Use this skill when asked to audit a live URL from Claude CLI.</p> <p>Respect robots directives and site terms of service for every live-site audit request.</p> <h5 id="required-execution">Required Execution</h5> <p>When the user asks to audit a page URL, run:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb577"><pre class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb577-1"><a href="#cb577-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">npx</span> <span class="at">--yes</span> <span class="at">--package</span><span class="op">=</span>github:mgifford/accessibility-skills cli-audit-inspect <span class="op"><</span>URL<span class="op">></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>This invocation is portable for Claude CLI users because it pulls the inspection command from this repository package instead of requiring a local <code>scripts/</code> file in the target project.</p> <h5 id="be-polite-with-live-sites">Be Polite With Live Sites</h5> <p>When auditing live URLs, keep behavior respectful and low impact:</p> <ul> <li>Prefer single-page or small-batch checks first.</li> <li>Avoid rapid repeated scans against production pages.</li> <li>If Cloudflare/WAF blocks requests, do not brute-force retries.</li> <li>Recommend owner-approved alternatives: staging URLs, allowlisting, or manual checks.</li> </ul> <h5 id="required-parsing">Required Parsing</h5> <p>Parse the emitted JSON and evaluate:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><code>axe.violations</code> for automated WCAG and best-practice failures.</li> <li><code>axe.incomplete</code> for potential violations that need manual confirmation.</li> <li><code>accessibilityTree</code> for behavioral issues that automated rules miss, including: <ul> <li>Missing or unclear names for interactive elements</li> <li>Unexpected roles or role mismatches</li> <li>Landmark and heading structure problems</li> <li>State communication gaps (<code>expanded</code>, <code>checked</code>, <code>selected</code>, disabled state)</li> <li>Dialog and menu semantics that can indicate focus-management risk</li> </ul></li> </ol> <h5 id="required-evaluation-method">Required Evaluation Method</h5> <p>Map findings to this repository’s guidance before reporting:</p> <ul> <li>Start with <code>skills/ACCESSIBILITY-general/SKILL.md</code>.</li> <li>Then apply relevant topic skills based on observed problems (for example: <code>forms</code>, <code>keyboard</code>, <code>navigation</code>, <code>color-contrast</code>, <code>aria-live-regions</code>, <code>image-alt-text</code>, <code>tables</code>, <code>svg</code>, <code>touch-pointer</code>, <code>tooltips</code>).</li> </ul> <h5 id="reporting-requirements">Reporting Requirements</h5> <p>For each issue reported:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Identify source: <code>axe</code> or <code>accessibilityTree</code>.</li> <li>Include affected selector/path from axe nodes when available.</li> <li>Provide impact summary and severity using the relevant skill scale.</li> <li>Cite WCAG 2.2 success criteria when determinable, and cite the source of the mapping (the axe rule’s documented mapping, or the specific skill rule) — do not invent a WCAG mapping this audit’s evidence does not support.</li> <li>Provide a concrete remediation recommendation tied to a skill rule.</li> <li>Preserve the tool’s raw outcome (<code>axe.violations</code> vs. <code>axe.incomplete</code>, or the accessibility-tree evidence) rather than collapsing it into a single pass/fail label.</li> <li>Report every <code>axe.violations</code> and <code>accessibilityTree</code> finding from this audit as <code>evidence_status: automated-indicator</code> with <code>handling: review</code> — this audit alone does not constitute the human confirmation needed for <code>confirmed-standards-failure</code>, <code>confirmed-user-facing-barrier</code>, or <code>handling: report</code>/<code>suppress</code>. See <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html#policy-classification">Accessibility Finding Tracking: Policy Classification</a>.</li> </ol> <p>If no issues are found, report residual risk clearly:</p> <ul> <li>Automated scans can miss interaction, timing, focus-flow, and assistive-tech behavior issues.</li> <li>Recommend manual keyboard and screen-reader validation using <code>skills/manual-testing/SKILL.md</code>.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="cross-page-analyzer">Cross-Page Analyzer</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> web</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>cross-page-analyzer</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> findings</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/cross-page-analyzer">skills/cross-page-analyzer</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> helper</li> </ul> <p>Internal helper: cross-page patterns, severity scoring, scorecards.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>cross-page-analyzer/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <p>You are a cross-page accessibility analyst. You receive aggregated scan findings from multiple web pages and identify patterns, compute scores, and generate analysis summaries.</p> <h4 id="capabilities-2">Capabilities</h4> <h5 id="pattern-detection-1">Pattern Detection</h5> <ul> <li>Identify issues that repeat across every audited page (systemic - usually layout/nav)</li> <li>Detect issues shared by pages using the same template/layout component (template-level)</li> <li>Isolate issues unique to individual pages (page-specific)</li> <li>Flag the highest ROI fixes (systemic issues that affect all pages)</li> </ul> <h5 id="severity-scoring-2">Severity Scoring</h5> <p>Compute a weighted accessibility risk score (0-100) for each page:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Page Score = 100 - (sum of weighted findings) Weights: Critical (high confidence, both sources): -15 points Critical (high confidence, single source): -10 points Critical (medium confidence): -7 points Serious (high confidence): -7 points Serious (medium confidence): -5 points Moderate (high confidence): -3 points Moderate (medium confidence): -2 points Minor: -1 point Floor: 0</code></pre> <h5 id="score-grades-5">Score Grades</h5> <p>Each score, with its grade and meaning.</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Score</th> <th>Grade</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>90-100</td> <td>A</td> <td>Excellent - meets WCAG AA</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>75-89</td> <td>B</td> <td>Good - mostly meets WCAG AA</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>50-74</td> <td>C</td> <td>Needs Work - partial compliance</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>25-49</td> <td>D</td> <td>Poor - significant barriers</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>0-24</td> <td>F</td> <td>Failing - unusable with AT</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="cross-page-pattern-classification-1">Cross-Page Pattern Classification</h5> <p>Each type, with its definition and fix strategy.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 20%" /> <col style="width: 36%" /> <col style="width: 43%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Type</th> <th>Definition</th> <th>Fix Strategy</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Systemic</td> <td>Same issue on every page</td> <td>Fix in shared layout - highest ROI</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Template</td> <td>Same issue on pages sharing a component</td> <td>Fix the shared component</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Page-specific</td> <td>Unique to one page</td> <td>Fix individually</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="accessibility-tree-diffing">Accessibility Tree Diffing</h5> <p>When Playwright accessibility tree snapshots are available from <code>playwright-scanner</code>, compare structural consistency across pages:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Landmark consistency</strong> — Verify the same landmark roles (banner, navigation, main, contentinfo) appear on every page. Flag pages where a landmark is missing that exists on all other pages.</li> <li><strong>Heading level consistency</strong> — Detect when the same content type uses different heading levels on different pages (e.g., page title is H1 on homepage but H2 on subpages).</li> <li><strong>ARIA label consistency</strong> — Flag inconsistent labeling of the same landmark (e.g., <code>aria-label="Main navigation"</code> on some pages but <code>aria-label="Nav"</code> on others).</li> <li><strong>Role drift</strong> — Detect components that have different roles on different pages (e.g., <code>role="navigation"</code> on homepage but <code>role="list"</code> on subpages for the same nav component).</li> </ol> <p>Tree diffing produces a <strong>structural consistency score</strong> (0-100) alongside the existing severity score. A score of 100 means all pages share identical landmark/heading/role structure.</p> <h5 id="keyboard-flow-comparison">Keyboard Flow Comparison</h5> <p>When Playwright keyboard scan results are available, compare tab-order sequences across pages:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Navigation order consistency</strong> — Check that shared navigation elements (header nav, skip links, footer links) appear in the same relative tab order across all pages.</li> <li><strong>Trap detection aggregation</strong> — If keyboard traps are detected on multiple pages, classify as systemic vs page-specific.</li> <li><strong>Tab count variance</strong> — Flag pages where the number of tab stops is dramatically different from the mean (possible hidden interactive elements or excessive tabbable items).</li> <li><strong>Focus management patterns</strong> — Compare how focus is handled on route changes across pages (focus moved to main content vs stays on nav vs lost entirely).</li> </ol> <h5 id="remediation-tracking-3">Remediation Tracking</h5> <p>When baseline report data is provided:</p> <ul> <li>Classify findings as Fixed, New, Persistent, or Regressed</li> <li>Calculate progress metrics (% reduction, score change, trend)</li> <li>Generate comparison summaries</li> </ul> <h4 id="output-format-9">Output Format</h4> <p>Return structured analysis including:</p> <ul> <li>Cross-page pattern summary with frequencies</li> <li>Per-page severity scores and grades</li> <li>Overall average score and grade</li> <li>Pattern classification (systemic / template / page-specific)</li> <li>Remediation progress (if baseline provided)</li> <li>Scorecard table ready for inclusion in the audit report</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="multi-agent-reliability-9">Multi-Agent Reliability</h4> <h5 id="role-9">Role</h5> <p>You are a <strong>read-only analyzer</strong>. You aggregate per-page findings from web scanners into cross-page patterns, scores, and scorecards. You do NOT modify files or re-scan pages.</p> <h5 id="output-contract-80">Output Contract</h5> <p>Your output MUST include:</p> <ul> <li><code>patterns</code>: list of cross-page patterns, each with frequency, severity, affected pages, and classification (<code>systemic</code> | <code>template</code> | <code>page-specific</code>)</li> <li><code>scores</code>: per-page score (0-100) and grade (A-F)</li> <li><code>overall_score</code>: average score and grade</li> <li><code>scorecard</code>: table with page URL, score, grade, issue counts by severity</li> <li><code>remediation_delta</code>: (if baseline provided) fixed/new/persistent/regressed counts</li> <li><code>tree_diff</code>: (if Playwright data available) structural consistency score, landmark/heading/role inconsistencies</li> <li><code>keyboard_comparison</code>: (if Playwright data available) tab-order consistency, trap aggregation, focus management patterns</li> </ul> <h5 id="handoff-transparency-9">Handoff Transparency</h5> <p>When invoked by <code>web-accessibility-wizard</code>:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Announce start:</strong> “Analyzing patterns across [N] scanned pages”</li> <li><strong>Announce completion:</strong> “Cross-page analysis complete: [N] systemic patterns, [N] template patterns, overall score [score]/100 ([grade])”</li> <li><strong>On failure:</strong> “Analysis incomplete: received findings from [N] of [M] expected pages. Proceeding with available data.”</li> </ul> <p>You return results to <code>web-accessibility-wizard</code> for report generation. You never present results directly to the user.</p> <h4 id="output-contract-81">Output contract</h4> <p>Return only JSON matching <code>skills/a11y-core/schemas/findings.schema.json</code>. No prose, no summary, no restated instructions. One object, one array of findings.</p> <p>Shared rules, dispatch contract and schemas: <code>skills/a11y-core/SKILL.md</code>. Authoritative specifications for this skill: <code>skills/a11y-core/references/sources.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="github-a11y-scanner-reference">Github A11y Scanner (Reference)</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> cross-cutting</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>kb-github-a11y-scanner</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> none</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/kb-github-a11y-scanner">skills/kb-github-a11y-scanner</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> reference</li> </ul> <p>Reference data, not a reviewer. Integrate GitHub Accessibility Scanner. Detects configuration, parses scanner issues, correlates with local scans, and tracks Copilot-assigned fixes.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>kb-github-a11y-scanner/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="github-accessibility-scanner-integration">GitHub Accessibility Scanner Integration</h4> <h4 id="what-is-the-github-accessibility-scanner">What Is the GitHub Accessibility Scanner?</h4> <p>The <a href="https://github.com/github/accessibility-scanner">GitHub Accessibility Scanner</a> (<code>github/accessibility-scanner@v2</code>) is an official GitHub Action that:</p> <ul> <li>Scans live URLs for accessibility barriers using axe-core in a headless browser</li> <li>Creates trackable GitHub Issues for each finding, with affected element, WCAG criterion, and remediation guidance</li> <li>Optionally assigns issues to GitHub Copilot for AI-powered fix suggestions and PR creation</li> <li>Caches results across runs for delta detection (new, fixed, persistent findings)</li> <li>Supports authenticated scanning (login flows, SSO, passkeys via Playwright auth context)</li> <li>Optionally captures screenshots and attaches them to filed issues</li> </ul> <p><strong>Current version:</strong> v2 (public preview)</p> <h4 id="detecting-scanner-presence">Detecting Scanner Presence</h4> <p>To determine whether a repository has the GitHub Accessibility Scanner configured:</p> <h5 id="workflow-file-detection">Workflow File Detection</h5> <p>Search for workflow files referencing the scanner action:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb579"><pre class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb579-1"><a href="#cb579-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># Search in .github/workflows/ for the scanner action reference</span></span> <span id="cb579-2"><a href="#cb579-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">grep</span> <span class="at">-rl</span> <span class="st">"github/accessibility-scanner"</span> .github/workflows/</span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Pattern to match in YAML:</strong></p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb580"><pre class="sourceCode yaml"><code class="sourceCode yaml"><span id="cb580-1"><a href="#cb580-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">-</span><span class="at"> </span><span class="fu">uses</span><span class="kw">:</span><span class="at"> github/accessibility-scanner@v2</span></span></code></pre></div> <h5 id="workflow-inputs">Workflow Inputs</h5> <p>When a scanner workflow is found, extract its configuration:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 23%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 43%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Input</th> <th>Required</th> <th>Description</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>urls</code></td> <td>Yes</td> <td>Newline-delimited list of URLs to scan</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>repository</code></td> <td>Yes</td> <td>Repository (owner/name) where issues and PRs are created</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>token</code></td> <td>Yes</td> <td>Fine-grained PAT with write access (contents, issues, PRs, metadata)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>cache_key</code></td> <td>Yes</td> <td>Filename for caching results across runs (e.g., <code>cached_results-mysite.json</code>)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>login_url</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Login page URL for authenticated scanning</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>username</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Username for authentication</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>password</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Password for authentication (via repository secret)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>auth_context</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Stringified JSON for complex authentication (Playwright session state)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>skip_copilot_assignment</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Set <code>true</code> to skip assigning issues to Copilot</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>include_screenshots</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Set <code>true</code> to capture screenshots (stored on <code>gh-cache</code> branch)</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="parsing-scanner-created-issues">Parsing Scanner-Created Issues</h4> <p>The scanner creates GitHub Issues with a structured format. Agents should parse these fields:</p> <h5 id="issue-identification">Issue Identification</h5> <p>Scanner-created issues can be identified by:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Author:</strong> The GitHub Actions bot that runs the workflow</li> <li><strong>Labels:</strong> The scanner applies labels to categorize findings (typically accessibility-related labels)</li> <li><strong>Body structure:</strong> Issues contain structured sections with violation details</li> </ol> <h5 id="issue-body-structure">Issue Body Structure</h5> <p>Scanner issues typically contain:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 31%" /> <col style="width: 31%" /> <col style="width: 37%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Section</th> <th>Content</th> <th>Agent Use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Violation title</td> <td>The axe-core rule that was violated</td> <td>Map to <code>help-url-reference</code> for remediation docs</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>WCAG criterion</td> <td>The specific WCAG success criterion</td> <td>Used for severity scoring and compliance mapping</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Affected element</td> <td>CSS selector or HTML snippet of the failing element</td> <td>Used by <code>scanner-bridge</code> to map to source code</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Impact level</td> <td>Critical, Serious, Moderate, or Minor</td> <td>Direct mapping to agent severity model</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Remediation guidance</td> <td>How to fix the issue</td> <td>Enriched by agent specialists with framework-specific fixes</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>URL</td> <td>The page URL where the issue was found</td> <td>Used for cross-referencing with local axe-core scans</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Screenshot link</td> <td>Link to screenshot on <code>gh-cache</code> branch (if enabled)</td> <td>Included in audit reports</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="severity-mapping-2">Severity Mapping</h5> <p>The scanner uses axe-core impact levels that map directly to the agent severity model:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Scanner Impact</th> <th>Agent Severity</th> <th>Score Weight</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Critical</td> <td>Critical</td> <td>-15 (both sources) / -10 (single source)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Serious</td> <td>Serious</td> <td>-7 (high confidence)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Moderate</td> <td>Moderate</td> <td>-3 (high confidence)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Minor</td> <td>Minor</td> <td>-1</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="axe-core-rule-correlation">axe-core Rule Correlation</h5> <p>The scanner uses axe-core under the hood. Scanner issue titles and violation IDs correspond to axe-core rules already cataloged in <code>help-url-reference</code>. Common scanner-reported rules:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 35%" /> <col style="width: 29%" /> <col style="width: 35%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>axe-core Rule ID</th> <th>WCAG Criterion</th> <th>Common Description</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>image-alt</code></td> <td>1.1.1</td> <td>Images must have alternate text</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>label</code></td> <td>1.3.1</td> <td>Form elements must have labels</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>color-contrast</code></td> <td>1.4.3</td> <td>Elements must have sufficient color contrast</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>link-name</code></td> <td>2.4.4</td> <td>Links must have discernible text</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>html-has-lang</code></td> <td>3.1.1</td> <td><code><html></code> element must have a lang attribute</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>button-name</code></td> <td>4.1.2</td> <td>Buttons must have discernible text</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>document-title</code></td> <td>2.4.2</td> <td>Documents must have <code><title></code> element</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>bypass</code></td> <td>2.4.1</td> <td>Page must have means to bypass repeated blocks</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>heading-order</code></td> <td>1.3.1</td> <td>Heading levels should increase by one</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>aria-allowed-attr</code></td> <td>4.1.2</td> <td>ARIA attributes must be allowed for element role</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="caching-and-delta-detection">Caching and Delta Detection</h4> <p>The scanner uses a <code>cache_key</code> to persist results across workflow runs. This enables delta tracking:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 47%" /> <col style="width: 52%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Status</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>New</strong></td> <td>Issue found in current scan but not in cached results</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Fixed</strong></td> <td>Issue in cached results but not found in current scan (issue auto-closed)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Persistent</strong></td> <td>Issue found in both current scan and cached results</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="cache-key-conventions">Cache Key Conventions</h5> <p>When setting up scanner integration, align the cache key with agent conventions:</p> <ul> <li>Use a descriptive name: <code>cached_results-{domain}-{branch}.json</code></li> <li>Include branch context for branch-specific scanning</li> <li>The cache is stored as a GitHub Actions artifact</li> </ul> <h4 id="correlation-with-local-scans">Correlation with Local Scans</h4> <h5 id="dual-source-confidence-boosting">Dual-Source Confidence Boosting</h5> <p>When both the GitHub Accessibility Scanner (CI) and a local axe-core scan (agent) find the same issue:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Match by rule ID:</strong> Both sources use axe-core rule IDs (e.g., <code>color-contrast</code>, <code>image-alt</code>)</li> <li><strong>Match by URL:</strong> Compare the scanned URL from the scanner issue with the local scan target</li> <li><strong>Match by element:</strong> Compare CSS selectors or HTML paths for the affected element</li> <li><strong>Boost confidence:</strong> Findings confirmed by both sources automatically receive <code>high</code> confidence</li> </ol> <h5 id="source-comparison-analysis">Source Comparison Analysis</h5> <p>Each scenario, with its interpretation and action.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 30%" /> <col style="width: 45%" /> <col style="width: 24%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Scenario</th> <th>Interpretation</th> <th>Action</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Found by scanner AND local scan</td> <td>High confidence – confirmed by both</td> <td>Report as high confidence, full severity weight</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Found by scanner only</td> <td>Environment-specific or intermittent</td> <td>Report as medium confidence, note “CI-only finding”</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Found by local scan only</td> <td>New since last CI scan, or local-only condition</td>
