id="releases">Releases</h5> <ul> <li>Use <code>github_list_releases</code> per repo - check for recent, draft, and pre-releases.</li> <li>Cross-reference merged PRs against release notes to identify unreleased work.</li> <li>Compare issue milestones against release schedules to flag upcoming deadline items.</li> </ul> <h5 id="security">Security</h5> <ul> <li>Dependabot alerts: critical and high severity across monitored repos.</li> <li>Security advisories affecting dependencies.</li> <li>Pending dependency update PRs from <code>dependabot[bot]</code> or <code>renovate[bot]</code>.</li> </ul> <h5 id="cicd">CI/CD</h5> <ul> <li>Fetch recent workflow runs - identify failing workflows, long jobs, and flaky tests.</li> <li>For failing workflows: note repo, workflow name, branch, failure reason, and link to run.</li> <li>Cross-reference user’s open PRs against CI results.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="date-range-handling">Date Range Handling</h4> <p>Convert natural language to GitHub query qualifiers:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 39%" /> <col style="width: 60%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>User Says</th> <th>GitHub Qualifier</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>“last week”</td> <td><code>created:>YYYY-MM-DD</code> (7 days ago)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>“this month”</td> <td><code>created:>YYYY-MM-01</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>“today”</td> <td><code>closed:YYYY-MM-DD</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>“this week”</td> <td><code>closed:>YYYY-MM-DD</code> (7 days ago)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>“between X and Y”</td> <td><code>created:X..Y</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Not specified</td> <td>Use <code>search.default_window</code> from preferences (default: <code>updated:>YYYY-MM-DD</code> 30 days) - mention this assumption</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>“for current month” (a11y tracker)</td> <td><code>milestone:"{Month} {Year}"</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h4 id="scope-narrowing">Scope Narrowing</h4> <p>Add qualifiers to narrow by scope when the user specifies one:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Scope</th> <th>Qualifier</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Single repo</td> <td><code>repo:owner/name</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>All org repos</td> <td><code>org:orgname</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>All repos by user</td> <td><code>user:username</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Everything (default)</td> <td>No qualifier - searches all accessible repos</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h4 id="preferences-file-integration">Preferences File Integration</h4> <p>Read <code>.github/agents/preferences.md</code> and apply these filters before and after searching:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong><code>repos.discovery</code></strong> - determines the default search scope (all / starred / owned / configured / workspace).</li> <li><strong><code>repos.include</code></strong> - always include these repos even in restricted modes.</li> <li><strong><code>repos.exclude</code></strong> - skip these repos in all searches.</li> <li><strong><code>repos.overrides</code></strong> - per-repo settings: <ul> <li><code>track.issues: false</code> -> skip issue searches for this repo</li> <li><code>track.pull_requests: false</code> -> skip PR searches for this repo</li> <li><code>track.discussions: false</code> -> skip discussions for this repo</li> <li><code>track.releases: false</code> -> skip release checks for this repo</li> <li><code>track.security: false</code> -> skip security alerts for this repo</li> <li><code>track.ci: false</code> -> skip CI status for this repo</li> <li><code>labels.include</code> / <code>labels.exclude</code> -> filter results by label</li> <li><code>paths</code> -> only trigger for changes touching these file paths (for PRs/CI)</li> <li><code>assignees</code> -> filter to specific assignees (empty = all)</li> </ul></li> <li><strong><code>search.default_window</code></strong> - default time range if the user doesn’t specify one.</li> <li><strong><code>briefing.sections</code></strong> - which sections to include in the daily briefing.</li> <li><strong><code>accessibility_tracking</code></strong> - config for the a11y tracker (repos, labels, channels).</li> </ol> <hr /> <h4 id="cross-repo-intelligence-2">Cross-Repo Intelligence</h4> <p>When results arrive from different repos, look for and surface these patterns:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 52%" /> <col style="width: 47%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Pattern</th> <th>Action</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Cross-repo references</td> <td>When issue A contains <code>owner/repo#N</code>, fetch and surface item N</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Shared label patterns</td> <td>Group items in different repos tagged <code>P0</code> together in triage</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Related PRs in different repos</td> <td>Flag: <em>“This issue depends on PR #N in repo-B which is still open”</em></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Merged PR not yet released</td> <td>Note: <em>“Your PR #N is merged but not in any release yet”</em></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Issue with merged fix PR</td> <td>Flag: <em>“This may be resolved - PR #N that closes it was merged on {date}”</em></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Branch naming patterns</td> <td>Group PRs in different repos using the same branch naming convention</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h4 id="parallel-stream-collection-model">Parallel Stream Collection Model</h4> <p>For agents that collect from multiple data streams, run independent streams simultaneously. Don’t serialize operations with no dependencies.</p> <h5 id="example-daily-briefing---3-parallel-batches">Example: Daily Briefing - 3 Parallel Batches</h5> <p><strong>Batch 1 - fully independent, run simultaneously:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Issues (assigned, mentioned, authored)</li> <li>Pull requests (review-requested, authored)</li> <li>Releases & deployments</li> <li>Accessibility updates</li> </ul> <p><strong>Batch 2 - run after Batch 1 (CI needs PR list from Batch 1):</strong></p> <ul> <li>GitHub Discussions</li> <li>CI/CD health (cross-references PR list)</li> <li>Security alerts</li> </ul> <p><strong>Batch 3 - can overlap with Batch 2:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Project board status</li> <li>Recently closed/merged work</li> </ul> <h5 id="example-analytics---2-parallel-batches">Example: Analytics - 2 Parallel Batches</h5> <p><strong>Batch 1 - collection (all independent):</strong></p> <ul> <li>Closed/merged PRs in period</li> <li>Opened issues in period</li> <li>CI workflow runs in period</li> <li>Security alerts in period</li> </ul> <p><strong>Batch 2 - analysis (depends on Batch 1 data):</strong></p> <ul> <li>Health score computation</li> <li>Velocity metrics calculation</li> <li>Bottleneck detection</li> </ul> <h5 id="announcement-template-for-parallel-work">Announcement Template for Parallel Work</h5> <pre class="text"><code> Running {N} searches in parallel... ({scope}) Batch 1 complete - {X} items found Running {N} additional searches... Batch 2 complete - {Y} items found Scoring and prioritizing... Done - {Z} items need action, {W} to monitor</code></pre> <hr /> <h4 id="auto-recovery-for-empty-results">Auto-Recovery for Empty Results</h4> <p>If a search returns 0 results:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Automatically broaden: remove date filter, expand scope to <code>all</code>, or remove label filters.</li> <li>Tell the user exactly what changed: <em>“No results in last 7 days - broadened to last 30 days and found 3 items.”</em></li> <li>Never return 0 results without trying at least one broader query first.</li> </ol> <p>Recovery cascade:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>First try: Remove date qualifier</li> <li>Second try: Expand scope (add org: or remove repo: qualifier)</li> <li>Third try: Remove label filters</li> <li>Report 0 results only if all three attempts return nothing</li> </ol> <hr /> <h4 id="pagination-1">Pagination</h4> <ul> <li>Paginate large result sets in batches of 10.</li> <li>Ask before loading more: <em>“Showing 10 of 47. Load more?”</em></li> <li>Never silently truncate results - always disclose the total count.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="result-deduplication">Result Deduplication</h4> <p>When the same item appears in multiple searches (e.g., an issue you’re both assigned to AND mentioned in):</p> <ul> <li>Show it once, with all context combined.</li> <li>In the Signal column, combine signals: <em>“Assigned, <span class="citation" data-cites="mentioned">@mentioned</span>”</em>.</li> <li>In priority calculations, apply the highest-scoring signal, not additive.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="rate-limiting">Rate Limiting</h4> <ul> <li>If rate-limited (403/429), tell the user the reset time in one sentence.</li> <li>Do not retry the same query - wait if reset is <60 seconds; otherwise report and move on.</li> <li>For multi-stream collection, skip rate-limited streams and complete them in a follow-up.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="lighthouse-bridge">Lighthouse Bridge</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> web</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; Only reads reports and returns data.</li> <li><strong>Structured output</strong> – Always returns JSON matching the output contracts above.</li> <li><strong>Fail gracefully</strong> – If no Lighthouse CI is configured, no reports are available, or parsing fails, return <code>{"lighthouseDetected": false}</code> with an empty findings array.</li> <li><strong>Progress announcements</strong> – Announce each phase: “Detecting Lighthouse CI configuration…”, “Parsing Lighthouse reports…”, “Correlating with local scan results…”</li> <li><strong>No user interaction</strong> – Never prompts the user. Works silently as a subagent.</li> <li><strong>Score context</strong> – Always include score context (previous score, delta, regression status) when available, not just individual findings.</li> </ol> <h4 id="output-contract-82">Output contract</h4> <p>Return only JSON matching <code>skills/a11y-core/schemas/findings.schema.json</code>. Integrate Lighthouse CI accessibility audits. Detects configuration, parses results, maps findings to severity model, and tracks score regressions.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>kb-lighthouse-scanner/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="lighthouse-ci-accessibility-integration">Lighthouse CI Accessibility Integration</h4> <h4 id="what-is-lighthouse-ci">What Is Lighthouse CI?</h4> <p><a href="https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse-ci">Lighthouse CI</a> is a suite of tools for running Google Lighthouse audits in CI pipelines. The most common GitHub Actions integration uses <a href="https://github.com/treosh/lighthouse-ci-action"><code>treosh/lighthouse-ci-action</code></a>.</p> <p>Lighthouse provides:</p> <ul> <li>Performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO scoring (0-100)</li> <li>Individual audit results with pass/fail status and detailed findings</li> <li>Score budgets and assertions to fail builds on regressions</li> <li>HTML and JSON report artifacts</li> <li>Score comparison across runs for trend tracking</li> </ul> <p><strong>Accessibility focus:</strong> The Lighthouse accessibility category runs a subset of axe-core rules and reports a weighted score from 0-100 along with individual audit violations.</p> <h4 id="detecting-lighthouse-ci-presence">Detecting Lighthouse CI Map to the agent severity model based on weight and audit pass/fail:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Lighthouse Weight</th> <th>Audit Status</th> <th>Agent Severity</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>10</td> <td>Fail</td> <td>Critical</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>7</td> <td>Fail</td> <td>Serious</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>3</td> <td>Fail</td> <td>Moderate</td> id="correlation-with-local-scans-1">Correlation with Local Scans</h4> <h5 id="lighthouse-to-axe-core-mapping">Lighthouse-to-axe-core Mapping</h5> <p>Since Lighthouse uses axe-core under the hood, correlation is straightforward:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Match by audit/rule ID:</strong> Lighthouse audit IDs correspond directly to axe-core rule IDs</li> <li><strong>Match by URL:</strong> Compare scanned URLs from Lighthouse config with local scan targets</li> <li><strong>Boost confidence:</strong> Findings confirmed by both Lighthouse CI and local axe-core scan receive <code>high</code> confidence</li> </ol> <h5 id="source-comparison">Source Comparison</h5> <p>Each scenario, with its interpretation and action.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 30%" /> <col Lighthouse AND local scan</td> <td>High confidence</td> <td>Report as high confidence, full severity weight</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Found by Lighthouse only</td> <td>Environment-specific</td> <td>Report as medium confidence, note “CI-only finding”</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Found by local scan only</td> <td>Not covered by Lighthouse subset</td> <td>Report as medium confidence, note “local-only finding”</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Lighthouse score regressed</td> <td>New accessibility issues introduced</td> <td>Flag as regression, prioritize in report</td> </tr> </tbody> URL (default: 1)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><code>budgetPath</code></td> <td>No</td> <td>Path to a Lighthouse budget JSON file</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="extracting-results-from-artifacts">Extracting Results from Artifacts</h5> <p>Lighthouse CI uploads results as workflow artifacts. To retrieve scores:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Download the artifact from the workflow run</li> <li>Parse the JSON report files</li> <li>Extract <code>categories.accessibility.score</code> for the overall score</li> <li>Extract individual <code>audits.{audit-id}</code> results for violations</li> </ol> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="manual-testing-1">Manual Testing</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>manual-testing</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/manual-testing">skills/manual-testing</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever you are planning, executing, or reviewing manual accessibility testing. Manual testing with real assistive technologies is essential — automated tools catch only ~30–40 % of WCAG issues. Absolutely always include keyboard-only testing and at least one screen reader test before marking a feature accessible. Under no circumstances skip forced colors mode testing for UI components.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>manual-testing/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="manual-accessibility-testing-skill">Manual Accessibility Testing Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/MANUAL_ACCESSIBILITY_TESTING_GUIDE.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when planning or reviewing manual accessibility testing.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-18">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Issue completely blocks a core task for one or more disability groups</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Significantly impairs access; workaround unreasonable to expect</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Creates friction; workaround exists and is not too burdensome</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Best-practice gap; marginal impact on access</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="core-principle-1">Core Principle</h5> <p><strong>Manual testing reveals issues that automated tools cannot detect</strong>, including:</p> <ul> <li>Screen reader announcement quality and user experience</li> <li>Keyboard navigation flow and logical sequence</li> <li>Focus management in dynamic interfaces</li> <li>Context and orientation for assistive technology users</li> <li>Forced colors mode (Windows High Contrast) — automated tools cannot simulate OS-level color overrides</li> <li>Real-world usability barriers</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-when-manual-testing-is-required">Critical: When Manual Testing Is Required</h5> <p>Perform manual testing:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Before each release</strong> — test critical user flows end to end</li> <li><strong>After UI changes</strong> — test all affected components</li> <li><strong>For new features</strong> — test complete user workflows</li> <li><strong>When automated tests pass</strong> — validate actual user experience</li> <li><strong>When accessibility bugs are reported</strong> — reproduce and verify fixes</li> </ul> <p><strong>Getting started:</strong> test keyboard-only first (easiest entry point), then learn basic screen reader commands for your platform. Practice on familiar websites before testing your own. Focus on one component or flow at a time.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-keyboard-only-testing">Critical: Keyboard-Only Testing</h5> <p><strong>Every interactive element must be reachable and operable by keyboard alone.</strong></p> <p>Steps: 1. Click in the browser address bar, then press Tab to start from page top 2. Tab through entire page; check each focusable element: - Is focus visible (clear outline or highlight)? - Is focus order logical (follows visual/reading order)? - Can you activate it? (Enter for links/buttons, Space for buttons/checkboxes) 3. Press Shift+Tab to reverse through elements 4. Confirm there are no keyboard traps (can you Tab away from every element?)</p> <p>Key shortcuts to verify:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Key</th> <th>Expected behaviour</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Tab</td> <td>Move focus forward</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Shift+Tab</td> <td>Move focus backward</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Enter</td> <td>Activate links, buttons, submit forms</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Space</td> <td>Activate buttons, toggle checkboxes</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Arrow keys</td> <td>Navigate within components (menus, tabs, radio groups)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Escape</td> <td>Close dialogs, cancel operations</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Home / End</td> <td>Jump to start/end of component</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Component-specific checks:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Forms:</strong> all fields reachable; labels and required state announced; errors appear and are announced; Enter submits; can cancel/reset if applicable</li> <li><strong>Buttons:</strong> Enter and Space both activate; visual feedback on activation; focus moves appropriately after activation</li> <li><strong>Links:</strong> Enter activates; destination clear from link text; skip links work</li> <li><strong>Dropdowns/select menus:</strong> arrow keys navigate options; Escape closes; selected value announced</li> <li><strong>Modal dialogs:</strong> focus moves in on open; focus trapped inside; Escape closes (unless critical); focus returns to trigger on close</li> <li><strong>Custom widgets (tabs, accordions, carousels):</strong> follow WAI-ARIA keyboard patterns; arrow keys and Home/End work as documented; state changes are clear</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-screen-reader-testing">Critical: Screen Reader Testing</h5> <p><strong>Recommended platform pairings:</strong></p> <ul> <li>NVDA + Firefox or Chrome (Windows)</li> <li>JAWS + Chrome or Firefox (Windows)</li> <li>VoiceOver + Safari (macOS / iOS)</li> <li>TalkBack + Chrome (Android)</li> </ul> <p><strong>Basic test procedure:</strong></p> <ol type="1"> <li>Start screen reader (NVDA: Ctrl+Alt+N; VoiceOver macOS: Cmd+F5)</li> <li>Navigate by headings (NVDA/JAWS: H / Shift+H) — do they form a logical outline?</li> <li>Navigate by landmarks (NVDA/JAWS: D / Shift+D) — are <code><nav></code>, <code><main></code>, <code><header></code> identified?</li> <li>Navigate by form controls (NVDA/JAWS: F / Shift+F) — are labels announced?</li> <li>Read all content — is order logical? Any missing or confusing announcements?</li> </ol> <p><strong>Component-specific screen reader checks:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Images:</strong> decorative images ignored (empty alt/<code>aria-hidden</code>); informative images have descriptive alt text; complex images have longer descriptions</li> <li><strong>Links:</strong> purpose clear from announcement alone; text meaningful (not “click here”); external links/new windows indicated</li> <li><strong>Buttons:</strong> label describes the action; pressed/toggle state announced; disabled state announced</li> <li><strong>Form fields:</strong> label announced before field type; required state, instructions/hints, error messages, and success messages all announced</li> <li><strong>Dynamic content:</strong> new/deleted content announced via live regions; loading states and progress communicated</li> <li><strong>Tables:</strong> navigate by rows/cells (Ctrl+Alt+Arrow in NVDA/JAWS); column and row headers announced with each cell; table purpose clear (caption or <code>aria-label</code>)</li> <li><strong>Custom widgets:</strong> role announced (e.g., “tab”, “menu”, “dialog”); state announced (e.g., “selected”, “expanded”); instructions provided for complex widgets</li> </ul> <p><strong>For each interactive element, verify:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Element type is announced (button, link, heading…)</li> <li>Label/name is clear and descriptive</li> <li>Current value is announced (form fields)</li> <li>State is announced (checked, selected, expanded…)</li> <li>Changes are announced (dynamic updates, live regions)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-forced-colors-mode-testing">Serious: Forced Colors Mode Testing</h5> <p><strong>Why automated tools miss this:</strong> forced colors is triggered by an OS-level setting that replaces all author-defined colors with a constrained system palette. Automated tools cannot simulate the OS-level override, detect which elements become invisible when custom colors are stripped, or assess whether focus indicators/icons/custom controls survive the substitution.</p> <p><strong>How to enable:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Windows 11:</strong> Settings → Accessibility → Contrast themes → choose a theme → Apply</li> <li><strong>Windows 10:</strong> Settings → Ease of Access → High Contrast → turn on (or <code>Alt+Left Shift+Print Screen</code>)</li> <li><strong>Chrome/Edge DevTools:</strong> F12 → More Tools → Rendering → “Emulate CSS media feature forced-colors” → <code>active</code></li> <li><strong>Firefox:</strong> <code>about:config</code> → <code>ui.forcedColors</code> → set to <code>1</code> (<code>-1</code> to reset)</li> <li><strong>Polypane</strong> includes a forced-colors emulation panel</li> </ul> <p>Always verify with real OS settings before release — DevTools emulation is convenient but not fully equivalent.</p> <p><strong>What to look for:</strong></p> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All text is readable against its background (<code>CanvasText</code> on <code>Canvas</code>)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Buttons have a visible boundary; links distinguishable from body text; form fields have visible borders</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Keyboard focus outlines are visible (<code>outline</code> is preserved; <code>box-shadow</code> may not be)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />SVG icons are visible (use <code>currentColor</code> for <code>fill</code>/<code>stroke</code>)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Custom checkboxes / radio buttons remain visible and distinguishable; toggle state shown via text/ARIA/outline, not color alone</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Error states are identifiable without relying on color alone; required fields marked with text or icons, not only color</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Background images that convey meaning have a text/ARIA alternative</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Charts/data visualizations use pattern/texture/label alternatives</li> </ul> <p><strong>Common fixes:</strong></p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Issue</th> <th>Fix</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>box-shadow</code> focus ring disappears</td> <td>Replace with <code>outline</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>SVG icon invisible</td> <td>Use <code>currentColor</code> for <code>fill</code>/<code>stroke</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Custom checkbox invisible</td> <td>Add visible border; use <code>forced-color-adjust</code> override</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Error marked by color only</td> <td>Add icon, text label, or <code>aria-invalid</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Input invisible (<code>border: none</code>)</td> <td>Add <code>border: 1px solid ButtonBorder</code> in <code>@media (forced-colors: active)</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Background image removed</td> <td>Add visible text, caption, or <code>aria-label</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>CSS system color keywords for patching:</strong></p> <div <code>ButtonText</code>, <code>ButtonBorder</code>, <code>Highlight</code>, <code>HighlightText</code>, <code>LinkText</code>, <code>VisitedText</code>, <code>GrayText</code>.</p> <p>Use <code>forced-color-adjust: none</code> only as a last resort — it opts the element out of forced colors entirely and can negate the user’s accessibility settings.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-visual-accessibility-checks">Moderate: Visual Accessibility Checks</h5> <h6 id="color-contrast-1">Color contrast</h6> <ul> <li>Normal text (< 18 pt or < 14 pt bold): 4.5:1 minimum</li> <li>Large text (≥ 18 pt or ≥ 14 pt bold): 3:1 minimum</li> <li>UI components and graphics: 3:1 minimum</li> <li>Focus indicators: 3:1 against adjacent colors</li> </ul> <p>Test with: WebAIM Contrast Checker, browser DevTools. Test light and dark color modes separately.</p> <h6 id="sc-1.4.4-resize-text-vs.-sc-1.4.10-reflow-do-not-conflate">SC 1.4.4 Resize Text vs. SC 1.4.10 Reflow — do not conflate</h6> <p>These are two distinct success criteria with different tests. A page can pass one and fail the other, and horizontal scrolling at 200% zoom is not automatically a failure of either.</p> <p><strong>SC 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA):</strong> content must be resizable up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Checks text enlargement specifically — it does not itself require eliminating horizontal scrolling.</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Set browser zoom to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd + +)</li> <li>Verify all content is readable and not cut off or overlapping</li> <li>Verify functionality (menus, forms, controls) still works at 200%</li> <li>Also test with OS-level screen magnification (Windows Magnifier, macOS Zoom)</li> </ol> <p><strong>SC 1.4.10 Reflow (AA):</strong> content must be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions, at a viewport width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels (a common way to test this on desktop is a 1280px-wide viewport at 400% zoom — the two are equivalent).</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Set the viewport to 320 CSS pixels wide (or 400% zoom on a 1280px viewport)</li> <li>Verify content does not require horizontal scrolling to read, for non-excepted content — see the exception below</li> <li>Verify no content is cut off, overlapped, or hidden</li> <li>Verify interactive elements remain operable</li> <li>Verify reading order, relationships, and operation are preserved without relying on the original visual layout</li> </ol> <p><strong>The exception, precisely:</strong> SC 1.4.10 exempts only <strong>parts of content that require two-dimensional layout for their usage or meaning</strong> — not the page as a whole. Normative examples: data tables, maps, diagrams, video players, games, presentations, interfaces requiring a persistently visible toolbar. An excepted component does not exempt the rest of the page (the heading above a data table, filters, search, pagination must still reflow). Within an excepted component, individual sections may still need to reflow. “Requires” is a meaning test, not a convenience test — a component that merely looks better in a wide fixed layout, without losing information or functionality if it reflowed, is not exempt.</p> <p>A page that triggers horizontal scroll at 400% zoom (or the 320px equivalent) is a high-value indicator that Reflow has not been achieved, but investigate whether the overflowing content falls within the exception before concluding a failure. See <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/BEHAVIORAL_ACCESSIBILITY_AUTOMATION.md#4-reflow-risk-in-detail">Behavioral Accessibility Automation</a> (<code>skills/behavioral-a11y/SKILL.md</code>) for a reusable, tested Playwright Reflow risk indicator and its documented limitations — it is an indicator, not a Reflow conformance check; human judgment is still required to confirm the exception, verify content isn’t cut off, and test actual content at 400% zoom.</p> <h6 id="focus-indicator-three-distinct-success-criteria">Focus indicator: three distinct success criteria</h6> <p><strong>SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA):</strong> every keyboard-focusable element must have a visible focus indicator. Binary check — either a visible indicator exists or it does not.</p> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Focus indicator is visible for every focusable element</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Focus indicator is not removed unless replaced with a superior alternative</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Focus indicator is not obscured by other content</li> </ul> <p><strong>SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA):</strong> focus indicators on UI components must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors. Applies to the indicator itself, not the component’s normal state.</p> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Focus indicator contrast meets 3:1 against adjacent colors, measured against the indicator color and the adjacent background/component color</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Custom focus styles meet the contrast requirement (not just the default outline)</li> </ul> <p><strong>SC 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA):</strong> stricter than SC 2.4.7 — requires a minimum area equal to the focusable element’s perimeter × 2 CSS pixels, a 3:1 contrast ratio between focused and unfocused states, and the indicator must not be fully obscured by author-created content. Projects targeting AA are not required to meet this, but meeting it provides stronger accessibility; document whether your project targets it.</p> <p><strong>Behavioral screenshot-difference testing:</strong> the <a href="https://github.com/GOVTNZ/cwac/">CWAC</a> project’s <code>FocusIndicatorAudit</code> sends real Tab presses and compares whole-page screenshots before/after each press, reporting a finding when no pixels changed. It does <strong>not</strong> measure contrast (SC 1.4.11), prove a detected change is local to the focused element (its comparison is whole-page), determine an indicator is sufficiently perceptible, or distinguish a missing indicator from one obscured by other content. This repository’s own reusable implementation (<code>skills/behavioral-a11y/SKILL.md</code>, <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/playwright/focus-visible-risk.mjs"><code>focus-visible-risk.mjs</code></a>) is an independent reimplementation of the documented method that instead captures a fresh unfocused/focused screenshot pair scoped to a padded region around each element, closing some of CWAC’s whole-page limitations while introducing its own documented tradeoffs. Neither implementation, nor any screenshot-diff approach alone, verifies SC 1.4.11 (contrast) or SC 2.4.13 (minimum area). Use screenshot-difference testing as a supplementary check alongside manual verification, not as a sole focus indicator test.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-workflows-by-component-type">Testing Workflows by Component Type</h5> <p><strong>Forms:</strong> navigate to form with keyboard only → fill all fields (check Tab order) → trigger validation errors → verify errors appear and are announced → correct and revalidate → submit with Enter/Space → verify success message is announced. With a screen reader, also confirm field labels/instructions/types are announced and errors are in logical reading order.</p> <p><strong>Modal dialogs:</strong> activate trigger → verify focus moves into modal → Tab through all elements → verify Tab doesn’t leave modal (focus trap) → Escape or close button dismisses → verify focus returns to trigger. With a screen reader, confirm the modal is announced (<code>role="dialog"</code>, <code>aria-labelledby</code>) and content is in logical reading order.</p> <p><strong>Single Page Applications:</strong> click a navigation link → verify content changes → verify focus moves to main heading/content → verify page title changes → verify the route change is announced or focus provides context. Confirm the back button works and new page structure (landmarks, headings) is clear.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="documenting-test-results">Documenting Test Results</h5> <p>For each issue found, record: component/page tested (URL or name), issue description, expected behavior, numbered steps to reproduce, assistive technology name/version, browser name/version, OS name/version, and severity. Optionally include a screenshot/recording and the WCAG success criterion violated.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb598"><pre class="sourceCode markdown"><code class="sourceCode markdown"><span id="encouraging-participation-from-people-with-disabilities">Encouraging Participation from People with Disabilities</h5> <p>People with disabilities are the experts in identifying barriers and validating solutions — their lived experience surfaces issues automated tools and non-disabled testers miss, and validates that fixes actually work.</p> <ul> <li>Remove barriers to participation: clear jargon-free instructions, flexible timeframes, asynchronous feedback, compensation for testing time, accessible issue-reporting formats</li> <li>Invite diverse testers: screen reader users, keyboard-only users, voice control users, users with cognitive disabilities, users with multiple disabilities</li> <li>Credit and compensate testers fairly; create opportunities for ongoing involvement</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="quick-reference-checklists">Quick Reference Checklists</h5> <p><strong>30-minute keyboard-only test:</strong> Tab start to end; focus visible everywhere; activate all buttons (Enter/Space) and links (Enter); fill and submit a form; open/close a modal; use custom widgets; navigate menus; check for keyboard traps.</p> <p><strong>30-minute screen reader test:</strong> navigate by headings, landmarks, and form fields; read full page content; activate buttons/links; fill and submit a form; test a custom widget; verify images have alt text; verify dynamic content updates are announced.</p> <p><strong>Visual accessibility quick check:</strong> 200% zoom; focus indicator visibility; color contrast (text and UI components); content readable without color alone; light and dark modes; forced colors mode.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-18">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Keyboard-only test completed; all interactions reachable and operable</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />No keyboard traps found</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Focus order is logical</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Screen reader test completed with at least one platform combination</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All images, icons, and charts have correct text alternatives</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Dynamic content changes are announced by screen reader</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Color contrast verified for text and UI components</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Forced colors mode tested for all custom UI components</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Zoom at 200% tested; no content cut off or horizontally scrolling</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Component workflow tests run for forms, modals, and SPA navigation where applicable</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Findings documented with URL, element, WCAG SC, severity, and steps to reproduce</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-16">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <ul> <li>1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)</li> <li>1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)</li> <li>1.4.1 Use of Color (A)</li> <li>1.4.3 Contrast Minimum (AA)</li> <li>1.4.11 Non-text Contrast <code>Referrer-Policy</code>, HTTPS for sensitive data, no sensitive data in URLs</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>E-Commerce</td> <td>30–68</td> <td>No pre-checked opt-ins, availability/delivery time/cost before checkout, explicit pricing incl. tax, two+ payment methods, order confirmation email, invoices online</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Forms</td> <td>69–98</td> <td><code><label for="..."></code>, format/case-sensitivity hints, required indicated in text, password strength + show/hide, <code>aria-invalid</code>, <code>aria-describedby</code>, preserve data on error, correct <code>input type</code>/<code>autocomplete</code>, paste not blocked, disabled buttons not <code>aria-hidden</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Identification</td> <td>99–115</td> <td>Unique page titles (<code>Page \| Site</code>), <code>lang</code> attribute, favicon, address/phone in footer, two+ contact methods, response-time/hours stated</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Images/Media</td> <td>116–127</td> <td>Meaningful <code>alt</code>, empty <code>alt=""</code> for decorative, image-link alt describes destination, transcripts + synchronised captions, no autoplay, pausable media</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Internationalisation</td> <td>128–135</td> <td>International dialling codes, country in addresses, <code>hreflang</code>/visible language indicator, <code>lang</code> on <code><html></code> and inline changes, translated-language link labels</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Links</td> <td>136–152</td> <td>Descriptive anchor text (no “click here”), <code>tel:</code> protocol, new-tab warning, file type + size for downloads, no broken internal links</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Navigation</td> <td>153–172</td> <td>Public content without forced login, no nav pop-ups, homepage link, breadcrumbs, consistent nav placement, visible icon labels, skip links, visible <code>:focus-visible</code>, logical tab order, internal search, sitemap</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Newsletter</td> <td>173–179</td> <td>Confirmed opt-in, unsubscribe link, one-click unsubscribe, archives online, stated frequency</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Presentation</td> <td>180–196</td> <td>Consistent visual identity, no colour-only info, contrast 4.5:1 normal / 3:1 large text, meaning survives with styles off, 24×24px+ touch targets, no zoom blocking, responsive layout, print styles</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Security</td> <td>197–217</td> <td>HTTPS everywhere + HSTS, no mixed content, self-service password reset, no plain-text passwords, <code>X-Content-Type-Options</code>, <code>X-Frame-Options</code>/<code>frame-ancestors</code>, CSP, SRI on third-party scripts, no exposed server versions, SPF/DKIM/DMARC</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Server/Performance</td> <td>218–230</td> <td><code>robots.txt</code>, <code>sitemap.xml</code>, proper 404 status (not 200), custom error page with nav, gzip/Brotli, cache-control headers, minified CSS/JS</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Structure/Code</td> <td>231–244</td> <td>Machine-readable dates (<code><time datetime></code>), UTF-8, unique IDs, no <code>meta refresh</code>, heading hierarchy <code>h1>h2>h3</code>, tagged (not scanned) PDFs, <code><caption></code>/<code><th scope></code> on data tables</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="workflow-12">Workflow</h5> <h6 id="identify-applicable-categories">1. Identify Applicable Categories</h6> <p>Not all 14 categories apply to every project:</p> <ul> <li><strong>All web projects</strong>: Content, Forms, Identification, Images/Media, Links, Navigation, Presentation, Security, Server/Performance, Structure/Code</li> <li><strong>Add if applicable</strong>: E-Commerce (online sales), Newsletter (email marketing), Internationalisation (multi-language), Personal Data/Privacy (user accounts/data collection)</li> </ul> <h6 id="consult-the-full-rule-text">2. Consult the Full Rule Text</h6> <p>For the complete rule text, code examples, and rule numbers, consult the <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/OPQUAST_DIGITAL_QUALITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md">canonical Opquast guide</a> or the <a href="https://checklists.opquast.com/en/digital-quality/">official checklist</a> directly — this skill summarizes the categories and highest-value patterns rather than reproducing all 245 rules verbatim.</p> <h6 id="apply-during-development">3. Apply During Development</h6> <p>When generating or reviewing code, apply rules as implementation requirements:</p> <ul> <li><strong>HTML generation</strong>: Include metadata, semantic structure, accessible forms, proper alt text</li> <li><strong>CSS generation</strong>: Ensure contrast ratios, focus styles, responsive layout, print styles</li> <li><strong>Server configuration</strong>: Set security headers, enable compression, configure caching</li> <li><strong>Content review</strong>: Check date formats, link text, abbreviation expansion</li> </ul> <h6 id="validate">4. Validate</h6> <p>After implementation, verify against applicable rules. Common automated checks:</p> <ul> <li>HTML validation and heading hierarchy</li> <li>Colour contrast ratios (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text)</li> <li>Missing <code>alt</code> attributes</li> <li>Missing form labels</li> <li>Security headers present</li> <li>Broken internal links</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="essential-code-patterns">Essential Code Patterns</h5> <h6 Key mappings:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Opquast Rules</th> <th>WCAG Criteria</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>116 (decorative images <code>alt=""</code>)</td> <td>1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>117-118 (meaningful alt text)</td> <td>1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>121-122 (transcripts, captions)</td> <td>1.2.2, 1.2.3, 1.2.5</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>124-127 (no autoplay, pausable)</td> <td>1.4.2, 2.2.2</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>131-132 (lang attribute)</td> <td>3.1.1, 3.1.2</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>164 (skip links)</td> <td>2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>165 (focus visible)</td> <td>2.4.7, 2.4.11 Focus Visible/Appearance</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>166 (keyboard operable)</td> <td>2.1.1 Keyboard (A)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>167 (logical tab order)</td> <td>2.4.3 Focus Order (A)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>181 (not colour alone)</td> <td>1.4.1 Use of Color (A)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>182 (contrast)</td> <td>1.4.3, 1.4.6, 1.4.11 Contrast</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>186 (touch targets 24×24px min)</td> <td>2.5.8 Target Size Minimum (AA, WCAG 2.2)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>193 (no zoom block)</td> <td>1.4.4 Resize Text (AA)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>69-70 (labels, instructions)</td> <td>1.3.1, 3.3.2</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>79-80 (error identification)</td> <td>3.3.1, 3.3.3</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Use Opquast as a holistic quality baseline and layer WCAG testing for full accessibility compliance.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="sustainability-connection">Sustainability Connection</h5> <p>Several Opquast categories directly align with <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/SUSTAINABILITY.md">SUSTAINABILITY.md</a> and the <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/web-sustainability-guidelines/">Web Sustainability Guidelines</a>:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Server/Performance</strong> (rules 226-230): compression, caching, minification — directly reduce data transfer and energy per page view</li> <li><strong>Presentation</strong> (rule 193): not blocking zoom; (rule 194): responsive layout — reduce need for separate mobile sites</li> <li><strong>Structure/Code</strong> (rule 239): no meta refresh — avoids unnecessary page reloads</li> </ul> <p>When applying Opquast Server/Performance rules, cross-reference with <code>SUSTAINABILITY.md</code> for additional guidance on carbon-aware delivery and asset optimisation.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-19">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <p>Apply to every project; skip categories not in scope:</p> <p><strong>Content & Identification</strong> * [ ] <code><meta name="description"></code> and OG tags on every page * [ ] Unique <code><title></code> in <code>Page | Site</code> format * [ ] <code><html lang="..."></code> present and correct * [ ] <code><link rel="icon"></code> present * [ ] Privacy policy linked from footer * [ ] At least two contact methods available</p> <p><strong>Forms</strong> * [ ] Every field has programmatically associated <code><label></code> * [ ] Native <code>required</code> used; <code>aria-required</code> omitted on native inputs * [ ] Required state indicated in visible text, not asterisk/colour alone * [ ] <code>aria-invalid="true"</code> set on invalid fields * [ ] Error messages associated via <code>aria-describedby</code>; prior data preserved on error * [ ] Correct <code>input type</code> and <code>autocomplete</code> values * [ ] Paste not blocked; disabled buttons not hidden via <code>aria-hidden</code></p> <p><strong>Images & Media</strong> * [ ] Decorative images have <code>alt=""</code> * [ ] Informative images have descriptive <code>alt</code>; image links describe the destination * [ ] All video has synchronised captions * [ ] All audio has text transcript * [ ] No autoplay (audio or video); all media pausable</p> <p><strong>Navigation & Keyboard</strong> * [ ] Skip link present and functional * [ ] <code>:focus-visible</code> styles defined; <code>outline: none</code> not used without replacement * [ ] All content keyboard operable; logical tab order * [ ] Breadcrumbs or equivalent location indicator present</p> <p><strong>Presentation</strong> * [ ] Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for normal text; ≥ 3:1 for large text and UI components * [ ] Information not conveyed by colour alone * [ ] <code>user-scalable=no</code> and <code>maximum-scale</code> not used * [ ] Touch targets ≥ 24×24px (44×44 recommended) * [ ] Print styles hide navigation; reveal link URLs</p> <p><strong>Security</strong> * [ ] HTTPS on all pages; HTTP redirects to HTTPS; no mixed content * [ ] HSTS header present * [ ] <code>X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff</code> present * [ ] <code>X-Frame-Options</code> or CSP <code>frame-ancestors</code> present * [ ] CSP header present * [ ] SRI on all third-party scripts/stylesheets * [ ] Server/framework version headers not exposed</p> <p><strong>Server/Performance</strong> * [ ] <code>robots.txt</code> present; <code>sitemap.xml</code> present * [ ] Proper <code>404</code> status for missing pages (not <code>200</code>) * [ ] Compression enabled (gzip or Brotli) * [ ] Cache-control headers on static assets * [ ] CSS and JS minified</p> <p><strong>Structure/Code</strong> * [ ] <code><meta charset="UTF-8"></code> in every <code><head></code> * [ ] No duplicate <code>id</code> attributes within a page * [ ] No <code><meta http-equiv="refresh"></code> * [ ] Heading hierarchy correct (<code>h1</code> > <code>h2</code> > <code>h3</code>, no skips) * [ ] Data tables have <code><caption></code> and <code><th scope="..."></code> * [ ] Internal PDFs are tagged (selectable text), not scanned images</p> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-17">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <p>See WCAG relationship table above. You are a <strong>read-only</strong> agent — you never edit source files, configuration, or documentation. You are invoked internally by <code>web-accessibility-wizard</code> to run live browser-based accessibility tests.</p> <p><strong>Knowledge domains:</strong> Playwright Testing, Web Severity Scoring</p> <hr /> <h4 id="capabilities-4">Capabilities</h4> <h5 id="full-behavioral-scan">1. Full Behavioral Scan</h5> <p>When invoked with a URL and scan profile, execute the following tests in order:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><p><strong>Keyboard Flow Mapping</strong> — Call <code>run_playwright_keyboard_scan</code> to record the complete Tab sequence, detect keyboard traps, and identify unreachable interactive elements.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Dynamic State Scanning</strong> — Call <code>run_playwright_state_scan</code> to click triggers (accordions, menus, modals, tabs) and run axe-core against each revealed state.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Responsive Viewport Scanning</strong> — Call <code>run_playwright_viewport_scan</code> at widths [320, 768, 1024, 1440] to detect reflow failures, horizontal scroll, and undersized touch targets.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Rendered Contrast Verification</strong> — Call <code>run_playwright_contrast_scan</code> to extract computed foreground/background colors and calculate contrast ratios after full CSS cascade resolution.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Accessibility Tree Snapshot</strong> — Call <code>run_playwright_a11y_tree</code> to capture the browser’s accessibility tree for landmark/heading/role/name verification.</p></li> </ol> <h5 id="focus-management-tests">2. Focus Management Tests</h5> <p>Combine keyboard and state scans for focused testing:</p> <ul> <li>Click a modal trigger → verify <code>activeElement</code> moves to the modal</li> <li>Close the modal → verify <code>activeElement</code> returns to the trigger</li> <li>Navigate to a skip link → press Enter → verify focus moves to main content</li> </ul> <h5 id="targeted-scans">3. Targeted Scans</h5> <p>When invoked with specific test parameters:</p> <ul> <li><strong>keyboard-only</strong> — Run only keyboard flow mapping</li> <li><strong>states-only</strong> — Run only dynamic state scanning</li> <li><strong>viewport-only</strong> — Run only responsive viewport scanning</li> <li><strong>contrast-only</strong> — Run only contrast verification</li> <li><strong>tree-only</strong> — Run only accessibility tree snapshot</li> </ul> <h4 id="graceful-degradation">Graceful Degradation</h4> <p>If Playwright is not installed:</p> <ul> <li>Report that behavioral scans are unavailable</li> <li>List the install command: <code>npm install -D playwright @axe-core/playwright && npx playwright install chromium</code></li> <li>Return a “degraded” status so the wizard can proceed with static-only analysis</li> </ul> <p>If <span class="citation" data-cites="axe-core/playwright">@axe-core/playwright</span> is not installed but Playwright is:</p> <ul> <li>Run keyboard scan, contrast scan, and accessibility tree (Playwright-only tools)</li> <li>Skip state scan and viewport scan (require <span class="citation" data-cites="axe-core/playwright">@axe-core/playwright</span>)</li> <li>Report partial results with a note about the missing dependency</li> </ul> <h4 id="wcag-coverage">WCAG Coverage</h4> <p>Each Analyzing changes and generating review document... Review ready.</code></pre> <p>For delta detection (reviewing a PR that was already reviewed):</p> <pre class="text"><code> Loading previous review for PR #{N}... Comparing against current diff... Delta detected: {N} new comments addressed, {M} findings remain open.</code></pre> <hr /> <h4 id="confidence-levels-5">Confidence Levels</h4> <p>Every finding in the review document must include a confidence level:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 35%" /> <col style="width: 65%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>When to Use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>High</strong></td> <td>Pattern definitively identified, multiple signals corroborate it</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Medium</strong></td> <td>Likely issue, but context outside the diff might explain it</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Low</strong></td> <td>Possible concern; flag for human judgment, not blocking</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Format in the review table:</p> <pre class="text"><code>| File | Finding | Severity | Confidence | |------|---------|----------|------------| | auth.ts | Token stored in localStorage | Critical | **High** | | utils.ts | No null check before .map() | Warning | **Medium** |</code></pre> <hr /> <h4 id="delta-tracking-3">Delta Tracking</h4> <p>When a previous review document exists for this PR:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 40%" /> <col style="width: 60%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Status</th> <th>Definition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Resolved</td> <td>Finding was in previous review; no longer present in diff</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>New</td> <td>Not in previous review; newly introduced</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Persistent</td> <td>Still present from previous review</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Regressed</td> <td>Was resolved in a previous round; has reappeared</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Show a delta summary at the top of the review:</p> <pre class="text"><code>## Changes Since Last Review | Change | Finding | |--------|---------| | Resolved | SQL injection risk in query builder | | New | Missing error boundary in UserPanel | | Persistent (#2) | No rate limiting on login endpoint |</code></pre> <hr /> <h4 id="behavioral-rules-20">Behavioral Rules</h4> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Always show Change Map first.</strong> Before any diff, output the file-level change summary with categorization (feature/bugfix/refactor/test/config).</li> <li><strong>Never show code without context.</strong> Every snippet includes 5 surrounding lines minimum.</li> <li><strong>Confidence on every finding.</strong> No finding goes in a review document without a High/Medium/Low confidence tag.</li> <li><strong>Delta-check before writing.</strong> If a review document already exists for this PR, run delta detection before generating a new one.</li> <li><strong>Check workspace context first.</strong> Look for scan config files (<code>.a11y-*-config.json</code>) and previous audit reports in the workspace root.</li> <li><strong>Narrate the asset pull.</strong> Use / announcements for metadata, diff, CI, and analysis steps.</li> <li><strong>Never post a review comment without confirmation.</strong> Preview the comment, ask for approval, then submit.</li> <li><strong>Flag security-sensitive files explicitly.</strong> Auth, crypto, tokens, and permissions changes get a dedicated security callout.</li> <li><strong>Surface test ratio.</strong> Flag any PR where test lines added < 20% of production lines changed.</li> <li><strong>Commit story before verdict.</strong> Reconstruct the narrative from commit messages before assigning an approval verdict.</li> <li><strong>Parallel asset collection.</strong> Fetch metadata, diff, CI status, and linked issues simultaneously - don’t wait for each before starting the next.</li> <li><strong>Never truncate diffs silently.</strong> If a diff is too large to show fully, say so and offer to show it file-by-file.</li> <li><strong>Dual output always.</strong> Every review document is saved as both <code>.md</code> and <code>.html</code> with full accessibility standards.</li> <li><strong>Release pressure gets a banner.</strong> If the PR targets a release branch or milestone, show a visible callout at the top of the review.</li> <li><strong>Reviewer consensus summary.</strong> When other reviews exist, summarize agreement/disagreement - never leave the user to read all threads manually.</li> </ol> <h4 id="resilience-architecture-v7.0-enhancement-1">2.0: RESILIENCE ARCHITECTURE (v7.0 Enhancement)</h6> <p><strong>Key improvements over v6.0:</strong></p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> id="graceful-degradation-decision-tree-1">2.3: Graceful Degradation Decision Tree</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Tools Succeeded</th> <th>Action</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>3/3</strong></td> <td>✅ Full coverage - proceed with all results</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>2/3</strong></td> <td>⚠️ Good coverage - note which tool failed in report</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>1/3</strong></td> <td>⚠️ Basic coverage - proceed but flag limited confidence</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>0/3</strong></td> <td>❌ Retry with Vibium MCP, or document failure</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="mandatory---check-for-videos-and-trigger-pipeline-1">2.4: MANDATORY - Check for Videos and Trigger Pipeline</h6> <p>After reading <code>aria-label="[DESCRIPTION]"</code> You output: <code>aria-label="Add to shopping cart"</code> because you understand context.</p> <h6 id="context-analysis-use-your-reasoning-1">3.1: Context class="sourceCode" id="cb640"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb640-1"><a href="#cb640-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"icon-cart"</span><span class="kw">></span>...<span class="kw"></svg></span></span> <span class="kw"></div></span></span></code></pre></div></li> <li><p><strong>INFER PURPOSE</strong> from:</p> <ul> <li>Class names: <code>add-to-cart</code>, <code>wishlist</code>, <code>menu-toggle</code></li> <li>Parent context: Inside <code>.product-card</code> with product data</li> <li>Icon classes: <code>icon-cart</code>, <code>icon-heart</code>, <code>icon-search</code></li> <li>Nearby text: Product name, price, “Add to bag”</li> <li>Page section: Header nav vs product grid vs checkout</li> </ul></li> <li><p><strong>GENERATE SPECIFIC FIX</strong>:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb641"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb641-1"><a href="#cb641-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">></span></span></code></pre></div></li> </ol> <h6 id="confidence-scoring-1">3.2: Confidence Scoring</h6> <p>Rate your confidence in each fix: - <strong>0.9+</strong>: Clear context id="step-4-user-impact-analysis-1">STEP 4: USER IMPACT ANALYSIS</h5> <p>For each violation, calculate user impact:</p> <h6 id="affected-user-groups-1">4.1: Affected User Groups</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Violation Type</th> <th>Affected Groups</th> <th>% of Users</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Missing alt text</td> <td>Blind, low-vision</td> <td>7-10%</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Missing form labels</td> <td>Blind, screen reader users</td> <td>5-8%</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Low color contrast</td> <td>Low-vision, color blind</td> <td>8-12%</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>No keyboard access</td> <td>Motor impaired, power users</td> <td>10-15%</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Missing captions</td> <td>Deaf, hard-of-hearing</td> <td>5-7%</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Flashing content</td> <td>Seizure sensitive</td> <td>0.5-1%</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Complex language</td> <td>Cognitive impairment</td> <td>10-15%</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="impact-severity-classification-1">4.2: Impact Severity Classification</h6> <pre><code>BLOCKS-USAGE: User cannot complete task at all - Missing form labels on required fields - Keyboard traps - Critical buttons without accessible names IMPAIRS-USAGE: User can complete task with difficulty - Low contrast (can read with effort) - Missing skip links (tedious navigation) - Incorrect heading structure (confusing) MINOR-INCONVENIENCE: Suboptimal but functional - Empty alt on decorative images - Redundant ARIA - Non-semantic HTML that works</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-5-roi-based-prioritization-1">STEP 5: ROI-BASED PRIORITIZATION</h5> <p>Calculate priority for each remediation:</p> <h6 id="priority-formula-1">5.1: Priority Formula</h6> <pre><code>PRIORITY_SCORE = (IMPACT_WEIGHT × USERS_AFFECTED) / EFFORT_HOURS Where: - IMPACT_WEIGHT: Critical=10, Serious=7, Moderate=4, Minor=1 - USERS_AFFECTED: Estimated % of users impacted - EFFORT_HOURS: Estimated fix time (0.25 to 8 hours)</code></pre> <h6 id="effort-estimation-guide-1">5.2: Effort Estimation Guide</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Fix Type</th> <th>Effort</th> <th>Complexity</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add aria-label</td> <td>0.25h</td> <td>Trivial</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Add alt text</td> <td>0.25h</td> <td>Trivial</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add form label</td> <td>0.5h</td> <td>Simple</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Fix color contrast</td> <td>0.5h</td> <td>Simple</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add skip links</td> <td>1h</td> <td>Simple</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Fix heading structure</td> <td>2h</td> <td>Medium</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add keyboard navigation</td> <td>4h</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Implement focus trap</td> <td>4h</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Add video captions</td> <td>8h</td> <td>High</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="priority-output-format-1">5.3: Priority Output Format</h6> <pre><code>| Rank | Violation | Impact | Users | Effort | ROI Score | |------|-----------|--------|-------|--------|-----------| | 1 | Form labels missing | Critical | 15% | 0.5h | 300 | | 2 | Keyboard trap | Critical | 12% | 4h | 30 | | 3 | Low contrast | Serious | 10% id="compliance-scoring-1">6.1: Compliance Scoring</h6> <pre><code>COMPLIANCE_SCORE = (PASSED_CRITERIA / TOTAL_CRITERIA) × 100 Production Ready if: ✓ Score ≥ 85% ✓ Zero critical violations ✓ Fewer than Document the failure reason in audit-summary.md 2. Still create video-captions violation in violations.json 3. Add remediation instructions WITHOUT generated captions 4. Mark video pipeline as “blocked” not “skipped”</p> <h6 id="analyze-each-frame-with-claude-vision-mandatory-1">7.3: Analyze Each Frame with Claude Vision (MANDATORY)</h6> <p><strong>USE THE READ TOOL ON EACH FRAME IMAGE.</strong></p> <p>Claude Code has native vision capabilities. When you Read an image file, you SEE it.</p> <pre><code>Read /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_01.jpg Read /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_02.jpg Read /tmp/a11y-work/frames/frame_03.jpg ... (continue for all frames)</code></pre> <p><strong>For EACH frame, describe:</strong> - <strong>SCENE</strong>: Setting, environment, lighting, location - <strong>PEOPLE</strong>: Who appears, what they’re doing, expressions, clothing - <strong>PRODUCTS</strong>: Items shown (for e-commerce: product names, colors, styles) - <strong>TEXT</strong>: Any visible text, logos, signs, prices - <strong>ACTION</strong>: Movement, transitions, what’s happening</p> <p><strong>Example output after reading frame_01.jpg:</strong></p> <pre><code>Frame 1 (0:00-0:03): A woman in white Adidas sneakers running on a forest trail. Morning light filters through trees. She wears black athletic leggings and a gray tank top. The Adidas three-stripe logo is visible on her shoes.</code></pre> <p><strong>THIS IS THE LLM VALUE.</strong> Generic tools output “[DESCRIBE CONTENT]”. You output actual descriptions because you can SEE the image.</p> <hr /> <p><strong>FALLBACK: If Read tool fails on images</strong></p> <p>Try Anthropic API directly:</p> <div class="sourceCode" from: - Video filename: “product-demo.mp4” → product demonstration - Page context: product page → product showcase - Surrounding text: nearby headings and descriptions</p> <p><strong>Document for each frame:</strong> - <strong>SCENE</strong>: Setting, environment, lighting - <strong>PEOPLE</strong>: Who, actions, expressions, clothing - <strong>OBJECTS</strong>: Products, props, equipment - <strong>TEXT</strong>: Visible text, logos, signs - <strong>ACTION</strong>: Movement, transitions - <strong>COLORS</strong>: Dominant colors, accessibility-relevant</p> <h6 id="generate-webvtt-captions-1">7.4: Generate WebVTT Captions</h6> <pre class="vtt"><code>WEBVTT Kind: captions Language: {detected-language} 00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.000 [Description from frame_01 analysis] 00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:06.000 [Description from frame_02 analysis]</code></pre> <h6 id="generate-audio-descriptions-1">7.5: Generate Audio Descriptions</h6> <pre class="vtt"><code>WEBVTT Kind: descriptions Language: en 00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.000 SCENE: [Detailed scene for blind users] VISUAL: [What's on screen] TEXT: [Any readable text] ACTION: [What's happening]</code></pre> <hr /> <h5 id="step-8-generate-comprehensive-reports-1">STEP 8: GENERATE COMPREHENSIVE REPORTS</h5> <h6 id="required-output-files-1">8.1: Required Output Files</h6> <p>Save ALL files to id="nvda-windows---free-1">10.1: NVDA (Windows - Free)</h6> <pre><code>1. Download: https://www.nvaccess.org/download/ 2. Install and start NVDA (Ctrl+Alt+N) 3. Navigate to audited page Key Commands: - H: Jump through headings - F: Jump through form fields - B: Jump through buttons - T: Jump through tables - K: Jump through links - D: Jump through landmarks - Tab: Move through focusable elements Verify: - [ ] All headings announced with correct level - [ ] Form fields announce labels - [ ] Buttons announce purpose - [ ] Images announce alt text or "decorative" - [ ] Dynamic content changes announced (aria-live)</code></pre> <h6 id="voiceover-macos---built-in-1">10.2: VoiceOver (macOS - Built-in)</h6> <pre><code>1. Enable: System Preferences → Accessibility → VoiceOver 2. Toggle: Cmd+F5 3. Navigate to audited page Key Commands: - VO+U: Open rotor (headings, links, forms, landmarks) - VO+Space: Activate element - VO+Right/Left: Move through content - VO+Cmd+H: Jump to next heading Verify: - [ ] Rotor shows all headings hierarchically - [ ] Forms are navigable and labels announced - [ ] Focus order matches visual order - [ ] All content is reachable</code></pre> <h6 id="jaws-windows---commercial-1">10.3: JAWS (Windows - Commercial)</h6> <pre><code>1. Trial: https://www.freedomscientific.com/products/software/jaws/ 2. correctly - [ ] Forms mode activates in forms - [ ] All ARIA roles announced properly</code></pre> <h6 id="screen-reader-testing-checklist-2">10.4: Screen Reader Testing Checklist</h6> <table> <thead> class="odd"> <td><strong>Parallel Execution</strong></td> <td>All 3 tools run simultaneously via Promise.allSettled</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Per-Tool Timeouts</strong></td> <td>axe: 60s, pa11y: 60s, Lighthouse: 90s</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Retry with Backoff</strong></td> <td>2 retries per tool with exponential backoff</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Graceful Degradation</strong></td> <td>Continue if 1+ tools succeed</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Progressive Output</strong></td> <td>Results stream as tools complete</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Bot Protection</strong></td> <td>Stealth mode, random delays, cookie dismissal</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="expected-output-structure-1">Expected Output Rules</h5> <h6 id="execution-rules-v7.0-1">Execution Rules (v7.0)</h6> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> run multi-tool scan with <strong>parallel execution</strong> (Promise.allSettled)</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> continue if at least <strong>1 of 3 tools</strong> succeeds (graceful degradation)</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> document which tools failed and why in audit-summary.md</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> use per-tool timeouts (60s/60s/90s) not global timeout</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> retry failed tools with exponential backoff before giving up</li> </ol> <h6 id="quality-rules-1">Quality Rules</h6> <ol start="6" type="1"> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> analyze context before generating fixes</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> include confidence scores with remediation</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> calculate user impact and ROI</li> <li><strong>ALWAYS</strong> generate copy-paste ready code</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> generate placeholder/template fixes</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> skip video pipeline if videos detected</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> complete without remediation.md</li> <li><strong>NEVER</strong> fail audit just because 1-2 tools failed (use graceful degradation)</li> </ol> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="qe-accessibility-testing">QE Accessibility <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe">proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe/tree/38caad1bdc872d2b520ee120fcda676e45ea7ff9/.kiro/skills/qe-accessibility-testing">.kiro/skills/qe-accessibility-testing</a></li> <li><strong>Tags:</strong> accessibility, wcag, a11y, screen-reader, ada, section-508, inclusive</li> </ul> <p>WCAG 2.2 compliance testing, screen reader validation, and inclusive design verification. Use when ensuring legal compliance (ADA, Section 508), testing for disabilities, or building accessible applications for 1 billion disabled users globally.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>qe-accessibility-testing/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="accessibility-testing-2">Accessibility Testing</h4> <p><default_to_action> When testing accessibility or ensuring compliance: 1. APPLY POUR principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust 2. TEST with keyboard-only navigation (Tab, Enter, Escape) 3. VALIDATE with screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS) 4. CHECK color contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text) 5. AUTOMATE with axe-core, integrate in CI/CD pipeline</p> <p><strong>Quick A11y Checklist:</strong> - All images have alt text (or alt=“” for decorative) - All form fields have labels - Color is never the only indicator - Focus visible on all interactive elements - Keyboard navigation works throughout</p> <p><strong>Critical Success Factors:</strong> - Automated testing catches 30-50% of issues - Manual testing with real assistive tech required - Include users with disabilities in testing </default_to_action></p> <h5 id="quick-reference-card-3">Quick Reference Card</h5> <h6 id="when-to-use-3">When to Use</h6> <ul> <li>Legal compliance (ADA, Section 508, EU Directive)</li> <li>New feature development</li> <li>Before release validation</li> <li>Accessibility audits</li> </ul> <h6 id="wcag-2.2-levels-1">WCAG 2.2 Levels</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Target</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>A</strong></td> <td>Basic accessibility</td> <td>Minimum legal</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>AA</strong></td> <td>Standard (most orgs)</td> <td>Industry standard</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>AAA</strong></td> <td>Enhanced</td> <td>Specialized sites</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="pour-principles-1">POUR Principles</h6> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 35%" /> <col style="width: 29%" /> <col style="width: 35%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Principle</th> <th>Meaning</th> <th>Key Tests</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Perceivable</strong></td> <td>Can perceive content</td> <td>Alt text, contrast, captions</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Operable</strong></td> <td>Can operate UI</td> <td>Keyboard, no seizures, navigation</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Understandable</strong></td> <td>Can understand</td> <td>Clear labels, predictable, errors</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Robust</strong></td> <td>Works with assistive tech</td> <td>Valid HTML, ARIA</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="color-contrast-requirements-1">Color Contrast Requirements</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Content</th> <th>AA Ratio</th> <th>AAA Ratio</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Normal text</td> <td>4.5:1</td> <td>7:1</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <li><p><strong>Read-only.</strong> Never create, edit, or close issues. Never comment on PRs. Never modify source code.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Structured output always.</strong> Return JSON findings, not prose. The calling orchestrator formats for the user.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Fail gracefully.</strong> If the scanner is not configured, return <code>{"scannerDetected": false}</code> – do not error.</p></li> <li><p><strong>No GitHub API calls without repo context.</strong> Always require the target repository before querying.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Respect rate limits.</strong> Batch issue queries where possible. Do not paginate beyond 100 issues per query.</p></li> <li><p><strong>Announce progress.</strong> Report each step as it completes:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Checking for GitHub Accessibility Scanner workflow... Scanner detected: .github/workflows/a11y-scan.yml Fetching open scanner issues (12 found)... Fetching recently closed scanner issues (5 found)... Normalizing findings... Checking Copilot fix status... Scanner bridge complete -- 17 issues processed.</code></pre></li> </ol> <h4 id="reference-files-44">Reference files</h4> <p>Read one only when the task reaches it. Do not read them all up front.</p> <ul> <li><code>references/capabilities.md</code> - Capabilities</li> </ul> <h4 id="output-contract-86">Output contract</h4> <p>Return only JSON matching <code>skills/a11y-core/schemas/findings.schema.json</code>.
