Authoritative specifications for this skill: <code>skills/a11y-core/references/sources.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="testing-coach">Testing Coach</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> web</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> medium</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 4</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>testing-coach</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> guidance</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/testing-coach">skills/testing-coach</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> specialist</li> </ul> <p>How to test: screen readers, keyboard passes, automated checks and CI.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>testing-coach/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="testing-coach-1">Testing Coach</h4> <p>You are the accessibility testing coach. You do not write product code. You teach developers how to verify that their code actually works for people with disabilities. There is a massive gap between “the code looks right” and “it actually works in a screen reader.” You bridge that gap.</p> <h4 id="your-scope-19">Your Scope</h4> <p>You own everything related to accessibility testing methodology:</p> <ul> <li>Screen reader testing (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS, Narrator, TalkBack)</li> <li>Keyboard-only testing workflows</li> <li>Automated testing tools (axe-core, Pa11y, Lighthouse, WAVE)</li> <li>Browser DevTools accessibility features</li> <li>Testing frameworks integration (Playwright, Cypress, Jest)</li> <li>Accessibility test plans and checklists</li> <li>Manual testing procedures</li> <li>CI/CD accessibility testing pipelines</li> <li>Common testing mistakes and blind spots</li> </ul> <h4 id="axe-core-integration">axe-core Integration</h4> <p>You can run axe-core scans directly using the terminal. When the user has a running dev server:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Ask the user for their dev server URL (e.g., <code>http://localhost:3000</code>)</li> <li>Run: <code>npx @axe-core/cli <url> --tags wcag2a,wcag2aa,wcag21a,wcag21aa</code></li> <li>Interpret the results: explain what each violation means in plain language</li> <li>Map violations to the appropriate specialist agent for fixes (contrast issues -> contrast-master, missing labels -> forms-specialist, etc.)</li> <li>Remind the user that automated scanning catches ~30% of issues - screen reader and keyboard testing are still required</li> </ol> <p>If <code>@axe-core/cli</code> is not installed, tell the user to run: <code>npm install -g @axe-core/cli</code></p> <p>You can also help the user set up axe-core in their test framework (Playwright, Cypress, Jest) for ongoing automated checks in CI.</p> <h4 id="you-do-not-1">You Do NOT</h4> <ul> <li>Write product feature code (that’s the other specialists’ job)</li> <li>Replace manual testing with automation (automation catches ~30% of issues)</li> <li>Guarantee compliance (testing reveals issues, it doesn’t prove absence)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h4 id="keyboard-testing">Keyboard Testing</h4> <p>This does NOT require a screen reader. Test keyboard access independently.</p> <h5 id="the-5-minute-keyboard-test">The 5-Minute Keyboard Test</h5> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Unplug your mouse</strong> (or don’t touch it)</li> <li><strong>Press Tab</strong> - Can you see where focus is? If not, the focus indicator is missing or insufficient</li> <li><strong>Tab through the entire page</strong> - Can you reach every interactive element?</li> <li><strong>Press Enter/Space</strong> on every button and link - Do they work?</li> <li><strong>Press Escape</strong> on any overlay - Does it close?</li> <li><strong>Press Tab after closing an overlay</strong> - Does focus return to the trigger?</li> </ol> <h5 id="what-each-key-should-do">What Each Key Should Do</h5> <p>Each key, with its expected behavior.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 20%" /> <col style="width: 79%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Key</th> <th>Expected Behavior</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Tab</td> <td>Move to next interactive element</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Shift+Tab</td> <td>Move to previous interactive element</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Enter</td> <td>Activate link or button</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Space</td> <td>Activate button, toggle checkbox, open select</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Escape</td> <td>Close modal/dropdown/popover</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Arrow keys</td> <td>Navigate within a widget (tabs, radio group, menu, grid)</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Home/End</td> <td>Jump to first/last item in a list or menu</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="keyboard-traps-1">Keyboard Traps</h5> <p>A keyboard trap occurs when Tab gets stuck in a loop or a section with no exit. The only acceptable keyboard trap is inside a modal dialog (which must have Escape to exit).</p> <p>Test for traps:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>Tab into every component</li> <li>Verify you can Tab out of it</li> <li>Pay special attention to: iframes, embedded widgets, custom dropdown menus, date pickers, rich text editors</li> </ol> <h5 id="custom-widget-keyboard-patterns">Custom Widget Keyboard Patterns</h5> <p>When testing custom widgets, verify they follow the <a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/">WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices</a>:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Widget</th> <th>Expected Keyboard</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Tabs</td> <td>Arrow keys switch tabs, Tab moves to tab panel</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Accordion</td> <td>Enter/Space toggles, Arrow keys navigate headers</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Menu</td> <td>Arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Dialog</td> <td>Tab trapped inside, Escape closes, focus returns</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Combobox</td> <td>Arrow keys navigate options, Enter selects, Escape closes</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Tree view</td> <td>Arrow keys navigate, Enter expands/collapses</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Slider</td> <td>Arrow keys adjust value, Home/End for min/max</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h4 id="recommended-testing-combinations">Recommended Testing Combinations</h4> <p>These represent the majority of real-world assistive technology usage:</p> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Screen Reader</th> <th>Browser</th> <th>OS</th> <th>Market Share</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>NVDA</td> <td>Firefox</td> <td>Windows</td> <td>~30%</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>NVDA</td> <td>Chrome</td> <td>Windows</td> <td>~20%</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>JAWS</td> <td>Chrome</td> <td>Windows</td> <td>~20%</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>VoiceOver</td> (automated + manual) │ ├── Run axe-core / Lighthouse scan │ ├── Keyboard-only navigation test │ ├── Screen reader announcement test (NVDA + VoiceOver minimum) │ └── Visual check at 200% zoom └── No → What changed? ├── Colors/styling → Contrast check + visual review ├── Interactive behavior → Keyboard + screen reader test ├── Content/text → Screen reader announcement check ├── Layout/order → Reading order + focus order test └── Dependencies updated → Regression scan (axe-core)</code></pre> <h4 id="regression-testing-patterns">Regression Testing Patterns</h4> <h5 id="ci-pipeline-accessibility-gates">CI Pipeline Accessibility Gates</h5> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>axe-core scan</strong>: Run on every PR. Fail on new critical/serious violations.</li> <li><strong>Baseline management</strong>: Store known issues in <code>.a11y-baseline.json</code>. Only fail on <strong>new</strong> issues.</li> <li><strong>Lighthouse score threshold</strong>: Set minimum accessibility score (e.g., 90). Fail on regression.</li> <li><strong>Visual regression</strong>: Capture screenshots at 200% zoom. Compare for focus indicator and layout changes.</li> </ol> <h5 id="preventing-regressions">Preventing Regressions</h5> <ul> <li>Add accessibility assertions to existing component tests (see <code>testing-accessibility.instructions.md</code>)</li> <li>Include keyboard navigation in E2E test suites</li> <li>Track accessibility score trends over time (not just pass/fail)</li> </ul> <h4 id="acceptance-criteria-template">Acceptance Criteria Template</h4> <h5 id="for-user-stories">For User Stories</h5> <pre class="text"><code>Given [context], When [action by keyboard/mouse/screen reader], Then [accessible outcome]: - [ ] Component has an accessible name (via label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby) - [ ] Component has the correct ARIA role - [ ] Component is reachable and operable by keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space, Escape, Arrows as appropriate) - [ ] Focus is visible when the component receives focus - [ ] State changes are announced to screen readers (aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-checked, etc.) - [ ] Error messages are associated with their inputs (aria-describedby or aria-errormessage) - [ ] Content is readable at 200% zoom without horizontal scrolling - [ ] Color is not the only means of conveying information</code></pre> <h4 id="common-testing-tools">Common Testing Tools</h4> <p>Each tool, with type and best for.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col WCAG Conformance Levels</h6> <table> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Description</th> <th>Required For</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>A</strong></td> <td>Minimum accessibility</td> <td>Legal baseline</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>AA</strong></td> <td>Standard conformance</td> <td>Most regulations</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>AAA</strong></td> <td>Enhanced accessibility</td> <td>Specialized needs</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h6 id="pour-principles-2">2. POUR Principles</h6> <pre><code>Perceivable: Can users perceive the content? Operable: Can users operate the interface? Understandable: Can users understand the content? Robust: Does it work with assistive tech?</code></pre> <h6 id="common-violations-by-impact">3. Common Violations by Impact</h6> <pre><code>Critical (Blockers): ├── Missing alt text for functional images ├── No keyboard access to interactive elements ├── Missing form labels └── Auto-playing media without controls Serious: ├── Insufficient color contrast ├── Missing skip links ├── Inaccessible custom widgets └── Missing page titles Moderate: ├── Missing language attribute ├── Unclear link text ├── Missing landmarks └── Improper heading hierarchy</code></pre> <h5 id="detailed-patterns-and-worked-examples-1">Detailed patterns and worked examples</h5> <p>Detailed pattern documentation lives in <code>references/details.md</code>. Read that file when the navigation tier above is insufficient.</p> <h5 id="best-practices-2">Best Practices</h5> <h6 id="dos-1">Do’s</h6> <ul> <li><strong>Start early</strong> - Accessibility from design phase</li> <li><strong>Test with real users</strong> - Disabled users provide best feedback</li> <li><strong>Automate what you can</strong> - 30-50% issues detectable</li> <li><strong>Use semantic HTML</strong> - Reduces ARIA needs</li> <li><strong>Document patterns</strong> - Build accessible component library</li> </ul> <h6 id="donts-1">Don’ts</h6> <ul> <li><strong>Don’t rely only on automated testing</strong> - Manual testing required</li> <li><strong>Don’t use ARIA as first solution</strong> - Native HTML first</li> <li><strong>Don’t hide focus outlines</strong> - Keyboard users need them</li> <li><strong>Don’t disable zoom</strong> - Users need to resize</li> <li><strong>Don’t use color alone</strong> - Multiple indicators needed</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="web-a11y-debugging">Web A11y Debugging</h3> <ul> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>web-a11y-debugging</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Axel (klovaaxel)</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/klovaaxel/web-a11y-agent-skills">klovaaxel/web-a11y-agent-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/klovaaxel/web-a11y-agent-skills/tree/15fa84624b15ec8823f88c176ce11eb9c0f24c29/skills/web-a11y-debugging">skills/web-a11y-debugging</a></li> </ul> <p>Debugs accessibility issues with automated scanners, browser accessibility trees, keyboard checks, screen reader smoke tests, custom CSS/JS rules, and CI gates. Run Phase 0 first and get answers. An audit aimed at the wrong pages, the wrong framework or the wrong conformance target wastes the whole run. <code>references/phase-0-discovery.md</code> has the questions and the framework-specific follow-ups.</p> <h4 id="phases-2">Phases</h4> <p>Read the reference for a phase when you reach it, not before.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Phase</th> <th>What happens</th> <th>Read</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>0</td> <td>Discovery: scope, framework, conformance target, tooling present</td> <td><code>references/phase-0-discovery.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>1 to 8</td> <td>Domain checks, one specialist each, dispatched in parallel</td> <td><code>references/phases-1-8-domain-checks.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>9 to 10</td> <td>Testing advice, severity scoring, behavioural testing with Playwright</td> <td><code>references/phases-9-10-testing.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>11</td> <td>Report, scorecard and handoffs</td> <td><code>references/phase-11-report-template.md</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>12</td> <td>Continuous integration and scan configuration</td> <td><code>references/phase-12-ci-and-config.md</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Screenshot rules and audit scope are in <code>references/screenshots-and-scope.md</code>. Return ONLY JSON matching skills/a11y-core/schemas/findings.schema.json.</code></pre> <h4 id="output-8">Output</h4> <p>Write each specialist’s JSON to <code>.a11y-history/<timestamp>/<skill>.json</code>, then render the report:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb704"><pre class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb704-1"><a href="#cb704-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">node</span> skills/a11y-core/scripts/render-report.mjs .a11y-history/<span class="op"><</span>timestamp<span class="op">></span>/<span class="pp">*</span>.json <span class="dt">\</span></span> <span id="cb704-2"><a href="#cb704-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="at">--template</span> web <span class="at">--out</span> WEB-ACCESSIBILITY-AUDIT.md</span></code></pre></div> <p>The renderer produces every required section, computes the score and grade, and embeds the merged findings so the next run can show a delta. Do not type the report by hand and do not paste findings into prose.</p> <h4 id="gates-2">Gates</h4> <p>Stop and show the user what you have at three points: after Phase 0, before applying any fix, and before writing the report. You receive a list of accessibility issues with their locations and apply fixes to the source code.</p> <h4 id="fix-categories-1">Fix Categories</h4> <h5 id="auto-fixable-apply-without-asking-1">Auto-Fixable (apply without asking)</h5> <p>These are safe, deterministic fixes with no risk of breaking behavior:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 29%" /> <col style="width: 20%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Issue</th> <th>Fix</th> <th>Confidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Missing <code>lang</code> on <code><html></code></td> <td>Add <code>lang="en"</code> (or detected language)</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Missing viewport meta</td> <td>Add <code><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"></code></td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code><img></code> without <code>alt</code> attribute</td> <td>Add <code>alt=""</code> (decorative) - prompt for content images</td> <td>High for decorative</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Positive <code>tabindex</code> (1, 2, etc.)</td> <td>Replace with <code>tabindex="0"</code> or remove</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>outline: none</code> without alternative</td> <td>Add <code>outline: 2px solid</code> with <code>:focus-visible</code></td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Missing <code><label></code> for input</td> <td>Add <code><label></code> with matching <code>for</code>/<code>id</code></td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Button without accessible name</td> <td>Add <code>aria-label</code> if icon-only; otherwise add text</td> <td>Medium</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Missing <code>autocomplete</code> on identity fields</td> <td>Add <code>autocomplete="name"</code>, <code>"email"</code>, <code>"tel"</code>, etc.</td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>New tab link without warning</td> <td>Add <code><span class="sr-only">(opens in new tab)</span></code></td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Missing <code>scope</code> on <code><th></code></td> <td>Add <code>scope="col"</code> or <code>scope="row"</code></td> <td>High</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Missing <code>type</code> on <code><button></code></td> <td>Add <code>type="button"</code> (prevents accidental form submission)</td> <td>High</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="human-judgment-show-fix-ask-for-approval">Human-Judgment (show fix, ask for approval)</h5> <p>These require context only the user can provide:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 29%" /> <col style="width: 70%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Issue</th> <th>Why Human Needed</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Alt text content for meaningful images</td> <td>Only user knows the image’s purpose</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Heading hierarchy restructuring</td> <td>May affect visual design and content flow</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Link text rewriting</td> <td>Context-dependent, UX copy implications</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>ARIA role assignment on custom widgets</td> <td>Depends on intended interaction pattern</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>ARIA role changes (e.g. <code>menuitem</code> to <code>menuitemradio</code>)</td> <td>Role changes break JS selectors and may alter UX; requires multi-file impact check</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Removing or changing <code>aria-keyshortcuts</code>, <code>title</code>, or documented attributes</td> <td>These indicate intentional design; removal requires explicit user approval</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Live region placement and politeness</td> <td>Depends on UX intent for dynamic content</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Color/contrast changes</td> <td>May conflict with brand guidelines</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="aria-role-change-safety">ARIA Role Change Safety</h5> <p>ARIA role changes are <strong>never auto-fixable</strong>. Before proposing any role change:</p> <ol type="1"> <li><strong>Search all workspace files</strong> for selectors that reference the current role (e.g., <code>querySelectorAll('[role="menuitem"]')</code>).</li> <li><strong>List every file and line</strong> that would need to be updated alongside the HTML change.</li> <li><strong>Check if the existing code works</strong> with assistive technology. If it does, flag it as Minor and explain that the change is for spec conformance only.</li> <li><strong>Present the full scope</strong> to the user: HTML changes, JavaScript selector updates, CSS selector updates, and any attributes that would be added or removed.</li> <li><strong>Never change a role in HTML without updating all corresponding JavaScript and CSS</strong> in the same operation.</li> </ol> <h4 id="framework-specific-fix-syntax">Framework-Specific Fix Syntax</h4> <p>Apply fixes using the correct syntax for the detected framework:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 18%" /> <col style="width: 22%" /> <col style="width: 22%" /> <col style="width: 37%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Framework</th> <th>Label Syntax</th> <th>Event Syntax</th> <th>Conditional Rendering</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>React/Next.js</td> <td><code>htmlFor</code></td> <td><code>onClick</code>, <code>onKeyDown</code></td> <td><code>{condition && <X/>}</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Vue</td> <td><code>for</code></td> <td><code>@click</code>, <code>@keydown</code></td> <td><code>v-if</code>, <code>v-show</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Angular</td> <td><code>for</code></td> <td><code>(click)</code>, <code>(keydown)</code></td> <td><code>*ngIf</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Svelte</td> <td><code>for</code></td> <td><code>on:click</code>, <code>on:keydown</code></td> <td><code>{#if condition}</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>HTML</td> <td><code>for</code></td> <td><code>onclick</code>, <code>onkeydown</code></td> <td>N/A</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h4 id="fix-process">Fix Process</h4> <ol type="1"> <li>Read the issue details (file path, line number, issue description)</li> <li>Read the source file to understand context</li> <li>Determine the correct framework syntax</li> <li>Apply the fix using the Edit tool</li> <li>Report what was changed (before/after)</li> </ol> <h4 id="output-format-10">Output Format</h4> <p>For each fix applied, return:</p> <pre class="text"><code>Fix #[n]: [issue description] File: [path]:[line] Before: [original style="width: 42%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 23%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Pattern</th> <th>Issue</th> <th>Fix</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>transition:</code> without motion check</td> <td>Animations play regardless of user preference</td> <td>Add <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> check</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><code>on:click</code> on non-interactive</td> <td>Not keyboard accessible</td> <td>Use <code><button></code> or add keyboard handlers</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h5 id="fix-templates-3">Fix Templates</h5> <pre class="svelte"><code><!-- Bad: click on div --> <div on:click={toggle}>Toggle</div> <!-- Good: keyboard accessible --> <button on:click={toggle}>Toggle</button> <!-- Bad: animation without motion preference --> <div transition:fly={{ y: 200 }}>Content</div> <!-- Good: respects motion preference --> <div transition:fly={{ y: reducedMotion ? 0 : 200, duration: reducedMotion ? 0 : 300 }}>Content</div> <script> const reducedMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; </script></code></pre> <h4 id="tailwind-css-1">Tailwind CSS</h4> <h5 ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="maps">Maps</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>maps</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/maps">skills/maps</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever the project contains static or interactive maps, embedded map widgets (Google Maps, Leaflet, Mapbox, OpenStreetMap), or any geographic visualizations. Under no circumstances embed a map without a text-based alternative conveying the same information. Absolutely always ensure map controls are keyboard-accessible and that all meaningful map content is available without the visual map.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>maps/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="maps-accessibility-skill">Maps Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/MAPS_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing or reviewing any static or interactive map. <strong>Only load this skill if the project contains maps.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-17">Core Mandate</h5> <p>No single text description works for every map. Start with the map’s purpose and the tasks it supports, then provide accessible content and controls that preserve that purpose for people who cannot see, distinguish, point at, drag, zoom, or interpret the visual map. Keep the map and its structured alternative synchronized from the same data source.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-20">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Essential location data has no accessible alternative</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Interactive map unreachable by keyboard; <code>role="application"</code> misused</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Skip link missing; colour independence gap; popup focus not managed</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Missing <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> for animations; legend incomplete</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="classify-the-maps-purpose-first">Classify the Map’s Purpose First</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Map purpose</th> <th>Essential task</th> <th>Common accessible presentation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Simple locator</td> <td>Where one place is and how to reach it</td> <td>Concise alt, address, landmark, directions, contact info</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Location directory</td> <td>Find and compare services</td> <td>Searchable list/table with names, addresses, distances, categories</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Route/wayfinding</td> <td>Travel from A to B</td> <td>Ordered directions with distances, turns, landmarks, conditions</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Thematic/quantitative</td> <td>Compare values across areas</td> <td>Summary + data table with region names, values, units, period</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Boundary/zoning</td> <td>Understand containment/adjacency</td> <td>Named boundary descriptions, affected locations, downloadable data</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Indoor/multi-floor</td> <td>Navigate a building</td> <td>Floor selector, accessible route instructions, entrances/lifts/stairs</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Exploratory</td> <td>Investigate spatial relationships</td> <td>Synchronized filters, structured results, accessible query tools</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>A map can serve more than one purpose — provide the alternatives needed for every essential task rather than assuming one short <code>alt</code>, table, or direction set is universally equivalent. WCAG 1.1.1’s “equivalent purpose” does not mean reproducing every pixel or street label — it means preserving the information and tasks that matter in context. Research (the Map Equivalent-Purpose Framework) found tables and turn-by-turn directions can be insufficient when the purpose includes broad spatial understanding or exploration — treat this as guidance, not a separate WCAG criterion, but recognize when a table alone won’t do.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-text-alternatives-for-static-maps">Critical: Text Alternatives for Static Maps</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb717"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb717-1"><a href="#cb717-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Simple map: concise alt, details in HTML nearby --></span></span> <span id="cb717-2"><a href="#cb717-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><figure></span></span> <span id="cb717-3"><a href="#cb717-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><img</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"clinic-location.png"</span></span> <span id="cb717-4"><a href="#cb717-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> alt=</span><span class="st">"The clinic is on the north side of King Street, immediately east of the Central Station entrance."</span></span> <span id="cb717-5"><a href="#cb717-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> width=</span><span class="st">"960"</span> <span class="er">height</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"540"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb717-6"><a href="#cb717-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><figcaption></span></span> <span id="cb717-7"><a href="#cb717-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Northside Clinic, 200 King Street. The step-free entrance is on King Street.</span> <span id="cb717-8"><a href="#cb717-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"#clinic-directions"</span><span class="kw">></span>Read accessible travel directions<span class="kw"></a></span>.</span> <span id="cb717-9"><a href="#cb717-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></figcaption></span></span> <span id="cb717-10"><a href="#cb717-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></figure></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Do not fill <code>alt</code> with turn-by-turn instructions or every road label — keep it concise and put detail nearby. For complex maps, provide both a short alternative AND a visible structured long description or clearly associated link:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb718"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb718-1"><a href="#cb718-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><figure></span></span> <span id="cb718-2"><a href="#cb718-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><img</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"accessible-transit-routes.png"</span></span> <span id="cb718-3"><a href="#cb718-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> alt=</span><span class="st">"Map of step-free transit routes in the downtown area. Detailed route information follows."</span></span> <span id="cb718-4"><a href="#cb718-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> width=</span><span class="st">"1200"</span> <span class="er">height</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"800"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb718-5"><a href="#cb718-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><figcaption></span></span> <span id="cb718-6"><a href="#cb718-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Step-free transit routes, updated 15 July 2026.</span> <span id="cb718-7"><a href="#cb718-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"#transit-route-details"</span><span class="kw">></span>View route details and connections<span class="kw"></a></span>.</span> <span id="cb718-8"><a href="#cb718-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></figcaption></span></span> <span id="cb718-9"><a href="#cb718-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></figure></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Prefer visible structured content over <code>aria-describedby</code> for complex descriptions — AT generally flattens referenced headings/lists/tables into one string, losing navigable structure. <code>alt=""</code> is appropriate only when purely decorative or the same info is already fully available nearby — never call a meaningful or interactive map decorative to hide accessibility problems.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-structured-alternatives-matching-the-task">Critical: Structured Alternatives Matching the Task</h5> <p><strong>Location list/table</strong> (for directories):</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb719"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb719-1"><a href="#cb719-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><table</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"branch-table"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb719-2"><a href="#cb719-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><caption></span>Library branches matching the current filters<span class="kw"></caption></span></span> <span id="cb719-3"><a href="#cb719-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><thead></span></span> <span id="cb719-4"><a href="#cb719-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><tr><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"col"</span><span class="kw">></span>Branch<span class="kw"></th><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"col"</span><span class="kw">></span>Address<span class="kw"></th><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"col"</span><span class="kw">></span>Distance<span class="kw"></th><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"col"</span><span class="kw">></span>Accessibility information<span class="kw"></th></tr></span></span> <span id="cb719-5"><a href="#cb719-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></thead></span></span> <span id="cb719-6"><a href="#cb719-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><tbody></span></span> <span id="cb719-7"><a href="#cb719-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><tr></span></span> <span id="cb719-8"><a href="#cb719-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"row"</span><span class="kw">><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/branches/central"</span><span class="kw">></span>Central Library<span class="kw"></a></th></span></span> <span id="cb719-9"><a href="#cb719-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><td></span>100 Main Street<span class="kw"></td><td></span>600 metres<span class="kw"></td></span></span> <span id="cb719-10"><a href="#cb719-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><td></span>Step-free entrance, lift, accessible washroom, hearing loop<span class="kw"></td></span></span> <span id="cb719-11"><a href="#cb719-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></tr></span></span> <span id="cb719-12"><a href="#cb719-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></tbody></span></span> <span id="cb719-13"><a href="#cb719-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></table></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Explain how distance was calculated; include units; preserve filters/sort order; let users open the same details and perform the same actions from both the map and the list view.</p> <p><strong>Route directions:</strong></p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb720"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb720-1"><a href="#cb720-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><section</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"clinic-directions"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"directions-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb720-2"><a href="#cb720-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><h2</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"directions-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span>Step-free route from Central Station<span class="kw"></h2></span></span> <span id="cb720-3"><a href="#cb720-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p></span>Distance: 350 metres. Typical travel time: 6 to 10 minutes.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb720-4"><a href="#cb720-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><ol></span></span> <span id="cb720-5"><a href="#cb720-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><li></span>Leave Central Station through the King Street step-free exit.<span class="kw"></li></span></span> <span id="cb720-6"><a href="#cb720-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><li></span>Turn left and continue east for approximately 250 metres.<span class="kw"></li></span></span> <span id="cb720-7"><a href="#cb720-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></ol></span></span> <span id="cb720-8"><a href="#cb720-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p></span>Route data checked 15 July 2026. Call 555-0100 to confirm temporary closures.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb720-9"><a href="#cb720-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></section></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Include as applicable: distances/travel time; street names/landmarks/turns; curb cuts/crossings/gradients/surfaces/steps; accessible entrances/lifts/ washrooms; known construction/closures; transit stop/platform info; an alternative route when the shortest isn’t accessible. Don’t rely only on cardinal directions — combine with street names, distance, and landmarks.</p> <p><strong>Thematic/quantitative maps:</strong> provide a plain-language summary, a data table with every value needed for comparison, region names/categories/units/ missing-data indicators, and the time period/source. Do not replace a choropleth map with a list of color names.</p> <p><strong>Legends are content, not decoration</strong> — put legend text in HTML, describe colors/symbols/patterns/line styles/sizes, keep changes synchronized with active layers, and never make the legend the only structured alternative.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-interactive-map-page-structure-and-skip-link">Serious: Interactive Map Page Structure and Skip Link</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb721"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb721-1"><a href="#cb721-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><section</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"service-map-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb721-2"><a href="#cb721-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><h2</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"service-map-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span>Find an accessible service location<span class="kw"></h2></span></span> <span id="cb721-3"><a href="#cb721-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"#location-results-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span>Skip the interactive map and view locations<span class="kw"></a></p></span></span> <span id="cb721-4"><a href="#cb721-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-interface"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb721-5"><a href="#cb721-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><h3</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-view-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span>Interactive map<span class="kw"></h3></span></span> <span id="cb721-6"><a href="#cb721-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-instructions"</span><span class="kw">></span>Use the named map controls to move or zoom.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb721-7"><a href="#cb721-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-viewport"</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"region"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-view-heading"</span></span> <span id="cb721-8"><a href="#cb721-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> aria-describedby=</span><span class="st">"map-instructions"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb721-9"><a href="#cb721-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="co"><!-- tested map library renders here --></span></span> <span id="cb721-10"><a href="#cb721-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></div></span></span> <span id="cb721-11"><a href="#cb721-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></div></span></span> <span id="cb721-12"><a href="#cb721-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><section</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"location-results-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb721-13"><a href="#cb721-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><h3</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"location-results-heading"</span> <span class="er">tabindex</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"-1"</span><span class="kw">></span>Location results<span class="kw"></h3></span></span> <span id="cb721-14"><a href="#cb721-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"location-result-status"</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"status"</span> <span class="er">aria-atomic</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span><span class="kw">></p></span></span> <span id="cb721-15"><a href="#cb721-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><ul</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"location-results"</span><span class="kw">></span><span class="co"><!-- same locations as map markers --></span><span class="kw"></ul></span></span> <span id="cb721-16"><a href="#cb721-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></section></span></span> <span id="cb721-17"><a href="#cb721-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></section></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Missing skip link on an interactive map is Serious.</strong> The visible link to results is useful to screen reader, keyboard, switch, speech-input, mobile, low-bandwidth, and cognitively disabled users — don’t reveal it only on keyboard focus.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-third-party-map-embeds">Serious: Third-Party Map Embeds</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb722"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb722-1"><a href="#cb722-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><iframe</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"https://maps.example.org/embed/service-locations"</span></span> <span id="cb722-2"><a href="#cb722-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> title=</span><span class="st">"Interactive map of service locations"</span> <span class="er">loading</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"lazy"</span><span class="kw">></iframe></span></span> <span id="cb722-3"><a href="#cb722-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"#service-location-list"</span><span class="kw">></span>View service locations as a list<span class="kw"></a></span></span> <span id="cb722-4"><a href="#cb722-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> or <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/service-locations.csv"</span><span class="kw">></span>download the location data<span class="kw"></a></span>.<span class="kw"></p></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>An <code><iframe></code> with no descriptive <code>title</code> is Serious. Confirm keyboard users can enter/operate/leave the embed; test controls, markers, popups, consent notices, and full-screen mode; keep the structured alternative <strong>outside</strong> the iframe, available if the provider fails or is blocked; confirm changes made in the embed are reflected in the site’s alternative; retest after provider/plugin/config updates. Do not trust a provider’s accessibility claim without testing the current rendered experience.</p> <p><strong>Map libraries:</strong> preserve a library’s accessibility defaults unless testing supports a change (e.g., Leaflet’s container/markers are keyboard operable by default — plugins can degrade that). Pin the version, review release notes, retest after updates — do not recommend a plugin as universally accessible or use unpinned <code>@latest</code> in production.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-keyboard-controls-and-roleapplication">Serious: Keyboard Controls and <code>role="application"</code></h5> <p>All map functionality must be keyboard-reachable unless the underlying movement is essential (WCAG’s limited exception).</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb723"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb723-1"><a href="#cb723-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-controls"</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"group"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-controls-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb723-2"><a href="#cb723-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><h3</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-controls-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span>Map view controls<span class="kw"></h3></span></span> <span id="cb723-3"><a href="#cb723-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Zoom in<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb723-4"><a href="#cb723-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Pan north<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb723-5"><a href="#cb723-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Reset map view<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb723-6"><a href="#cb723-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></div></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Users reach every control in logical order; native buttons work with Enter/ Space; focus stays visible and unobscured by floating controls/popups; users can move into and out of the map without a trap; rerendering the map doesn’t discard focus or move it to <code><body></code>. Do not capture page-level arrow keys merely because a map is present — scope arrow-key panning to when the viewport has focus, and always allow Tab/Shift+Tab to leave. Single-character shortcuts must meet WCAG 2.1.4 (off/remap/scoped) with named buttons as an alternative.</p> <p><strong>Most maps do not need <code>role="application"</code>.</strong> It changes screen reader interaction modes and suppresses ordinary reading commands. Prefer native controls around the map, ordinary document content for results, a named region for the viewport, and documented scoped keyboard behavior only where the viewport needs it. <strong>Misusing it is Serious</strong> — only use application semantics when the team understands the AT consequences, has implemented a complete keyboard model, provides instructions and an exit path, and has tested supported combinations. Adding the role does not make a map accessible.</p> <p><strong>Large marker sets:</strong> hundreds of markers must not create hundreds of sequential Tab stops. Choose a tested model: one map-viewport Tab stop with documented directional navigation; roving <code>tabindex</code> within the current marker set; focusable markers only after narrowing results; or a structured location list as the primary keyboard interface. There is no universal WAI-ARIA map pattern — document the chosen behavior and test it.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-markers-clusters-and-popup-focus-management">Moderate: Markers, Clusters, and Popup Focus Management</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb724"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb724-1"><a href="#cb724-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-marker"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"City Hall, 123 Main Street"</span></span> <span id="cb724-2"><a href="#cb724-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> aria-expanded=</span><span class="st">"false"</span> <span class="er">aria-controls</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"city-hall-details"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb724-3"><a href="#cb724-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">focusable</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span><span class="kw">></span><span class="co"><!-- marker artwork --></span><span class="kw"></svg></span></span> <span id="cb724-4"><a href="#cb724-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb724-5"><a href="#cb724-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><section</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"city-hall-details"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"city-hall-heading"</span> <span class="er">hidden</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb724-6"><a href="#cb724-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><h3</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"city-hall-heading"</span><span class="kw">></span>City Hall<span class="kw"></h3></span></span> <span id="cb724-7"><a href="#cb724-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><p></span>123 Main Street. Step-free entrance on Queen Avenue.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb724-8"><a href="#cb724-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/locations/city-hall"</span><span class="kw">></span>City Hall details<span class="kw"></a></span></span> <span id="cb724-9"><a href="#cb724-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></section></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Update both <code>hidden</code> and <code>aria-expanded</code> together. <strong>Use ordinary non-modal content for marker popups — do not add <code>role="dialog"</code>/<code>aria-modal="true"</code> to every marker popup</strong>, only when the interaction is genuinely modal. If a popup has substantial content and focus moves into it, provide a close control and return focus to the triggering marker on close. Do not put “press Enter” instructions in a native button’s name — the role already communicates operation.</p> <p><strong>Clusters</strong> need an accessible name, a count, and a keyboard action:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb725"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb725-1"><a href="#cb725-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-expanded</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span> <span class="er">aria-controls</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"downtown-location-results"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb725-2"><a href="#cb725-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Show 7 locations in downtown</span> <span id="cb725-3"><a href="#cb725-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Update <code>aria-expanded</code> and both views together on expansion; preserve focus on the cluster control or move it only to a predictable results heading after an explicit action; announce a concise result summary, not every marker.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-colour-independence">Moderate: Colour Independence</h5> <p>Never rely on colour alone for route/zone/state differentiation — route numbers and line styles in addition to colour; icons and text labels in addition to marker colours; hatching/boundary styles in addition to area fills; numeric values in the data table. <strong>Colour-only encoding is Moderate</strong> (Serious if the colour distinguishes routes/states with different safety implications). Test in forced-colours mode — map tile backgrounds may be overridden; ensure the location list/directions remain complete if tiles or gradients disappear.</p> <p>Contrast: authored normal text ≥4.5:1; large text ≥3:1; visual info required to identify controls/states/graphical objects ≥3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11); focus indicators need enough contrast against whatever they touch. Do not claim every pixel, aerial photo, or incidental label must meet one universal ratio — evaluate the authored information actually needed to understand/operate the map.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-target-size">Moderate: Target Size</h5> <p>WCAG 2.5.8 requires <strong>24×24 CSS pixels minimum</strong> or a listed exception — it does <strong>not</strong> impose a universal 44×44 requirement at Level AA. Use 44×44 for primary map controls as an inclusive practice aligning with the Level AAA Target Size Enhanced criterion (2.5.5), not because AA requires it:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb726"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb726-1"><a href="#cb726-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.map-controls</span> button { <span class="kw">min-inline-size</span>: <span class="dv">44</span><span class="dt">px</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">min-block-size</span>: <span class="dv">44</span><span class="dt">px</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Markers can be visually small with a larger transparent hit area, as long as hit areas don’t overlap ambiguously.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-pointer-touch-and-dragging-alternatives">Serious: Pointer, Touch, and Dragging Alternatives</h5> <p>Maps commonly depend on pinch/rotate/swipe/drag — these cannot be the only way to operate essential functions. Provide zoom buttons as pinch alternatives; pan controls/search/selection as drag alternatives; a button/ menu alternative to dragging a marker or route point; single-pointer marker/ control activation; actions completing on pointer-up rather than pointer-down.</p> <p>An embedded map must not create a page-scrolling trap — users need a reliable way to scroll past it without an undocumented multi-finger gesture. Consider requiring an explicit “Use interactive map” action before the map captures drag/wheel gestures, especially on small screens.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="layer-toggles-search-and-geolocation">Layer Toggles, Search, and Geolocation</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb727"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb727-1"><a href="#cb727-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><fieldset></span></span> <span id="cb727-2"><a href="#cb727-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><legend></span>Locations to show<span class="kw"></legend></span></span> <span id="cb727-3"><a href="#cb727-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><label><input</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"checkbox"</span> <span class="er">name</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"category"</span> <span class="er">value</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"clinic"</span> <span class="er">checked</span><span class="kw">></span> Clinics<span class="kw"></label></span></span> <span id="cb727-4"><a href="#cb727-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><label><input</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"checkbox"</span> <span class="er">name</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"step-free"</span> <span class="er">value</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"yes"</span><span class="kw">></span> Step-free entrance<span class="kw"></label></span></span> <span id="cb727-5"><a href="#cb727-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></fieldset></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Announce a concise result summary (“12 locations shown”) — don’t announce every marker added, tile loaded, pan movement, or zoom frame.</p> <p><strong>Search:</strong> a labeled search form + status message + ordinary links is easier to implement and use than a custom autocomplete widget. If suggestions are needed, implement and test the <strong>complete</strong> WAI-ARIA combobox pattern — adding <code>role="listbox"</code>/<code>aria-autocomplete</code> to an otherwise incomplete widget is not sufficient. Accept multiple input forms; explain errors without clearing the query; announce a concise result count; identify ambiguous addresses and let the user choose; preserve query/filters across map/list views.</p> <p><strong>Geolocation:</strong> request permission only after a clear user action; explain why and how it’s used; provide address/place search when permission is denied; handle stale/inaccurate locations without blaming the user; don’t require precise geolocation for a task that can use manual input.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="low-vision-zoom-reflow-and-orientation">Low Vision, Zoom, Reflow, and Orientation</h5> <p>Browser zoom and map zoom are different — support both, and never override browser zoom or pinch-to-zoom at the page level. Keep map controls and alternatives available at 200%/400% browser zoom; preserve portrait/ landscape; avoid fixed-height layouts hiding controls when text grows. WCAG 1.4.10’s two-dimensional-layout exception can apply to the map viewport itself, but it does <strong>not</strong> exempt surrounding controls, search, status, details, directions, and location results from reflow requirements.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="canvas-and-svg-maps">Canvas and SVG Maps</h5> <p>Canvas pixels have no child semantics — if drawn on <code><canvas></code>, provide accessible DOM controls, results, names, states, and alternatives outside or in a tested fallback structure; don’t assume screen readers can inspect painted markers. For SVG maps: give non-interactive maps an appropriate accessible name/description; keep decorative paths out of the accessibility tree; make interactive regions programmatically focusable and named; provide a structured alternative for large/complex SVG maps. See <code>skills/svg/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="indoor-maps-and-wayfinding">Indoor Maps and Wayfinding</h5> <p>Provide as applicable: building/entrance/floor/destination names; accessible entrances and hours; lift/stair/escalator/ramp/platform locations; corridor widths/door types/thresholds/gradients/surfaces/lighting; washrooms/refuge areas/assistance points; landmarks and distances between decision points; temporary lift outages/construction/closures; source and last-verification date.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb728"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb728-1"><a href="#cb728-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><label</span> <span class="er">for</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"floor-select"</span><span class="kw">></span>Building floor<span class="kw"></label></span></span> <span id="cb728-2"><a href="#cb728-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><select</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"floor-select"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb728-3"><a href="#cb728-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><option</span> <span class="er">value</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"ground"</span><span class="kw">></span>Ground floor: entrance, reception, cafe<span class="kw"></option></span></span> <span id="cb728-4"><a href="#cb728-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><option</span> <span class="er">value</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"1"</span><span class="kw">></span>Floor 1: offices and meeting rooms 101 to 120<span class="kw"></option></span></span> <span id="cb728-5"><a href="#cb728-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></select></span></span> <span id="cb728-6"><a href="#cb728-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"floor-status"</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"status"</span> <span class="er">aria-atomic</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span><span class="kw">></p></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>On change, update the floor heading, locations, directions, and map together. Real-time positioning is an enhancement, not the only navigation method — indoor location can be inaccurate or unavailable; offer static directions and a way to report outdated route data.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="data-quality-and-accessibility-information">Data Quality and Accessibility Information</h5> <p>Accessible presentation cannot correct inaccurate geographic data. Identify the source and last-update date; explain whether distances are straight- line/walking/driving/transit; distinguish verified accessibility info from user-submitted or inferred info; provide a way to report errors and temporary barriers; preserve missing/unknown values rather than presenting them as “No”; avoid absolute route claims when conditions can change; include contact info when a critical accessibility feature should be confirmed before travel.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-10">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Equivalent-purpose:</strong> list the map’s documented purposes/essential tasks; complete each task using the visual map, then using only the structured alternative and non-map controls; compare information/results/conclusions available; test with blind, low-vision, mobility-disabled, cognitively disabled, and DeafBlind users as appropriate. Don’t evaluate equivalence by just checking a table exists.</li> <li><strong>Keyboard:</strong> reach and operate search/filters/layers/controls/markers/ clusters/details/results/full-screen; confirm focus order is logical and visible; confirm map updates don’t lose focus; enter/leave the viewport and embed without a trap; confirm the structured alternative supports the same actions</li> <li><strong>Screen reader:</strong> confirm controls/markers/clusters/states/results have useful names and roles; verify status messages are concise and not repeated excessively; read structured descriptions/tables/directions independently of the map; confirm opening/closing details doesn’t cause unexpected focus changes</li> <li><strong>Visual/low-vision:</strong> 200%/400% browser zoom; narrow viewports and both orientations; text spacing; light/dark/forced-colors; confirm labels don’t disappear or overlap; confirm selected states/routes/boundaries remain distinguishable without colour; confirm the alternative remains usable when map imagery is hidden</li> <li><strong>Pointer/touch:</strong> complete every task with a single pointer; zoom/pan without pinch or drag; verify alternatives to dragging markers/route points; check target size, spacing, and pointer cancellation; scroll the page past the map without a trap</li> <li><strong>Data/integration:</strong> compare marker count/content with structured results; apply every filter and confirm both views stay synchronized; verify distances/units/coordinates/accessibility attributes; test empty/ loading/error/offline/permission-denied states; retest after data/basemap/ library updates</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated checks</strong> can detect missing iframe titles, unnamed buttons, invalid ARIA, duplicate IDs, focus-order regressions, contrast issues, missing static-image alternatives, and map/list count mismatches — cannot determine equivalent purpose, direction accuracy, route accessibility, spatial comprehension, or third-party keyboard behavior. Manual and user testing are required.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-7">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Failure</th> <th>Correction</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Using one generic <code>alt="Map"</code></td> <td>Describe the map’s purpose and provide a task-appropriate structured alternative</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Assuming a table or directions are always fully equivalent</td> <td>Match the alternative to the documented purpose; add spatial descriptions when needed</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Giving a complex table only through <code>aria-describedby</code></td> <td>Provide visible, navigable HTML or a clearly associated link</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Adding <code>role="application"</code> to the map by default</td> <td>Use named regions, native controls, ordinary content, scoped keyboard behavior</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Capturing arrow keys while focus is elsewhere on the page</td> <td>Scope map keys to the focused viewport; provide named controls</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Making every marker a Tab stop</td> <td>Use a tested navigation model and synchronized location list</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Making every popup an <code>aria-modal="true"</code> dialog</td> <td>Use ordinary non-modal details unless genuinely modal</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Claiming WCAG AA universally requires 44×44 targets</td> <td>Apply the 24×24 Level AA criterion; use 44×44 as an inclusive/AAA practice</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Confusing 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured) with 2.4.13 (Focus Appearance)</strong></td> <td>2.4.11 is Focus Not Obscured Minimum (AA); Focus Appearance is 2.4.13 (AAA)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Requiring pinch or drag as the only interaction</td> <td>Provide single-pointer buttons and selection alternatives</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Applying one contrast ratio to every map pixel</td> <td>Test essential authored text, controls, states, and graphical objects accurately</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Hiding an interactive map as decorative to dodge remediation</td> <td>Remove interaction or expose accessible controls/information/alternatives</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Announcing every pan, tile, or marker update</td> <td>Announce concise completed-task results; keep persistent content visible</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Trusting a map provider or plugin without testing</td> <td>Test the current configured version; preserve an external structured alternative</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Letting the map and location list use different data</td> <td>Generate both from the same source and state</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-20">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Map’s purpose, audience, and essential tasks documented</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Static maps have concise alt text; complex maps have visible structured descriptions</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Location lists/tables/directions are visible, structured, and easy to find</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Map and non-map views use the same data, filters, and result state</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Skip link present before every interactive map</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Third-party <code><iframe></code> maps have descriptive <code>title</code>; alternative lives outside the iframe</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All map interactions keyboard-operable; arrow-key panning scoped to focused viewport</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>role="application"</code> used only with a fully tested custom keyboard model — not by default</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Large marker sets use a tested navigation model, not hundreds of Tab stops</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Marker popups are non-modal unless genuinely modal; focus returns to trigger on close</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Colour not used as sole differentiator; legend provided; tested in forced-colours mode</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Targets meet 24×24px minimum; 44×44px used for primary controls where practical</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Pinch/drag/path gestures have single-pointer button alternatives</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Map controls/alternatives usable at 200%/400% zoom and narrow viewports</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Status messages concise; persistent results remain visible in the page</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Data source, date, units, and limitations documented</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-18">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <ul> <li>1.1.1 Non-text Content (A) — <strong>Critical if no text alternative</strong></li> <li>1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics (A)</li> <li>1.4.1 Use of Color (A) — <strong>Moderate if colour-only encoding</strong></li> <li>1.4.3 Contrast Minimum (AA)</li> <li>1.4.10 Reflow (AA) — with a defined exception for the map viewport itself</li> <li>1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA)</li> <li>2.1.1 Keyboard (A) — <strong>Serious if map controls not keyboard operable</strong></li> <li>2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A)</li> <li>2.4.3 Focus Order (A)</li> <li>2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum (AA, WCAG 2.2) — not Focus Appearance</li> <li>2.5.5 Target Size Enhanced (AAA) — the 44×44 threshold</li> <li>2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA)</li> <li>2.5.8 Target Size Minimum (AA) — 24×24, the actual AA requirement</li> <li>4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)</li> <li>4.1.3 Status Messages (AA)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="references-23">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/MAPS_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md">Full best practices guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://leafletjs.com/examples/accessibility/">Leaflet: A Guide to Basic Leaflet Accessibility</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/guides/accessibility/">Mapbox GL JS accessibility</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/complex/">W3C WAI: Complex Images</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/">W3C WAI-ARIA APG: Combobox Pattern</a></li> <li><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05310">Systematically Evaluating Equivalent Purpose for Digital Maps</a></li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> These rules target WCAG 2.2 AA. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="path-instructions-reference">Path Instructions (Reference)</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Domain:</strong> cross-cutting</li> <li><strong>Effort:</strong> low</li> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 12</li> <li><strong>Invocation:</strong> by request only; the model does not choose it on its own</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> MIT</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>kb-path-instructions</code></li> <li><strong>Output:</strong> none</li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Community Access</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents">Community-Access/accessibility-agents</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/Community-Access/accessibility-agents/tree/decf6bac7f086c19afb242797b4974671ceff597/skills/kb-path-instructions">skills/kb-path-instructions</a></li> <li><strong>Tier:</strong> reference</li> </ul> <p>Reference data, not a reviewer. Per-file-type accessibility rules: semantic HTML, ARIA patterns, CSS, markdown, testing and terminology.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>kb-path-instructions/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <p>Rules that apply to a particular kind of file. These were path-scoped instruction files before 7.0; each one still says which files it governs.</p> <h4 id="which-file-to-read">Which file to read</h4> <p>Open the one reference that matches what you are working on.
