links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>print</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/print">skills/print</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever the project includes print stylesheets, print media queries (<span class="citation" data-cites="media">@media</span> print), or any content intended for physical printing. Under no circumstances omit print CSS that ensures readable, accessible printed output. Absolutely always hide decorative elements, expand link URLs, and maintain sufficient contrast and font sizing in print styles.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>print/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="print-accessibility-skill">Print Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/PRINT_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing or reviewing print stylesheets. <strong>Only load this skill if the project has print CSS in scope.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-18">Core Mandate</h5> <p>Printing is an accessibility feature. Users with cognitive disabilities may find printed material easier to process; users with low vision may enlarge it; users without reliable internet need offline copies. Print styles must keep content useful, readable, and free of colour-only meaning. Print CSS should be a progressive enhancement — write screen styles first, then layer <code>@media print</code> on top, and confirm the content is still comprehensible in the browser’s default print mode before adding custom styles.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-21">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Print output is completely unusable (blank page, navigation only)</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Content lost or meaning broken due to colour stripping; tables unreadable</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Orphaned headings; link URLs not revealed; layout breaks across pages</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Typography not print-optimised; missing QR alternative to long URLs</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-scope-all-print-styles">Critical: Scope All Print Styles</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb729"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb729-1"><a href="#cb729-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">/* Preferred: single inline block */</span></span> <span id="cb729-2"><a href="#cb729-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> <span class="dv">print</span> {</span> <span id="cb729-3"><a href="#cb729-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="co">/* all print styles here */</span></span> <span id="cb729-4"><a href="#cb729-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb729-5"><a href="#cb729-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb729-6"><a href="#cb729-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">/* Alternative: separate file */</span></span> <span id="cb729-7"><a href="#cb729-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">/* <link rel="stylesheet" href="print.css" media="print"> */</span></span></code></pre></div> <p>A site with no <code>@media print</code> block at all may print navigation, cookie banners, and sidebars while omitting content — <strong>Critical</strong>. Prefer the inline approach to keep styles co-located and reduce HTTP requests.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-hide-non-essential-elements">Critical: Hide Non-Essential Elements</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb730"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb730-1"><a href="#cb730-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> <span class="dv">print</span> {</span> <span id="cb730-2"><a href="#cb730-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> nav<span class="op">,</span> header nav<span class="op">,</span> footer<span class="op">,</span> aside<span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">.sidebar</span><span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb730-3"><a href="#cb730-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.cookie-banner</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">.skip-link</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">.ad</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">.social-share</span><span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb730-4"><a href="#cb730-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.print-hide</span><span class="op">,</span> video<span class="op">,</span> audio<span class="op">,</span> iframe<span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb730-5"><a href="#cb730-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="ex">[role</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">"complementary"</span><span class="ex">]</span><span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb730-6"><a href="#cb730-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> form button<span class="ex">[type</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">"submit"</span><span class="ex">]</span><span class="in">:not(</span><span class="fu">.print-show</span><span class="in">)</span> {</span> <span id="cb730-7"><a href="#cb730-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">none</span> <span class="at">!important</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb730-8"><a href="#cb730-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> }</span> <span id="cb730-9"><a href="#cb730-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>Utility classes: * <code>.print-hide</code> — elements to suppress in print only (navigation buttons, interactive controls) * <code>.print-show</code> — elements hidden on screen but needed in print (e.g., postal address, expanded content, supplementary notes)</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-colour-dependence-in-print">Serious: Colour Dependence in Print</h5> <p>When browsers print with backgrounds off (the default in most browsers), any information conveyed via background colour is lost. This is <strong>Serious</strong> for data tables or status indicators that use colour alone. Ink colour rendering also varies significantly between printers — always test print output in grayscale mode.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb731"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb731-1"><a href="#cb731-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> <span class="dv">print</span> {</span> <span id="cb731-2"><a href="#cb731-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.status-error</span><span class="in">::after</span> { <span class="kw">content</span>: <span class="st">" [Error]"</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb731-3"><a href="#cb731-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.status-success</span><span class="in">::after</span> { <span class="kw">content</span>: <span class="st">" [OK]"</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb731-4"><a href="#cb731-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.status-warning</span><span class="in">::after</span> { <span class="kw">content</span>: <span class="st">" [Warning]"</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb731-5"><a href="#cb731-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb731-6"><a href="#cb731-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="co">/* Remove colour-coded highlights; use borders instead */</span></span> <span id="cb731-7"><a href="#cb731-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.status-warning</span> {</span> <span id="cb731-8"><a href="#cb731-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">border</span>: <span class="dv">2</span><span class="dt">pt</span> <span class="dv">solid</span> <span class="cn">#000</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb731-9"><a href="#cb731-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">color</span>: <span class="cn">#000</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb731-10"><a href="#cb731-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">background</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb731-11"><a href="#cb731-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> }</span> <span id="cb731-12"><a href="#cb731-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>For table cells with coloured backgrounds, ensure the cell already contains a text label — do not rely on background colour to convey meaning. Force-print backgrounds only when the SVG/image requires it:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb732"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb732-1"><a href="#cb732-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> <span class="dv">print</span> {</span> <span id="cb732-2"><a href="#cb732-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.required-background</span> {</span> <span id="cb732-3"><a href="#cb732-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb732-4"><a href="#cb732-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> print-color-adjust: exact<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb732-5"><a href="#cb732-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> }</span> <span id="cb732-6"><a href="#cb732-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Grayscale testing checklist:</strong></p> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All text is legible in black-and-white output</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Charts and graphs include patterns, shapes, or labels in addition to colour</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Status indicators (warnings, errors, successes) use text labels, not colour alone</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Links remain distinguishable (underline or URL disclosure)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-reveal-link-urls">Serious: Reveal Link URLs</h5> <p>Printed links are dead without the URL. <strong>Missing URL expansion is Serious</strong> for content-heavy pages where links carry information.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb733"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb733-1"><a href="#cb733-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> <span class="dv">print</span> {</span> <span id="cb733-2"><a href="#cb733-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> a<span class="ex">[href]</span><span class="in">::after</span> {</span> <span id="cb733-3"><a href="#cb733-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">content</span>: <span class="st">" ("</span> <span class="fu">attr(</span>href<span class="fu">)</span> <span class="st">")"</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb733-4"><a href="#cb733-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">font-size</span>: <span class="dv">0.875</span><span class="dt">em</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb733-5"><a href="#cb733-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">color</span>: <span class="cn">#333</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb733-6"><a href="#cb733-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">word-break</span>: break-all<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb733-7"><a href="#cb733-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> }</span> <span id="cb733-8"><a href="#cb733-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="co">/* Suppress non-informative and internal links */</span></span> <span id="cb733-9"><a href="#cb733-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> a<span class="ex">[href</span><span class="op">^=</span><span class="st">"#"</span><span class="ex">]</span><span class="in">::after</span><span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb733-10"><a href="#cb733-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> a<span class="ex">[href</span><span class="op">^=</span><span class="st">"javascript:"</span><span class="ex">]</span><span class="in">::after</span><span class="op">,</span></span> <span id="cb733-11"><a href="#cb733-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> href="#cb733-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>For pages with many long URLs, consider providing QR codes as an alternative. A QR code adjacent to key links is printable, scannable, and avoids long URL wrapping issues:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb734"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb734-1"><a href="#cb734-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Print-only QR code linking to the page --></span></span> <span id="cb734-2"><a href="#cb734-2" <span id="cb735-3"><a href="#cb735-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">font-family</span>: Georgia<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">"Times New Roman"</span><span Use <code>pt</code> units for font sizes in print stylesheets. Set <code>orphans</code> and <code>widows</code> to prevent isolated single lines.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-page-setup">Moderate: Page Setup</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb736"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb736-1"><a href="#cb736-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@page</span> {</span> <span id="cb736-2"><a href="#cb736-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">margin</span>: <span class="dv">2</span><span class="dt">cm</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">/* Minimum for most printers; leave more for bound documents */</span></span> <span id="cb736-3"><a href="#cb736-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb736-4"><a href="#cb736-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@page</span> <span class="in">:first</span> {</span> <span id="cb736-5"><a href="#cb736-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">margin-top</span>: <span class="dv">3</span><span class="dt">cm</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb736-6"><a href="#cb736-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb736-7"><a href="#cb736-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@page</span> <span class="in">:left</span> { <span class="kw">margin-left</span>: <span class="dv">3</span><span class="dt">cm</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb736-8"><a href="#cb736-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@page</span> <span class="in">:right</span> { <span class="kw">margin-right</span>: <span class="dv">3</span><span class="dt">cm</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Avoid specifying <code>size: A4</code> unless the document is specifically designed for A4. Under no circumstances build features that break completely when JavaScript is unavailable or fails. Absolutely always start with semantic HTML, layer CSS enhancements, and add JavaScript as the final, optional layer. Prioritize resilience and universal access over cutting-edge features.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>progressive-enhancement/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="progressive-enhancement-accessibility-skill">Progressive Enhancement Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/PROGRESSIVE_ENHANCEMENT_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when building any web feature or reviewing architecture decisions.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-19">Core Mandate</h5> <p>Start with a solid foundation that works for every user, then layer enhancements. Every user — regardless of browser capability, network speed, assistive technology, or JavaScript availability — must be able to access core content and complete core tasks.</p> <p>Progressive enhancement is also a sustainability practice. Pages that work without JavaScript are dramatically lighter: fewer bytes transferred, less CPU spent on parsing and executing scripts, and less energy consumed per page view. See <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/SUSTAINABILITY.md">SUSTAINABILITY.md</a> and the <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/web-sustainability-guidelines/">Web Sustainability Guidelines</a>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-22">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Core content or task inaccessible without JS/CSS</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Core content accessible but significantly degraded without JS/CSS</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Enhancement degrades gracefully but with friction</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Best-practice gap; marginal impact</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="the-three-layers">The Three Layers</h5> <h6 id="layer-1-semantic-html-always-required">Layer 1 — Semantic HTML (always required)</h6> <p><strong>Failure here is Critical.</strong></p> <ul> <li>All core content readable in plain HTML — no CSS or JS required</li> <li>Forms submittable with native browser behaviour</li> <li>Navigation functions as standard links</li> <li>Headings, lists, tables, and landmarks accurately reflect document structure</li> </ul> <h6 id="layer-2-css-enhance-presentation">Layer 2 — CSS (enhance presentation)</h6> <p><strong>Failure here is Moderate to Serious.</strong></p> <ul> <li>External stylesheets that can be disabled without losing content</li> <li>Respect user preferences: <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code>, <code>prefers-color-scheme</code>, <code>prefers-contrast</code>, <code>forced-colors</code></li> <li>Page remains usable if stylesheets fail to load</li> </ul> <h6 id="layer-3-javascript-enhance-interactivity">Layer 3 — JavaScript (enhance interactivity)</h6> <p><strong>JS that gates core content or tasks is Critical.</strong></p> <ul> <li>JS enhances; it does not gate access to core content or tasks</li> <li>Apply JS-dependent classes/behaviours from scripts, not static markup</li> <li>Handle script failure gracefully — the HTML layer must still work</li> <li>Use feature detection, not browser detection:</li> </ul> <div class="sourceCode" class="bu">document</span>) {</span> <span id="cb742-2"><a href="#cb742-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="co">// apply enhanced experience</span></span> <span id="cb742-3"><a href="#cb742-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <h6 id="layer-3-extension-service-workers-offline-capability">Layer 3 extension — Service Workers (offline capability)</h6> <p>Service Workers are a Layer 3 enhancement: they require JavaScript, are registered by a script, and must degrade gracefully when unavailable (private browsing, unsupported browsers, HTTPS not available).</p> <p>When implemented, they extend both accessibility and sustainability:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Accessibility</strong>: users on unreliable connections (common in rural areas, low-income households, and developing regions) can continue to access previously loaded content offline</li> <li><strong>Sustainability</strong>: cached responses eliminate repeat network <p>Service Worker caching strategies (cache-first, network-first, stale-while- revalidate) should be chosen based on content update frequency. Avoid caching strategies that serve stale content for content that changes frequently without a cache-invalidation plan.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-core-content-must-not-require-javascript">Critical: Core Content Must Not Require JavaScript</h5> <p>Rendering page content exclusively in JavaScript is <strong>Critical</strong> — users with JS disabled, AT users encountering compatibility issues, and low-bandwidth users are completely excluded.</p> <ul> <li>Deliver complete HTML from the server; hydrate interactivity in the browser</li> <li>Core content must be in the initial HTML response</li> <li>When using React/Vue/Angular/Svelte: configure SSR or static generation</li> <li>Avoid SPA patterns that require JS to render any visible content</li> </ul> <p>Every byte of JavaScript that is not needed to access core content is unnecessary energy consumption. Prefer server rendering — it transfers HTML once; a JS bundle transfers code that must then be parsed, compiled, and executed on every visit.</p> <hr /> <h5 Ignoring them is <strong>Moderate</strong> at minimum; ignoring <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> for fast or flashing animations can reach <strong>Serious</strong>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="what-to-avoid">What to Avoid</h5> <ul> <li>Rendering page content exclusively in JavaScript — <strong>Critical</strong></li> <li><code>display:none</code> / <code>visibility:hidden</code> on content required at the HTML layer — <strong>Critical</strong></li> <li>Requiring JS to navigate between pages without a server-rendered fallback — <strong>Critical</strong></li> <li><code>user-scalable=no</code> — <strong>Serious</strong> (prevents zoom for low-vision users)</li> <li>Assuming scripts will execute — always handle failure states</li> <li>Polyfills as a substitute for progressive enhancement (they patch features; PE builds around their absence)</li> <li>Shipping large JS bundles for functionality that could be server-rendered — this is both an accessibility risk and a sustainability cost</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-22">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Core content readable with JavaScript disabled</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Core tasks completable with JavaScript disabled</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Forms submit via native browser behaviour</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Navigation works as standard HTML links</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />CSS respects <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code>, <code>prefers-color-scheme</code>, <code>prefers-contrast</code></li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Script failure handled gracefully</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Feature detection used (not browser detection)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />SSR or static generation configured for JS frameworks</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Service Worker registered with feature detection and silent failure handling</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Offline fallback page is valid Layer 1 HTML</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Caching strategy documented and matched to content update frequency</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Tested: disable JS → verify core content; disable CSS → verify logical reading order</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-20">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <ul> <li>2.1.1 Keyboard (A) — native elements have built-in keyboard support</li> <li>4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)</li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Note:</strong> WCAG 4.1.1 Parsing was <strong>removed in WCAG 2.2</strong> (August 2023). Modern browsers handle parsing errors uniformly. Valid semantic HTML remains important as a progressive enhancement foundation, but it is no longer a testable WCAG criterion. Do not cite it in audits or compliance statements.</p> </blockquote> <hr /> <h5 id="references-25">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/PROGRESSIVE_ENHANCEMENT_BEST_PRACTICES.md">Full best practices guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/SUSTAINABILITY.md">SUSTAINABILITY.md</a> — PE reduces page weight and energy use; see WSG alignment</li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/web-sustainability-guidelines/">Web Sustainability Guidelines (WSG) 1.0</a></li> <li><a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Service_Worker_API">MDN: Service Worker API</a></li> <li><a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Offline_and_background_operation">MDN: Offline and background operation</a></li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> WCAG 3.0 is in development. No breaking changes to progressive enhancement principles are anticipated. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="svg">SVG</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>svg</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/svg">skills/svg</a></li> </ul> Load this skill whenever the project contains SVG graphics — inline SVGs, external SVG files, SVG icons, SVG illustrations, or SVG-based data visualizations. Under no circumstances use SVG without proper accessible titles, descriptions, and ARIA roles where required. Absolutely always add <title> <p>and <desc> to meaningful SVGs and set role=“img” with aria-labelledby pointing to those elements. Also apply this skill whenever the project accepts untrusted or user-uploaded SVG content, which requires sanitization before rendering.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>svg/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="svg-accessibility-skill">SVG Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/SVG_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when creating, optimising, or reviewing SVG graphics. <strong>Only load this skill if the project contains SVGs.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-20">Core Mandate</h5> <p>SVG accessibility depends on the graphic’s purpose and how it is embedded. A decorative icon, an informative image, an icon inside a button, and an interactive diagram require different patterns. Start by deciding what users need from the graphic, then provide the simplest semantic implementation that delivers the same information or function. The presence of <code><title></code>, <code><desc></code>, <code>role="img"</code>, or <code>aria-label</code> does not by itself make an SVG accessible — test the result in its final context.</p> <p>SVG is also an active XML format that can contain scripts, event handlers, and external resource references. <strong>Untrusted SVG (uploads, pasted markup, AI-generated output) must be sanitized before rendering</strong> — see the Security section below.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-23">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>SVG conveys essential information with no accessible alternative; untrusted SVG rendered without sanitization</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>SVG is interactive but unreachable or unlabelled for AT users</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>AT experience degraded but content still partially accessible</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Best-practice gap; marginal impact</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="choose-the-pattern-by-purpose-and-context">Choose the Pattern by Purpose and Context</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th style="text-align: left;">Context</th> <th style="text-align: left;">Preferred pattern</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Decorative SVG loaded with <code><img></code></td> <td style="text-align: left;"><code><img src="…" alt=""></code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Meaningful SVG loaded with <code><img></code></td> <td style="text-align: left;"><code><img src="…" alt="Useful description"></code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Decorative inline SVG</td> <td style="text-align: left;"><code><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg></code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Simple meaningful inline SVG</td> <td style="text-align: left;"><code><svg role="img" aria-labelledby="…"><title>…</title></svg></code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Icon inside a named button or link</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Name the HTML control and hide the SVG</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Complex graphic</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Short name plus visible summary, data, or detailed description</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Reused sprite icon</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Label or hide each outer <code><svg></code> instance, not the shared symbol</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Interactive graphic</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Prefer native HTML controls; provide an equivalent structured alternative</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Use native HTML semantics before ARIA. Do not add <code>role="img"</code> to an <code><img></code> merely because its source is an SVG file — that’s redundant.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-decorative-svgs-must-be-hidden-completely-from-at">Critical: Decorative SVGs Must Be Hidden Completely from AT</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb748"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb748-1"><a href="#cb748-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">focusable</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb748-2"><a href="#cb748-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="co"><!-- decorative icon — no title, no desc, no role needed --></span></span> <span id="cb748-3"><a href="#cb748-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></svg></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><code>aria-hidden="true"</code> removes the SVG and its descendants from the accessibility tree — do not place focusable or interactive content inside an element hidden this way. <code>focusable="false"</code> addresses legacy IE/older Edge behavior; it can remain for projects still supporting those browsers but isn’t a universal modern requirement. Do not add <code><title></code>/<code><desc></code> to an intentionally-hidden SVG. <strong>Never use <code>role="presentation"</code> as a substitute</strong> for <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> — it does not reliably suppress announcement across browser/screen-reader combinations.</p> <p><strong>When is an SVG decorative?</strong> If the same meaning is conveyed by adjacent visible text, or the image is purely ornamental, it’s decorative. If removing it would leave a user without needed information, it’s meaningful.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="external-svg-used-with-img">External SVG Used with <code><img></code></h5> <p>Follows the same text-alternative rules as other image formats.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb749"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb749-1"><a href="#cb749-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Informative --></span></span> <span id="cb749-2"><a href="#cb749-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><img</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/assets/images/service-area.svg"</span> <span class="er">alt</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Map showing the service area extending from Kingston to Ottawa"</span> <span class="er">width</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"640"</span> <span class="er">height</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"360"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb749-3"><a href="#cb749-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb749-4"><a href="#cb749-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Decorative --></span></span> <span id="cb749-5"><a href="#cb749-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><img</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/assets/images/flourish.svg"</span> <span class="er">alt</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">""</span> <span id="cb749-6"><a href="#cb749-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb749-7"><a href="#cb749-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Functional (destination-describing) --></span></span> <span id="cb749-8"><a href="#cb749-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/reports/annual-report.pdf"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb749-9"><a href="#cb749-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><img</span> <span class="er">src</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/assets/icons/download.svg"</span> <span class="er">alt</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Download annual report"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb749-10"><a href="#cb749-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></a></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><code>role="img"</code> is redundant on <code><img></code>; <code>aria-label</code> unnecessary when <code>alt</code> can provide the name. <strong>Internal SVG <code><title></code>/<code><desc></code> does not replace HTML <code>alt</code></strong> when loaded through <code><img></code> — the HTML alt is what’s read.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-simple-meaningful-inline-svg">Serious: Simple Meaningful Inline SVG</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb750"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb750-1"><a href="#cb750-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"img"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"download-icon-title"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb750-2"><a href="#cb750-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><title</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"download-icon-title"</span><span class="kw">></span>Download<span class="kw"></title></span></span> <span id="cb750-3"><a href="#cb750-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><path</span> <span class="er">d</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"M12 3v12m0 0 5-5m-5 5-5-5M5 21h14"</span><span class="kw">></path></span></span> <span id="cb750-4"><a href="#cb750-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></svg></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>The <code><title></code> must be a direct child of <code><svg></code> with a unique ID, referenced via <code>aria-labelledby</code>. A plain <code>aria-label</code> is a reasonable alternative when managing a unique title ID adds needless complexity:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb751"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb751-1"><a href="#cb751-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"img"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Download"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">></span>…<span class="kw"></svg></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Do not use both patterns</strong> without a specific tested reason — ARIA labelling attributes take priority over <code><title></code> in the accessible-name calculation (<code>aria-labelledby</code> > <code>aria-label</code> > direct child <code><title></code>). Note: some browsers show <code><title></code> as a pointer tooltip — that is not a substitute for visible text or a real accessible tooltip; it may not be discoverable by keyboard, touch, or speech-input users.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-icons-inside-buttons-and-links">Serious: Icons Inside Buttons and Links</h5> <p>The HTML control should own the accessible name — hide the SVG icon.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb752"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb752-1"><a href="#cb752-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Visible text --></span></span> <span id="cb752-2"><a href="#cb752-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb752-3"><a href="#cb752-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">><path</span> <span class="er">d</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"M6 6 18 18M18 6 6 18"</span><span class="kw">></path></svg></span></span> <span id="cb752-4"><a href="#cb752-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Close</span> <span id="cb752-5"><a href="#cb752-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb752-6"><a href="#cb752-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb752-7"><a href="#cb752-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Icon-only --></span></span> <span id="cb752-8"><a href="#cb752-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Close dialog"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb752-9"><a href="#cb752-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">><path</span> <span class="er">d</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"M6 6 18 18M18 6 6 18"</span><span class="kw">></path></svg></span></span> <span id="cb752-10"><a href="#cb752-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Do not give both the button and its hidden icon separate versions of the same name</strong> — that produces duplicate or inconsistent announcements. Prefer a visible label when the action may not be obvious — a familiar-looking icon can mean different things across products.</p> <p>For an external SVG asset loaded via <code><img></code> inside an already-labelled button (e.g., a theme selector), use <code>alt=""</code> since the button supplies the name — note that an external <code><img></code>-loaded SVG does not inherit <code>currentColor</code> from the surrounding button; validate the asset’s own colors on every background it appears on, or inline the paths if it must follow a manual theme.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-accessible-names-and-descriptions-correct-aria-relationship">Serious: Accessible Names and Descriptions — Correct ARIA Relationship</h5> <p>SVG accessible-name priority: <code>aria-labelledby</code> > <code>aria-label</code> > direct child <code><title></code> > other fallbacks. Descriptions: <code>aria-describedby</code> > direct child <code><desc></code>.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb753"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb753-1"><a href="#cb753-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"img"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"weather-title"</span> <span class="er">aria-describedby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"weather-desc"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 320 180"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb753-2"><a href="#cb753-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><title</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"weather-title"</span><span class="kw">></span>Weekly temperature trend<span class="kw"></title></span></span> <span id="cb753-3"><a href="#cb753-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><desc</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"weather-desc"</span><span class="kw">></span>Temperatures rise from 12 degrees Monday to 21 degrees Friday.<span class="kw"></desc></span></span> <span id="cb753-4"><a href="#cb753-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></svg></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Keep IDs unique in the whole HTML document — a repeated component with fixed SVG IDs can cause one instance to be labelled by another. <strong>Do not put both title and description IDs in <code>aria-labelledby</code></strong> — that concatenates both strings into the accessible <em>name</em>; use <code>aria-labelledby</code> for the name and <code>aria-describedby</code> for the description separately. <strong>Do not bury essential information in <code><desc></code></strong> — support for navigating long SVG descriptions varies across AT; put essential details in visible HTML instead.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-complex-graphics-diagrams-and-charts">Moderate: Complex Graphics, Diagrams, and Charts</h5> <p>A complex SVG needs more than one long accessible name: a concise name, a visible summary of the purpose/conclusion, complete data in structured HTML when needed, and keyboard-operable controls if interactive.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb754"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb754-1"><a href="#cb754-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><figure></span></span> <span id="cb754-2"><a href="#cb754-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">role</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"img"</span> <span class="er">aria-labelledby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"visitors-title"</span> <span class="er">aria-describedby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"visitors-summary"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 640 360"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb754-3"><a href="#cb754-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><title</span> aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Visitors increased each month, from 12,400 in January to 19,200 in March.</span> <span id="cb754-7"><a href="#cb754-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><table></span></span> <span id="cb754-11"><a href="#cb754-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><caption></span>Monthly website visitors<span class="kw"></caption></span></span> <span id="cb754-12"><a href="#cb754-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><thead><tr><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"col"</span><span class="kw">></span>Month<span class="kw"></th><th</span> <span class="er">scope</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"col"</span><span class="kw">></span>Visitors<span class="kw"></th></tr></thead></span></span> <span id="cb754-13"><a href="#cb754-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><tbody><tr><th</span> <span <span id="cb754-14"><a href="#cb754-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></table></span></span> <span id="cb754-15"><a href="#cb754-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></details></span></span> <span id="cb754-16"><a href="#cb754-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></figure></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Do not duplicate a detailed table into <code>aria-label</code>/<code><title></code>/<code><desc></code> — long image-name strings are hard to navigate. The ARIA Graphics Module defines structured roles (<code>graphics-document</code>, <code>graphics-object</code>, <code>graphics-symbol</code>) but support must be tested with actual AT combinations; these don’t remove the need for an equivalent text presentation. See <code>skills/charts-graphs/SKILL.md</code> for chart-specific requirements.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="reused-icons-and-svg-sprites">Reused Icons and SVG Sprites</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb755"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb755-1"><a href="#cb755-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">hidden</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb755-2"><a href="#cb755-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><symbol</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"icon-download"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb755-3"><a href="#cb755-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><path</span> <span class="er">d</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"M12 3v12m0 0 5-5m-5 5-5-5M5 21h14"</span><span class="kw">></path></span></span> <span id="cb755-4"><a href="#cb755-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></symbol></span></span> <span id="cb755-5"><a href="#cb755-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></svg></span></span> <span id="cb755-6"><a href="#cb755-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb755-7"><a href="#cb755-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 24 24"</span><span class="kw">><use</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"#icon-download"</span><span class="kw">></use></svg></span></span> <span id="cb755-8"><a href="#cb755-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Download report</span> <span id="cb755-9"><a href="#cb755-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Names inside a shared symbol are rarely appropriate for every instance — “Arrow” could mean Next, Previous, Expand, or Collapse depending on context. Name the control or the outer rendered instance, not the shared symbol. An external <code><use></code> target must reference a real distinct element (usually a <code><symbol></code> with an ID) — <strong>do not create recursive self-references</strong>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-colour-contrast-and-themes">Moderate: Colour, Contrast, and Themes</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb756"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb756-1"><a href="#cb756-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.icon</span> {</span> <span id="cb756-2"><a href="#cb756-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">fill</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb756-3"><a href="#cb756-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> stroke: currentColor<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb756-4"><a href="#cb756-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> stroke-linecap: round<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb756-5"><a href="#cb756-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> stroke-width: <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb756-6"><a href="#cb756-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p><code>currentColor</code> is useful, not mandatory — multi-colour graphics may need several semantic tokens; validate every meaningful pairing in every theme. Do not rely on colour alone — add text labels, patterns, line styles, or shapes for statuses/series/selected states. Text inside SVG is subject to text contrast requirements; required graphical information generally needs 3:1; decorative details don’t need 3:1 merely for appearing in a meaningful graphic.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb757"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb757-1"><a href="#cb757-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">forced-colors</span>: active) {</span> <span id="cb757-2"><a href="#cb757-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.icon</span> { <span class="kw">color</span>: <span class="cn">ButtonText</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb757-3"><a href="#cb757-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.chart-line</span> { <span class="kw">fill</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> stroke: CanvasText<span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb757-4"><a href="#cb757-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.chart-line</span><span class="ex">[data-selected</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span><span class="ex">]</span> { stroke: <span class="cn">Highlight</span><span class="op">;</span> stroke-width: <span class="dv">4</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb757-5"><a href="#cb757-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>Do not set both <code>fill</code> and <code>stroke</code> on every path indiscriminately — it can turn line artwork into solid shapes. Avoid <code>forced-color-adjust: none</code> unless essential and tested against multiple system palettes.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="text-inside-svg">Text Inside SVG</h5> <p>Keep essential labels visible and legible; meet text contrast requirements. <strong>Do not convert essential labels to paths</strong> merely to preserve a typeface, and do not use <code>font-size="0"</code>, off-canvas positioning, or transparent SVG text as a substitute for a real text alternative. Provide important explanations in HTML. Test resizing/zoom — SVG labels can overlap or clip even when the outer SVG scales. <code><foreignObject></code> can embed HTML in SVG but adds rendering/fallback complexity — use ordinary HTML outside the SVG when it can provide the same result.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-interactive-svg">Critical: Interactive SVG</h5> <p>Prefer native HTML buttons, links, and disclosures placed near the graphic over interaction inside the SVG itself:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb758"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb758-1"><a href="#cb758-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb758-2"><a href="#cb758-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><svg</span> <span class="er">aria-hidden</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"true"</span> <span class="er">viewBox</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"0 0 640 360"</span><span class="kw">></span><span class="co"><!-- Visual map --></span><span class="kw"></svg></span></span> <span id="cb758-3"><a href="#cb758-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><ul</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-locations"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb758-4"><a href="#cb758-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><li><a</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/locations/ottawa"</span><span class="kw">></span>Ottawa service centre<span class="kw"></a></li></span></span> <span id="cb758-5"><a href="#cb758-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"></ul></span></span> <span id="cb758-6"><a href="#cb758-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></div></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>If interaction must occur within the SVG: use SVG <code><a href="…"></code> for genuine navigation; provide a purpose-describing accessible name; preserve logical DOM/focus order; support expected keyboard activation; show a visible, unclipped focus indicator; meet target-size requirements; expose selected/ expanded/pressed states; ensure the accessible name contains the visible label for speech input; provide an equivalent HTML list/table when the visual layout can’t be navigated non-visually. <strong>Do not put every data point in the tab order</strong> — hundreds of focus stops make a visualization technically reachable but practically unusable. <strong>Do not create a “button” by adding only <code>tabindex="0"</code> and a click listener to <code><path></code>/<code><g></code></strong> — that provides no native button semantics or keyboard behaviour. An interactive SVG unreachable by keyboard is <strong>Critical</strong>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-motion-animation-and-flashing">Serious: Motion, Animation, and Flashing</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb759"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb759-1"><a href="#cb759-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.loading-icon</span> { <span class="kw">transform-origin</span>: <span class="dv">center</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb759-2"><a href="#cb759-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">prefers-reduced-motion</span>: no-preference) {</span> <span id="cb759-3"><a href="#cb759-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.loading-icon</span> { <span class="kw">animation</span>: spin <span class="dv">1</span><span class="dt">s</span> <span class="dv">linear</span> <span class="dv">infinite</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb759-4"><a href="#cb759-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Do not use a blanket <code>svg *</code> rule to reduce motion</strong> — it can affect unrelated components and override meaningful states. Target the specific animated component and define an understandable static state:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb760"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb760-1"><a href="#cb760-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">prefers-reduced-motion</span>: reduce) {</span> <span id="cb760-2"><a href="#cb760-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.diagram-panel</span> { <span class="kw">animation</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">transition</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb760-3"><a href="#cb760-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>For <code><animate></code>/<code><animateTransform></code>, use <code>begin="indefinite"</code> and only trigger via <code>beginElement()</code> when <code>prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference</code> is confirmed.</p> <p><strong>Rapid SVG animation is Critical</strong> if it flashes at 3+ Hz (WCAG 2.3.1) — this is not replaced by respecting reduced-motion preference; the flash threshold applies regardless. WCAG 2.2.2 requires pause/stop/hide controls for moving/blinking/auto-updating content lasting 5+ seconds and not essential. WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) requires users be able to disable non-essential interaction-triggered motion — respecting <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> is an effective approach even at AA.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="responsive-svg-and-zoom">Responsive SVG and Zoom</h5> <p>Preserve <code>viewBox</code> so the graphic scales without cropping its internal coordinate system — its removal during optimization is not just Minor, it will break fluid layouts.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb761"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb761-1"><a href="#cb761-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.responsive-diagram</span> { <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">block</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">max-inline-size</span>: <span class="dv">100</span><span class="dt">%</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">block-size</span>: <span class="bu">auto</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Test at 200%/400% zoom and narrow viewports — a scalable canvas doesn’t guarantee labels reflow or stay readable. For dense diagrams, consider a simplified small-screen view plus an adjacent HTML explanation. Never disable page zoom to compensate for an inflexible SVG layout.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="standalone-svg-documents">Standalone SVG Documents</h5> <p>An SVG opened directly in a browser is a document, not an <code><img></code> — include namespace, language, and an accessible name:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb762"><pre class="sourceCode xml"><code class="sourceCode xml"><span id="cb762-1"><a href="#cb762-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><<span class="kw">svg</span><span class="ot"> xmlns=</span><span class="st">"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"</span><span class="ot"> role=</span><span class="st">"img"</span><span class="ot"> aria-labelledby=</span><span class="st">"diagram-title"</span></span> <span id="cb762-2"><a href="#cb762-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ot"> viewBox=</span><span class="st">"0 0 800 450"</span><span class="ot"> lang=</span><span class="st">"en"</span><span class="ot"> xml:lang=</span><span class="st">"en"</span>></span> <span id="cb762-3"><a href="#cb762-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <<span class="kw">title</span><span class="ot"> id=</span><span class="st">"diagram-title"</span>>Request approval workflow</<span class="kw">title</span>></span> <span id="cb762-4"><a href="#cb762-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></<span class="kw">svg</span>></span></code></pre></div> <p>If the standalone file is complex, link to an equivalent HTML description near where users open it.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-security-sanitization-and-build-processing">Critical: Security, Sanitization, and Build Processing</h5> <p>SVG is an active XML format that can contain scripts, event handlers, links, external resources, CSS, animation, filters, and embedded HTML via <code><foreignObject></code>. <strong>A file that looks like an image must not automatically be treated as inert content.</strong> Accessibility metadata must survive processing, but never at the cost of weakening the security boundary — apply security and accessibility checks to the same final artifact.</p> <p><strong>Classify the SVG’s trust level before processing:</strong></p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th style="text-align: left;">Source</th> <th style="text-align: left;">Required treatment</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Author-controlled (reviewed icons in the repo)</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Review changes, restrict build tooling, validate final output</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Generated from a controlled source (Mermaid/chart renderer)</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Treat renderer + config as dependencies; validate generated SVG</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Platform-generated (hosted diagram service)</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Record platform/renderer version; verify hosted result</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;"><strong>Untrusted</strong> (uploads, pasted markup, user-edited, remote files, AI-generated)</td> <td style="text-align: left;"><strong>Enforce input limits, parse securely, sanitize with an SVG-aware allowlist, validate before display or export</strong></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Inline SVG, <code><object></code>, <code><embed></code>, and standalone documents have broader capabilities than <code><img></code> and need greater scrutiny — an SVG safe for <code><img></code> today may be downloaded, opened directly, or embedded inline by someone else later. There is no single accessibility treatment across all embedding contexts.</p> <p><strong>Sanitize untrusted SVG</strong> with a maintained, SVG-aware sanitizer/allowlist (e.g., DOMPurify with a reviewed SVG profile) — a generic HTML allowlist may remove essential SVG features or permit unneeded ones. <strong>Do not:</strong></p> <ul> <li>insert untrusted SVG using <code>innerHTML</code> before sanitization</li> <li>treat well-formed XML as safe SVG</li> <li>treat <code>DOMParser</code>, <code>XMLSerializer</code>, a formatter, or SVGO as a sanitizer</li> <li>use regular expressions as an SVG sanitizer</li> <li>assume a filename, MIME type, or successful image preview proves safety</li> <li>modify sanitized markup with untrusted strings afterward</li> </ul> <p>Sanitization should remove/reject: <code><script></code> and event-handler attributes (<code>onclick</code>); <code>javascript:</code> and other unapproved URL schemes; unexpected external <code>href</code>/<code>xlink:href</code>; external resources in CSS/<code>@import</code>/<code>url()</code>; <code><foreignObject></code>/embedded HTML unless explicitly required; unapproved animation/interactive elements; processing instructions, DTDs, external entities. Same-document <code>#fragment</code> references (<code><use href="#icon"></code>, <code>marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"</code>) are commonly needed and safe to allow — but validate every permitted fragment resolves to an allowed element in the same sanitized document; allowing fragments does not imply allowing arbitrary external URLs.</p> <p><strong>Parse XML securely</strong> when processed server-side: disable DTD processing and external entity resolution; prevent network/local-file access from the parser; avoid XSLT/XInclude unless explicitly required and secured; set input/nesting/entity limits; fail closed on parse/sanitization failure.</p> <p><strong>Limit resource consumption</strong> — SVG can exhaust CPU/memory without executing a script: cap input/decompressed size, element/attribute counts, path complexity, <code><use></code> nesting depth, filter complexity, embedded data-URL size, and rendered dimensions. Reject recursive references and content exceeding policy.</p> <p><strong>Preserve accessibility during optimization</strong> — configure the build to keep <code>viewBox</code>; <code><title></code>/<code><desc></code> when used; <code>role</code>/<code>aria-*</code>/language attributes; IDs referenced by ARIA, <code><use></code>, clip-paths, masks, filters, gradients; semantic <code><text></code>; focus/theme/forced-colors/reduced-motion styles; public sprite symbol IDs. Generate unique IDs for repeated inline components — an optimizer that collapses every copy to the same ID breaks both rendering and accessible names. Lock the optimizer version and test configuration changes against representative fixtures; use separate edit-safe vs. production optimization profiles.</p> <p><strong>Recommended processing sequence:</strong> (1) apply input/resource limits, (2) parse with secure XML settings, (3) sanitize untrusted input with the approved profile, (4) apply only controlled transformations, (5) optimize with a reviewed versioned config, (6) validate the final SVG for both security and accessibility, (7) insert/serve/export only the validated result. If any later step can introduce untrusted markup, sanitize again after that step.</p> <p>A restrictive CSP reduces the effect of some unsafe SVG features but does not replace parsing, sanitization, resource limits, or output validation — use it as defence in depth, not a substitute.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="what-is-not-required">What Is NOT Required</h5> <ul> <li>A <code><desc></code> for every SVG — <code><title></code> + <code>aria-labelledby</code> suffices when a name alone fully conveys meaning</li> <li>Focus styling inside non-interactive SVGs</li> <li>A <code>forced-colors</code> block when the SVG remains perceivable without it</li> <li><code>role="img"</code> on decorative SVGs — use <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> instead</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-11">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Code review:</strong> classify each SVG as decorative/informative/functional/ complex/interactive; confirm embedding pattern matches; inspect name/ description relationships; search repeated inline components for duplicate IDs; confirm build optimization preserves required attributes; classify the source’s trust level and identify all embedding contexts it can be used in; review sanitizer/parser/optimizer/renderer config changes; confirm final output validation covers both security and accessibility</li> <li><strong>Browser/AT:</strong> inspect the accessibility tree for expected role/name/ description; confirm decorative icons are silent and named graphics announced once; navigate all SVG controls by keyboard only; test speech- input names against visible labels; 200%/400% zoom and narrow viewports; every supported theme; <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code>/<code>prefers-contrast</code>/forced colors; colour-independent meaning; test with images unavailable when the SVG is essential</li> <li><strong>Security/processing:</strong> maintain valid AND adversarial fixtures; test the complete pipeline, not just the sanitizer in isolation — script/event handlers rejected; unsafe URL schemes rejected; unexpected external resources blocked; DTDs/external entities rejected without resolving; unapproved <code><foreignObject></code> rejected; recursive/excessive <code><use></code> rejected; oversized/complex input rejected; permitted same-document references still render; repeated inline instances keep unique IDs; optimized output still passes security rules and matches the accessible alternative. Run these whenever the sanitizer/parser/optimizer/renderer/allowlist/dependency version changes.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated tools</strong> can detect missing <code><img alt></code>, some accessible-name problems, duplicate IDs, contrast failures, and certain ARIA errors — cannot decide whether an alternative is equivalent, whether a graphic is truly decorative, or whether an interactive visualization is usable. No automated pass replaces manual SVG review.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-8">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th style="text-align: left;">Failure</th> <th style="text-align: left;">Correction</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;"><code><img src="graphic.svg"></code> has no <code>alt</code></td> <td style="text-align: left;">Add context-appropriate <code>alt</code>, including <code>alt=""</code> for decoration</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;"><code>role="img"</code> added to every HTML <code><img></code></td> <td style="text-align: left;">Use native <code><img></code> semantics and <code>alt</code></td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Both title and description IDs put in <code>aria-labelledby</code></td> <td style="text-align: left;">Use <code>aria-labelledby</code> for name, <code>aria-describedby</code> for description</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">A long table placed in <code><desc></code></td> <td style="text-align: left;">Provide essential detail as visible, structured HTML</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Repeated inline icons contain identical title IDs</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Generate a unique ID per instance, or use direct <code>aria-label</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">A sprite symbol references itself</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Put real paths in the symbol; reference only from rendered instances</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Forced-colours CSS sets both fill and stroke on every path</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Apply targeted system colours without changing geometry</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">A clickable <code><path></code> has only a click handler</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Use a native HTML control or implement complete keyboard semantics</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Reduced motion implemented with <code>svg *</code> and <code>!important</code></td> <td style="text-align: left;">Target each animated component; define a meaningful static state</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Well-formed XML treated as sanitized SVG</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Parse securely and apply an SVG-aware allowlist sanitizer</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">A regex removes <code><script></code> and is called a sanitizer</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Use a maintained SVG-aware sanitizer with a documented policy</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Sanitized SVG later modified with untrusted strings</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Keep later transforms controlled, or sanitize again before final validation</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">CSP treated as a replacement for sanitization</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Use CSP only as an additional layer</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">An optimizer update accepted because the SVG “still looks correct”</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Lock and test the optimizer; verify semantics, references, and alternatives</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-23">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Every SVG classified by purpose (decorative/informative/functional/complex/interactive) and embedding context</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Decorative SVGs: <code>aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"</code>, no <code><title></code>, no <code><desc></code></li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Meaningful <code><img></code> SVGs have useful <code>alt</code>; decorative external images use <code>alt=""</code></li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Meaningful inline SVGs: <code>role="img"</code> + <code><title></code> + <code>aria-labelledby</code> (or <code>aria-label</code>)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Complex SVGs: name + visible summary + structured HTML detail</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Icons inside named controls don’t duplicate the control’s accessible name</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Names/descriptions use the correct ARIA relationship (labelledby ≠ describedby)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />All referenced IDs preserved through optimisation; unique across repeated instances</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>currentColor</code> used where appropriate; non-text elements meet 3:1 contrast</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>viewBox</code> present and preserved</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Animated SVGs run only under <code>prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference</code>; no flashing at 3+ Hz regardless of preference</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Interactive SVGs keyboard operable with Under no circumstances create tooltips that are only triggered by hover without keyboard equivalent access. Absolutely always ensure tooltips are dismissible, persistent enough to read, and not the sole source of essential information.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>tooltips/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="tooltips-accessibility-skill">Tooltips Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/TOOLTIP_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing or reviewing tooltip components. <strong>Only load this skill if the project contains tooltips.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-21">Core Mandate</h5> <p>A tooltip is a short, non-interactive description that appears automatically when its trigger receives keyboard focus or pointer hover. An accessible tooltip must be available to keyboard, pointer, touch, magnification, and assistive technology users without hiding essential information or blocking the interface.</p> <p>Tooltips are often the wrong solution. Persistent visible text, a clear control label, a disclosure, or a dialog is usually easier to discover and use. This guide covers authored tooltips; the HTML <code>title</code> attribute produces a browser-controlled tooltip with different behavior and limitations (see below).</p> <p>Use the project’s <code>skills/bug-reporting/SKILL.md</code> severity/priority framework to grade findings. The severity scale below is a skill-local shorthand, not a universal standard.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-24">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Tooltip contains essential information with no other access route</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Tooltip unreachable by keyboard or AT; interactive content trapped in a tooltip</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Tooltip accessible but WCAG 1.4.13 requirements not fully met</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Best-practice gap; marginal impact</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="choose-the-right-pattern-first">Choose the Right Pattern First</h5> <p>Calling every small popup a tooltip leads to incorrect semantics and keyboard behavior. Classify the interaction before choosing ARIA:</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Need</th> <th>Use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>A control needs a clearer label</td> <td>Improve its visible label</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Short supplementary text should appear automatically on focus or hover</td> <td>Tooltip</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Instructions or requirements are needed to complete a task</td> <td>Persistent visible help text</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>A user explicitly asks to show or hide short help</td> <td>Button-controlled disclosure</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>The popup contains links, buttons, or other controls</td> <td>Non-modal dialog or another appropriate popup pattern</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>A decision is required before work can continue</td> <td>Modal dialog or alert dialog</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>An action completed or a process changed state</td> <td>Status message, not a tooltip</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Text is truncated only because of layout</td> <td>Allow wrapping, expansion, or another way to read the full text</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>An authored tooltip: describes an element, appears automatically after focus or hover, contains only non-interactive content, does not receive focus, is associated with its trigger through <code>aria-describedby</code>, remains available while the trigger has focus or the pointer is over the trigger or tooltip, and can be dismissed with <code>Escape</code>.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-essential-information-must-not-live-only-in-a-tooltip">Critical: Essential Information Must Not Live Only in a Tooltip</h5> <p>A tooltip is supplementary by definition. Put instructions, errors, requirements, and other essential information in persistent visible text. <strong>Hiding essential content behind hover/focus only is Critical.</strong></p> <p>Do not place error messages, legal text, security warnings, or task requirements only in a tooltip. Do not attach essential explanations only to a disabled control — a disabled native form control may not dispatch the pointer/focus events a tooltip expects:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb763"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb763-1"><a href="#cb763-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><p</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"publish-requirement"</span><span class="kw">></span>Add a page title before publishing.<span class="kw"></p></span></span> <span id="cb763-2"><a href="#cb763-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">disabled</span> <span class="er">aria-describedby</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"publish-requirement"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb763-3"><a href="#cb763-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Publish</span> <span id="cb763-4"><a href="#cb763-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-tooltips-must-appear-on-both-hover-and-focus">Serious: Tooltips Must Appear on Both Hover and Focus</h5> <p>A tooltip that only appears on hover is <strong>Serious</strong> — keyboard users cannot trigger it. information.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb765"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb765-1"><a href="#cb765-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span
