href="#cb765-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></span></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Tooltip element must have <code>role="tooltip"</code>; use a native interactive element for the trigger when the trigger performs an action</li> <li>Trigger must reference tooltip via <code>aria-describedby</code> (not <code>aria-labelledby</code>); <code>aria-describedby</code> may hold a space-separated list — preserve existing help, error, or instruction references when adding a tooltip</li> <li>Use <code>hidden</code> to conceal; never <code>aria-hidden="true"</code> on an active tooltip</li> <li>Each tooltip must have a unique <code>id</code>, including across repeated components; render the descriptive node before focus reaches the trigger</li> <li>Do not put <code>role="tooltip"</code> on the trigger itself</li> <li>Tooltips must <strong>not</strong> be focusable — no <code>tabindex</code> on the tooltip container</li> <li>Do not add <code>aria-live</code>, <code>role="status"</code>, or <code>role="alert"</code> to a tooltip</li> <li>Do not use <code>aria-expanded</code> or <code>aria-haspopup</code> for an automatically-displayed tooltip — those apply to button-controlled disclosures, not tooltips</li> <li>Let the tooltip’s text provide its accessible description; avoid an <code>aria-label</code> that replaces different visible tooltip text</li> </ul> <p>For icon-only triggers, name the control independently — the tooltip is a description, not a replacement for the accessible name:</p> <div id="serious-button-controlled-help-is-not-a-tooltip">Serious: Button-Controlled Help Is Not a Tooltip</h5> <p>When a user activates a button to show content, use a disclosure pattern instead — do not class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb767-5"><a href="#cb767-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"password-help"</span> <span class="er">hidden</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb767-6"><a href="#cb767-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> Use at least 12 characters. Include a number and a symbol.</span> <span id="cb767-7"><a href="#cb767-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></div></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>The expanded state communicates the change; focus remains on the button. If the popup contains interactive controls or must manage focus, use an appropriate dialog or popup pattern.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-wcag-1.4.13-content-on-hover-or-focus">Moderate: WCAG 1.4.13 — Content on Hover or Focus</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> <col style="width: 33%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Description</th> <th>Severity if failing</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Dismissible</strong></td> <td><code>Escape</code> dismisses without moving pointer or focus</td> <td>Serious</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Hoverable</strong></td> <td>User can move pointer over tooltip without it disappearing</td> <td>Moderate</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Persistent</strong></td> <td>Stays visible until trigger/tooltip loses hover or focus, is dismissed, or the info is no longer valid</td> <td>Moderate</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Do not invent an auto-close duration — a tooltip that disappears after a fixed timeout does not meet the persistence requirement while its trigger remains active.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-touch-and-activation">Moderate: Touch and Activation</h5> <p>Touch devices do not provide dependable hover. Do not depend on a tooltip for touch access. Use one of:</p> <ul> <li>Keep the information visible near the control</li> <li>Include it in the control’s accessible name or existing description</li> <li>Provide a separate help button that opens a disclosure (see above)</li> <li>Use a non-modal dialog when the additional content is structured or interactive</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-do-not-rely-on-the-title-attribute">Moderate: Do Not Rely on the <code>title</code> Attribute</h5> <p>Browser-controlled <code>title</code> tooltips fall under the WCAG 1.4.13 exception when their presentation is entirely user-agent controlled, but that exception does not make <code>title</code> a dependable interface pattern. Authors cannot ensure consistent keyboard, touch, magnification, timing, text size, or dismissal behavior for <code>title</code>. Do not use <code>title</code> as the only:</p> <ul> <li>accessible name for a control</li> <li>source of instructions or validation requirements</li> <li>explanation of an icon</li> <li>way to reveal truncated text</li> <li>access path for touch users</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-visual-design">Moderate: Visual Design</h5> <ul> <li>Normal-size tooltip text needs at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (WCAG 1.4.3); large text needs 3:1</li> <li>A boundary, shape, or arrow needs 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors (WCAG 1.4.11) only when that visual information is required to identify the component or state — a decorative arrow is not automatically subject to this</li> <li>Do not rely on color alone to associate a tooltip with its trigger</li> <li>At 400% zoom and narrow viewports: keep the tooltip within the viewport, allow text to wrap, avoid horizontal scrolling, don’t cover the trigger or critical content, and preserve a way to dismiss it</li> <li>Detect viewport edges and reposition; recalculate placement after zoom, resize, content changes, and text-direction changes; avoid rendering inside an ancestor whose <code>overflow</code> clips the tooltip</li> <li>An icon-button trigger must still meet WCAG 2.2 Target Size (Minimum)</li> <li>Respect <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code>:</li> </ul> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb768"><pre class="sourceCode id="content-requirements">Content Requirements</h5> <ul> <li>Keep content to a short phrase or sentence; describe the trigger, don’t introduce an unrelated message</li> <li>Avoid repeating the trigger’s accessible name word for word</li> <li>Do not include headings, lists, links, buttons, fields, or other controls</li> <li>Write in plain language; keep dynamic descriptions stable while the trigger has focus</li> <li>If content needs structure or several sentences, use persistent help, <code>aria-details</code>, a disclosure, or a dialog instead</li> <li>Do not make ordinary prose focusable merely to attach a tooltip — extra tab stops make keyboard navigation harder</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="when-not-to-use-a-tooltip">When NOT to Use a Tooltip</h5> <ul> <li>Label of control is self-explanatory</li> <li>Information must be readable at all times → use persistent help text</li> <li>Touch-only interface → use a help button/disclosure or persistent help text</li> <li>Content is long or structured → use a popover, disclosure, or dialog</li> <li>Content contains interactive elements (links, buttons) → use a popover or dialog</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-12">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Keyboard:</strong> reach the trigger with Tab/Shift+Tab, confirm the tooltip appears without moving focus, confirm <code>Escape</code> closes it while focus stays on the trigger, confirm no tooltip tab stop exists, confirm the focus indicator remains visible</li> <li><strong>Pointer/magnification:</strong> hover the trigger, move the pointer onto every part of the tooltip and confirm it stays visible, confirm it closes when neither hover nor focus retains it, test with screen magnification</li> <li><strong>Touch:</strong> confirm every action is usable without first discovering hover content; confirm essential information is visible or reachable via an explicit control; test screen reader gestures and confirm long press is not required</li> <li><strong>Screen reader:</strong> confirm the trigger’s accessible name is correct without the tooltip, the tooltip text is exposed as a description, name/description aren’t needlessly duplicated, focus is not moved, and repeated focus doesn’t produce stale descriptions. Test supported browser/AT combinations and record versions — presentation varies and no single announcement is universal</li> <li><strong>Visual/responsive:</strong> 200%/400% zoom, narrow viewports, text-spacing overrides, forced-colors mode, reduced motion, RTL text, viewport-edge placement</li> <li><strong>Automated:</strong> can catch missing/duplicate IDs, unresolved <code>aria-describedby</code> references, invalid ARIA values, focusable descendants inside a tooltip, inadequate contrast, hidden triggers, and stale open tooltips in component tests — but cannot prove hoverability, persistence, positioning, or screen-reader presentation. Keep manual tests in the release process.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-9">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Failure</th> <th>Correction</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td>Showing the tooltip only on hover</td> <td>Show it on keyboard focus too</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Hiding it when the pointer leaves the trigger</td> <td>Keep it open while the pointer is over the trigger or tooltip</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Hiding it when pointer leaves even though focus remains</td> <td>Track pointer and focus state separately</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Closing it after a fixed timeout</td> <td>Keep it visible until trigger removal, dismissal, or invalidation</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Moving focus into the tooltip</td> <td>Keep focus on the trigger</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Putting a link or button in <code>role="tooltip"</code></td> <td>Use a disclosure, non-modal dialog, or other popup</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Using <code>aria-expanded</code>/<code>aria-haspopup</code> for an automatic tooltip</td> <td>Use <code>aria-describedby</code> and <code>role="tooltip"</code></td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Relying on <code>title</code> for a control label or instruction</td> <td>Provide a visible label and persistent/authored help</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td>Overwriting existing <code>aria-describedby</code> IDs</td> <td>Append and preserve all relevant references</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td>Attaching essential help only to a disabled control</td> <td>Make the explanation visible</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="definition-of-done-checklist-24">Definition of Done Checklist</h5> <ul class="task-list"> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />A tooltip is the correct pattern (see the pattern-choice table above)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Essential information is visible without opening the tooltip</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />The trigger has a complete accessible name without depending on the tooltip</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>role="tooltip"</code> on tooltip element with a unique <code>id</code></li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Trigger references it via <code>aria-describedby</code> without losing other descriptions</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Tooltip appears on both hover and keyboard focus</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>Escape</code> dismisses without moving focus; not closed on a fixed timer</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Tooltip hoverable (pointer can move over it without dismissal)</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Tooltip and all descendants are not focusable; no interactive content inside</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Touch users have visible information or an explicit help control</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Disabled controls do not hide their explanation</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Text contrast 4.5:1; required non-text contrast 3:1</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Reflows/wraps and remains operable at zoom and with text-spacing overrides</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" /><code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> respected for animations</li> <li><input type="checkbox" disabled="" />Tested across keyboard, pointer, touch, magnification, and supported screen readers</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="key-wcag-criteria-22">Key WCAG Criteria</h5> <ul> <li>1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)</li> <li>1.4.3 Contrast Minimum (AA)</li> <li>1.4.10 Reflow (AA)</li> <li>1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA)</li> <li>1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA)</li> <li>1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA) — <strong>Serious if hover-only or not dismissible</strong></li> <li>2.1.1 Keyboard (A) — <strong>Serious if keyboard cannot trigger tooltip</strong></li> <li>2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (A)</li> <li>2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA)</li> <li>2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum (AA)</li> <li>2.5.8 Target Size Minimum (AA)</li> <li>4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)</li> </ul> <hr /> <h5 id="references-27">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/TOOLTIP_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md">Full best practices guide</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F95">Failure F95: Content Shown on Hover Is Not Hoverable</a></li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Standards horizon:</strong> WCAG 3.0 is in development; 1.4.13 requirements are expected to carry forward. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="touch-pointer">Touch Pointer</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 3</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>touch-pointer</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/touch-pointer">skills/touch-pointer</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever the project contains interactive UI elements that users touch, tap, click, drag, swipe, or gesture with — buttons, links, drag-and-drop interfaces, sliders, carousels, or custom touch interactions. Under no circumstances create touch targets smaller than 44×44 CSS pixels. Absolutely always provide pointer cancellation, single-pointer alternatives to gestures, and load alongside keyboard/SKILL.md since pointer and keyboard requirements are complementary.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>touch-pointer/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="touch-and-pointer-accessibility-skill">Touch and Pointer Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/TOUCH_POINTER_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing any interactive UI that users touch, click, tap, drag, or gesture with. <strong>Load alongside <code>keyboard/SKILL.md</code> — pointer and keyboard requirements are complementary, not interchangeable.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-22">Core Mandate</h5> <p>Build interfaces that work with touchscreens, mice, trackpads, pens, head pointers, switch-controlled pointers, and other pointing devices. Do not infer a person’s abilities from the device they use — a touchscreen user may also use a keyboard, speech input, a screen reader, or a mouse.</p> <p><strong>A keyboard-only alternative does not by itself satisfy pointer-gesture (2.5.1) or dragging (2.5.7) requirements</strong> — the alternative must work with a single pointer, without a path-based gesture or drag, even though keyboard operability is separately required by 2.1.1. Native buttons conveniently satisfy both at once.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-25">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Functionality only available via multi-point gesture with no single-pointer alternative; <code>user-scalable=no</code> prevents zoom</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>Drag-to-reorder with no single-pointer alternative; touch target under 24×24px for primary actions</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Mousedown/touchdown action with no up-event cancellation; motion gesture without UI alternative</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Target under 44×44px for non-primary actions; spacing between targets too small</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Prioritize by actual user impact, task criticality, reach, and frequency — don’t assign severity solely from a success-criterion number or tool output.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="start-with-an-input-agnostic-base">Start With an Input-Agnostic Base</h5> <p>Use native HTML controls and links — their built-in <code>click</code> activation works across mouse, touch, pen, keyboard, and many AT.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb769"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb769-1"><a href="#cb769-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Incorrect --></span></span> <span id="cb769-2"><a href="#cb769-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">ontouchend</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"saveChanges()"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save changes<span class="kw"></div></span></span> <span id="cb769-3"><a href="#cb769-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb769-4"><a href="#cb769-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Correct --></span></span> <span id="cb769-5"><a href="#cb769-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"save-button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Save changes<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb769-6"><a href="#cb769-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><script></span></span> <span id="cb769-7"><a href="#cb769-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="bu">document</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">querySelector</span>(<span class="st">"#save-button"</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">addEventListener</span>(<span class="st">"click"</span><span class="op">,</span> saveChanges)<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb769-8"><a href="#cb769-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></script></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Use Pointer Events for custom direct-manipulation components rather than maintaining separate mouse/touch implementations. Do not gate core functionality on <code>pointerType</code> — a pen user shouldn’t lose a function a mouse user gets.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-never-block-zoom-user-scalableno">Critical: Never Block Zoom (<code>user-scalable=no</code>)</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb770"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb770-1"><a href="#cb770-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Critical violation — never do this --></span></span> <span id="cb770-2"><a href="#cb770-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><meta</span> <span class="er">name</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"viewport"</span> <span class="er">content</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb770-3"><a href="#cb770-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb770-4"><a href="#cb770-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Correct --></span></span> <span id="cb770-5"><a href="#cb770-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><meta</span> <span class="er">name</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"viewport"</span> <span class="er">content</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"width=device-width, initial-scale=1"</span><span class="kw">></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Some libraries/frameworks add <code>user-scalable=no</code> automatically — audit the viewport meta tag on every project. Do not rely on browsers ignoring restrictive viewport settings; remove the restriction from the source. Test text at 200% and layout at 400% zoom.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-single-pointer-alternatives-for-multi-pointpath-gestures-wcag-2.5.1">Critical: Single-Pointer Alternatives for Multi-Point/Path Gestures (WCAG 2.5.1)</h5> <p>A <strong>multipoint gesture</strong> uses two or more contact points (pinch zoom). A <strong>path-based gesture</strong> depends on the route/direction/shape traced, not just start/end points. When content defines such a gesture, provide a way to perform the same function with a single pointer and no path-based gesture — the alternative must exist <strong>in the content</strong>, not just as a keyboard command.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb771"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb771-1"><a href="#cb771-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><div</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"map-controls"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Map controls"</span><span class="kw">></span></span> <span id="cb771-2"><a href="#cb771-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">data-map-action</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"zoom-in"</span><span class="kw">></span>Zoom in<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb771-3"><a href="#cb771-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">data-map-action</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"zoom-out"</span><span class="kw">></span>Zoom out<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb771-4"><a href="#cb771-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">data-map-action</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"north"</span><span class="kw">></span>Pan north<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb771-5"><a href="#cb771-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"></div></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Examples: buttons for zooming/panning a map; previous/next buttons for a swipe carousel; a menu command alongside drawing a shape; visible rotate/ resize controls. Gestures required by the browser or AT itself (a mobile screen reader’s navigation gestures) are outside the author’s control — don’t reproduce or interfere with them.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-non-dragging-alternatives-wcag-2.5.7-wcag-2.2">Critical: Non-Dragging Alternatives (WCAG 2.5.7 — WCAG 2.2)</h5> <p>If a function uses dragging, provide a way to complete it with a <strong>single pointer without dragging</strong> — a keyboard-only alternative does not by itself satisfy 2.5.7. Native buttons satisfy both the pointer requirement and keyboard access at once.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb772"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb772-1"><a <span id="cb772-2"><a href="#cb772-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw"><li></span></span> <span id="cb772-3"><a href="#cb772-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span Other patterns: select item + destination + activate Move; tap a map control to pan; enter a value or click the track alongside dragging a slider thumb.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-pointer-cancellation-wcag-2.5.2">Serious: Pointer Cancellation (WCAG 2.5.2)</h5> <p>Activate ordinary controls on <code>click</code>, not <code>pointerdown</code>/<code>mousedown</code>/<code>touchstart</code>.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb774"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb774-1"><a href="#cb774-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Right — fires on click; user can drag away to cancel</span></span> <span id="cb774-2"><a href="#cb774-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>deleteButton<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">addEventListener</span>(<span class="st">"click"</span><span class="op">,</span> deleteItem)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div> <p>WCAG permits several patterns: (1) the down event doesn’t execute the function; (2) the function completes on the up event and the user can abort before releasing or undo after; (3) releasing reverses the down event’s outcome; (4) completing on down is essential. For destructive or hard-to-reverse actions, also confirm or provide Undo:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb775"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb775-1"><a class="st">"undo-archive"</span> <span class="er">hidden</span><span class="kw">></span>Undo archive<span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-target-size-minimum-wcag-2.5.8-wcag-2.2">Serious: Target Size Minimum (WCAG 2.5.8 — WCAG 2.2)</h5> <p>Pointer targets must be at least <strong>24×24 CSS pixels</strong>, except when:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Spacing</strong> — a 24px-diameter circle centered on the target doesn’t intersect another target’s equivalent circle (this is a specific geometric test, not just “add some margin”)</li> <li><strong>Equivalent</strong> — another control on the same page performs the same function and meets the size requirement</li> <li><strong>Inline</strong> — the target is in a sentence, size constrained by line height</li> <li><strong>User agent control</strong> — the browser determines the size, unmodified by the author</li> <li><strong>Essential</strong> — the specific presentation is essential or legally required</li> </ul> <p><strong>44×44 CSS pixels is the recommended default</strong> for important/frequent controls — easier to implement and test than relying on the spacing exception, and it’s also the WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) Target Size Enhanced threshold.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb776"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb776-1"><a href="#cb776-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.icon-button</span> {</span> <span id="cb776-2"><a href="#cb776-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">inline-grid</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb776-3"><a href="#cb776-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">min-inline-size</span>: <span class="dv">2.75</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">/* 44px at default 16px root */</span></span> <span id="cb776-4"><a href="#cb776-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">min-block-size</span>: <span class="dv">2.75</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb776-5"><a href="#cb776-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">padding</span>: <span class="dv">0.625</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb776-6"><a href="#cb776-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="kw">place-items</span>: <span class="dv">center</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb776-7"><a href="#cb776-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb776-8"><a href="#cb776-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.icon-button</span> svg { <span class="kw">inline-size</span>: <span class="dv">1.5</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">block-size</span>: <span class="dv">1.5</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Use <code>rem</code> so the target grows with the user’s default text size. <strong>Put padding on the interactive element itself, not a non-interactive wrapper</strong> — the whole padded area must be clickable:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb777"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb777-1"><a href="#cb777-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><a</span> <span class="er">class</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"nav-link"</span> <span class="er">href</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"/account/"</span><span class="kw">></span>Account<span class="kw"></a></span></span></code></pre></div> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb778"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb778-1"><a href="#cb778-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.nav-link</span> { <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">inline-flex</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">min-block-size</span>: <span class="dv">2.75</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">padding</span>: <span class="dv">0.625</span><span class="dt">rem</span> <span class="dv">0.875</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">align-items</span>: <span class="dv">center</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Do not apply a blanket minimum width/height to every <code><a></code> — inline prose links have a defined exception and forcing them into square boxes damages reading and wrapping. Associate checkboxes/radios with visible <code><label></code> elements so the label extends the operable area.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-motion-actuation-alternative-wcag-2.5.4">Serious: Motion Actuation Alternative (WCAG 2.5.4)</h5> <p>If shaking, tilting, or gesturing toward a camera performs a function: provide a conventional UI control for the same function; let the user disable motion actuation; request sensor permission only in response to a clear user action.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb779"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb779-1"><a href="#cb779-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"undo-button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Undo last change<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb779-2"><a href="#cb779-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><label><input</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"checkbox"</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"shake-toggle"</span><span class="kw">></span> Enable shake to undo<span class="kw"></label></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Keep the conventional button available whether motion input is enabled or not — default the sensor feature to off.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-do-not-depend-on-hover">Serious: Do Not Depend on Hover</h5> <p>Every function revealed on hover must also be available through a persistent control or keyboard focus — touch devices may not support hover reliably.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb780"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb780-1"><a href="#cb780-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-expanded</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"false"</span> <span class="er">aria-controls</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"account-menu"</span><span class="kw">></span>Account menu<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb780-2"><a href="#cb780-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><ul</span> <span class="er">id</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"account-menu"</span> <span class="er">hidden</span><span class="kw">></span>…<span class="kw"></ul></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Content on hover/focus must be dismissible, hoverable, and persistent (WCAG 1.4.13) unless an exception applies. A visible button/disclosure is usually more reliable than a tooltip for essential instructions.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-use-pointerhover-media-features-carefully">Moderate: Use <code>pointer</code>/<code>hover</code> Media Features Carefully</h5> <p><code>pointer</code>/<code>hover</code> describe the <em>primary</em> device; <code>any-pointer</code>/<code>any-hover</code> report capabilities across all available devices. <strong>These do not detect keyboard use, identify a disability, or reliably classify every pen as coarse or every touchscreen as primary</strong> — hybrid devices can report several capabilities that change while the page is open.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb781"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb781-1"><a href="#cb781-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.toolbar</span> button { <span class="kw">min-inline-size</span>: <span class="dv">2.75</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">min-block-size</span>: <span class="dv">2.75</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb781-2"><a href="#cb781-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">any-pointer</span>: coarse) { <span class="fu">.toolbar</span> { <span class="kw">gap</span>: <span class="dv">0.75</span><span class="dt">rem</span><span class="op">;</span> } }</span></code></pre></div> <p><strong>Never hide essential controls behind an accurate-pointer query:</strong></p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb782"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb782-1"><a href="#cb782-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">/* Incorrect: touch and keyboard users may lose the controls */</span></span> <span id="cb782-2"><a href="#cb782-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">pointer</span>: fine) { <span class="fu">.editing-controls</span> { <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">flex</span><span class="op">;</span> } }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Start with an accessible base layout, then use media queries only for enhancements.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-prefer-pointer-events-for-custom-interaction">Moderate: Prefer Pointer Events for Custom Interaction</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb783"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb783-1"><a href="#cb783-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>surface<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb783-17"><a href="#cb783-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Track the active <code>pointerId</code>; finish on <code>pointerup</code>; cancel cleanly on <code>pointercancel</code>; account for <code>lostpointercapture</code>; don’t assume every pointer reports pressure/tilt/dimensions; still provide non-gesture, non-dragging controls for the same function. Do not register both <code>touchend</code> and <code>click</code> for the same action without preventing duplicate activation.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-preserve-browser-panningzooming-with-touch-action">Moderate: Preserve Browser Panning/Zooming With <code>touch-action</code></h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb784"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb784-1"><a href="#cb784-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">/* A horizontal carousel handles horizontal movement;</span></span> <span id="cb784-2"><a href="#cb784-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"> preserve vertical page scroll and pinch zoom */</span></span> <span id="cb784-3"><a href="#cb784-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.carousel-viewport</span> { touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom<span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>Use <code>touch-action</code> only on the smallest custom surface that needs it. <strong>Never broadly apply <code>touch-action: none</code> to <code>html</code>, <code>body</code>, page containers, maps, canvases, or carousels</strong> — it suppresses browser panning/zooming starting on that element. Before restricting a gesture, confirm: the component genuinely needs to handle it; page scrolling still works from the component; pinch zoom remains available; a simple control provides the same function. <code>touch-action</code> is preferable to non-passive <code>preventDefault()</code> on every touch move.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="component-patterns">Component Patterns</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th style="text-align: left;">Component</th> <th style="text-align: left;">Required approach</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Carousel</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Prev/next/pause controls; don’t require swiping; preserve scrolling and reduced-motion</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Map</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Named zoom/pan controls; address/coordinates/list alternative when the visual map alone isn’t sufficient</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Slider</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Prefer <code><input type="range"></code>; provide numeric input or click-the-track alongside thumb dragging</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Sortable list</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Move up/down/to controls in addition to drag-and-drop; announce result, preserve focus</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Swipe action</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Expose via a visible button/menu; swipe must not be the only way to delete/archive/reveal</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Long press</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Provide an ordinary button/menu; must not be the only route to a function</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Drawing/signature</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Avoid requiring fine path accuracy when not essential; offer typed/uploaded alternatives where the task allows</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Canvas control</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Provide an accessible DOM interface for all operations, names, values, and results — canvas pixels alone create no semantics</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Do not depend on double-tap, pressure, tilt, edge swipes, or device-specific gestures for essential functions.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-keep-the-visible-label-in-the-accessible-name-wcag-2.5.3">Serious: Keep the Visible Label in the Accessible Name (WCAG 2.5.3)</h5> <p>Speech-input users (Dragon, iOS Voice Control) often activate a control by saying its visible label — the accessible name must contain that text.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb785"><pre class="sourceCode html"><code class="sourceCode html"><span id="cb785-1"><a href="#cb785-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Good --></span></span> <span id="cb785-2"><a href="#cb785-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span><span class="kw">></span>Send<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb785-3"><a href="#cb785-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Send application"</span><span class="kw">></span>Send<span class="kw"></button></span></span> <span id="cb785-4"><a href="#cb785-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb785-5"><a href="#cb785-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"><!-- Incorrect: visible text absent from accessible name --></span></span> <span id="cb785-6"><a href="#cb785-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw"><button</span> <span class="er">type</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"button"</span> <span class="er">aria-label</span><span class="ot">=</span><span class="st">"Submit application"</span><span class="kw">></span>Send<span class="kw"></button></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Putting the visible label at the <strong>start</strong> of a longer accessible name is a useful convention for speech input. An icon-only button has no visible label to compare under 2.5.3, but still needs a clear accessible name under 4.1.2 — use familiar icons and a visible label where space allows; a tooltip is not a substitute for a reliably available label.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="preserve-orientation-reflow-and-reachability">Preserve Orientation, Reflow, and Reachability</h5> <p>Support portrait and landscape unless one orientation is essential — don’t use orientation locks to compensate for an inflexible layout. At narrow widths and high zoom: keep controls in a meaningful order; wrap toolbars instead of shrinking targets below minimum size; prevent sticky headers/banners/chat widgets from obscuring focused controls; keep dialogs/ menus within the viewport; avoid horizontal page scrolling except where genuinely 2D content requires it. When an on-screen keyboard opens, focused inputs/errors/submit controls must remain visible or scrollable into view.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="account-for-touch-screen-readers">Account for Touch Screen Readers</h5> <p>Mobile screen readers change how touch input reaches the page — users may explore by touch, swipe through the accessibility tree, and use a screen-reader activation gesture instead of directly tapping. Use native elements and accurate accessible names; keep the accessible target aligned with the visible control; expose current state (expanded/selected/checked/ value); avoid custom gestures conflicting with AT gestures; don’t require spatial knowledge (“tap the shape in the upper-right corner”). Test both direct touch with the screen reader off and touch exploration with it on — passing one doesn’t establish the other works.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="prevent-accidental-activation-and-data-loss">Prevent Accidental Activation and Data Loss</h5> <p>Touch input can be imprecise or interrupted. For consequential actions: separate adjacent destructive/constructive actions; use clear labels instead of ambiguous icons; don’t execute on pointer-down; confirm hard-to-reverse actions; offer Undo when practical; preserve entered data after validation errors, orientation changes, or temporary disconnection. Target size is not the only safeguard — a large Delete button next to Save with no recovery path can still cause harm.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-13">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Review:</strong> inventory all controls/gestures; identify multipoint, path- based, dragging, swipe, long-press, pressure, tilt, and motion interactions; confirm each has the required single-pointer alternative (not just keyboard); measure actual target boxes in CSS pixels; search for restrictive viewport settings and broad <code>touch-action</code> rules; verify visible labels are in accessible names</li> <li><strong>Input:</strong> complete every task with touch alone, mouse/trackpad alone, pen (if supported), and keyboard alone; test speech input for visible labels; test touch exploration and activation with mobile screen readers; test a hybrid device switching between input modes. <strong>Use physical devices for final testing</strong> — emulation doesn’t reproduce hand occlusion, reach, accidental contact, or sensor permissions reliably</li> <li><strong>Visual/layout:</strong> portrait/landscape; 200%/400% zoom; smallest supported viewport with on-screen keyboard; sticky/fixed content not obscuring controls; pinch zoom and page scroll from every custom gesture surface</li> <li><strong>Interaction state:</strong> press down, move away, release — confirm cancellation works where required; interrupt a direct-manipulation interaction with scrolling/orientation change/loss of pointer capture; confirm drag alternatives produce the same result and preserve focus; confirm motion input can be disabled with its alternative still available</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated checks</strong> can identify some small targets, invalid names, restrictive viewport settings, and duplicate event patterns — cannot determine whether a gesture is essential, whether an alternative is equivalent/discoverable, or whether touch screen-reader interaction is understandable. Manual testing remains required.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-10">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr Orientation (AA)</li> <li>1.4.4 Resize Text (AA) — <strong>Critical if zoom blocked</strong></li> <li>1.4.10 Reflow (AA)</li> <li>1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA)</li> <li>2.1.1 Keyboard (A) — and 2.2). WCAG 3.0 is expected to extend pointer and touch requirements further. Monitor: <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/">w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0</a></p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="upstream-first">Upstream First</h3> <ul> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>upstream-first</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/upstream-first">skills/upstream-first</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill before implementing a fix for a barrier that may originate in a shared component, design system, renderer, or external dependency rather than this project’s own code. Decide whether the responsible fix is local, an existing installed capability, or an upstream contribution before writing a workaround. Absolutely always record any temporary local divergence with an owner and removal condition. Under no circumstances open, comment on, or submit anything in an external project without explicit human approval.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>upstream-first/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="upstream-first-skill">Upstream First Skill</h4> <p>This skill is a pointer to <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first">mgifford/upstream-first</a>, a separate, standalone set of agent skills for deciding where an accessibility (or any other) fix belongs and preparing it for the receiving project. It does not restate that project’s decision hierarchy, classification steps, or contribution workflow — those stay owned there so this skill does not drift out of sync with a project that is still a pre-release review draft.</p> <h5 id="when-to-use-this">When to Use This</h5> <p>Before implementing a fix for an accessibility barrier, check whether the affected code is actually owned by this project:</p> <ul> <li>a shared component or design system used across multiple projects;</li> <li>a renderer, framework, or platform dependency;</li> <li>an npm/PyPI/Packagist/Composer package rather than first-party code;</li> <li>a pattern that would benefit other consumers of the same dependency, not only this project.</li> </ul> <p>If the barrier may originate outside this project’s own code, load <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/upstream-first/SKILL.md"><code>upstream-first</code></a> to decide whether the responsible fix is:</p> <ol type="1"> <li>an existing installed capability;</li> <li>an existing public API or extension point;</li> <li>a suitable maintained open-source package;</li> <li>a focused contribution to an existing project;</li> <li>a new reusable open-source package with credible ownership; or</li> <li>a local implementation, with a written justification for why every higher option is unsuitable.</li> </ol> <p>Do not default to a local patch without going through this decision. A local fix for a shared-component barrier repeats the same maintenance burden for every other consumer of that component, and this project’s users are not the only people affected by the barrier.</p> <h5 id="preparing-a-contribution">Preparing a Contribution</h5> <p>If the decision favors an upstream contribution, use <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/maintainer-ready-contribution/SKILL.md"><code>maintainer-ready-contribution</code></a> to prepare an issue, proposal, patch, or pull request the receiving project’s maintainers can actually review and accept.</p> <p>If the issue may be a security vulnerability, do not open a public issue, reproduction, branch, fork, or pull request. Use <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/responsible-security-disclosure/SKILL.md"><code>responsible-security-disclosure</code></a> instead.</p> <p>If AI materially assisted a known contribution, run <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/ai-contribution-review/SKILL.md"><code>ai-contribution-review</code></a> before submission, when the receiving project’s policy permits that use.</p> <h5 id="human-approval-is-required">Human Approval Is Required</h5> <p>Never open, comment on, assign, label, fork, branch, or submit anything in an external project without a human explicitly approving that specific action. Deciding that a change belongs upstream is not the same as being authorized to act on that decision in someone else’s project.</p> <h5 id="tracking-temporary-local-divergence">Tracking Temporary Local Divergence</h5> <p>An urgent local patch, override, fork, pin, or workaround may be necessary while an upstream correction is pending — accessibility barriers should not wait on a release the project does not control. When this happens, do not treat it as resolved. Record it as debt with:</p> <ul> <li>a downstream owner;</li> <li>an upstream reference or a documented exception if none exists;</li> <li>a risk-based review date;</li> <li>the supported versions the patch applies to;</li> <li>a removal condition (a supported upstream release adopted and verified); and</li> <li>a rollback plan.</li> </ul> <p>If this project uses the <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md">ACCESSIBILITY.md</a> template, use the <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/ACCESSIBILITY-template.md#temporary-downstream-divergence-record">downstream divergence record</a>. Otherwise use the <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/examples/upstream-debt.example.json"><code>upstream-debt</code> record shape</a> directly.</p> <p><strong>A merged or closed upstream tracker item is not resolution.</strong> Closure requires the supported release to be adopted downstream and the original user-facing behavior to be retested — see <a href="https://mgifford.github.io/ACCESSIBILITY.md/examples/ACCESSIBILITY_FINDING_TRACKING.html#local-and-upstream-trackers">Accessibility Finding Tracking, “Local and upstream trackers”</a> if this project tracks findings with that schema.</p> <h5 id="relationship-to-other-skills">Relationship to Other Skills</h5> <ul> <li><a href="../ACCESSIBILITY-general/SKILL.md"><code>ACCESSIBILITY-general</code></a> governs when and how all skills in this repository are loaded; this skill is one of the things it points to when a fix’s ownership is unclear.</li> <li><a href="../bug-reporting/SKILL.md"><code>bug-reporting</code></a> records scope, likely source, and (when applicable) local and upstream tracker relationships for a filed finding — this skill decides what to do about that source before a fix is written, not after.</li> <li>Per-topic skills (<code>forms</code>, <code>keyboard</code>, <code>color-contrast</code>, and so on) define <em>how</em> to fix a barrier once ownership is decided. This skill decides <em>where</em> the fix belongs.</li> </ul> <h5 id="references-29">References</h5> <ul> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first">Upstream First</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/WHY_UPSTREAM_FIRST.md">Why Upstream-First Matters in the Age of AI</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/upstream-first/SKILL.md"><code>upstream-first</code> skill</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/maintainer-ready-contribution/SKILL.md"><code>maintainer-ready-contribution</code> skill</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/ai-contribution-review/SKILL.md"><code>ai-contribution-review</code> skill</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/upstream-first/blob/main/skills/responsible-security-disclosure/SKILL.md"><code>responsible-security-disclosure</code> skill</a></li> <li><a href="https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/examples/ACCESSIBILITY-template.md#temporary-downstream-divergence-record">ACCESSIBILITY.md: downstream divergence record</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>Skill text ends.</strong></p> <h3 id="user-personalization">User Personalization</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Files in the skill:</strong> 2</li> <li><strong>License:</strong> GNU Affero General Public License, version 3</li> <li><strong>Modified:</strong> on 30 September 2026, for this page: headings moved down and links written as reference links; wording unchanged</li> <li><strong>Name:</strong> <code>user-personalization</code></li> <li><strong>Publisher:</strong> Mike Gifford</li> <li><strong>Repository:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills">mgifford/accessibility-skills</a></li> <li><strong>Source:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/mgifford/accessibility-skills/tree/ada839399f053c55e1a776a98c02f8904d70dd32/skills/user-personalization">skills/user-personalization</a></li> </ul> <p>Load this skill whenever the project has personalization features, user preference controls, theme selectors, font size adjusters, motion toggles, contrast settings, or any user-configurable accessibility accommodations. Under no circumstances override or ignore user OS-level accessibility preferences without explicit user consent. Absolutely always persist user preferences, apply them immediately, and respect prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast, and similar media queries.</p> <p><strong>Skill text begins.</strong> Save as <code>user-personalization/SKILL.md</code>.</p> <h4 id="user-personalization-accessibility-skill">User Personalization Accessibility Skill</h4> <blockquote> <p><strong>Canonical source</strong>: <code>examples/USER_PERSONALIZATION_ACCESSIBILITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md</code> in <code>mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md</code> This skill is derived from that file. When in doubt, the example is authoritative.</p> </blockquote> <p>Apply these rules when implementing user preference controls or reviewing existing personalization features. <strong>Only load this skill if the project has personalization features.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="core-mandate-23">Core Mandate</h5> <p>Personalization is an enhancement to an accessible foundation — not a repair layer and not a substitute for WCAG conformance. Start by respecting OS, browser, and AT settings; add site-specific controls only when they provide a meaningful choice users cannot reliably get from those existing tools. The page must still satisfy browser zoom, text resizing, text-spacing overrides, forced colors, and keyboard operation whether or not it offers a preference editor.</p> <p><strong>Preference precedence model:</strong> (1) start with an accessible default; (2) follow a recognized system/browser preference when the site setting is “System”/“Default”; (3) let an explicit site choice override only the corresponding presentation dimension; (4) let “Reset to defaults” remove site overrides and resume following the system. Do not interpret a media-query match as a diagnosis — people choose dark mode, reduced motion, or increased contrast for many reasons.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="severity-scale-this-skill-26">Severity Scale (this skill)</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th>Level</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Critical</strong></td> <td>Overlay used as compliance substitute; interferes with user’s AT</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Serious</strong></td> <td>OS-level preferences (reduced-motion, colour scheme) not respected</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td><strong>Moderate</strong></td> <td>Personalization widget not keyboard accessible; state not announced</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td><strong>Minor</strong></td> <td>Preferences not persisted; <code>prefers-reduced-data</code> not considered</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <hr /> <h5 id="critical-never-use-accessibility-overlays-as-a-compliance-substitute">Critical: Never Use Accessibility Overlays as a Compliance Substitute</h5> <p>Third-party “accessibility overlay” widgets that claim to auto-fix issues <strong>must not</strong> be used as a compliance substitute. <strong>Using an overlay as a compliance claim is Critical</strong> — they cannot fix underlying structural issues (missing labels, incorrect ARIA, tab order), actively interfere with users’ own AT (screen readers, browser zoom, OS high contrast), provide false compliance assurance, and are widely rejected by the disability community (see <a href="https://overlayfactsheet.com/">overlayfactsheet.com</a>).</p> <p>A preference editor is different from an overlay: it lets a user choose among presentations the site has deliberately designed and tested. Personalization must not: claim to make an otherwise inaccessible site conformant; rewrite semantics generically at runtime; interfere with AT or user styles; conceal unresolved defects; or replace remediation in source templates. Runtime remediation for a locked legacy system can be a documented, tested, temporary risk mitigation — not conformance, and not a reason to stop underlying remediation work.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="required-outcome-separate-wcag-requirements-from-enhancements">Required Outcome: Separate WCAG Requirements From Enhancements</h5> <p>WCAG usually requires content to <em>adapt</em> to user settings — it does not generally require a site to reproduce browser settings in a custom panel.</p> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col style="width: 50%" /> </colgroup> <thead> <tr class="header"> <th style="text-align: left;">Requirement</th> <th style="text-align: left;">What authors must actually do</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">1.4.4 Resize Text (AA)</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Don’t prevent user-agent resizing; content/controls stay usable at 200%. A site text-size control is one technique, not a universal requirement.</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA)</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Allow user overrides of line/paragraph/letter/word spacing without loss of content or function — the site does not have to <em>provide</em> spacing controls</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">1.4.10 Reflow (AA)</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Preserve content/functionality at the required narrow width</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Contrast / non-text contrast</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Every author-provided theme or preset must independently meet the applicable criteria</td> </tr> <tr class="odd"> <td style="text-align: left;">Reduced motion</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Respect <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code> where motion may create a barrier; a site control can add an additional override</td> </tr> <tr class="even"> <td style="text-align: left;">Reading mode, font choice, density</td> <td style="text-align: left;">Useful enhancements when research demonstrates need — not automatic WCAG requirements</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Do not claim that adding a preference panel makes inaccessible content conformant.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-respect-user-preference-media-features-progressive-enhancement">Serious: Respect User Preference Media Features (Progressive Enhancement)</h5> <p>Unsupported queries are ignored, so the default presentation must remain accessible without them.</p> <h6 id="color-scheme">Color scheme</h6> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb786"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb786-1"><a href="#cb786-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="in">:root</span> {</span> <span id="cb786-2"><a href="#cb786-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> color-scheme: <span class="dv">light</span> dark<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-3"><a href="#cb786-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="va">--page-background</span>: <span class="cn">#ffffff</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-4"><a href="#cb786-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="va">--text-color</span>: <span class="cn">#1f2937</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-5"><a href="#cb786-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb786-6"><a href="#cb786-6" aria-hidden="true" class="in">:root:not(</span><span class="ex">[data-theme]</span><span class="in">)</span> {</span> <span id="cb786-8"><a href="#cb786-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="va">--page-background</span>: <span class="cn">#111827</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-9"><a href="#cb786-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="va">--text-color</span>: <span class="cn">#f3f4f6</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-10"><a href="#cb786-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> }</span> <span id="cb786-11"><a href="#cb786-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb786-12"><a href="#cb786-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="in">:root</span><span class="ex">[data-theme</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">"dark"</span><span class="ex">]</span> {</span> <span id="cb786-13"><a href="#cb786-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> color-scheme: dark<span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-14"><a href="#cb786-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="va">--page-background</span>: <span class="cn">#111827</span><span class="op">;</span></span> <span id="cb786-15"><a href="#cb786-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="va">--text-color</span>: <span means “System”; an explicit selection sets the attribute. See <code>skills/light-dark-mode/SKILL.md</code> for the complete theme-selector pattern.</p> <h6 id="reduced-motion">Reduced motion</h6> <p><strong>Do not apply a universal rule forcing every animation/transition to <code>0.01ms !important</code></strong> — that pattern can break state changes and scripted event assumptions that rely on <code>transitionend</code>/<code>animationend</code> firing. Instead, remove or replace specific non-essential motion:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb787"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb787-1"><a href="#cb787-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">.panel</span> { <span class="kw">transition</span>: translate <span class="dv">200</span><span class="dt">ms</span> <span class="dv">ease-out</span><span class="op">,</span> opacity <span class="dv">200</span><span class="dt">ms</span> <span class="dv">ease-out</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb787-2"><a href="#cb787-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span> <span id="cb787-3"><a href="#cb787-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">prefers-reduced-motion</span>: reduce) {</span> <span id="cb787-4"><a href="#cb787-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="in">:root:not(</span><span class="ex">[data-motion]</span><span class="in">)</span> <span class="fu">.panel</span> { <span class="kw">transition</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb787-5"><a href="#cb787-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="in">:root:not(</span><span class="ex">[data-motion]</span><span class="in">)</span> { scroll-behavior: <span class="bu">auto</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb787-6"><a href="#cb787-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb787-7"><a href="#cb787-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="in">:root</span><span class="ex">[data-motion</span><span class="op">=</span><span class="st">"reduce"</span><span class="ex">]</span> <span class="fu">.panel</span> { <span class="kw">transition</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span></code></pre></div> <p>If motion communicates essential state, replace it with an immediate state change — don’t remove the information.</p> <h6 id="contrast-preferences">Contrast preferences</h6> <p><code>prefers-contrast</code> can express <code>more</code>, <code>less</code>, or <strong><code>custom</code></strong> — do not treat every match as a request for high contrast:</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb788"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb788-1"><a href="#cb788-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">prefers-contrast</span>: more) {</span> <span id="cb788-2"><a href="#cb788-2" class="va">--muted-text-color</span>: currentColor<span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb788-3"><a href="#cb788-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span> <span id="cb788-4"><a class="kw">background-image</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">box-shadow</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb788-9"><a href="#cb788-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>An unqualified <code>prefers-contrast</code> query is appropriate for reducing visual complexity generally — it is not appropriate for imposing a specific high-contrast palette, since the user may have requested <em>less</em> contrast or a custom palette.</p> <h6 tested response — it is not a general focus-indicator fix. Media Queries Level 5 remains a W3C Working Draft — treat newer features as evolving, not a replacement for a tested default.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-use-an-accessible-preference-editor">Moderate: Use an Accessible Preference Editor</h5> <p>Prefer an inline <code><details></code> disclosure when options are few — this avoids modal focus-management requirements:</p> <div class="sourceCode" class="kw"></details></span></span></code></pre></div> <p>Native radio buttons and selects already expose selected values — don’t add a live-region announcement for every visual change unless testing shows it’s necessary; a concise status message when saved/reset/unsaved is enough. Label the entry point by its purpose (“Display preferences”, “Reading settings”), not “Accessibility” — no single icon communicates every possible preference, so keep a visible text label even if an icon is present.</p> <p>If a modal is genuinely necessary, implement the complete pattern: accessible name, initial focus, contained tab sequence, Escape dismissal, visible close button, focus return to opener.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-apply-presentation-with-css-variables-not-raw-stored-strings">Moderate: Apply Presentation With CSS Variables, Not Raw Stored Strings</h5> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb791"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb791-1"><a href="#cb791-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="in">:root</span> { <span class="va">--content-measure</span>: <span class="dv">80</span><span class="dt">ch</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="va">--reading-line-height</span>: <span class="dv">1.5</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb791-2"><a href="#cb791-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="in">:root</span><span class="ex">[data-text-size</span><span Avoid fixed-height text containers or clipping that fail when font/text size/language/spacing changes.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-validate-apply-and-persist-values-safely">Serious: Validate, Apply, tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <p>Version the storage key (<code>.v1</code>) and migrate or discard old data deliberately when the schema changes — don’t try to interpret obsolete values. Explain persistence accurately: say “saved on this device,” not “follows you everywhere,” unless account sync actually provides that. Handle storage denial/corruption safely and always provide a working Reset.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="serious-persist-preferences-without-creating-a-privacy-profile">Serious: Persist Preferences Without Creating a Privacy Profile</h5> <p>Store only the values needed to reproduce the chosen presentation — never a presumed diagnosis or disability. Do not send preference values to analytics merely because they’re available; do not expose preferences in public profiles; make account sync intentional and transparent; protect synced settings as account data; document retention/cookie use under the project’s privacy process. User-preference media features can contribute to browser fingerprinting — prefer CSS responses over reading/transmitting values through JavaScript when possible.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-reduce-motion-and-distraction-without-removing-meaning">Moderate: Reduce Motion and Distraction Without Removing Meaning</h5> <p>Reduced motion isn’t the same as removing all visual change. Prefer: immediate state changes instead of movement across the viewport; crossfades where opacity alone isn’t problematic; paused decorative animation; manual controls for carousels; no smooth scrolling; stable control positioning. If moving/blinking/scrolling/auto-updating content meets WCAG 2.2.2’s conditions, provide Pause/Stop/Hide or update-frequency control — don’t hide these controls inside the same motion-heavy component. A site-level “Reduce motion” setting can supplement <code>prefers-reduced-motion</code>; “System” must keep responding when the OS setting changes.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="moderate-font-choices-and-reading-adaptation">Moderate: Font Choices and Reading Adaptation</h5> <p>Evidence does not support naming one font as universally best for dyslexia or any disability — do not tell users which font they need based on a disability; let them choose based on the result they can see. If offering a font choice: describe neutrally (Sans serif/Serif/Monospace); ensure full language/character coverage; provide robust fallbacks; preserve user-agent minimum font-size settings; provide Default and Reset.</p> <p>A reading layout may constrain line length, increase spacing, remove decorative backgrounds, reduce density, or reorder primary vs. supplementary content — but must never silently remove instructions, warnings, error messages, or required task information. If a setting hides optional material, tell users what’s hidden and provide an immediate way to restore it. W3C COGA guidance and WAI-Adapt are supplemental resources, not additional WCAG 2.2 conformance requirements.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="keep-every-theme-and-preset-independently-accessible">Keep Every Theme and Preset Independently Accessible</h5> <p>Every author-provided theme must independently meet: text contrast; non-text contrast; focus visibility/not-obscured; visited-link distinction; selected/ checked/expanded/current/error states; chart/icon legibility; forced-color behavior; print output. Do not label a site preset “High contrast” unless it’s a defined, tested, complete theme — and don’t imply it’s equivalent to the OS forced-colors mode. <strong>“Higher contrast” is often the more accurate label.</strong></p> <hr /> <h5 id="progressive-enhancement-and-failure-handling">Progressive Enhancement and Failure Handling</h5> <p>The unenhanced page must remain readable and operable: use CSS media queries even when a site control is also present; use native HTML controls before custom widgets; don’t require third-party scripts for basic access; don’t block rendering on remote preference services; preserve system preferences if storage fails; keep reset/recovery available after a partial failure.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="minor-prefers-reduced-data">Minor: <code>prefers-reduced-data</code></h5> <p>An emerging media query for serving lighter content on metered connections. Support is currently limited — gate behind <code>@supports</code> or feature detection and treat as forward-looking, not a current requirement.</p> <div class="sourceCode" id="cb793"><pre class="sourceCode css"><code class="sourceCode css"><span id="cb793-1"><a href="#cb793-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">@media</span> (<span class="kw">prefers-reduced-data</span>: reduce) {</span> <span id="cb793-2"><a href="#cb793-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> <span class="fu">.decorative-hero-image</span> { <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb793-3"><a href="#cb793-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a> video<span class="ex">[autoplay]</span> { <span class="kw">display</span>: <span class="dv">none</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span> <span id="cb793-4"><a href="#cb793-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div> <hr /> <h5 id="testing-14">Testing</h5> <ul> <li><strong>Default/failure states:</strong> test before JS runs and with JS disabled; block local storage and confirm settings still apply for the current page; insert malformed/obsolete stored values and confirm they’re ignored; test first visit, returning visit, Reset, sign-out; confirm storage/network failure doesn’t block content</li> <li><strong>System preferences:</strong> test light/dark schemes and changing scheme while the page is open (System mode should follow); test reduced motion before and after load; test <code>prefers-contrast</code> values (more/less/custom); test at least one light and one dark forced-color palette</li> <li><strong>Site controls:</strong> operate every setting with keyboard, touch, pointer, and speech input; confirm labels/groups/values/focus/status with a screen reader; confirm applying a setting doesn’t move focus or navigate unexpectedly; confirm Reset returns presentation and controls to defaults</li> <li><strong>Content/layout:</strong> resize text to 200%; test 400% zoom and required narrow width; apply all four Text Spacing override values; confirm controls, tables, diagrams, and messages remain available</li> <li><strong>Combinations:</strong> test individual settings first, then high-risk combinations (extra-large text + comfortable layout, dark theme + reduced motion, explicit theme + forced colors, 400% zoom with panel open, stored preferences after a schema update) — use pairwise/risk-based coverage, not exhaustive combination testing</li> </ul> <p><strong>Automated checks</strong> can verify some contrast, labels, states, storage behavior, and target sizes — cannot determine whether a preference is understandable, whether combinations create cognitive overload, or whether an injected remediation conflicts with AT. Include people who use relevant personalization/AT features in usability testing.</p> <hr /> <h5 id="common-failures-11">Common Failures</h5> <table> <colgroup> <col style="width: 50%" /> <col
